https://telex.hu/techtud/2026/08/03/magy.text: Menü Kereső Nagyon súlyos lehet az államkincstárt ért kibertámadás, a közzétett képek alapján a támadó gyakorlatilag ahhoz férhetett hozzá, amihez akart Techtud Flachner Balázs Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Telex által megkérdezett szakértők szerint a belső rendszerek ismerete nélkül nehéz megítélni a teljes érintettség mértékét, de a közzétett felvételek alapján úgy tűnik, hogy nagyon súlyos lehet az a kibertámadás, ami a Magyar Államkincstár alá tartozó Mezőgazdasági és Vidékfejlesztési Hivatalt (MVH) érte a múlt héten. Ha a támadó valóban mindenhez hozzáférést szerzett, amiről képernyőképeket tett közzé, akkor „egy 10-es skálán ez egyértelműen 10-es besorolású incidens”. A szervezet vasárnap erősítette meg a Telexnek , hogy kibertámadás érte az informatikai hálózatát, de a jelenlegi információik szerint adatvesztés nem történt, a szükséges lépéseket pedig megtették. Azt is hozzátették, hogy a támadás orosz szerverekről történt, de a támadásról egy fórumon és a saját honlapján is részleteket posztoló, ByteToBreach nevű hekker kérdésünkre azt írta, fogalma sincs, honnan származhat ez az infó. „A támadás állítólagos orosz eredete engem is meglep, nem tudom, hogy juthatott valaki erre a következtetésre, hacsak nem a korábbi traumáiból indult ki” – írta kérdésünkre a hekker. Levelében beismerte, hogy ő áll a támadás mögött, és, mint írta, ahogy két hete az általa feltört román földhivatali rendszer (ANCPI) esetében , úgy itt is egyedül a pénz motiválta a támadást. Ahogy ott, úgy állítása szerint itt sem követel váltságdíjat, és azt is írta, hogy a megszerzett adatokat szinte sosem adja el, inkább alkualapnak használja őket. Mint írta, csak a titkosított adatok feloldásában ajánlja fel a „segítségét”, az államkincstártól pedig senkit nem keresett meg, és nem is fog. A hekker a támadásról szóló posztjában elég részletesen végigment azon, hogy hogyan férkőzött be az államkincstár rendszereibe, erről a Telexnek annyit írt, hogy kizárólag dokumentált sérülékenységeket használt, és ezeket kombinálva szerzett egyre magasabb privilégiumokat a hálózaton belül. Mint írta, a Mezőgazdasági és Vidékfejlesztési Hivatal és egy nyugdíjakkal foglalkozó hivatal áldozatául esett egy zsarolóvírusnak, ami rengeteg adatot titkosított, de arra, hogy ezen túl milyen mértékben kompromittálódott a hálózat, nem válaszolt. Utalt viszont arra, hogy más rendszerekhez is hozzáfért, ami a közzétett képernyőképek alapján is valószínűnek tűnik. Ahogy a Telexnek nyilatkozó kiberbiztonsági szakértők kiemelték, ezekből látszik az is, hogy az egész támadás kiindulópontja az volt, hogy a támadó talált egy publikusan elérhető szervert, amelyen egy régi Java programokhoz használt alkalmazásszerver (az Oracle WebLogic) futott. Ez a rendszer tartalmazott egy olyan, magas kockázatú sebezhetőséget, amelyet a támadó ki tudott használni. Ez egyébként nagyon régi, már 2017 októbere óta ismert, az Oracle akkor ki is adott rá egy javítást . Ez önmagában még nem jelentett teljes sikert a hekkernek, de elég volt ahhoz, hogy tovább mozogjon a belső hálózatban, és további sebezhetőségeket, esetleg potenciális célpontokat keressen. „A támadók gyakorlatilag minden kritikus rendszerben megszerezték a legmagasabb szintű rendszergazdai jogosultságokat, vagyis teljesen szabadon mozoghattak a környezetben” – írta egy szakértő a közzétett képek és videók alapján arra a kérdésre, hogy a támadónak meddig sikerült eljutnia. A sebezhetőségekkel és a megszerzett jogosultságokkal ki tudták nyerni a felhasználók belépési adatait, és számos más szolgáltatás hitelesítését kezelő rendszer teljes adatbázisát, az itt tárolt jelszavakat pedig vissza is tudták fejteni. Ez azt jelenti, hogy ha valóban mindenhez hozzáfértek, ami a képeken látszik, akkor lényegében az MVH szinte összes felhasználójának belépési adataihoz hozzáférhettek. A szakértők szerint szintén rendkívül súlyos probléma, hogy az MVH teljes Windows-tartományához és tartományvezérlőjéhez is rendszergazdai hozzáférést szereztek. Ezekkel a jogosultságokkal a tartományhoz tartozó összes kliens- és szervergép, sőt akár a levelezőrendszer is elérhetővé válik. A virtualizációs környezethez szintén adminisztrátorjogot szereztek, mert az egyik gépen egy fájlban titkosítatlanul, olvasható formában szerepelt egy egyébként sem bonyolult jelszó. Így nemcsak az összes virtuális géphez, hanem azok adattárolóihoz és biztonsági mentéseihez is hozzáfértek, ami összesen 116 virtuális gépet és 229 terabyte-nyi adatot érint. Ezek alapján a támadók az MVH környezetében lényegében mindenhez hozzáférhettek, amihez hozzá akartak, akár az MVH tartományán túl is – de mivel erről a hekker a posztban és a válaszában sem árult el semmit, nehéz megmondani, hogy ez a gyakorlatban mit jelenthet. „Nagyon súlyos a helyzet. A fent említett okok miatt a támadók gyakorlatilag bármihez hozzáférhettek, és ha továbbra is jelen vannak a környezetben, akkor jelenleg is hozzáférhetnek bármely rendszerhez, amelyet el akarnak érni” – írta a Telexnek egy kiberbiztonsági szakértő. Szerinte nagyon sok munka lesz helyreállítani a rendszert, nem is lehet megmondani, hogy mennyire, mert ilyenkor csak teljes újratelepítéssel garantálható a teljes biztonság, ami egy ekkora hálózatnál rendkívül erőforrás- és időigényes feladat. A szakértő szerint a jövőbeni megelőzéshez sok helyen kellene megerősíteni a rendszert, mert ezek olyan problémák, amelyeket idejében észlelni kellett volna. A bemutatott támadói aktivitásnak riasztást kellett volna kiváltania, amire a biztonsági szakembereknek lett volna lehetőségük kellő időben reagálni. Ehelyett a támadó egy közel 10 éves sebezhetőséget kihasználva tudott bejutni a rendszerbe, ez idő alatt nem történt meg a szükséges frissítés. Az államkincstár közleménye szerint az érintett szervereket az észlelés után leválasztották a hálózatról, és lépéseket tettek a további károk elkerüléséért, adatvesztés pedig nem történt. Azt írták, csak belső felhasználók számítógépén tárolt állományok váltak titkosítottá, az általuk kezelt ügyféladatokat a jelenlegi információk szerint nem érintette a támadás. Az esemény teljes körű kivizsgálása a Nemzeti Kiberbiztonsági Intézet szakértőinek közreműködésével zajlik, összehangoltan dolgoznak a támadás elhárításán és a biztonságos működés mielőbbi helyreállításán. Hogy mi fog kiderülni az állítólagos orosz érintettségről, amit az államkincstár említ, de a hekker tagad, érdekes kérdés. A KELA nevű kiberbiztonsági cég nemrég azt állította , hogy a rendelkezésre álló adatok alapján ByteToBreach egy algériai férfi lehet, aki egyedül dolgozik, de ezt, vagy bármilyen hasonló állítást nagyon nehéz alátámasztani. A mostani támadás képein látható IP-cím holland volt, de önmagában erre nem lehet alapozni semmit, az ilyen támadásoknál a hekkerek mindig el szokták fedni a valós forráscímüket. Az mindenesetre az általa közzétett posztok és a Telexnek írt válasza alapján nagyon valószínű, hogy a támadást valóban ByteToBreach követte el, aki az elmúlt időszakban több kelet-európai országban is hajtott végre hasonló kaliberű akciókat. A legutóbbi ilyen a román ANCPI elleni támadás volt, ott a hekker annyira súlyos károkat okozott a rendszerben, hogy egy hétig tartott helyreállítani a működést, és ezalatt gyakorlatilag nem lehet földhivatali ügyeket intézni az országban. A hekkernek ott sem kellett túlzottan megerőltetnie magát, korábban kiszivárgott belépési adatokat és az ügynökség számára is ismert szoftveres sérülékenységeket használt ki. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/03/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter a Mavir vezénylő központjából megüzente Mészáros egyik érdekeltségének, hogy még nem késő visszafogni a fogyasztásukat Belföld Vida Benjámin Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Magyar Péter miniszterelnök a Mavir, azaz a Magyar Villamosenergia-ipari Átviteli Rendszerirányító Zrt. vezénylő központjából jelentkezett be hétfő este, a Védelmi Munkacsoport ülése után. A kormányfő azt mondta a Facebookon közzétett videójában , hogy országosan figyelik az energiafogyasztás egyensúlyát, „jelenleg már jócskán benne járunk a legkritikusabb időszakban”. Magyar a vezénylő központban lévő térképen megmutatta, hogy jelenleg a hálózat terhelése 6300 megawatt környékén jár. „Az áramfogyasztás ma is, ahogy az elmúlt napokban is, jóval lejjebb jár a tervezettnél” – mondta, hozzátéve, hogy az eltérés meghaladja az 500 megawattot. Ennyivel fogyaszt kevesebbet az ország a szakértői előrejelzésekhez képest. A miniszterelnök azt reméli, hogy a nap kritikus óráiban és a következő napokban is fenn tudják tartani ezt az előnyt. „Ha ezt el tudjuk érni, akkor továbbra is igaz lesz, hogy nem szükséges szigorúbb beavatkozás” – fogalmazott. Magyar Péter a nagyfogyasztó vállalatokról azt mondta, hogy a hétfői adatok szerint összesen már több mint 630 megawattnyi önkéntes korlátozást vállaltak. De továbbra is elvárják az önkéntes hozzájárulást, és ha lehetséges, vállaljanak a korábbinál nagyobb teljesítménycsökkentést. Magyar egy vállalatot név szerint is megemlített, a Mészáros Lőrinc érdekeltségébe tartozó izocukorgyárat, a Kall Ingredients Kft.-t, a vállalat eddig ugyanis nem válaszolt arra, hogy vállalja-e a 13 megawattos fogyasztásuk önkéntes visszafogását. „Innen is üzenem az olasz partoknál ringatózó, Rose d'Or nevű harmincmilliárdos jacht tulajdonosának, hogy még nem késő önkéntes felajánlást tenni, ahogy azt megtette több száz másik vállalat is” – mondta a miniszterelnök, utalva arra a luxusjachtra , amin 2023 óta többször is lefotózták Mészáros Lőrincet és a feleségét. A paksi vízállásról azt mondta Magyar, hogy jelenleg stagnál a vízszint, és a következő órákban eldőlhet, hogy megőrizhető-e a termelés az utolsó paksi turbinánál. https://www.theweek.in/news/world/2026/0.text: Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate, who were popular in the “manosphere” circles, were arrested in Miami on Saturday after fresh charges of rape and sex trafficking were filed in the UK, US and British officials said. The additional charges against Andrew, 39 and Tristan, 38, were brought on by the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service. The agency said that it is awaiting the the brother’s extradition to the UK. Andrew Tate is facing seven additional counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges relating to illegal child images and pornography. Tristan Tate faces one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation The charges cover alleged offences from July 2010 to August 2017, MBC news reported. The brothers hold dual US and British citizenship. The news charges relate to four additional alleged victims. Previous charges were connected to three alleged victims. The Tates have long denied all criminal allegations against them.  The brother’s lawyer said that the pair 'would walk' free before travelling across the Atlantic, the BBC reported. "We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free," he said “This is not law enforcement, this is a political hit... America does not do Britain’s political dirty work,” he added. The Tates were both former kickboxers and have been long associated with the manosphere, a social media phenomenon that is anti feminist and which has been accused of promoting toxic masculinity and misogyny. In 2022, they were arrested along with two Romanian women in Bucharest and subsequently indicted. Last year, a Romanian travel ban on the two was lifted, which allowed them to move to the US. The previous allegation included the coercion of a 17-year-old girl into pornography and the rape of a minor. They returned in 2025 and have remained under criminal investigation in Romania on allegations of organised crime, human trafficking, trafficking of minors and money laundering. The Crown Prosecution Service said that the decision to file new charges came after it received new evidence from police in Bedfordshire and neighbouring Hertfordshire County.

Sam Navarro/Imagn Images Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Andrew and Tristan Tate, “hypermasculine” influencers and former professional kickboxers, remain jailed in Miami as their lawyer fights their possible extradition to the United Kingdom to face charges of rape and human trafficking. The British request for extradition triggers a process that will ultimately be decided by Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But the Tate brothers have traveled to the United States repeatedly — including as recently as attending a UFC fight in Miami in April — without repercussions, despite pending criminal charges in Britain and Romania, and numerous civil lawsuits. The Tates have denied the charges. Joseph McBride, a defense attorney who represents the Tate brothers, told reporters outside the courthouse that an initial hearing July 20 was the first small step in fighting extradition. A lawyers-only meeting expected in several days to develop a schedule for filing written arguments, he said. U.S. Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis scheduled another hearing July 27. McBride is also fighting to stop having the Tate brothers held in solitary confinement. The brothers are being held in a 5-foot-by-12-foot cell, he said. “Solitary confinement is torture,” McBride said. “We’re working to get them out of there as soon as possible.” Because the case is being handled as an extradition rather than criminal complaint, bail is not available, McBride said. The arrests are the latest court action against the Tates, who have been the subject of numerous civil lawsuits alleging sexual violence and criminal prosecution in the United Kingdom and Romania. McBride said the arrests came days after the Tate brothers visited the Capitol to discuss political parties and upcoming elections, and after some members of Congress criticized them. “This feels political,” McBride said. “Of course they didn’t like it. No innocent man likes being taken to jail. It’s a horrible situation.” Who are the Tates? The Tates have millions of social media followers and are key figures in the “manosphere,” a collection of influencers, websites and spaces online. They promote fitness, lifestyle and get-rich-quick advice alongside a toxic blend of misogynistic and anti-feminist rhetoric while insisting they respect women. The brothers have faced numerous civil lawsuits and criminal investigations into potential sexual abuse. A civil lawsuit in Palm Beach, Florida, is proceeding and Andrew Tate faces trial in Britain this year in a civil case brought by four women who allege physical and sexual abuse from 2013 to 2015. Two of the women said they were in an intimate relationship with Tate while the two worked for his online webcam business. Tate denies the allegations and contends all sexual activity was consensual. Besides the British charges, the brothers face criminal proceedings in Romania, where authorities have been investigating them since December 2022. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier opened a criminal investigation into the Tates, characterizing its scope as “what very much appears to be soliciting, trafficking, preying upon women around the world.” What are the United Kingdom charges? The United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service announced a slew of charges against the Tates shortly before the brothers were arrested July 18 by U.S. Marshals based on an extradition warrant. The charges against Andrew Tate include seven new counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges for offenses relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate is being prosecuted on one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. The charges are in addition to 21 original charges, including rape and human trafficking, brought in the United Kingdom, bringing the total charges against both brothers to 59. “We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the Special Crime Division at the Crown Prosecution Service, said in a statement. “These charging decisions followed receipt of a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and bring the total number of alleged victims in this case to seven.” McBride issued a statement asking followers to “pray for” the brothers in their fight against “baseless” allegations. McBride, who has been defending the Tates in a civil defamation case in Palm Beach, Florida, accused the British government of seeking extradition before the civil case collapsed. “This extradition demand has one purpose: to kidnap Andrew and Tristan through paperwork before an American jury exposes the truth to the entire world,” McBride said in a statement. President Donald Trump courted members of the manosphere in his election campaign, including appearing on podcasts hosted by allies of the Tate brothers. After the Tate brothers were arrested in Romania, Donald Trump Jr. posted on social media that the prosecution was “absolute insanity.” The New York Times reported in December 2025 that the Tates had long cultivated friendships and influence with the president’s allies, including his youngest son, Barron Trump, who communicated with Andrew Tate over Zoom. But the Trump administration denied any connection to the Tates, calling the reports “fake news.” Rubio must ultimately decide whether to extradite the Tate brothers. The Justice Department traditionally examines whether the allegations merit extradition. The factors include any statutes of limitations, evidence of crimes, severity of allegations, whether the charges appear politically motivated and the nationality of the suspects. “If the court finds the fugitive to be extraditable, it certifies the extradition and sends the record to the Secretary of State, who decides whether to surrender the fugitive,” according to a Justice Department manual. Appeals are possible. The Tate brothers have dual citizenship with the United States and the United Kingdom. McBride argued that “America does not do Britain’s political dirty work.” “We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts the egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,” McBride said. Photo: X/@rashtrapatibhvn President Droupadi Murmu arrived here on a two-day state visit, as part of her three-nation tour of European countries aimed at boosting ties. She is the first Indian President to visit North Macedonia. During the second leg of her visit to this landlocked country in southeastern Europe, beginning from Tuesday (July 19, 2026), Ms. Murmu will hold bilateral talks with her counterpart Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova. President Murmu arrives in Moldova; first by any Indian head of State She will also meet Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski, Speaker of the Assembly Afrim Gashi and address the Parliament here. Ms. Murmu is scheduled to address the India-North Macedonia Business Forum as well. Both sides have a keen interest in deepening economic ties in priority sectors such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, science and technology, Information Technology, and IT-enabled Services. President Murmu will also visit Memorial of Mother Teresa. Mother Teresa was born on August 26, 1910 in Skopje— the modern day capital of North Macedonia. She lived in Skopje until 1928, when she left to join the Sisters of Loreto in Ireland before eventually moving to India. Built in 2009, this museum sits on Macedonia Street in the heart of Skopje. It stands on the exact site of the former Sacred Heart of Jesus Roman Catholic Church, where she was baptised the day after her birth. Mother Teresa was awarded Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian honour, in 1980. North Macedonia, which shares land borders with Greece to the south, Albania to the west, Bulgaria to the east, Kosovo to the northwest and Serbia to the north, covers an area of 25,713 square kilometres. The Indian community in North Macedonia is very small. Most of them are engaged in the IT sector, teaching at universities or working as executives in multinational companies. In the final leg of her tour, Ms. Murmu will visit Romania from July 23 to 25 at the invitation of President Nicusor Dan. It will be the first visit by an Indian president to Romania in more than three decades. The state visit to the three nations reflects the importance India attaches to strengthening its bilateral ties with these countries, along with New Delhi's engagement with the wider Eastern European region. One of the most important focus of the visit is on 3Ts - trade, technology and tourism, Secretary (West) in the Ministry of External Affairs Sibi George has said. https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/cul.text: By Kat Tenbarge Kat Tenbarge View all posts by Kat Tenbarge July 21, 2026 Tristan (left) and Andrew Tate at a UFC fight in Miami on April 11. Julia Demaree Nikhinson - Pool/Getty Images Andrew Tate , the infamous internet misogynist and human-trafficking suspect , was arrested in Miami alongside his brother Tristan on Saturday after the U.K. leveled new charges of rape and child exploitation against them. A one-minute clip of U.S. marshals putting the two in handcuffs quickly went viral, with their ill-fitting outfits and especially Andrew’s gaping purple blouse inspiring widespread mockery . But the new charges brought by the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) are no laughing matter, and the Tate brothers are currently being held in a federal detention center awaiting an extradition process to potentially face trial in the U.K. According to The New York Times , court documents that were unsealed on Monday include allegations against Andrew from two alleged victims in the U.K. One woman said Andrew choked her until she passed out and then raped her in her home in Bedford, England, in 2015. Another woman said she met him on a dating app and that he later choked her to the point she was afraid he would kill her. Another alleged victim described a physically and sexually abusive relationship with Tristan, where she said he regularly choked her, assaulted her, and raped her in 2012 and 2013. This is separate from the ongoing Romanian investigation into the Tates on suspicion of human trafficking, the trafficking of minors, sexual intercourse with a minor, and money laundering. According to Romanian authorities , the brothers are suspected of convincing dozens of women that they were in relationships to coerce them into making pornography that was sold for more than $2.8 million and close to a million crypto tokens online. After the Tate brothers were first arrested in their compound outside Bucharest, Romania, in late 2022, procedural issues led to a judge lifting their travel restrictions in early 2025. They immediately flew to Florida, where Donald Trump’s administration reportedly intervened to try and help them regain access to their electronic devices that were seized by Customs and Border Protections officials — a move that divided Trump’s conservative base and contributed to mounting criticism that Trump has worked to protect sexual predators while in office. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century This time, it seems unlikely that Trump’s team will move to shield the Tates from accountability. Trump has denied knowing anything about their case. A legal representative for the brothers didn’t immediately respond to Rolling Stone ’s request for comment, but previously told outlets that they would “exhaust all remedies” to fight extradition. The Tates strongly deny all of the allegations against them, which now span at least three criminal investigations and four civil lawsuits in three countries. “The elephant in the room is the Trump administration and their reported interference,” says Nathan Pope, an Australian YouTuber who has been making content about the Tates for years and is currently fighting a defamation lawsuit they refiled against him this year. “Blocking the extradition would be a far more extreme measure, and I feel like it would be such a PR and potential political disaster that I would be very surprised.” Why the Tate Brothers Were Arrested — Again The new plan to extradite the Tate brothers to the U.K. is a departure from the previous arrangement between the CPS and Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT). Originally, the Tates were going to face trial in Romania first, then head to Europe for another round. But in late 2024 , a Romanian judge ruled that prosecutorial mishaps had axed the upcoming trial. A second criminal investigation in Romania is underway, with hate speech charges added as of May, but the ball is now in Britain’s court. Now, CPS says four new accusers have come forward, and new evidence collected by the Bedfordshire Police in England laid the groundwork for a combined 38 new charges against Andrew, 39, and Tristan, 38. The previous rape and sexual assault case against Andrew in the U.K. was opened in 2015 and closed in 2019, but it was reopened in 2025 after media reports detailed how alleged victims felt they were failed by the system, which declined to prosecute Andrew based on “an ounce of doubt.” Related Content Andrew and Tristan Tate Arrested in Miami, Await Extradition to U.K. on New Rape Charges I Paid $49 for Clavicular’s ‘Looksmaxxing’ Academy. What I Saw Should Scare Us All Andrew Tate Agrees to 3-Year Restraining Order, Can’t Possess Firearms in U.S. Alt-Right YouTuber Lauren Southern Alleges in Memoir That Andrew Tate Sexually Assaulted Her The case also drew renewed scrutiny after the award-winning British series Adolescence highlighted the role the online manosphere had in radicalizing young men into committing acts of violence against women, even mentioning “the Andrew Tate shite” (to which a spokesperson replied: “The reference to Andrew Tate in Adolescence is an attempt to pin broader societal issues on one individual, which is neither fair nor accurate”). A statement released by CPS on Sunday said prosecutors have charged Andrew with “seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm, and 19 additional charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” Tristan has been charged with “one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape, and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.” This brings the total number of pending charges against the brothers to 59 counts involving seven alleged victims. These new offenses were alleged to have taken place between 2010 and 2017, while the original U.K. case against Andrew was linked to events in 2013 and 2015. That initial police investigation was reportedly the reason why Andrew was removed from the U.K. reality show Big Brother in 2016, although at the time he attributed it to a video of him hitting a woman with a belt that had been leaked online. (She then posed with the belt for a photo with Andrew while he referred to the incident as consensual.) Malcolm McAffie, the head of the Special Crime Division at CPS, stated in a release, “It is extremely important that there be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information online which could in any way prejudice these proceedings.” But this is unlikely, especially given the Tate brothers’ own inflammatory commentary about their supposed innocence and the “matrix” conspiracy they’ve pushed to explain their staggering legal predicament. How the Tate Brothers Got Here After Andrew’s dismissal from the Big Brother house in 2016, the then-burgeoning influencer’s profile soon exploded online. He built an empire from misogynistic rants — largely spread by an army of short-form video clippers — and subscription schemes like Hustlers University and the Real World, where hundreds of thousands of users paid to learn about the art of exploiting women from the Tate brothers. What they preached in their lessons would ultimately become the backbone of the Romanian criminal case against them, which outlined the “loverboy” method of targeting and lovebombing vulnerable women to groom and trap them in relationships where they then performed coerced sexual labor like webcamming and handed over their profits to the Tates. Alleged victims, including women who were discovered working at the Romanian compound after authorities raided the property, described the Tates’ escalating sexual and physical abuse once they were isolated from family and friends. Some of them were branded with tattoos like “Owned by Tate” and “Tate Girl.” As alleged victims started cooperating with Romanian authorities, the Tate brothers harnessed their loyal fan armies and the legal system to begin a campaign of alleged harassment and lawfare . In 2023, they filed a defamation suit against one accuser in Florida and her parents, alleging that they conspired to falsely accuse the brothers. In 2025, that anonymous woman filed a countersuit , alleging in turn that the Tates defamed her. “We are thankful to the United States and United Kingdom authorities for courageously pursuing justice with the arrest and extradition of accused sex traffickers Andrew and Tristan Tate . Most importantly, our client Jane Doe and her family, who have been victims of a campaign of harassment and witness intimidation at the hands of the Tate brothers, are safer,” said her attorney, Dani Pinter, in a statement shared with Rolling Stone on Monday. Pinter is the chief legal officer and director of the law center at the National Center on Sexual Exploitation, which has represented multiple alleged victims of the Tates. The minute that Andrew and Tristan touched down in Florida last year, James Uthmeier, the state’s attorney general, opened a criminal probe based on the allegations in Romania, announcing that “these guys have themselves publicly admitted to participating in what very much appears to be soliciting, trafficking, preying upon women around the world.” With Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis’ sights set on another presidential run, his state administration’s stance on the Tates is another way to differentiate himself from Trump 2.0. The status of Florida’s investigation into the brothers remains unclear. What’s Next for the Tate Brothers Even as they dodge criminal investigations in the U.S., the U.K., and Romania, the Tates have continued to sue their critics. After a 2025 defamation lawsuit against online sleuths was dismissed , they filed an amended complaint this year. Pope, who is a named defendant in the Tates’ latest defamation lawsuit over his channel , tells Rolling Stone he feels “partly vindicated” by Saturday’s arrests. “Some of the Tates’ allegations of defamation have been with my coverage of their U.K. cases and me expressing my opinion that the initial investigation into women who complained to the police in the U.K. was not handled correctly,” he says. “The authorities seem to, in a way, have corroborated my feeling that I have not defamed them.” On Monday, a Miami judge ruled that the brothers must remain in federal custody while he considers their argument against extradition. At a press conference, their lawyer claimed that the Tates are being subjected to “torture” in solidary confinement. Previously, he said that the extradition order was approved by a “low-level functionary” at the Justice Department without higher-up input, but the department said the arrests were approved by the leader of its Criminal Division. Since their initial 2022 arrest, the Tates have “fallen off” significantly online, Pope says, losing a lot of their audience to competing manosphere influencers who have taken Andrew’s place at the helm of the extremist movement. Pope hopes that government officials and schools will continue to invest resources into combating the new faces of online misogyny in addition to prosecuting the Tate brothers. Somebody appears to have access to his X account, because it has been active since the arrest — a post on Sunday said, “The U.K. can try, but it can’t actually stop me from tweeting,”which included a smiley-face emoji. It’s a classic Tate maneuver, but as his online appeal fades, so do his chances of regaining his freedom. https://www.fox2detroit.com/news/andrew-.text: article Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate talk to the media outside their residence on March 23, 2025 in Bucharest, Romania. (Photo by Andrei Pungovschi/Getty Images) Expand The Brief Andrew and Tristan Tate will fight extradition to the U.K. following their arrest in Miami over the weekend. British prosecutors recently filed new rape and sex trafficking charges against them related to investigations involving four victims. The pair already face similar charges in the UK in cases that involved multiple other victims. Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate plan to fight being sent to the United Kingdom where they face a host of rape and sex trafficking charges. Big picture view: The brothers were detained in Miami over the weekend and appeared in a federal court for the first time on Monday as a judge weighs whether they meet the conditions to be extradited. The Tate brothers’ attorney, Joseph McBride, told the court that his clients should not be sent to the U.K. to stand trial because "they’ve never done nothing wrong. They shouldn’t be extradited for crimes they did not commit." Lawyer suggests political motivation McBride also hinted at the Tates’ arrests being politically motivated, telling reporters that "there’s no question about it." He alleged his clients’ case was a big factor in the recent fall of British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, although he did not say how. McBride also indicated that the brothers were arrested after meeting "friends in Washington, D.C." Again, though, he was light on details when it came to who they may have met or why. The charges The Tate brothers had already faced rape, human trafficking, and other charges relating to allegations by three women regarding events that occurred between 2012 and 2015 in North London, when prosecutors revealed even more charges Saturday in connection with four more victims. Including prior charges, Andrew Tate, 39, now faces a total of 10 counts of rape. Among the new allegations against him are three related to sex trafficking, three of assault, and 19 for offenses connected to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate, 38, faces two more counts of rape, in addition to the three already filed against him. The other new charges include a single count of sexual assault, and three counts related to sex trafficking, prosecutors said. Dig deeper: The brothers, who are former professional kick-boxers, are proponents of hypermasculinity and have gained millions of followers, particularly among young men and boys, by advocating a life of luxury and misogyny. The Tate brothers are dual U.S. and British citizens and moved to Romania in 2016, where they were arrested six years later on allegations of sexual exploitation. They denied the charges and the cases ended up not going forward because of legal and procedural irregularities. The Source: Information for this article was taken from The Associated Press and previous coverage. This story was reported from Orlando. https://www.politico.eu/article/eurogrou.text: Can money appear out of thin air? Greek Finance Minister Kyriakos Pierrakakis says he can make it appear from the airwaves. Pierrakakis, who chairs the Eurogroup, the informal gathering of finance ministers from countries that use the euro, is floating a potentially bold new way to raise money for the EU: redirecting lucrative proceeds from national spectrum auctions to Brussels just as debate heats up over the bloc's seven-year budget. “It’s telecom policy à la Draghi,” he said in an interview, invoking the former Italian prime minister’s blueprint for reversing Europe’s economic decline, which called for greater coordination and harmonization in how national governments license the frequencies that power mobile networks. Such an arrangement would also have the benefit of encouraging more European buildout of crucial bloc-wide technology. Advertisement Advertisement Europe’s telecom operators currently face a patchwork of national procedures to secure access to this coveted and critical asset, including auctions whose proceeds flow into national budgets. Since 2020, operators have spent more than €50 billion on spectrum licenses, according to trade association Connect Europe . The process has long been criticized for squeezing operators for cash rather than encouraging investment, with former EU Commissioner Thierry Breton once disparaging spectrum as a government “cash cow.” Pierrakakis — also the Greek finance minister — called for Europe to build on what he described as its “most innovative auction,” referring to Greece’s plan in 2020 to reserve 25 percent of spectrum-auction revenues for a new venture capital fund investing in the growing 5G ecosystem. The Eurogroup boss envisions allocating 75 percent of the auction proceeds to the Multiannual Financial Framework, the EU's long-term spending plan, and 25 percent channeled through an endowed European Investment Bank fund. With such a fund, he argued, "you would end up with a much larger amount in the hands of Europe overall." The outside-the-box proposal could give negotiators a fresh source of EU-level revenue — known in Brussels jargon as an “own resource” — as Europe remains divided over the bloc’s €2 trillion budget between the so-called frugal countries that want to limit spending and those that want to maintain current levels. Pierrakakis said he also wanted to link this "non-zero sum" idea to the push to boost European industrial champions and reduce the bloc’s dependence on U.S. technology. But the proposal may land with a thud among EU capitals, which have long resisted reform in this area and bristled at Brussels encroaching on a national competence — and a source of budget revenue. Advertisement Advertisement "This idea has layers. There is a very visible layer, which is simply synchronizing the auctions," Pierrakakis said, arguing that reducing fragmentation and moving closer to a single market would already be a big win. "The value for our champions and for our telecom operators is self-evident, before we go into the revenue discussion." He argued that a new paradigm is emerging in the wake of recommendations over the past years since the reports on European competitiveness from Draghi and fellow former Italian Prime Minister Enrico Letta. Specifically, he cited the Capital Markets Union, the EU’s long-running project to create a single market for investment and finance, which has recently gained traction. Mario Draghi is pictured in Paris on Nov. 13, 2024. | Pool photo by Teresa Suarez via EPA Still, even by his own admission, Pierrakakis' idea of the new allocation of airwave revenue will be a tough sell. “I don’t think it would win broad support,” a national government official said, granting anonymity to discuss an informal proposal. The official noted that countries would be reluctant to give up the revenue, and are likely to resist any attempt by the European Commission to secure a bigger role in spectrum coordination through the Digital Networks Act , which is currently under negotiation. "In general, letting the Commission collect spectrum fees is not something member states like," echoed a second official from another government. The lead negotiator for the proposal in the European Parliament, centrist Polish MEP Michał Kobosko, previously said in an interview that he didn't want to stick to the "status quo that the government is taking this huge money from the operators and then nobody has any say in how the money is being used." Advertisement Advertisement Pierrakakis voiced hope that his idea could feed into negotiations over the EU’s 2028-2034 budget and the broader debate over European competitiveness. He said "many" of his colleagues have already "endorsed the core philosophy of the idea." "We need to go into a more detailed and thorough phase where we need a concrete impact study, steps, et cetera, to further discuss this.” This article was updated to clarify Kyriakos Pierrakakis was elected Eurogroup president for a mandate of two and a half years.

https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/2629.text: Ryanair warns Edinburgh Airport passengers of EES queues Edinburgh Airport Ryanair Leisure Travel By Katie Collier Trending News Reporter Share 0 Comments Ryanair has warned everyone travelling from Edinburgh Airport to be aware of the long EES queues at 16 European airports this summer (Image: Getty) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Ryanair has issued a warning to Brits flying from Edinburgh Airport to Europe this summer, saying passengers should be prepared for "significant" queues at 16 major airports. The disruption, which is affecting 16 airports (all of which Edinburgh flies to), is linked to the European Union’s Entry Exit System (EES), which has continued to cause delays months after its introduction. First launched in October last year, the rollout accelerated on April 10. The system now requires British travellers and other non-EU visitors to provide biometric data, including fingerprints and facial scans, when entering the Schengen Area. The new EES has received significant backlash since its introduction, with it causing long waits for passengers at airports. Some travellers have already experienced waits of up to six hours, and industry experts warn these disruptions could continue for up to two years. Major airlines, including Jet2 and Ryanair, have called for the rollout of the new system to be suspended until after the summer to allow for a "smoother airport experience" during peak travel season. CEO of Malta Air, David O’Brien, even threatened to pull all flights to Malta due to the extended wait times caused by the EES at airports. EES to cause long queues at 16 major airports this summer Brits heading to Europe this summer have been told to expect more delays due to the EES. Ryanair has outlined 16 European airports where travellers can expect "significant" queues, which you can travel to from Edinburgh Airport: Tenerife South Palma/Majorca Alicante Malaga Milan Bergamo Milan Malpensa Krakow Paris Beauvais Lisbon Madrid Lanzarote Verona Berlin Cologne Frankfurt Hahn Budapest Chief operations officer at Ryanair, Neal McMahon, said: "Families heading away for a well-earned summer holiday should be thinking about suitcases, suncream and sangria, not standing in passport queues for hours. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Edinburgh Airport (@edinburghairport) "The reality is that the EES system isn’t working properly and families are paying the price for a system that does not work months after launch. "Passengers should not be the testing ground for unfished border infrastructure." Mr McMahon has backed calls from EU Member States to extend current EES flexibilities into early 2027. This extension would give airports and border authorities more time to fix malfunctioning kiosks, increase staffing levels, and ensure the system can operate efficiently before full enforcement is introduced. He said: "We support calls from EU Member States to urgently extend the EES flexibilities. "This will give airports and border authorities the time to improve the infrastructure, fix the broken devices and hire more staff so that families can travel through Europe without disruption." Ryanair has advised UK passengers travelling to and from non-Schengen destinations, or transiting through affected European airports, to allow extra time for their journey and be prepared for lengthy waits at passport control. What you need to apply for ETIAS ETIAS launch delayed until 2027 Meanwhile, the launch of the EU's new European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) has been delayed until 2027. The ETIAS is a pre-authorisation scheme which will apply to UK passport holders and other visa-exempt travellers entering 30 European countries for short stays. Applicants will be required to pay a €20 fee, though travellers under 18 or over 70 will be exempt. The ETIAS was expected to launch later this year, but it has now been delayed until 2027, according to the Financial Times. The decision is due to "technical glitches" and delays with the EES, which only recently came online after being postponed from 2022. EU home affairs commissioner, Magnus Brunner, said the delays were due to "other factors", including insufficient staff or lack of adequate infrastructure. EU-Lisa, the agency responsible for ETIAS, has reportedly acknowledged that "launching it by the end of this year as planned was no longer feasible". Recommended reading: Edinburgh Airport passengers warned rule change could see them denied entry to Spain Edinburgh Airport passengers warned of 6-hour airport queues in this holiday hotspot Edinburgh Airport passengers warned of six-hour queues at four holiday hotspots The European Commission will set the official launch date only after EU-Lisa confirms the system has been fully tested and is ready. A commission spokesperson said: "Preparations for the launch of ETIAS are ongoing. "Obviously, as with any large-scale IT system, many factors come into play when deciding when to launch it." https://auto.economictimes.indiatimes.co.text: During a government news conference last week, Magyar said that as far as I know, an investigation had been launched concerning Szijjartos connections to the Russian government.Hungary's government announced an investigation Monday into a large foreign investment by Chinese automaker BYD negotiated by a former foreign minister who last week resigned from Parliament to take an executive position at the company.Peter Szijjarto's announcement last Wednesday that he would take the job at the world's top electric carmaker prompted accusations of a conflict of interest and criticism over his role in facilitating substantial government subsidies to the company while in office.Prime Minister Peter Magyar told lawmakers on Monday that Szijjarto, a close ally of former Prime Minister Viktor Orban, had helped BYD while he was in office "with hundreds of billions (of forints) in public money, diplomatic support and state infrastructure.""We will examine all the decisions, negotiations and state commitments made by Peter Szijjarto that were related to the BYD Hungary investment," Magyar said Monday.He added the investigation would look into all subsidies, tax breaks, permits, environmental exemptions and publicly-funded investments given to large multinational firms during Orban's tenure."We will investigate who made these decisions, who prepared them, what professional warnings were ignored, and how much burden they left on Hungarian taxpayers, workers, local communities and the environment," Magyar said.Neither Szijjarto nor BYD have responded to Magyar's allegations of conflict of interest while Szijjarto was in office. The former foreign minister has posed his new job as a "prestigious" opportunity to work for one the "greatest success stories" in the automotive industry.While serving in government, Szijjarto was instrumental in securing foreign investments in Hungary from Chinese companies, including his now-employer BYD, which received considerable state subsidies during his tenure.In 2023, Szijjarto announced that BYD would open its first European factory in Hungary - allowing the conglomerate to skirt European Union import tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles imposed to protect the continent's domestic auto manufacturing sector.In 2025, Szijjarto also announced BYD would locate its European headquarters and a research and development center in Budapest and receive 20 billion forints ($63.7 million) in government assistance.The investments were part of the Orban government's push to make Hungary a global hub of lithium-ion battery manufacturing, largely through attracting Chinese battery manufacturers who opened a series of plants across the country.The moves led local residents, environmentalists and opposition politicians to protest over fears the new industry would exacerbate existing environmental problems, hit the country's precious water supplies and further undermine its economy to China.While foreign minister, Szijjarto also maintained close relations with Russia despite its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022. Breaking with nearly all of his EU counterparts, he frequently traveled to Moscow to negotiate agreements on purchasing Russian oil and gas and to meet with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, whom he referred to as his "friend."He was embroiled in controversy during Hungary's 2026 election campaign when the Washington Post reported that he made regular phone calls to Lavrov during high-level EU meetings with "live reports on what's been discussed."Szijjarto has dismissed the report while acknowledging that he conferred with Lavrov before and after EU foreign minister meetings about their agenda and decisions.During a government news conference last week, Magyar said that "as far as I know," an investigation had been launched concerning Szijjarto's connections to the Russian government.

The concerns gained attention after Norwegian public transport company Ruter tested two buses last year and found potential security risks linked to OTA technology.Auto makers are increasingly using over-the-air (OTA) software updates, a technology that smartphone companies like Google, Apple and Samsung have relied on for more than a decade to deliver new features and security fixes. While the technology has made updating vehicles faster and cheaper, cybersecurity experts are warning that it also creates new risks. According to a CNBC report, analysts say wireless updates could leave connected vehicles vulnerable to cyberattacks, data breaches and even attempts by foreign actors to interfere with vehicle systems.OTA updates raise cybersecurity concerns: AnalystOver-the-air (OTA) technology allows manufacturers to wirelessly send software updates, bug fixes and new features to internet-connected devices without requiring a visit to a service center.Tesla began rolling out OTA updates for its Model S vehicles in 2012, helping popularize the technology across the automotive industry. Today, many car makers use OTA updates to improve vehicle software and fix issues remotely."The technology is increasingly welcomed as it is a quick and cost-effective way to manage systems on vehicles, over traditional methods which may have required a recall or update at routine maintenance," Siraj Ahmed Shaikh, professor in systems security at Swansea University in the UK, told CNBC.However, analysts say the growing use of OTA updates also introduces new cybersecurity risks.Its use represents "a unique national security concern," Gabriel Lim, senior analyst at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies in Singapore, told CNBC."Aside from data privacy concerns, the potential of a foreign actor sabotaging the controls of a moving vehicle is a possibility that countries like Norway, Denmark, and Britain have expressed concerns about," Lim added.Norwegian bus test highlights potential risksThe concerns gained attention after Norwegian public transport company Ruter tested two buses last year and found potential security risks linked to OTA technology."There is access to the control system for battery and power supply via mobile network through a Romanian SIM card. In theory, therefore, this bus can be stopped or rendered inoperable by the manufacturer," the company said.The findings prompted authorities in the UK and Denmark to launch their own investigations.

Linert Contact Us Contact Advertise Submit News Statement of Values Terms of Service Public Notices Browse notices Place a notice Lifestyles Antibiotic ointment cures foot odor By Joe Graedon, M.S. and Teresa Graedon, Ph.D. July 21, 2026 3 min read Trending Q. It was suggested that I apply a thin coat of antibacterial ointment on my feet when they get smelly. One application keeps the smell away from my feet for months. A. We have been intrigued to learn that over-the-counter antibiotic ointments such as Polysporin (bacitracin and polymyxin B) can sometimes help against nail fungus. That's because some nail infections are bacterial rather than fungal (Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association, March 1, 2021). Your report suggests that bacteria may also contribute to some cases of foot odor. People should be aware that neomycin, found in Neosporin, may trigger an allergic reaction (contact dermatitis). Q. Why do doctors prescribe so much gabapentin without warning people that it could be bad for their brains? My husband and I have both been prescribed large amounts by several doctors with instructions to take it three times daily. I'm so glad I looked up potential side effects and found that it can increase the chance of dementia or mild cognitive impairment. This is one drug we won't be taking. A. Gabapentin is the most frequently prescribed pain medicine in the U.S., although the Food and Drug Administration has only approved its use for epilepsy and post-shingles pain (postherpetic neuralgia). Nervous system side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, abnormal thinking and amnesia. A recent systematic review in the journal Drugs & Aging (June 22, 2026) concluded that "Gabapentinoid use was associated with modestly higher estimated odds of ADRD [Alzheimer's disease and related dementia] in pooled observational data." This does not demonstrate a cause-and-effect relationship. However, the authors urge colleagues to exercise caution when prescribing gabapentin for "off-label" use. That would include most pain relief prescriptions. Q. I recently began taking atorvastatin for high LDL cholesterol. I haven't been tested yet to see how it's working, but I have had a weird side effect. My butt got really itchy. My stool was a little softer, but not diarrhea. I have a bidet, so I feel confident that everything stays pretty clean down there. But the itching interfered with my sleep. Hydrocortisone and zinc oxide paste helped a little. Then, I ran out of my pills and couldn't get a refill for several days over a long holiday weekend. After about three days, the itching was gone. I am hesitant to start back on the statin and wonder if a lower dose might have fewer side effects. Are there other formulations of statins that might not have this effect? I am concerned about my high LDL and will ask my doctor about testing for LP(a). A. Itching is not listed as a common side effect of atorvastatin, not to mention itching in that specific body part. Nevertheless, Polish investigators have found an association between statins and itching (Advances in Dermatology and Allergology, Oct. 20, 2024). Moreover, there is a case report on statin-associated itching in the journal Cureus (Sept. 10, 2022). A lower dose might help, but there is not enough research on this topic to tell. You should ask your doctor whether a different approach to lowering your LDL might be appropriate. To prepare for that conversation, you might want to read our "eGuide to Cholesterol Control and Heart Health." This online resource may be found under the Health eGuides tab at www.PeoplesPharmacy.com. In their column, Joe and Teresa Graedon answer letters from readers. Kim Jae-heun Subscribe + Blackpink star unveils song after teasing it at major music festivals in the US and Europe Jennie performs at the Governors Ball Music Festival in New York City on June 7. (Odd Atelier) Blackpink's Jennie will release her new single "Less Than a Lover" on Friday after previewing the song at major international music festivals in the US and Europe. Her agency, Odd Atelier, announced Tuesday that the single will be released at 1 p.m. KST on major global streaming platforms. The agency also unveiled a teaser image showing Jennie and a man through the window of a truck, with a natural landscape in the background. Jennie participated in directing the music video as well as writing and producing the song, reflecting her creative involvement in the project. Known for the high-energy performances and striking visuals of previous songs such as "Like Jennie" and "Mantra," Jennie takes a different approach with "Less Than a Lover." The song features lo-fi guitar, vintage electric keyboard textures and restrained vocals, offering a softer, more introspective sound. Jennie first performed "Less Than a Lover" at the Governors Ball Music Festival in New York City in June. She also showcased the song at Denmark's Roskilde Festival, Poland's Open'er Festival and Spain's Mad Cool Festival in July. Ahead of the song's official release, videos of Jennie's festival performances circulated on social media platforms including TikTok and Instagram, helping the song gain traction online. Jennie is set to continue her festival circuit with upcoming appearances at Lollapalooza Chicago in the US and Summer Sonic 2026 in Japan in July and August, respectively. jaaykim@heraldcorp.com Related Stories Coffee with Jennie? Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/Reuters View image in fullscreen Haruto Kubo holds his pet dog Miku, outside a house that collapsed in an earthquake with a magnitude of 7.1 that struck Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture. Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/Reuters Japan Japan’s prime minister tours quake-hit sites as recovery efforts hampered by soaring temperatures Prime minister Sanae Takaichi visited Kumamoto prefecture almost a week after a magnitude 7.1 quake hit, killing 38 people Associated Press Mon 3 Aug 2026 20.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, has visited the south-western prefecture of Kumamoto, where recovery efforts are being hampered by heat and a lack of water supplies, almost a week after a magnitude 7.1 earthquake killed dozens and caused widespread damage. Thirty-eight people died during the quake , including one person who died of apparent heatstroke while taking shelter in a car in hot weather, officials said on Monday. ‘The shaking was terrifying’: stories of survival and loss emerge after Japan earthquake Read more Residents put out heaps of debris, broken furniture and damaged appliances for collection, while in the towns of Uki and Hikawa, construction of temporary housing began. Some hotels and inns were offering their rooms for evacuees. More than 46,000 households remain without water and many also face fuel shortages as the region suffers sweltering heat, stoking fears of heat-related illness. Temperatures were as high as 40C in the country’s south on Monday. More than 8,500 people remain at crowded emergency shelters in converted community centres, school gyms and classrooms, many of which lack airconditioning. Others are sleeping in cars at town hall parking lots and parks, or outside their homes. View image in fullscreen Sanae Takaichi greets evacuees in Hikawa in the southern Kumamoto prefecture after a major earthquake hit. Photograph: undefined/Japan Pool/Kyodo News/AP Takaichi on Monday flew over the affected areas from an army helicopter and visited one of the area’s best-equipped shelters, with cardboard beds, partitions and airconditioning, triggering criticism on social media that her visit distorted reality. The governor of Kumamoto, Takashi Kimura, in his meeting with Takaichi, stressed the “abnormal heat” over recent days. He said he sought further government support to improve the conditions at evacuation centres, saying many of them lacked clean water and medical care. “While taking into consideration the governor’s requests, we will quickly examine what the government can do for the disaster-hit region and affected people and move proactively,” Takaichi said. View image in fullscreen A house is seen collapsed onto a car in Hikawa. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images Meanwhile, a company that owned a general store in the shopping mall that collapsed during last weeks earthquake , acknowledged that it had instructed two employees to return to the building to put sales proceeds into a safe, where they were killed in an explosion that followed the quake. Two executives of Habita, a local general store operator that had a shop inside the collapsed Aeon mall in the town of Kashima, attended the wake on Sunday of one of the two victims, 22-year-old Kurumi Otake, and apologised to her parents for the death. View image in fullscreen Vehicles wait in line to transport disaster debris to a temporary storage site in Hikawa, amid sweltering temperatures. Photograph: Jiji Press/EPA Company sales manager Goji Yuse acknowledged that the company instructed the two to put sales proceeds into the safe if it was possible. “I wish someone had stopped her,” Otake’s tearful mother told them. “My daughter is not coming back.” The mall’s operator said it believes the explosion was due to a gas leak and occurred after about 3,000 shoppers had been evacuated to a parking lot after the quake, but some employees remained inside. Rescuers recovered five people and the bodies of seven others from the mall. Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body was found inside a suitcase in Athens. Photograph: Facebook Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body was found inside a suitcase in Athens. Photograph: Facebook Greece Athens suitcase death: suspect admits hiding body but denies murder Police are focusing on Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s final hours in hope of discovering motive for her killing Helena Smith in Athens Mon 3 Aug 2026 15.36 EDT Last modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 21.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Greek authorities are investigating what may have motivated a 26-year-old Afghan man to kill a Scottish charity worker found dead in a suitcase in an abandoned building in Athens last month. Inquiries have focused increasingly on Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s last few hours alive and police believe they hold the key to revealing why the 38-year-old was targeted. On Sunday the suspect, identified as Sharif Ahmadzai, was accused of intentional homicide after three days of questioning. He will appear before an investigating magistrate to be formally charged on Wednesday. George Kalliakmanis, the honorary president of the police officers’ association in Athens, told the Guardian the homicide division was now intent on discovering the motive behind “the murder” because the Afghan was continuing to deny any role in it, although he had confessed to hiding Ross in a suitcase. “He has admitted to carrying her body to the site. Police have CCTV footage of him doing this on the night of 16 July. He has also confessed to withdrawing €10,000 from ATMs using credit cards that belonged to her. But he has denied murder which police do not believe,” Kalliakmanis said. The Afghan, a professional boxer in the lightweight division, is believed to have arrived in Greece via the island of Lesbos as a child refugee at the height of Europe’s migration crisis 10 years ago. View image in fullscreen Sharif Ahmadzai and his wife, US citizen Alaina Hall. She is said to have played a ‘significant role’ in the investigation. Photograph: Twitter/X He has been quoted as telling police he discovered Ross’s lifeless body in the first floor flat of an apartment block he helped manage in Exarchia, a bohemian district in downtown Athens popular among leftists, foreigners and NGOs. Ahmadzai, who married a US citizen and devout Christian, Alaina Hall, in 2023, had keys to the flat where their own refugee solidarity group, Love Every Nation, regularly met. Investigators have confirmed that Ross, a friend of Hall’s with similar volunteering experience and religious views, had moved to the apartment on 10 July after staying with Greek friends when she arrived in the Athens from Edinburgh on 26 June. Her last telephone call was made from her mobile phone on the night of 15 July – three days before her body was discovered by a homeless man in an abandoned building in Kypseli, about two miles away. Two possible scenarios in the run up to Ross’s death were being studied, police said. “We believe there was a confrontation,” said one source. “But was that spurred by Ross discovering the Afghan rummaging through her things and stealing her credit cards, or was it a case of sexual assault or the Briton spurning his advances?” View image in fullscreen Sharif Ahmadzai arrived in Greece via the island of Lesbos as a child refugee. He has been accused of intentional homicide. Photograph: Twitter/X Forensic scientists believe Ross was “likely asphyxiated” after an initial on-site postmortem, which showed there were no evident signs of injuries on her body. However, the autopsy was also deemed inconclusive because of advanced decay. Further toxicological tests and analysis of vital organs are expected to determine the exact cause of death in the coming days. Hall, who met Ahmadzai on Lesbos, is widely described as having played a “significant role” in the investigation. After allegedly becoming suspicious of Ahmadzai’s movements – and newfound wealth, the result of making cash withdrawals with Ross’s credit cards – she reportedly contacted the police, handed over cash he had given her and moved into a hotel. Adding to the mystery that has engulfed the inquiry, Ross’s phone was used for several days after her death, with text messages sent to family and friends. The messages were described as “deliberately misleading” by police, who believe they were sent in a bid to delay Ross being declared missing. One spoke of her “need to be alone”. “The Afghan’s partner was very helpful,” said Kalliakmanis. “From the day the victim was identified the investigation faced several challenges but thanks to the homicide division being so thorough they cracked it.” Police, who collaborated with the UK’s National Crime Agency and the Scottish service, combed through CCTV footage from cameras in the area where the suitcase was found and from banks where cash withdrawals were made before identifying the suspect. Photograph: Dave Decker/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Florida Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback. Photograph: Dave Decker/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock Florida Far-right Republican accused of stiffing student debate champion of $8,000 Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback calls failure to pay Briana Whatley money owed ‘an oversight’ Richard Luscombe in Miami Mon 3 Aug 2026 20.05 EDT First published on Mon 3 Aug 2026 17.21 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A far-right Republican candidate in Florida’s governor’s race has been accused of stiffing a high school debate champion over the better part of $11,000 in scholarship money she won from a company he founded. Student Briana Whatley landed the awards as regional and national champion of Incubate Debate, a league-style competition set up by the candidate, James Fishback, to encourage youth to engage in political discourse. A recording posted to Substack by Fishback in May 2024 shows Whatley, now a second-year history student at Florida State University, accepting a $10,000 check for besting seven other finalists in the 2024 Incubate Debate national championship, adding to two $500 area awards she previously won. According to Florida Politics , Whatley is suing Fishback for not delivering $8,000 of the money that a letter from the company promised would be paid to her in full on the day she graduated high school in May last year. The filing names Incubate Foundation Inc, the parent of Incubate Debate, and Fishback, 31, who is challenging front-running US congressman Byron Donalds and Jay Collins, the lieutenant governor of Florida, for the Republican nomination for state governor in November. The candidates face off in an 18 August primary. Whatley’s lawsuit, seen by the Guardian, was filed in small claims court in Broward county, where both she and Fishback went to school. Among the allegations are that Incubate Debate initially failed to respond to emails asking where the money was, then tried to change the terms of how it would be paid to her. Fishback, it said, “personally evaded and defrauded Plaintiff by initially ignoring communications, later blaming a terminated employee for the written award terms, falsely claiming an unwritten ‘installment policy,’ and delaying payment for months”. The document said Fishback admitted he “totally dropped the ball on this one” in a November 2025 text asking her to resend her bank details, then in December paid only $3,000 via Zelle. In another text, Fishback allegedly claimed that the employee who sent the original award letter promising payment in full on graduation had been fired, and that installment payments had “always been the case”, despite no previous mention of it. The text exchanges indicate a previously cordial relationship between the pair, with Fishback calling Whatley “a star”, and the student thanking him for “wanting to make it right”. Whatley claims Fishback broke off communication five months ago after she questioned why a promised 1 February installment was not paid. She is suing for the outstanding $8,000 plus interest and costs, and a pretrial conference is scheduled for 9 September. Whatley, the lawsuit said, has “suffered severe financial injury and out-of-pocket damages” as a result of Fishback’s alleged failure to pay. In a brief emailed statement to the Guardian on Monday, Fishback said: “This was an oversight on my part. We are fixing it.” In a court ruling last week, Fishback survived a legal challenge by Collins to remove him from this month’s primary. A judge in Tallahassee ruled that Fishback had not violated a rule requiring a gubernatorial candidate to be a resident of the state for seven years prior to the election, even though he bought a condo in Washington DC in 2020 that he declared his primary residence, and voted there. The lawsuit over scholarships follows a May 2023 episode in which Fishback and Whatley appeared to be on the same page in their criticism of the National Speech and Debate Association (NSDA), a rival to Incubate Debate, over censorship. Fishback wrote an essay for The Free Press , then owned by Bari Weiss, the CBS news editor-in-chief, stating that the NSDA had become a “woke” organization “hijacked by left-wing politics” that was telling students what they could and could not talk about. Whatley, then a high school sophomore, told Fox News Digital that she was warned by the organization to refrain from bringing up then former president Donald Trump during debates because it would be “inappropriate”. Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters House of Representatives US House ethics panel recommends censure for Republican Chuck Edwards North Carolina congressman’s campaign rejects committee finding that Edwards ‘engaged in sexual harassment’ Chris Stein in Washington Mon 3 Aug 2026 18.52 EDT First published on Mon 3 Aug 2026 17.06 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US House of Representatives ethics committee on Monday recommended that Chuck Edwards, a Republican congressman, face censure after determining he “fostered a hostile work environment and engaged in sexual harassment” by giving gifts and lavishing attention on two young female staffers. The bipartisan panel began investigating the second-term North Carolina congressman earlier this year, after receiving complaints about his conduct. In a report approved by Democratic and Republican committee members, they determined there “was substantial reason to believe” Edwards broke House rules by singling out the two unidentified aides for special treatment that made them uncomfortable and harmed relations with other employees. While the investigation uncovered no evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity with the staffers or suggested it, his behavior likely violated provisions in the House code of conduct that prohibit sexual harassment and unwanted advances. The congressman “acknowledged at least some of the behavior at issue could be viewed as inappropriate”, but “has not acknowledged or taken responsibility for the harm he caused”, the committee wrote in its report. “A member of Congress should not single out a staffer and isolate them from other staff, make frequent comments regarding that person’s appearance and weight, send messages in the middle of the night, text staff deeply personal and seemingly romantic thoughts, intrude on personal occasions without invitation, pay for personal vacations, and spend thousands of dollars on gifts for staffers,” they continued. Edwards’s re-election campaign criticized the report, arguing its findings “completely exonerate” the congressman while saying ethics committee staff “have taken it upon themselves to write their own rules based upon an interpretation that is inconsistent with the written rule of law or House rules”. “Representative Edwards looks forward to having his name cleared and will work to ensure that the full light of day is brought on this process and that every member of Congress and the public can see the attempt to harm the congressman who has brought no harm to others,” the campaign said in a statement. If the House agrees to censure Edwards, he would have to stand in the well of the chamber while the text of a resolution rebuking him is read aloud. The congressman was already viewed as vulnerable to losing re-election to his western North Carolina district in the November midterm elections. Last week election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball announced it was rating his race a “toss-up” in a sign of improving Democratic chances. “My heart goes out to the young women who took these roles to serve our community,” his Democratic opponent, Jamie Ager, said following the report’s release. “We deserve leaders with the moral character western North Carolina can be proud of.” Elected in 2022 after ousting the scandal-plagued Madison Cawthorn in the Republican primary, Edwards, a former state senator, left most of the hiring for his new office up to his chief of staff, but insisted on bringing “three young women” into his operation, according to the report. This group included a woman who was still in college and identified by the committee as “Staffer 1” and a second in her early 20s, identified as “Staffer 2”. “Both young women were subject to increasingly unusual attention from the congressman while they worked for him, creating an environment where both they and their coworkers felt uncomfortable,” the committee found. These behaviors included Edwards bringing Staffer 1 to a White House event without telling the rest of his staff, buying her flowers and texting her in advance that he was “so excited about tonight” and wanted it to be “perfect”. After the event, the staffer said Edwards tried to “pressure” her into continuing the night together, which the congressman told the committee he did not recall. He invited both staffers to private dinners, and at one point told Staffer 2 to ensure the event was not put on his calendar by his office scheduler. He would also send both “personal texts” later in the evening about planning events together or expressing “personal sentiments”, the committee found. Edwards also planned lengthy and elaborate trips with the two staffers either together or individually, at one point suggesting to Staffer 2 that they “go to Annapolis for lunch, meditate by its water, stroll about town, find a day spa, see a movie, or wipe out the casino”. “I’m probably over thinking being impulsive but I really want you to enjoy our time together nearly as much as [I] know [I] will,” he wrote in a text message to the staffer released by the committee. His actions made the two staff members uncomfortable, and when a senior employee of his office spoke to Edwards on their behalf, that staffer told the committee the congressman “got very angry” and said she “didn’t understand the unique relationship” he had with the two women. Both staffers later resigned because of his behavior, but gave Edwards other reasons why when they departed. The behavior affected the morale of his office, the committee found, with one senior aide telling investigators Edwards “lashes out at everyone on the team except” the two women. The congressman denied yelling at his staff. Another staffer said they had told Edwards that an “unfair standard existed” in his office, which he said was caused by employees being “jealous”. Even after she left his employment, Staffer 2 agreed to a trip to Las Vegas with Edwards, saying she felt pressured to do so in part because he had influence over her being hired for another job in civil service. He paid for her flights, accommodation at the Bellagio hotel and a show at the Sphere. After receiving a bouquet of flowers upon arrival, Staffer 2 texted Edwards: “I’m almost ready and just got the flowers – they’re very pretty. Thank you! I did want to flag that the message made me uncomfortable. Just want to make sure this trip isn’t meant to be anything it’s not?” “Understood, and agree. I’m sorry it made you uncomfortable. Nothing was meant by it, other than what was intended to be a cute play on the name of the arrangement,” Edwards responded.
