Photograph: Chandan Khanna/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Tom Rahill holding a Florida-native water snake as he searches for Burmese pythons in August 2022. Photograph: Chandan Khanna/AFP/Getty Images Florida Winner of Florida python hunting contest nabs 96 snakes: ‘I was on a mission’ Burmese pythons are an invasive species in the Everglades, and the challenge is part of initiative to remove them Lucy Campbell Wed 5 Aug 2026 19.50 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 19.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The winner of this year’s annual Florida Python Challenge hunted down and eliminated 96 invasive Burmese pythons from the Everglades national park, as part of an initiative to remove hundreds of the snakes from the area every year. The challenge invites hunters to participate in 10 days of capturing and humanely euthanizing as many of the invasive snakes as possible across eight designated hunting locations, with the winner taking home a cash prize of $10,000. The event is hosted by Florida fish, wildlife and conservation (FWC), the south Florida water management district, the National Park Service and others. This year’s competition drew 907 participants from 30 US states, as well as Canada and Vietnam. The winner, Tom Rahill, harvested 96 Burmese pythons, all from the Everglades. A python hunter by trade, Rahill founded an organization called SwampApes in Broward county that takes veterans suffering from PTSD on python hunts in Florida’s wetlands. Far-right Republican accused of stiffing student debate champion of $8,000 Read more In comments reported by Naples Daily News , Rahill told an FWC meeting in Panama City on Wednesday: “I was on a mission to get one of our veterans a big snake. I did it. And we wrestled this thing … The veteran was just over the moon.” Once that was achieved, he said he went deeper into the Everglades, where he found the 96 snakes. Over the course of 10 days in July, 280 snakes in total were removed. Before the competition began, 1,400 pythons had been taken out this year. The challenge also awards several other cash prizes, including $1,000 for the longest python killed, which this year went to Rahm Levinson, who hunted a snake measuring 16ft 5in. Burmese pythons are native to south-east Asia, and have wreaked havoc since they were first found in the Everglades ecosystem in the 1990s, consuming resources and wiping out a significant portion of the area’s native wildlife. The apex predators are incredibly hard to detect, contributing to the population ballooning to a number that conservative estimates put in the tens of thousands. Females can lay dozens of eggs, sometimes up to 100 annually, and although many hatchlings do not survive to adulthood, there are fears the pythons are reproducing faster than they can be caught. The annual challenge is therefore now held during the summer hatching season in a bid to boost the number captured. Aimed at raising public awareness of invasive species, and getting the public involved in conservation and efforts to protect the Everglades ecosystem by controlling the number of Burmese pythons, the event has seen more than 1,600 of the snakes removed from the area since 2017. Combined with FWC contractors, who hunt the reptiles year-round, that figure rises to more than 19,000 snakes removed since 2017. Sarah Funck, program coordinator at the FWC, told Wednesday’s meeting that there is no “silver bullet” to solve Florida’s python invasion, but stressed that the elimination of just one python “is a win for Florida’s native wildlife”. Photograph: CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP View image in fullscreen Lindsay Clancy awaits the start of proceedings at Plymouth superior court in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on 30 July 2026. Photograph: CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP Massachusetts Lindsay Clancy murder trial: toxicologist testifies about medications found in defendant’s blood Variety of prescriptions were found in blood of mother accused of strangling her three children, court hears Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email Edward Helmore Wed 5 Aug 2026 19.27 EDT First published on Wed 5 Aug 2026 12.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of killing her three children in January 2023, continued on Wednesday with a forensic toxicologist testifying to the variety and concentration of medications found in the defendant’s blood. Justin Brower, a forensic toxicologist with NMS Laboratories, testified that his lab examined the levels of four psychiatric medications detected in Clancy’s blood after she allegedly strangled her children and attempted to take her own life. Those drugs included the antidepressant mirtazapine, the mood stabilizer lamotrigine, the antidepressant trazodone and quetiapine, a drug used to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder. Brower noted that quetiapine could also be prescribed in low doses to treat insomnia. Postpartum psychosis or murder? Trial of mother who killed her kids spotlights mental health Read more Asked if the concentrations of each drug were different from what was prescribed, Brower said the only drug that appeared slightly elevated was quetiapine, but noted that it was not at a “toxic concentration” or “suicidal concentration”. “Usually people take handfuls of pills when they’re trying to harm themselves and take their own life, and this is not consistent with that,” Brower testified. He later testified, upon questioning from Clancy’s defense attorney, that the toxicology results “don’t tell the entire story”. Prosecutors say Clancy acted intentionally when she killed her children Callan, eight months old; Dawson, three years old; and Cora, five years old. Clancy’s defense team says she was a loving mother who was overcome by postpartum psychosis, had undiagnosed bipolar disorder and was on problematic medications. The court has heard from a range of experts for the prosecution, with testimony at times halted when witnesses, including Clancy’s ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, or the defendant have become overwhelmed. On Wednesday, the family’s nanny, Elaine Rossi, was asked on the stand if she’d ever had concerns about Clancy’s care for her children. “Not at all. She was a wonderful mom,’ she said. “I observed a wonderful mom who loved her kids.” If convicted, Clancy faces life in prison without parole. A not-guilty verdict by reason of a lack of criminal responsibility could lead to her being placed in a state mental health facility. On Monday, jurors heard excerpts from Clancy’s journals that revealed her mental struggles including thoughts of suicide and her feeling overwhelmed with motherhood, including her struggles to get her newborn to sleep, going back to work as a labor and delivery nurse, not being able to breastfeed, and feeling disconnected from her children and husband. “I’m so desperate to get a mental break from taking care of everyone that my mind is trying to find something physically wrong with me,” she wrote in an entry on 18 November 2022. The trial has shone a light on significant gaps in the diagnosis and treatment of postpartum psychosis and postpartum depression. Clancy’s attorneys say her condition seemed to worsen on an ever-shifting lineup of psychiatric prescriptions. In the three months before the killings, clinicians prescribed a range of antidepressants, sleep aids, an antipsychotic and other medications while Clancy reported increasingly profound insomnia, anxiety, despair and confusion about what was real, according to a civil lawsuit filed against caregivers that claims they should have recognized that Clancy and her children were at risk. In her diaries, Clancy wrote, “I want help. I want to be well,” and described feeling “incredibly sad and guilty” about not breastfeeding. She also wrote that she was “obsessed” with managing Callan’s sleep and nap schedule. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion “I have crazy brain fog. I feel like I can’t make a plan,” she wrote in another, undated entry. “I live moment to moment waiting for the next nap time. I’m terrified of Cal getting overtired now because I feel can’t help him.” “Hearing him cry for 1 plus hours and not intervening just about killed me,” Clancy wrote, adding that she had told her husband, Patrick, “I want to die.” She also wrote: “I now have horrible insomnia and anxiety which is causing depression. I have no appetite. I don’t know what’s wrong with me. I want help. I want to be well.” Clancy first sought help from a postpartum depression program in late December 2022. She went on to check herself into a psychiatric hospital and later told a psychiatrist that she heard a “man’s voice” in her head telling her to “kill the children so you can kill yourself”. Nineteen days later, after being discharged, she carried out the killings. The defendant is now paralyzed from her attempt to take her own life. When she woke up in hospital and was asked by a forensic psychologist how she felt, she responded: “Horrified.” Dr Jhilam Biswas of Brigham and Women’s hospital testified that Clancy asked “can she have visitors, and where her family is”. The court has also heard from Patrick Clancy, who recounted the medications his former wife was taking, her health and demeanor, and the destructive thoughts she was having. He has said he forgives Lindsay and believes that the killings were motivated purely by her mental health. When the jury heard the anguished 911 call Patrick Clancy made on the night of the killings, several members could be seen holding back tears. He described returning home after collecting medications and a takeout meal to find their home “quiet”. Patrick Clancy went upstairs to find found the door to their bedroom locked. After breaking in, the room was covered in blood and the window was open. His wife was lying on the ground below. She told him she had tried to take her own life. He asked where the children were, and she told him they were in the basement. When emergency services arrived, he ventured downstairs to find their three children with exercise resistance bands around their necks. Duxbury police officer Brian Josephine testified that he heard Patrick scream: “She killed the fucking kids.” Explore more on these topics Massachusetts Mental health US crime news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

Photograph: Jay L Clendenin/Getty Images Donald Trump Man arrested at Trump’s California golf course faces more charges Jeanine John Taele detained for ‘suspicious’ behavior and charged with possession of unregistered short-barreled rifle Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency Wed 5 Aug 2026 19.02 EDT First published on Wed 5 Aug 2026 18.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A California man who was arrested at Donald Trump ’s Los Angeles-area golf course ahead of a presidential visit is facing more charges, as authorities released new details about the investigation. Authorities say federal agents first observed 38-year-old Jeanine John Taele near the golf grounds in Rancho Palos Verdes on 31 July, wearing an earpiece and capturing photographs and videos of security agents assessing the property. Taele returned on 2 August, authorities say, two days before Trump was scheduled to visit the resort for a fundraising dinner with the Republican National Committee (RNC). Taele approached federal agents and said he was employed by the state department and was there for a security detail. After detaining Taele for “suspicious” behavior, Los Angeles county sheriff’s deputies found a loaded magazine in his pocket. In his pickup truck, which was parked at the golf club, deputies found a loaded 9mm pistol, binoculars and a badge labeled “security protection agent”, authorities have said. Armed man arrested at Trump’s California golf course Read more Law enforcement officers also recovered a trove of armaments from his residence in the nearby city of Downey, including a .45-caliber pistol, body armor and an illegally modified AR-type pistol, among others, officials said. Law enforcement officials also located notebooks containing “concerning statements” in the home. The Los Angeles county sheriff’s office declined to comment on the nature of the remarks. Taele was due in court on Wednesday on a federal weapons charge but the hearing was canceled. He was charged federally with possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle that was found at this home, authorities said. The complaint alleges the firearm is an illegally modified AR-style rifle with a barrel that was cut down to 10in (25cm) from 14in (35cm). He is being held at a downtown Los Angeles jail on state charges, according to booking records. He was not yet in federal custody, said a spokesperson for the US attorney’s office. Taele is facing a misdemeanor charge for carrying a concealed weapon in a vehicle and two felony charges for possession of a short-barreled rifle or shotgun and the manufacture, importation or sale of a large-capacity magazine, court records show. The Los Angeles county public defender’s office, which is representing Taele in the state criminal case, declined to comment. Trump addressed the arrest on Tuesday, telling Fox News that “only consequential presidents” are targeted, “and I am definitely consequential”, which he said brought him “a little solace”. Taele already appeared in court on state weapons charges and a second-degree robbery charge for an unrelated incident. “There is no room for error, particularly in light of previous attempts on President Trump’s life,” said Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI’s Los Angeles office, in a statement. In April, Cole Tomas Allen, a California man who authorities say harbored resentment for the Trump administration, rushed past a security checkpoint during the White House correspondents’s association dinner, where the president was in attendance, and shot a firearm before being apprehended by Secret Service agents. He has been charged with an attempt to assassinate a US president, to which he has pleaded not guilty . In July 2024, a gunman opened fire at a rally where Trump was speaking as the Republican presidential nominee. A crowd member was killed and a bullet grazed Trump’s ear. Federal agents fatally shot the suspected shooter, 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks. An FBI investigation found no clear motive behind the deadly shooting. Ryan Routh was recently sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of attempting to assassinate Trump on a Florida golf course in September 2024. Prosecutors said Routh spent weeks plotting to kill Trump before aiming a rifle through shrubbery as Trump played golf at his West Palm Beach country club. Taele was a corporal in the US marines who was deployed to Iraq in 2008 and Afghanistan in 2010 and worked as a warehouse clerk, according to the US Marine Corps. He earned numerous commendations, including an award for good conduct, during his service from 2008 to 2016. In October 2016, Taele was issued a California firearm permit for .40-caliber, .45-caliber and 9mm weapons, state records show. That permit expired in 2020. Taele was also a licensed security guard in the state between February 2019 and February 2025, records show. What we know on day 1,625 Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Wed 5 Aug 2026 21.26 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 21.27 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukraine could benefit from a Lockheed Martin project to build a new, lower-cost Patriot interceptor , the PAC-3 Adapted Capability Effector (ACE) missile , Reuters has reported. The news agency, citing defence and US government sources, said that despite Donald Trump casting doubt on a deal for Ukraine to build desperately needed Patriots, “no order was given to halt the discussions”, and talks continued with US arms makers, military officials and others. Ukraine has proven adept at producing large volumes of dramatically cheaper yet equally or more effective missiles and drones compared with those made by western allies. At least 17 people died on Wednesday as Kyiv again came under heavy Russian bombardment . Ukrainian forces, starved of suitable interceptors, were unable to shoot down a single missile . A US official told Reuters that the most feasible option for Patriots would be making some components in Ukraine and assembling them in Germany , where an older Patriot model is already made and the more advanced PAC-3 is expected to be produced as well. Trump has raised security concerns about handing over highly secretive Patriot blueprints in their entirety to Ukraine. 1:19 Deadly overnight Russian missile attack sparks fires across Kyiv – video Any plan for Ukraine to be involved in Patriot production could still take a year or more to come to fruition , officials have cautioned, with new component lines typically not up and running until three to seven years after a licensing deal is signed. Lockheed Martin suggested an accelerated timeline for Patriot PAC-3 ACE in an announcement on 20 July , emphasising that the use of the same launchers and software would speed up development. The interceptors would cost less than half of a normal Patriot missile, it claimed. Germany’s interior minister warned of “a new level of danger” after a drone carrying explosives was found at Leipzig airport, while a DHL plane in flight was hit by a flying object. German police used a bomb disposal robot to defuse and destroy the explosive device. Deborah Cole and Andrew Roth write that suspicion has fallen on Russia given the airport’s status as a Nato and German military logistics hub, and as the base for Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines in Europe. The quadcopter fitted with an explosive device was found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane , according to media reports. The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe Read more Vladimir Tkachuk, the head of Russian drone manufacturer Uraldronzavod , was critically injured in a car bombing , in what appeared to be the latest in a series of assassination attempts targeting figures linked to the country’s war in Ukraine, Pjotr Sauer writes . A bomb planted beneath his Mercedes exploded, according to Russian state media, killing his bodyguard. On Saturday an explosion outside an upmarket restaurant in central Moscow killed five people. Col Gen Aleksandr Chayko, the commander of Russia’s aerospace forces, was reportedly celebrating his birthday at the restaurant. Ukrainian authorities have ordered hundreds of families with children to leave the city of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine because of intensifying Russian strikes. Russian forces are within 20km (12 miles) of the city’s eastern edge, according to DeepState, a war monitor close to the Ukrainian army. A total of 525 children and their guardians are being forcibly evacuated. Kramatorsk is part of the “fortress belt” that Ukraine’s troops are fighting to hold. Russia’s Saratov refinery stopped processing crude oil on 2 August after ⁠a Ukrainian drone attack damaged production facilities and triggered fires at the plant owned by ⁠the country’s ⁠largest ​oil company Rosneft, two industry sources told Reuters. They said the refinery’s CDU-6 crude ‌distillation unit, its ‌only crude processing unit, was shut down. The unit, with a nominal capacity of 20,000 tonnes of oil per day, could take between two and three weeks to repair. Russia’s imports of gasoline and diesel from Belarus surged in July because of Ukrainian strikes disabling Russian oil refineries, according to calculations by Reuters. Image: Yevgeny Sofiychuk/TASS/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Russian authorities are planning to "expand mobilization" in autumn this year, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, citing intelligence services. According to Zelenskyy, Russian President Vladimir Putin is reportedly preparing to recruit additional Russian soldiers to fight in the war against Ukraine . "He is concealing his intention behind different words and signals, but he is making preparations," Zelenskyy said. "It is important that we, together with our partners, exert sufficient pressure on Russia so that the idea of ending this aggression — the idea of peace, rather than further Russian mobilization — prevails," he added. The Ukrainian president also said Russia's army was losing more fighters at the front than it can recruit, even though Putin wants to intensify the attacks and expand the war. Putin issued a decree in autumn 2022 launching a "partial mobilization," which remains in effect to this day, as confirmed by the presidential administration in 2023. The document, it said, "regulates additional measures necessary to ensure that the armed forces fulfill their objectives." Scores of Russians fled abroad after the Kremlin announced a partial mobilization in September 2022 Image: AP/picture alliance What points to a possible new mobilization drive? Independent Russian exile media outlet Verstka and Latvia-based Russian-language news portal Vaschnyje Istorii published an investigative report in late June stating that Russia's leadership was secretly "discussing mobilization" given the difficulties in recruiting new conscripts. One source quoted by Verstka said figures by Moscow ' s mayoral office show the city sent 1,708 people to the front in April of this year and 1,378 in May — around 1,000 fewer people than during the same period last year. This low recruitment rate reportedly continued in June as well. Vaschnyje Istorii reported that the recruitment rate for soldiers serving on fixed-term contracts more than halved in the last quarter of 2025 compared with the same period the previous year. The outlet said the recruitment rate had dropped even further in early 2026. The news outlet also cited sources from different Russian regions revealing that the number of people applying for army contracts was falling. Military personnel interviewed by Verstka said that contract soldiers being sent to fight this year were "unfit for combat," with many new arrivals fleeing the front lines. One conscript told the news outlet that "units are staffed at 30 to 40%, at best." Droves of Russian fighting-age men made also their way to Georgia in 2022 Image: Daro Sulakauri/Getty Images The US-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reported in late July that the Kremlin is laying the groundwork for a fresh mobilization drive. ISW analysts wrote that such a move would be "a personal decision for Putin that is contingent on his personal perception of the battlefield situation and his perception of the stability and integrity of the Kremlin." They added that it "remains unclear whether or how Putin will decide to implement mobilization." A few days ago, Verstka reported that demand for Armenian rental apartments had shot up, driven by Russian interest — just as it had in 2022, when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The outlet said rents in the Armenian capital, Yerevan, have risen by about 30% in recent months. According to the report, Russians are planning to leave the country ahead of the State Duma election, scheduled to be held from September 18 to 20. One landlord told the outlet that in recent years most of his clients had been Russians who had already been living in Armenia for quite some time. Now, however, 80% of inquiries were from Russians who had recently moved to Armenia or were planning to relocate there. What has Russia said? Speaking at a press conference in late July, Russian presidential spokesman Dmitry Peskov chose not to comment on Ukrainian President Zelenskyy's remarks regarding a possible new mobilization drive, saying "it is not Zelenskyy's job to talk about our plans." Andrei Klishas, a member of the Russian Federation Council, told Russian-language media outlet RTVI in early summer 2026 that a new mobilization was not currently being discussed in the country as it was unnecessary. Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of the Russian Security Council, dismissed rumors about a possible new mobilization, calling them "pre-election propaganda." The former Russian president also claimed that in the first half of 2026, some 200,000 people had enlisted in the Russian army. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has refused to comment on rumors of a looming mobilization Image: Ulf Mauder/dpa/picture alliance "Of course, you can't blindly trust information provided by the Russian authorities," military expert Yan Matveyev told DW. "Information is adjusted to align with their objectives," he added, with regard to Medvedev's statements on the number of new Russian contract soldiers. That said, figures provided by Russian officials are not too far off when compared with analyses by independent researchers, Matveyev said. "Instead of Medvedev's nearly 200,000 new soldiers, that number would probably be closer to 170,000 or 180,000 over six months." In his view, the current recruitment rate is not sufficient for Russia to secure a military victory over Ukraine. A new mobilization drive would not change that, Matveyev added. "Even if they doubled the size of their army, Russia would not be able to defeat Ukraine, but as can be seen from the statements made by Putin and his officials, that is precisely their goal." Matveyev believes that, given the losses on the front lines, the strength of Russia's army will dwindle unless a fresh mobilization is launched. This decline, he believes, will continue slowly at first but then accelerate. "Losses are growing and will continue to rise given current trends." https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c998.text: Image source, Reuters By David Gritten Published 5 hours ago One person has been killed in an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon, the country's health ministry says, after the Israeli military said it was responding to a "blatant violation of the ceasefire" by the Iran-backed group Hezbollah. A man died and 12 other people were injured when the roof of a prayer hall at the cemetery of the town of Tibnin was hit, according to Lebanese media. Strikes were also reported to the west in the town of Mansouri, where the Israeli military issued its first evacuation order for more than a month. Hezbollah has not commented on the events, which came as Israeli and Lebanese officials attended US-sponsored talks in Rome aimed at maintaining the ceasefire. In late June, the three countries agreed a trilateral framework that should see the Israeli military gradually withdraw from territory it is occupying in southern Lebanon in exchange for the disarmament of Hezbollah. Two weeks ago, the Lebanese army was allowed to deploy to one of the first "pilot zones", after Israeli troops pulled out of the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh. Hezbollah has rejected the agreement, saying the provisions linking Israel's withdrawal to the group's disarmament crossed "all red lines". The Israeli military announced that it had begun carrying out "precise strikes" in southern Lebanon on Wednesday afternoon, about 30 minutes after its Arabic spokesperson had told residents of Mansouri to evacuate ahead of "forceful action" there. Both statements accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire but gave no further details. However, an Israeli military source told Israeli media that displaced residents of Mansouri had returned to their town "under the auspices of the Lebanese army, which established a checkpoint in the area in violation of the agreements". The source said the town was inside the Israeli-declared "security zone" - a 10km (six-mile) deep strip of occupied Lebanese territory running along the border - and "military activity that endangers the lives of Lebanese civilians" was taking place there. The evacuation order was the first issued in southern Lebanon since 14 June, when residents of 29 towns and villages were told to flee their homes. Earlier on Wednesday, the mayor of Mansouri, Haidar Madihli, told local media that Israeli warplanes had carried out four strikes on buildings and villas in the Ghazaleh neighbourhood on the outskirts of the town, causing extensive damage to the targeted structures. The strikes triggered a wave of displacement, with families filling cars with their belongings and heading towards Tyre, the largest city in the south, Madihli said. He added that around 120 families had returned to Mansouri after the 19 June ceasefire, but that the number had steadily fallen as Israeli strikes intensified. In recent days, only 40 to 50 families remained in the town. The evacuation order came as the UN's humanitarian office said more than 820,000 people displaced in Lebanon by the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah had begun returning to their home areas following a reduction in hostilities. However, the UN said about 360,000 other people remained displaced across Lebanon, including 26,000 living in government shelters. Lebanon was drawn into the war between Israel, the US and Iran on 2 March, when Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for a strike that killed Iran's supreme leader. Israel responded by launching a bombing campaign across Lebanon and invading a significant part of the country's south. At least 4,333 people have been killed during the conflict, including 392 women and 253 children, according to the Lebanese health ministry. Since the ceasefire was announced, the ministry has recorded the killing of 353 people. Israeli authorities say 38 Israeli soldiers and four civilians have been killed on both sides of the border during the conflict. Beállítom A napokban került fel a YouTube-ra a Kéz, szív, lélek – magyar kortárs művészek nyomában című film első két része, amelynek elkészítésére közel 56 millió forintot kaptak Fásy Zsüliett és anyja, Fásyné Gruzó Mária cégei. A Corvus-Kora Róbert Békés megyei festőművészről szóló dokumentumfilm első két része összesen körülbelül 6700 megtekintést ért el öt nap alatt. A sorozat első része július 30-án, a második pedig augusztus 4-én jelent meg, a rendező szerint egyébként így is sokkal korábban a tervezettnél. Eredetileg ugyanis akkorra időzítették volna a premiert, amikor mind a négy rész elkészül, de „a negatív sajtóvisszhang arra sarkallta őket, hogy véget vessenek a találgatásoknak és a különböző teóriáknak” – mondta a Blikknek Jankai Béla, a dokumentumfilm rendezője. A Telex információja szerint a cég idén márciusban ugyan beadta a négyrészes dokumentumfilmről szóló beszámolót, de magukból a filmekből nem mutattak be semmit. A filmet a Munkácsy Art Kft. készítette a Nemzeti Kulturális Alap (NKA) által biztosított forrásokból. A 444 cikke szerint a projekt első két epizódjára a cég az NKA 790-es, úgynevezett egyedi támogatási keretéből 82,55 millió forintot kapott. A harmadik és negyedik részre a volt kulturális miniszter, Hankó Balázs a saját, 447-es miniszteri keretéből utalt ki további 89,9 millió forintot. A Telex információja szerint ezt az összeget is teljes egészében a két epizód, a harmadik és a negyedik rész elkészítésére kapták. A Munkácsy Art a dokumentumfilm elkészítésében szerepet adott két olyan vállalkozásnak is, ami Fásy Ádám lányához, Fásy Zsülietthez és feleségéhez, Fásyné Gurzó Máriához kapcsolódik. Az egyik a Fásy Zsüliett kizárólagos tulajdonában álló Jules Media Kft., ami 12,25 millió forint plusz áfa értékű megbízást kapott a Munkácsy Arttól a dokumentumfilm első két részének tartalomgyártására. A 2026. január 22-én kötött szerződés szerint Fásy Zsüliett cége felelt a koncepció kidolgozásáért és az utómunkázott anyag átadásáért is. A gyártásba a Fásy Zsüliett és az édesanyja, Fásyné Gurzó Mária tulajdonában lévő MVSZ 2015 Kft. is bekapcsolódott. A 2025. december 29-án aláírt szerződés szerint ez a cég 31,8 millió forint plusz áfa értékben dolgozott be a projektbe, ők foglalkoztak a gyártás előkészítésével, a forgatókönyv kidolgozásával, a stáb koordinálásával és a technikai eszközök biztosításával. Emellett a filmhez kapcsolódó PR- és marketingfeladatok is hozzájuk tartoztak. Vagyis az NKA 790-es kollégiumától érkező 82,55 millió forint több mint fele, 44,05 millió forint plusz áfa, vagyis nagyjából 56 millió forint a Fásy családhoz köthető cégekhez került. Arról, hogy mire fordították a fennmaradó több mint 26 millió forintot, megkérdeztük a Munkácsy Art Kft.-t, ha érdemben válaszolnak, frissítjük a cikket. A film rendezője, Jankai Béla a Blikknek arról is beszélt, hogy Fásy Zsüliett vágóként dolgozott a projektben. A lap szerint kétmillió forint volt a munkabére, amit több hónap munkáért kapott. Kérdéseinkkel kerestük a Fásy családot is, de egyelőre nem értük el őket. A Munkácsy Art Kft.-nek papíron egyébként semmi köze a Fásy családhoz, a céget egy Szabó Sándor nevű férfi vezeti, akinek korábban viszont volt közös vállalkozása Fásy Ádámmal. A cégük, az IRM Magyarország Zrt. érintett volt egy őssejtkezelési botrányban, ami miatt Fásyt tíz hónap felfüggesztett börtönbüntetésre ítélték . Na de nézzük – milyenek is ezek az epizódok, és lehet-e látni bennük ezt a több mint százmillió forint közpénzt? „Nem, semmiképp, semmi sem indokol ekkora összegeket ilyen videókra” – idézzük innentől kollégánkat, Lengyel-Szabó Pétert, aki 16 éve foglalkozik online videózással. Az NKA-támogatás – Munkácsy Art Kft. – Fásy család Bermuda-háromszögében nagyon nehéz szétszálazni, hogy az összesen 171,5 millió forint (egyszer 82,5; egyszer 89 millió forint) pontosan mekkora része ment a négy filmre, de az elérhető adatok alapján hivatalosan mindenképp jóval több mint 100 millió forintjába került ez az alkotás az adófizetőknek. És ha valaki keresi, hogy miért is felháborító az egész NKA-ügy, az ezekben a videókban megnézheti. Az eddig feltöltött két epizód mindegyike egyszerű felépítésű, húsz perc körüli riport a festőről: hosszú interjút vagy interjúkat készítettek a főszereplővel, és azokat rövidebbre vágták, vágóképekkel fedték, illetve néha archív videókat is felhasználnak. Gyakori visszatérő elemek a festő munkájáról készült fotók, vágóképek, ezek legtöbbször egészen egyszerű, bemozgatott effektekkel jelennek meg ( lásd itt ). Az aláfestő zenéket a videó alatt meg lehet nézni, ezek a YouTube-on ingyenesen vagy olcsón felhasználható zenék. Semmi olyan elem nincs benne, amit ne láttak volna már tévés vagy online videókban ezerszer a nézők, semmi olyan, amihez igazán magas szintű videós vagy animációs képesség kell, és semmi olyan, ami indokolná, hogy ezek az alkotások percenként több mint egymillió forintból készüljenek. Egyetlen olyan percük sincs, ami egymillió forintnál többe kerülne, sőt túlzás nélkül állíthatjuk, hogy egy egész epizódért is korrekt költség lenne az összesen egymillió forint. Ha a Telex, a 444 vagy az RTL Klub a Kéz, szív, lélek hez hasonló, több tízmilliós elszámolásban készítené a riportjait, nagyon hamar csődbe menne. Ugyan az archív felvételekről nem tudjuk, hogy mennyibe kerültek, meglepő lenne, ha nem ingyen vagy néhány tíz-, maximum százezer forintért adták volna oda őket a készítőknek. De nehéz róluk többet megtudni, mert részletes hivatkozáslista, ahogy az másoknál lenni szokott, nincs a film végén. És ha már archívok: az sem a legmagasabb színvonalú munkára enged következtetni, hogy a legtöbb archív felvétel rossz képaránnyal jelenik meg, mindenkinek a feje két oldalról össze van nyomva, talán ezen a képen a leglátványosabb: Forrás: A Munkácsy Art Kft. hivatalos YouTube-csatornája Ugyan az NKA-támogatást leírják az epizódok végén, a készítőkről semmit sem tudunk meg – pedig abból egyértelmű lenne, hogy egy ilyen munkára beírtak-e tíz készítőt, vagy három ember csinálta, ahogy az egyébként szakmai alapon logikus lenne. A feltöltött két epizód anyaggyűjtéssel, szervezéssel, forgatással és vágással együtt három ember számára (egy szerkesztő, egy operatőr és egy vágó) nem vehet igénybe több időt két-három hétnél. Más kérdés, hogy még a szakértők is megosztottak azzal kapcsolatban, hogy a home office jó válságkezelő intézkedés-e. Alulnézet: több magyarországi nagyvállalat és intézmény is a távmunka bevezetésével reagált az elmúlt napokban a paksi atomerőmű teljesítménycsökkenése miatt létrejött energiaválságra. A Magyar Telekom például ezen és a következő héten kötelező home office-t rendelt azoknak a munkavállalóknak, akik tudnak otthonról dolgozni, a Yettelnél pedig erre a hétre írták elő a távmunkát azoknak a dolgozóknak, akiknél ez szóba jön. Az Allianznál az eredetileg augusztus 10. és 23. közé tervezett teljes home office időszakot egy héttel korábban, hétfőtől vezették be. A Richternél és az OTP-nél is rugalmasabban kezelik a távmunkát az energiaválság miatt. Több egyetem is (pl. a Széchenyi István Egyetem és a Szegedi Tudományegyetem) otthoni munkavégzést biztosít a dolgozóinak, a kormány pedig hétfőtől szerdáig otthoni munkavégzést rendelt el az államigazgatásban és az állami cégeknél is. Egyes önkormányzatoknál is távmunkában dolgoznak a hőség miatt. Mit mondanak ők? „Arra kérjük a piaci vállalatokat és munkáltatókat, hogy a következő napokban ők is biztosítsanak otthon dolgozást minden olyan dolgozó számára, akinek a munkája távolról elvégezhető, és csökkentsék a lehetséges minimumra az irodaépületek energiafelhasználását” – mondta Magyar Péter miniszterelnök szombaton. Felülnézet: a hőség miatt így ideiglenesen megugrik a távmunkában dolgozók hazai aránya, ami egyébként az egyik legalacsonyabb az Európai Unióban. A Eurofound július végi jelentése szerint 2024-ben csak Olaszországban és Romániában dolgoztak kevesebben home office-ban legalább néha, mint Magyarországon. A jelentésből az is kiderül, hogy miközben 2015 és 2024 között szinte minden tagállamban nőtt a legalább néha távmunkázók aránya, Magyarországon ez az arány változatlan maradt (ez még Romániában alakult így). Igen, de: ha nincsenek bent az emberek az irodában, attól azt még hűteni kell, tehát elképzelhető, hogy így még növekedhet is a fogyasztás, mondta Balogh József energetikai szakértő az RTL Híradónak , megjegyezve, hogy a háztartási légkondik száma itthon 1 millió felett van, amelyek együttes fogyasztása jelentős lehet. Összetett kérdésnek látja az intézkedés energiafogyasztásra gyakorolt hatását Zubor András, a Magyar Mérnöki Kamara főtitkára, aki a 444 -nek azt mondta, ha csak a dolgozók egy része marad otthon, és az irodát továbbra is hűtik, többletfogyasztás jöhet létre, de ha a bent dolgozókat egy-két szintre csoportosítják, valódi energiamegtakarítás érhető el. A napi fogyasztási csúcs kisimítása is fontos, és Zubor szerint ha home office-ban napközben indítják be az emberek például a mosógépet, az intézkedés ehhez a célhoz hozzájárulhat. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/j.text: Organisers submitted more than 100 proposed routes to authorities in Oradea, but all were rejected Photograph: Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights View image in fullscreen Organisers submitted more than 100 proposed routes to authorities in Oradea, but all were rejected Photograph: Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights Romania Pride organisers vow to march in Romanian city that has blocked event four years in a row Oradea is only major city in EU where local authorities have repeatedly blocked Pride plans Ashifa Kassam European community affairs correspondent Thu 23 Jul 2026 04.36 EDT Last modified on Thu 23 Jul 2026 21.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Campaigners in a Romanian city have vowed to go ahead with a Pride march after local authorities denied permission for the fourth consecutive year. Since 2023, campaigners in the western city of Oradea, which has a population of about 180,000, have sought permission to hold Pride events. However, each year they have faced opposition, making Oradea the only major city in the EU where local authorities have repeatedly blocked Pride marches. “Every year the local authorities have managed to find legal or technical excuses to ban Oradea Pride events,” said Iulian Dițiu, the co-founder and president of Ark Oradea, the local organiser of Pride. In 2024, they were told none of the city’s parks were available at the times requested, he said. The following year, campaigners submitted 12 potential routes for the march, only to be told that none was suitable. In the run-up to Saturday’s proposed march, organisers submitted more than 100 possible routes. On Wednesday, the city authorities said none of them was viable because they clashed with other events or public infrastructure works. The mayor, who belongs to a party that describes itself as liberal, conservative and Christian democratic, did not respond to a request for comment from the Guardian. Dițiu said the repeated refusals sent a broader message. “It feels like the message that they are trying to send our way is that we’re not welcome here,” he said. “They have never said out loud that they are banning Pride for LGBT reasons. They’re always hiding behind technical reasons.” The dispute has attracted growing international attention. More than 152 organisations from 30 countries have signed a statement calling on officials to allow the march to take place “in complete safety” and in line with EU law. “After four consecutive years in which the Pride march has been unable to take place, there can be no question of administrative or logistical difficulties,” the statement said. “When an authority consistently prevents a community from assembling peacefully, a principle that concerns all citizens is undermined.” Their appeal, delivered recently to the local administration in Oradea, drew comparisons between Oradea and Budapest, where Hungary’s former prime minister Viktor Orbán and his rightwing populist movement had sought to ban Pride events. “In recent years, the restriction of Pride marches has become, in several European states, an indicator of democratic backsliding and the weakening of the rule of law,” the statement said. Dițiu said organisers intended to proceed with the march on Saturday despite the lack of official permission, repeating last year’s approach. In 2025, between 500 and 600 people attended an unauthorised march, with nine participants later fined the equivalent of about €4,000 (£3,420) he said. This time representatives from several diplomatic missions have said they will take part, along with Romania’s ombudsman, he added. Dițiu described the situation as both “encouraging and disappointing”. “The institutions that are supposed to protect the rights of every community are trying to use our community as a scapegoat. But many more people are behind us. Many more people understand what the stakes are,” he said. “This is not an LGBT issue. This is a democratic issue. It’s about the freedom to public assembly. And if the local LGBT community here in Oradea can be denied this basic human right without any repercussion, it can happen pretty much anywhere in Europe, for pretty much any community.” Explore more on these topics Romania Pride LGBTQ+ rights Europe Human rights news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

StaceviÄius / LRT Lithuanian and Polish border officials are meeting Thursday to discuss ways to make inspections at their shared border more efficient while Poland maintains temporary controls aimed at curbing secondary migration, Lithuaniaâs interior minister said. Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas said the two countries should seek to streamline inspections by focusing on higher-risk vehicles and cargo while allowing regular travellers to cross more quickly. âTrucks and cargo vans can be inspected, but when we see two people traveling for business, holidays or other purposes, or perhaps a single person, the check could probably be faster,â Katelynas told reporters. The minister said he raised the issue with Polish counterparts during an informal meeting of European Union justice and home affairs ministers in Dublin last week. According to Katelynas, border officials from both countries were due to meet Thursday to discuss practical measures to reduce queues at the crossing. Poland reintroduced temporary border controls with Lithuania and Germany in July 2025, saying the measures were needed to stem secondary irregular migration. Warsaw argues that migrants who enter Latvia from Belarus travel through Lithuania before attempting to reach Poland and continue onward to Western Europe. The number of migrants intercepted after entering Lithuania from Latvia has risen sharply. In the first half of this year, Lithuanian authorities stopped more than 1,200 people arriving from Latvia, compared with just over 300 during the same period last year. Lithuania has responded by sending teams of border guards to assist Latvian authorities, although it has said it will not provide the full contingent of 100 officers requested by Riga. Katelynas has also not ruled out the possibility that Lithuania could temporarily restore controls on its border with Latvia if secondary migration continues to increase. Under European Union rules, countries in the Schengen area may temporarily reintroduce internal border controls only in exceptional circumstances when public policy or internal security is under threat. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases.text: Drive-side force sensing and a 1:1 motion-mimicking interface make every procedure a training-grade record of expert clinical skill KAUNAS, Lithuania , July 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sentante , the medical robotics company building a haptic, device-agnostic platform for remote vascular surgery, is turning its newly CE-marked robotic system into a data engine for the next generation of intelligent, endovascular intervention. Much of the field claims autonomy ahead of the data needed to deliver it. Sentante built the opposite: a system architected from the start to capture force and torque, device kinematics and time-aligned fluoroscopy together, on every procedure. Hardware and AI are one effort, and each procedure refines the dataset that makes increasing machine assistance possible. "The next wave of technology is physical AI: systems that can sense, act and operate in the real world, not just process information," said Edvardas Satkauskas, CEO and co-founder of Sentante. "For endovascular intervention, the constraint has never been ambition, it has been data. You cannot train a system to navigate a living vessel without a rich, accurate record of how the best clinicians do it. We have spent years building the platform that captures exactly that, and CE mark means it is now generating that data in real clinical settings across Europe." Imaging is being deliberately reduced, and force has to fill the gap: Fluoroscopy and contrast media both carry harm: radiation exposure for patients and staff, and contrast-related risk, notably renal injury. Guidelines accordingly push every endovascular procedure toward minimum imaging, which means the situational-awareness data available to the operator goes down, not up. The hand fills the gap: the load profile up the catheter column distinguishes safe contact from a perforation precursor. On a dose-limited 2D image the two can look identical, and no computer-vision force indicator can recover a signal that was never captured. An AI built on imaging alone is extracting more from a data source the field is deliberately driving down. Drive-side force and torque sensing remains rare in medical robotics; da Vinci 5 only brought force feedback to laparoscopy in March 2024, with preclinical evidence of up to 43% less force on tissue . Sentante engineered force and torque sensing into the catheter drive from day one, and the endovascular setting makes the case even stronger: a thin column of wire and catheters in continuous contact with the vessel wall, where the safety envelope is a load profile, not a position. "The image tells you where the device is. The hand tells you what the vessel is doing," said Dr. Tomas Baltrūnas, co-founder and Chief Medical Officer of Sentante. "A system that captures only the image is missing the half that matters most for safety." The interface decides whether the data carries real skill: Every joystick or screen-based controller in endovascular robotics forces the operator to translate a career of feel and micro-adjustment through an artificial input layer. The captured demonstration records expert joystick operation, not expert catheter operation, and the demonstrator pool is limited to physicians who have completed a months-long learning curve on that specific robot. Sentante's platform is different: the clinician manipulates standard catheters and guidewires exactly as in manual intervention, with authentic force feedback at the fingertips, and the system records that natural motor program directly. The captured behaviour carries the actual clinical skill, the demonstrator pool expands to every existing interventionalist, and every procedure performed on the platform is a training-grade demonstration in its natural form. Da Vinci proved the principle in 1999: its one-to-one motion-mimicking console let manual surgical skill transfer without re-learning, and that made it adoptable. Sentante applies the same logic to the catheter, removing the training-bandwidth bottleneck of every prior platform: an expert is competent from day one, and the system accumulates training data from day one. "What I learned to do with my hands over fifteen years of intervention is replicable with the Sentante platform." said Baltrūnas . "The motion-mimicking interface lets me operate as I always have, with the platform recording what I do as I do it. The expertise stays in the operator's hands, and the data stays in the system." Over the past year the company has run a world-first transatlantic remote thrombectomy on perfused human cadaver models and a GLP animal study of 24 remote procedures across three continents, each adding to a dataset built under procedure-authentic conditions. The CE-marked system integrates with existing cath-lab infrastructure and supports peripheral vascular interventions, with remote stroke thrombectomy on a parallel regulatory pathway. The latest-generation robot uses NVIDIA hardware, and Sentante was among the first to develop on NVIDIA Isaac for Healthcare. Sentante is continuing its European commercial rollout, progressively introducing AI-driven assistance as the dataset matures. About Sentante: Sentante is a medical robotics company founded in 2017 building a haptic, device-agnostic endovascular platform that enables clinicians to perform complex vascular procedures remotely with full tactile feedback. Designed to integrate with existing cath-lab infrastructure, Sentante aims to expand access, improve clinician safety, and elevate procedural consistency across peripheral vascular, neurovascular and cardiovascular applications. https://iberonews.com/not_det.php?lang=e.text: Taiwan Children’s Choirs Garner Major Awards at Hungarian Choral Competition TAIPEI, Taiwan (Business Wire) Texto completo a continuación 23/07/2026 - 09:35 CET Competing against 36 leading contenders from 20 countries, four Taiwanese children’s choirs have garnered several major awards and top honors at the 5th Budapest International Choral Celebration, showcasing Taiwan’s cultural diversity and music excellence. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260722613876/en/ Puzangalan Children’s Choir and Yo Wu Wei Children’s Chorus join forces with international choral ensembles and orchestras to perform Mozart’s Requiem Mass in D minor, K. 626 at the Béla Bartók National Concert Hall of Müpa Budapest. With its pure, angelic voices and exceptional vocal techniques, Puzangalan Children’s Choir from Pingtung County won the top prize, Laurea Summa Cum Laude, in the Grand Prix Competition’s Youth Choir of Equal Voices, Folklore, and Sacred Music categories. In the Open Competition, Yo Wu Wei Children’s Chorus claimed three gold prizes in the categories of Youth Choir of Equal Voices, Modern, and Folklore. The choir also secured two championships in the Youth Choir of Equal Voices and Modern categories and received the highest honor in the Modern category. Meanwhile, Taipei Fuhsing Elementary School Choir earned the Children’s Choirs Gold Diploma and was named the Category Winner. Kaohsiung Children’s Choir received a gold prize in the Folklore category and the Children’s Choirs Silver Diploma. Invited by the organizer, Puzangalan Children’s Choir and Yo Wu Wei Children’s Chorus joined forces with international choral ensembles and orchestras to perform Mozart’s Requiem Mass in D minor, K. 626 at the Béla Bartók National Concert Hall of Müpa Budapest. The two choirs then embarked on a tour of the Baltic states, bringing Taiwan’s choral artistry to audiences in Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia while sharing Taiwanese music and culture with local communities. The Taipei Representative Office in Hungary noted that the award-winning achievements at the choral competition demonstrate the confidence of Taiwan’s younger generation on the global stage. It added that the children’s voices have become a powerful form of cultural diplomacy, leaving a lasting impression at this year’s event. https://www.surinenglish.com/malaga/mala.text: The picture of gender-based violence in Malaga so far this year is devastating. In just seven months, the province has seen six confirmed femicides, as reported by the government delegation against gender-based violence.With this tragic figure, Malaga has already reached the total number of femicides in 2025, when it broke its all-time record (2003) and topped the national map. It surpassed provinces such as Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia.In July alone, by far the deadliest month of the year, five women were found dead in the province with signs of violence, two of them this week within just 24 hours of each other. The latest case, which occurred on Tuesday, is pending confirmation. Sources, however, believe that the autopsy will confirm the gender-based nature of the murder.At the national level, the number of women murdered has now reached 31 (compared to 24 recorded at the end of July last year), nine of whom were killed in Andalucía (three more than in the same period last year). The diversity of variables such as nationality, age, romantic relationship, family responsibilities and socioeconomic level once again demonstrates the absence of a defined pattern: sexism strikes regardless of social status or origin.Two of the women murdered this year were named María and two others, Victoria. The other names are Cristina and Patricia. All were stabbed to death, except for one, who died after being shot. She was the only one who lived with her murderer (her husband) at the time of the incident. In two other cases, the perpetrators were ex-husbands, whom the victims had previously reported for domestic abuse. María, murdered this week in Antequera , had been registered in the VioGén system since 2023. It so happens that, just days before the crime, the court revoked her protection order after she had apparently requested it herself. The family of the 29-year-old woman, who leaves behind two orphaned children, suspect that she was coerced by her ex-partner into taking that step. The assailant took his own life after killing her.British-born Victoria, 33, was also murdered by her ex-husband , Juan Antonio, whom she had also reported to the police. Despite the restraining order, he repeatedly violated it. He had two prior convictions for minor threats and breach of a restraining order. Victoria was the first victim of gender-based violence in the province in 2026. Her ex-partner stabbed her to death on 26 January in front of her three children, who were between the ages of seven and eleven, in her home in Alhaurín el Grande. Later, the man turned himself in at the Alhaurín de la Torre prison and confessed to the crime.Almost five months later, in the early hours of 5 June, the bodies of Victoria, 51, and her husband, Francisco, 56, were found with gunshot wounds in their home in the Palma-Palmilla district in Malaga city. From the beginning, all hypotheses suggested that the man, who had been under psychiatric treatment and on sick leave for years, had killed her and then taken his own life with the same gun. In this case, neither of them was registered in the VioGén System.On 1 July, the body of 35-year-old Cristina, a resident of Malaga city's Ciudad Jardín district, was found in a well in Rincón de la Victoria . That same day, her ex-partner confessed that he had stabbed her to death weeks earlier.The man appeared in the VioGén system for three other previous victims. Both he and another individual, who allegedly helped him dispose of the body, remain in pretrial detention, while a woman has been released pending investigation.Just one week later, in the early hours of 8 July, a 61-year-old woman and her 31-year-old daughter were found dead in their home in Mijas after the house had been set on fire . Their names were María and Patricia, respectively. Both had stab wounds, leading investigators to suspect from the outset that the perpetrator had tried to disguise the double murder with arson.The following day, the mother's ex-partner, 67, was arrested for his alleged involvement in the double murder and for suspected robbery with violence . The man appeared in the police database as a "persistent aggressor".People who knew him well told SUR that he had been in prison several years prior for attempting to strangle a former partner.On Monday, the police discovered the body of 29-year-old María in her home in Antequera. Less than 24 hours later, 45-year-old Melinda, from Hungary, was was found stabbed to death in a home in Benahavís . Her case is the only one that has not yet confirmed a motive. Neighbours raised the alarm after hearing a loud assault and seeing a man flee in a vehicle. For now, the police only know that Melinda and her murderer knew each other.The province has recorded 68 femicides since 2003. January and July stand out as the deadliest months, with nine women murdered by their partners or ex-partners each. By age, the most affected group is the 18-30 (18 victims), followed by 41-50 (17) and 31-40 (12). There were also nine victims between the ages of 51 and 60, five between 61 and 70 and seven between 71 and 84.The other major victims are the orphans, who face a complex and painful process to regularise their family status, continue their studies or apply for assistance. Since 2003, the number of children orphaned by gender-based violence in the province has reached 29.Review the latest crime and judicial news reports

Log in here » BUCHAREST, Romania (AP) — A sailor injured when a Ukraine-bound tanker ship caught fire off Romania’s Black Sea coast has died, Romanian media reported on Thursday, as authorities investigate a possible link to Russia’s war against Ukraine. The ship, a Liberian-flagged vessel named Gas Lisbon, was sailing across the Black Sea toward a Ukrainian port when it was “struck” late Monday around 20 nautical miles off Romania’s coast, Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Tuesday. Romanian authorities approached the vessel and evacuated the entire 17-member crew, including three injured sailors. Two of those injured had burns on approximately 10-15% of their bodies while the third suffered multiple wounds, according to Romania’s Department for Emergency Situations. An image released by ISU Tulcea, Romanian Inspectorate for Emergency Situations, shows a rescue ship evacuating injured crew members approaching the port in Tulcea, Romania, Tuesday, July 21, 2026, after an LPG tanker ship sailing across the Black Sea toward a Ukrainian port caught fire off the coast of Romania last night, an incident Romania's president said was "most likely" related to Russia's war in Ukraine. (ISU Tulcea via AP) On Thursday, Romanian news outlet news.ro reported that one of the injured sailors, a 45-year-old Philippine national, had died. The outlet quoted the director of the Tulcea County Hospital, Tudor-Ion Nastasescu, as saying the sailor “had a burn of the airways and a pulmonary complication related to this burn that caused his death.” Nastasescu added that the other two injured sailors, both Philippine nationals, are currently being treated in the hospital’s intensive care unit and are in stable condition. The vessel had departed the Egyptian port of Alexandria and was headed to the Ukrainian port of Reni on the Danube River. It was carrying over 3,790 tons of liquefied petroleum gas. Sign up for Business Weekly Romania’s Department for Emergency Situations said the “incident” aboard the ship caused major damage and a fire in the vessel’s superstructure, but no official explanation has been given for the cause. Dan said authorities would “clarify the circumstances, causes, and responsibilities” related to the incident. Romanian television network Digi24 broadcast interviews with two crew members on Tuesday who said they believed the ship had been struck by multiple drones. A series of drone incursions from both Russia and Ukraine have hit Romania and other NATO members since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. In June, a Ukrainian maritime drone that was being used in the war exploded at the Black Sea port of Constanta, while three other sea drones exploded outside the port. No one was hurt. A month earlier, a Russian drone that was part of an attack on Ukraine went astray and struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, injuring two people. https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/baltic-.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.23 11:04 Baltic States will develop joint electricity system reserve capacity Translated by Karolis Broga Source: ELTA Saulės ir vėjo elektrinės PHOTO: APChanel | Shutterstock Follow Delfi on Google The energy ministers of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have agreed to develop joint reserve capacity for the Baltic energy system, which would allow electricity supply to be restored more quickly for residents and businesses in the event of various threats or damage to critical infrastructure. On Wednesday, Lithuania’s Minister of Energy Lukas Savickas, together with Latvian and Estonian counterparts, signed a joint declaration on the development of the reserve capacity for the Baltic energy system. „Geopolitical tensions and increasingly frequent natural disasters caused by climate change pose growing challenges for energy infrastructure. Joint reserves and an agreement to coordinate actions during emergencies will help ensure a more reliable energy supply for residents, while shared solutions will allow to strengthen the security of energy infrastructure more effectively and at a lower cost,“ says Savickas. Under the agreement, electricity transmission system operators of the Baltic States will jointly assess the emergency power grid equipment, which is needed to ensure the fastest possible restoration of electricity supply in all three Baltic countries in the event of various threats or disruptions. The emergency equipment may include transformers, transmission poles, generators and other reserve resources. After completing the joint assessment, it is planned to submit a joint application for European Union funding in order acquire and maintain reserve capacity at the level of the Baltic region. https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/lithuan.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.23 11:05 Lithuania’s priority is stronger strategic partnership, PM tells Polish president Source: ELTA Seimas svarsto ir tvirtina Vyriausybės programą PHOTO: Julius Kalinskas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google During a telephone conversation with Polish President Karol Nawrocki on Wednesday, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius emphasised Lithuania’s commitment to further strengthening its strategic partnership with Poland, said the prime minister’s press service. Lithuania regards Poland as an indispensable ally, a strategic partner and a neighbouring country linked by a shared history. In his conversation with President Karol Nawrocki, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius expressed Lithuania’s interest in deepening bilateral relations and discussed regional security, support for Ukraine and other current issues with the Polish leader. „Today, the words of Pope John Paul II remain especially relevant: our nations are united by ties of neighbourliness, friendship and brotherhood. The challenges we face together oblige us to work jointly for the security and prosperity of our region, while our shared history reminds us that this is not only possible – it is precisely what we should strive for. Further strengthening our strategic partnership with Poland is a central objective of my Government,“ said Prime Minister Sinkevičius. The discussion focused primarily on security and defence issues. In the bilateral agenda, the Government will devote particular attention not only to this area but also to the resilience of energy and other critical infrastructure, transport and military mobility projects, economic ties – which are already strong but have further potential for growth – and cultural exchanges. The prime minister noted that, as Russia continues its military aggression against Ukraine and remains a threat to the security of Europe as a whole, it is essential to maintain active support for Ukraine and increase pressure on Russia. Mr Sinkevičius also stressed the importance of close coordination between the two countries in responding to both conventional and hybrid threats, as well as the importance of strong transatlantic relations. Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.23 11:04 Lithuania is assessing Latvia’s request for assistance in border protection Translated by Karolis Broga Source: ELTA Martynas Katelynas PHOTO: Andrius Ufartas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google As Latvia faces a spike in irregular migration from Belarus, it has asked for more assistance from Lithuania. Minister of the Interior Martynas Katelynas says the request is being considered but Lithuania’s priority is the security of its own border. „We take into account all the needs they have expressed, what they would like and how much we can help. However, my priority, as minister, is the security of our borders. It is not like our border guards are sitting at home doing nothing, just waiting for us to send them somewhere. We use the capabilities that we have for the protection of our borders. We are assessing possibilities where we could move them, use them to assist Latvia and we hope to find these possibilities,“ Katelynas told ELTA on Wednesday. Lithuania has recently sent two rotations of border guards to help Latvia, which faces irregular migration from Belarus. A team of 9 officers from the State Border Guard Service (VSAT) was deployed to help the neighbouring country secure its border and was later replaced by another team of 9 officers. However, when Latvian Interior Minister Janis Dombrava visited Lithuania recently, he said that Latvia would expect Lithuania to send 100 officers. Katelynas reiterates that Lithuania will explore ways to help, but Latvia should take action as well, for instance, by invoking the assistance of its Armed Forces. When Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs paid a state visit to Lithuania last week, President Gitanas Nausėda said that reintroducing border checkpoints beteween the countries of the Schengen Area would be treated as defeat in tackling irregular migration. Nausėda says it is more important to strengthen the security of the EU’s external borders. Latvia shares a 172 km border with Belarus, an ally of Russia, compared with Lithuania’s 679 km long border. The Baltic States and Poland accuse Belarusian strongman Alexander Lukashenko of deliberately directing irregular migrants to the borders of EU countries in order to exert pressure on the EU. As a result, Lithuania, Latvia and Poland have stepped up their border protection and built border fences. So far this year, Lithuania has stopped 957 foreigners from entering the country illegally. Since the start of the migrant crisis caused by Belarus in 2021, Lithuania has thwarted nearly 26 thousand illegal border crossing attempts. Latvian news agency LETA reports that Latvia stopped 67 illegal migrants from entering Latvia from Belarus on Tuesday, 21 July, and a total of 8,413 migrants so far in 2026. In 2025, Latvia prevented more than 12 thousand foreigners from illegally accessing the country from Belarus. The figure stood at 5,388 in 2024. Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty Images South Korea Starbucks Korea raided by police after ‘Tank Day’ campaign sparks public outrage Coffee chain has faced backlash over marketing promotion tied to anniversary of Gwangju massacre Associated Press in Seoul Thu 6 Aug 2026 03.45 EDT Last modified on Thu 6 Aug 2026 03.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google South Korean police have raided the headquarters of Starbucks Korea as part of an investigation into a marketing campaign accused of trivialising the country’s 1980s pro-democracy movement. Investigators searched the building in southern Seoul on Tuesday, police said on Wednesday. No further details were released, although South Korean media reported that officers also searched the homes of the Starbucks Korea executives. How a Starbucks marketing stunt spiralled into mass boycotts in South Korea Read more The coffee chain triggered a public outcry after launching a range of stainless-steel reusable tumblers it called “SS Tank” and declaring 18 May “Tank Day”. The date marks the anniversary of the 1980 Gwangju uprising, when pro-democracy demonstrators were brutally suppressed by South Korea’s then military-backed government. The campaign also used the slogan “Thwack it on the table!”, which many interpreted as a reference to a notorious 1987 police claim that the student activist Park Jong-chul died after investigators “hit the desk with a thwack”. Authorities had falsely used the phrase to conceal the fact that Park had died by torture during an interrogation. The backlash over the coffee chain’s marketing campaign prompted Shinsegae Group, which owns a 67.5% stake in Starbucks Korea, to cancel the promotion within hours and dismiss the company’s chief executive . The Shinsegae chair, Chung Yong-jin, later issued a televised apology. Starbucks Korea closed all of its stores nationwide on 22 June for mandatory training in history and social awareness. The police investigation was launched after complaints from relatives of victims of the Gwangju crackdown, in which, official records say, about 200 people were killed. South Korea’s transition to democracy gained momentum in 1987, when the authoritarian president Chun Doo-hwan, whose government had overseen the Gwangju crackdown, accepted constitutional reforms introducing direct presidential elections after months of nationwide pro-democracy protests. Photograph: Sergey Dolzhenko/EPA View image in fullscreen Rescuers work at the site of a Russian missile strike on a goods storage in Kyiv on Wednesday. Photograph: Sergey Dolzhenko/EPA Ukraine Nato to ‘urgently’ get air defences for Ukraine, as Zelenskyy warns of surge in Russian missile production After Ukraine failed to shoot down a single ballistic missile fired by Russia on Wednesday, the president urged allies to increase supplies of Patriot interceptors Guardian staff and agencies Wed 5 Aug 2026 22.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 23.22 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nato is working to get Ukraine the air defences it “urgently needs”, its secretary general has said, after Kyiv failed to shoot down a single Russian missile in an attack on Wednesday, and as Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was seeking to significantly boost missile ⁠production ahead of winter. Speaking at a National Security and Defense Council meeting on winter resilience, the Ukrainian president did not rule out the idea that stalling missile supplies from western allies were “aimed at making Ukraine , so to speak, more willing to compromise” in peace talks with Russia. Ukraine war briefing: Cut-price Patriot among options in desperate search for missile defence Read more After meeting Nato’s Mark Rutte, Zelenskyy said: “It is important to cut through all red tape and make the necessary political decisions. Literally every day, people’s lives here in Ukraine depend on the resolve of our partners in Europe and the United States.” Russia launched 24 ballistic missiles in an overnight attack on Wednesday , killing at least 17 people. Preliminary data from the Ukrainian air force showed its defences shot down 98 of the 115 drones fired by Russia overnight, but none of the ballistic missiles. On Wednesday, Zelenskyy said that in the first half of 2026, supplies of air defence missiles from Ukraine’s allies had fallen to a third of their 2025 level. View image in fullscreen Ukrainian service members view a Patriot air defence system in 2024. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters The president also warned that Moscow was looking to significantly increase ballistic missile ⁠production as winter neared, when it is expected to renew its campaign against Ukraine’s energy sector. Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukraine’s president on the development of defence technology, estimated that Russia was capable of launching 100 ballistic missiles every month to attack logistic ​hubs, industrial facilities, food stores and warehouses. “The war of attrition has entered its next phase,” he said on the Telegram app. Ukraine has been short on US-made Patriot interceptors capable of downing Russian ballistic missiles since the ⁠start of the war. But in recent weeks, an acute shortage has come into focus , with Moscow pummelling Kyiv, on ​average, every three days in July alone. Zelenskyy said the shortage of interceptor missiles was mainly caused by the war in the Middle East. Patriot missile systems are the only system in Ukrainian service able to intercept the Russian Iskander-M, S-400 and Zircon missiles, according to the Ukrainian air force. Russia often combines ballistic missiles with cruise missiles, drones and decoys, forcing defenders to track many threats and ration scarce interceptors, but Ukraine says it has too few batteries and interceptors to properly protect itself. View image in fullscreen Ukrainian firefighters work to put out a fire following a massive Russian ballistic missile and drone strike on Kyiv. Photograph: Tetiana Dzhafarova/AFP/Getty Images The interceptor shortage has become more acute as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has consumed large numbers of Patriot and other interceptors . An analysis by the Associated Press estimated that the US Patriot inventory had fallen by at least 65% since before the war. The Pentagon claims it retains a deep arsenal of supplies. Production cannot immediately close the gap. Lockheed Martin delivered more than 600 of the newest model of interceptors in 2025 and is working toward annual capacity of 2,000 by the end of 2030. But according to some estimates, Gulf states collectively fired more than 1,100 interceptors in the first three months of the Iran war. Nato says Europe’s first Patriot missile production facility is expected to open in September in Germany. Political signals from Washington have also shifted. At a Nato summit last month, Donald Trump said the US would give Ukraine a licence to produce Patriots . About three weeks later, he said he had not made a final decision . Even with a licence, officials and experts estimate that starting production in Ukraine would take years. Despite Trump casting doubt on the deal last month, the US is pressing ahead with talks on allowing Ukraine to make Patriot interceptors, according to reports from Reuters. The discussions ⁠include an option for Ukraine to ⁠build some components for final assembly elsewhere in ​Europe, according to the report.
