https://www.dw.com/en/drought-threatens-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IPa0 Cargo ships anchor near Petrovaradin, Serbia, on the Danube amid extremely low levels of water following an extended period of drought Image: Darko Vojinovic/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Riverbeds reduced to tiny streams, asphalt melting like butter, dried-up fields — these are currently the images of drought in Central and Southeastern Europe. The record-breaking lack of rainfall in recent months and this summer's heatwaves have caused severe damage to the region's economy and infrastructure. In the agriculture sector, it has been clear for some time that harvests in Southeastern Europe, especially maize and sunflower crops, will be significantly below average. The heatwaves are also repeatedly disrupting road, rail and, above all, shipping transport. But, most importantly, the drought has triggered an unprecedented crisis in electricity generation in several Central and Southeastern European countries, forcing companies to halt production due to the historically low water level of the Danube. Hungary and Romania are currently most affected by the energy crisis. Other countries bordering the Danube — Austria , Slovakia , Serbia and Bulgaria — are also suffering from low water levels, although not as severely as Hungary and Romania. DW outlines the situation in each country and explains why, despite facing similar weather conditions, some are more severely affected than others. Hungary: Most severe energy crisis in decades No country in the region is currently as severely affected by drought and heat as Hungary. For months, there has been little or no rainfall in large parts of the country. On Wednesday, temperatures reached 43 degrees Celsius (109.4 degrees Fahrenheit) in the capital Budapest , and exceeded 40 degrees in many places across the country. Due to the record-low water levels of the Danube, the Paks nuclear power plant south of Budapest had to largely shut down operations, as there is no longer sufficent cooling water available and the temperature of the Danube water is too high. The plant is currently operating at around 12% of its capacity. If Danube water levels continue to drop, the plant will have to be shut down completely. Due to the energy crisis, the Hungarian government has been urging large energy consumers to conserve electricity. As a result, several car manufacturers, including Audi Gyor, oil and gas company MOL and other large companies have scaled back production. Hungary's energy crisis — the worst in decades — is so severe because of the country's unfavorable energy mix. Paks generates around 50% of the electricity produced in Hungary and about one-third of the electricity consumed. Although Hungary has significant solar energy capacity, it lacks storage facilities, has too few modern gas-fired power plants and very little wind or hydropower capacity. In Prahovo (eastern Serbia), the Danube's low water level has revealed the remains of a German WW II warship Image: Darko Vojinovic/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Even if the Danube water levels rise significantly again, the Paks nuclear power plant cannot simply be brought back online quickly — the process takes a considerable amount of time. Therefore, Hungary's energy crisis will continue for at least several more weeks, during which the country will have to import electricity at high prices. In response to the crisis, the new government under Peter Magyar has announced a comprehensive review of Hungary's energy development strategy. Romania: Blasting rocks to redirect water Romania is experiencing a similar, though somewhat less severe, energy crisis. The Cernavoda nuclear power plant, also located on the Danube in the southeast of the country, produces roughly one-fifth of Romania's electricity. Due to the river's exceptionally low water level, one of the plant's two 700-megawatt reactors was taken offline last week. Southwest of the Cernavoda plant, Romanian authorities blasted a rock formation this week to divert more water into the Danube's eastern branch, where the nuclear plant is located. In addition, dozens of tons of rock were dumped into the river to channel more water into that branch. Romania's navy carried out a controlled blast of submerged rocks to allow more water to flow into the eastern branch of the Danube Image: Vadim Ghirda/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Romania has a relatively balanced energy mix consisting of hydropower, nuclear energy, natural gas, coal and wind power. However, because hydropower accounts for around one-fifth of the country's electricity generation — primarily through the Iron Gate hydroelectric plant on the Danube — Romania is particularly vulnerable to droughts such as the current one. Due to the energy crisis, several major companies, including Dacia and Ford Romania, have scaled back production. The government has announced that it would, if necessary, issue a decree ordering large factories to suspend production. Romania is also among the Southeastern European countries most affected by aridification — the long-term climatic process through which regions become increasingly dry — and desertification, as soils gradually become barren and take on desert-like characteristics. Serbia: An unfavorable energy mix Serbia, too, is suffering badly from drought and the Danube's low water level. Its energy mix is similarly ill-suited to prolonged dry periods. Around 65% of its electricity is generated by coal-fired power plants, while about 25% comes from hydropower. The two Iron Gate hydropower plants are currently generating only a fraction of their average electricity output. The coal-fired power plants Kostolac A and B east of Belgrade , which rely on Danube water for cooling, have also had to cut back production. In Hungary, dropping water levels of the Danube threaten the complete shutdown of the Paks nuclear power plant Image: David Balogh/Xinhua/IMAGO Serbia relies heavily on the Danube as a transport route for coal and petrochemical products. However, due to the low water level, cargo vessels can currently only carry a fraction of their normal loads. Nonetheless, the energy crisis has so far not been so severe that large industrial plants have had to scale back production. Slovakia, Austria less affected In Slovakia, some 60% of electricity is generated by nuclear power plants, with another 20% by hydropower. Unlike Hungary and Romania, Slovakia's two nuclear power plants, Bohunice and Mochovce, are located on smaller rivers and use cooling towers rather than once-through cooling systems. Once-through cooling requires large quantities of river water that are drawn from the river and then channeled back to it at a higher temperature. In contrast, cooling towers recirculate water in a closed system, releasing heat mainly through evaporation. As a result, Slovakia's nuclear plants require much less river water and are therefore less affected by the current drought. In comparison, Slovakia's Gabcikovo hydropower on the Danube has been significantly affected by the low water level. At present, only one of its eight turbines is in operation. Electricity generation in Gabcikovo, however, is only about 12% lower compared to the same time last year. So far, Slovakia has not experienced any major industrial production stoppages. Austria, which generates around 60% of its electricity from hydropower, has also been less severely affected than Hungary. One reason is that part of Austria's hydropower capacity comes from storage and pumped-storage plants rather than run-of-river facilities. Run-of-river plants depend directly on the volume of water flowing through rivers, whereas storage and pumped-storage plants can generate electricity using water stored in reservoirs when needed, making them less vulnerable during prolonged heatwaves and droughts. In addition, Austria generates some 30% of its electricity from other renewable energy sources. Bulgaria: Large battery storage capacity Unlike in neighboring Romania, drought and heat are not yet causing an energy crisis in Bulgaria. The country generates up to 40% of its energy through the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, which is also located on the Danube. Its cooling system, however, is better designed to operate under low-water conditions than those of Hungary's Paks plant and Cernavoda in Romania. As a result, it is currently operating at almost full capacity. At the same time, Bulgaria depends only marginally on hydropower and has, in recent years, considerably expanded its solar and wind energy capacity. The biggest difference to all the other countries lies in Bulgaria's large-scale battery storage facilities. The country currently has storage systems with a capacity of 3.4 gigawatts and a storage capacity of 8.6 gigawatt-hours. This storage capacity corresponds to 16% of the country's total installed power generation capacity — a figure unmatched by any other country in the world. These storage facilities enable Bulgaria to balance supply shortages and peak demand, without relying on expensive imports. At the same time, the country is developing into a regional market leader in new energy concepts and as a hub for power grid stabilization and greater price stability in the electricity market. https://www.politico.eu/article/elon-mus.text: Owner of X and world’s first trillionaire Elon Musk attacked French presidential candidate Marine Tondelier on Thursday, after the Greens party leader said French authorities should be able to suspend the platform during electoral campaigns in case of foreign interference. “I demand that she be shut down for treason against France!” Musk wrote on X, prompting a strong reaction from Tondelier. “France does not need lessons in patriotism from a foreign billionaire who thinks he gets to decide which European political leaders should be silenced. Democracy is not for sale. Not even to the richest man in the world,” she responded . Advertisement Advertisement “I’d rather be accused of defending democracy than of trying to buy it.” Musk, who is a former adviser to U.S. President Donald Trump, has regularly weighed in on European politics and thrown his support behind far-right candidates and parties — and France is no exception. In July, Musk said far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen was “France’s last hope,” but her National Rally party was quick to downplay his backing to avoid being associated with the controversial owner of Tesla and SpaceX. Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon also slammed Musk’s attacks against Tondelier on Thursday, before accusing the French government of not doing enough to fight foreign interference. “The French presidential election is an open bar for all the manipulators in the world,” he wrote — a criticism Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot promptly rejected . Earlier this week, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the government was boosting efforts to detect and punish foreign interference in the upcoming 2027 election, while presidential candidates Gabriel Attal and Édouard Philippe , as well as likely candidate Raphaël Glucksmann shared they had been victims of Russian disinformation campaigns. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckgd.text: Image source, Jens Schlueter/Getty Images Image caption, A special robot was sent to remove the detonator from the device By Sarah Rainsford Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent Published 4 hours ago As Germany investigates how a drone loaded with explosives reached a runway at Leipzig airport, there is renewed talk in Europe of hybrid war. The interior minister is warning of a "new level of danger" from an attack that "may involve foreign powers". There is no proof at this stage to link the flying bomb directly to Russia, which denies any role. But as well as the means and the motive, Moscow does have form. The BBC has seen details of the investigation into a plot in 2024 in which Russian-linked proxies in Poland and Lithuania not only handled drones and explosives but also delivered them to Germany. The flying bomb The quadcopter was discovered at Leipzig airport late on Tuesday night, forcing one runway into lockdown as a bomb disposal robot rolled into action. On the tarmac close by were several Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes, stripes along their enormous bodies in the blue and yellow of the country's flag. One reads, "Be Brave Like Kherson", the southern city now on the frontline of Russia's invasion. Pictures published by German media suggest the drone was a relatively small device which airport staff spotted "floating" between the Ukrainian planes. Around the same time, a DHL cargo plane collided with an "unidentified object" as it pulled up into the sky, unable to land in Leipzig. Teams are still working to establish whether that was a second drone. They are also trying to trace who launched the devices and why. Figure caption, Watch: Robot deployed to inspect device at German airport A previous plot A previous Russian-backed plot involving Leipzig airport could provide clues. In 2024, a parcel containing a sophisticated incendiary device caught fire at the airport's DHL hub shortly before it was loaded onto a plane. Similar packages then ignited in the UK and Poland, causing extensive damage. A group of men are currently on trial in both Lithuania and Poland, where prosecutors believe they were part of a substantial network of proxies recruited by Russian military intelligence. But there was a subplot that has been little discussed before. Last September, Lithuanian prosecutors said that investigators had also seized RDX explosives meant for "other terrorist attacks". The amount was significant: equivalent to 6kg of TNT. "Some of the devices were manufactured to intensify the blast," the prosecutor added. The BBC has since had access to case documents that describe how several of the men on trial were paid to transport those explosives around Europe, concealed in cans of sweetcorn and chopped tomatoes. The detonators were hidden inside headphone sets. The suspects also handled drone parts and the case talks specifically of attachments, suitable for holding a bomb. Prosecutors allege that some of the items were brought into the EU from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Almost two dozen suspects have been charged with terror offences, but with the men's handlers still at large, believed to be in Russia, it is not clear whether the entire network was disbanded or all the hidden material found. While there is no evidence of a link to the Leipzig drone bomb, the 2024 plot certainly highlights the potential. Vladyslav's story One of the suspects charged in Poland, a Ukrainian called Vladyslav D., described in detail to investigators how he made multiple long car trips in July 2024 following instructions from someone he knew as "Warrior". He has since pleaded not guilty in court. One message sent him to the edge of a Lithuanian forest where he found a carrier bag containing "three or four packs of headphones", soggy with rain. He had already collected two cans of corn "lightly covered with soil" from another location, telling investigators he had no idea what was inside. He was ordered to leave the headphones many hours' drive away in Poland where he noticed "a guy on a bicycle" collect them from beside the road. For another assignment he received a pin for a location inside a Lithuanian cemetery and was told to dig beneath some plastic flowers. He quickly uncovered a bin bag wrapped in brown tape. "Inside were drone components: small plastic propellers, I think four pieces," Vladyslav told investigators. These items were to be left by a road in central Poland for pick-up. Finally there was a trip to Germany where he was given the code to access a hostel room in Dusseldorf. He was instructed to leave the drones and other items inside. The intended targets were never revealed. Moscow's motive? In statements to investigators, Vladyslav D. said he was paid more than $2,000 (Â£1,487) in cryptocurrency for his efforts. His motive was clear. And what about the Leipzig case? Few details about the drone bomb are yet public. Some German sources report that the explosive was Semtex, which contains RDX - the explosive found in the food cans in a Lithuanian cemetery. We do not know how much the drone found at the airport was carrying and the physical damage may have been limited. "The drone casing, if it was metal, might have put a hole in the plane but just a blast wave probably would just have dented it unless they put some fragmentation inside," explosives expert Professor Jackie Akhavan of Cranfield University explained. But if Russia was behind this, its aim was more likely to sow fear. Andrei Soldatov, an expert on Russia's intelligence agencies, said it "makes sense" to suspect Moscow, pointing to a clear pattern of sabotage and hostile activity, from arson attacks on facilities supporting Ukraine to drones over sensitive sites in Europe. Germany is one of Kyiv's biggest suppliers of military aid. "It's a message. You get something like that [bomb] into one of the biggest European airports and you send the message that, 'Guys, we can do that. Remember'," Soldatov explained. "You hint to the adversary that you might cause a really big problem: that tomorrow might be more serious." And the potential motive? Moscow is under intense pressure from Ukraine's long-scale drone attacks, he said, and the fact that Russian President Vladimir Putin "has been humiliated, repeatedly". International response "We are aware of the incident, which the German authorities continue to investigate," a Nato official told the BBC. Antonov Airlines has also been cautious so far in its response. The firm supplies planes for certain Nato operations but declined to say whether that includes military support for Ukraine. Asked whether the Ukrainian planes might have been targeted, a spokeswoman in Kyiv told the BBC: "We are not making any such assumptionsâ¦We don't know what this drone was or why it was there." But Russia watchers are clear. "This is Russian interference," said John Lough of the New Eurasian Strategies (NEST) Centre. "It's all part of undermining support for Ukraine by pointing to the dangers of escalation and, frankly, scaring the German authorities." He sees high potential for a surge in such hybrid attacks now because Ukraine has "changed the balance" of the war. "My expectation is that such activity will increase quite sharply over the coming months. I think it's a dangerous moment." https://telex.hu/english/2026/08/07/hung.text: Menü Kereső Hungarian inflation at its lowest in ten years English Bicsérdi-Fülöp Ádám Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom According to the flash report of the Central Statistical Office (Központi Statisztikai Hivatal-KSH), consumer prices in Hungary were, on average, 1.2 percent higher in July than in the same month of the previous year. The report also notes that prices fell by 0.1 percent compared to June of this year. Compared with July 2025, however, consumer food prices fell by 1.1 percent, and retail prices were down 4.4 percent. Compared with June of this year, consumer food prices fell by an average of 1 percent, and retail prices were 1.7 percent lower. Prices for services have increased by an average of 1.6 percent. The price of household energy fell by 0.9 percent; within this category, the price of piped gas fell by 1.5 percent, electricity by 0.2 percent, while central heating prices remained unchanged. Fuel became 1.3 percent cheaper, and clothing became 2.1 percent cheaper. After the data was released, Prime Minister Péter Magyar posted that inflation had fallen to a level that had not been seen in 10 years. According to his post, this was the first time in a long time that grocery prices had decreased in Hungary. Portfolio has pointed out that Hungary has not seen such a low rate of price increases since the end of 2016. According to the National Trade Association (Országos Kereskedelmi Szövetség-OKSZ), the 4.4 percent price decrease in what is perhaps the most important product category for the general public is a more favorable figure than anyone expected to see. The body states that the price-margin caps (introduced by the previous government in May 2025) have not played any role in shaping food prices since May; the current numbers are solely the result of favorable trends in both domestic and international markets, as well as the forint's exchange rate, which more than offset the increases stemming from rising energy costs. According to the OKSZ, conditions are now favorable for phasing out the price-margin cap, which was introduced by the Orbán government. The organization believes this would have numerous benefits for consumers: promotions offering substantial discounts would return, the range of goods and the quality of service would improve, and, thanks to long-delayed investments, store interiors could also be upgraded. A kormányfő példátlannak nevezte a mostani összefogást, szerinte az első kutatások azt mutatják, hogy szinte minden család részt vett a takarékoskodásban. https://telex.hu/after/2026/08/07/locker.text: Menü Kereső A gép néhány másodperc alatt darabokra szakadt, a lezuhanó roncsok házakat, autókat semmisítettek meg After Külföld Legfontosabb Mentőalakulatok a gép orr részénél Lockerbie-ben 1988. december 24-én – Fotó: Blick / RDB / ullstein bild / Getty Images Dévai László 1988. december 21. néhány másodperc alatt vált a modern repülés történetének egyik legsötétebb napjává. A Pan American World (Pan Am) Airways 103-as járata alig fél órával londoni felszállása után a skóciai Lockerbie fölött a levegőben felrobbant, majd a repülő darabjai a kisvárosra zuhantak. A fedélzeten tartózkodó 259 ember meghalt, a becsapódó roncsok pedig további 11 embert öltek meg. A világ egyik legismertebb légi katasztrófájának négy magyar áldozata is volt. A tragédia közel negyven évvel később is a világ legismertebb terrortámadásai közé tartozik, merthogy a 103-as járatot terroristák robbantották fel. Nemcsak azért ez a világ egyik legismertebb terrorcselekménye, mert a nyomozás több mint három évig tartott, és példátlan nemzetközi együttműködést igényelt, hanem azért is, mert az ügy körül máig rengeteg a vitatott részlet. Bár hivatalosan két líbiai hírszerzőt neveztek meg felelősként, az elmúlt évtizedekben számos alternatív elmélet látott napvilágot, amik szerint a történet korántsem olyan egyértelmű, mint amilyennek elsőre tűnik. Ezt dolgozza fel a Netflix új, hatrészes sorozata, a Lockerbie: A Pan Am 103-as járata, ami nemcsak a merényletet, hanem az azt követő nyomozást és a lockerbie-i közösség példátlan helytállását is bemutatja. Néhány másodperc alatt darabokra szakadt December 21-én reggel a Pan Am 103A számú járata elindult Frankfurtból Londonba. A fedélzeten utazók mit sem sejtettek arról, hogy a raktérben egy gazdátlan barna Samsonite bőrönd is helyet kapott. A poggyászt senki sem vette át Londonban, mégis automatikusan átpakolták a Heathrow repülőtéren várakozó, New Yorkba tartó Pan Am 103-as járatra. A Clipper Maid of the Seas nevű Boeing–747-es aznap valamivel este fél hét után szállt fel Londonból. A járat fedélzetén 243 utas és 16 fős személyzet tartózkodott. James MacQuarrie kapitány rutinszerű átkelésre készült az Atlanti-óceán felett, a gép pedig a megszokott útvonalon, Skócia irányába fordult. Minden a menetrend szerint haladt, néhány perccel este hét óra előtt a Boeing már elérte a közel kilencezer méteres utazómagasságot. A pilóták felvették a kapcsolatot a légi irányítással, majd elhangzott az utolsó rádióüzenet: „Clipper 103 óceánrepülési engedélyt kér.” Néhány másodperccel később a radar képernyőjéről egyszerűen eltűnt a repülőgép. A légi irányítók először kommunikációs hibára gyanakodtak, de hamar nyilvánvalóvá vált, hogy sokkal súlyosabb történt. 19 óra 2 perckor a gép első osztályának magasságában elhelyezett bőröndben felrobbant egy pokolgép. A robbanás akkora erejű volt, hogy a Boeing–747-es néhány másodperc alatt darabokra szakadt. A gép orra levált, a törzs szétszakadt, a szárnyak és a hajtóművek különböző irányokba repültek. Az utasoknak és a személyzetnek esélyük sem volt a túlélésre. A roncsok szétszóródtak Dél-Skóciában, a legnagyobb darabok azonban Lockerbie kisvárosára zuhantak. Az egyik szárny és több tízezer liter repülőgép-üzemanyag egy lakónegyedet ért. Az üzemanyag hatalmas tűzgolyóvá válva azonnal felrobbant. Házak semmisültek meg, utcák tűntek el, autók égtek ki. A becsapódás akkora erejű volt, hogy a szeizmográfok egy 1,6-os erősségű földrengést is rögzítettek. A törmelékek becsapódásának helyszínei Lockerbie-ben, 1988 decemberében – Fotó: Bryn Colton / Getty Images és Blick / RDB / ullstein bild / Getty Images A gépen utazókon kívül a földön további tizenegy ember halt meg. A helyiek először azt hitték, katonai repülő zuhant le, vagy egy fegyverraktár robbant fel. A város lakói az utcára rohantak, ahol mindenhol égő törmelék, poggyászok, repülőgép-alkatrészek és személyes tárgyak hevertek. A mentők, rendőrök és tűzoltók perceken belül megkezdték a mentést, de hamar nyilvánvalóvá vált, hogy a repülőgépen senki sem élhette túl a robbanást. A fedélzeten utazott a háromtagú váci Roller család, valamint egy budapesti nő is, akik szintén életüket vesztették a merényletben. Óriási nemzetközi összefogás a felelősök kézre kerítéséhez Miközben Lockerbie lakói még mindig a romok között keresték a túlélőket, a brit hatóságok ezzel párhuzamosan már egy egészen más feladatra is koncentráltak. A következő napokban ugyanis megkezdődött Skócia történetének addigi legnagyobb bűnügyi nyomozása. Több ezer rendőr, katonai szakértő, igazságügyi szakértő és hírszerző érkezett a helyszínre, hogy egyenként összegyűjtsék a több százezer szétszóródott roncsdarabot. Eleinte még senki sem tudta biztosan, mi okozta a katasztrófát. Felmerült, hogy műszaki hiba történt, de hamar egyértelművé vált, hogy a gépet nem baleset, hanem szándékos robbantás semmisítette meg. A nyomozóknak nem volt könnyű dolguk, a becsapódás helyszíne ugyanis nem egyetlen kráter vagy roncsmező volt: a Boeing darabjai kétezer négyzetkilométeres területen szóródtak szét Skóciában. A szakemberek szó szerint centiméterről centiméterre kutatták át a vidéket, minden egyes fémdarabot, ruhadarabot és személyes tárgyat összegyűjtve. A cél az volt, hogy a repülőgépet a lehető legnagyobb részletességgel újra összeállítsák a darabokból, mert csak így derülhetett ki, mi okozta a robbanást. A vizsgálat során a roncsok között robbanóanyag-maradványokat találtak. A szakértők aztán megállapították, hogy a gépet Semtex típusú robbanóanyaggal robbantották fel, amit egy rádiós magnóba rejtett időzítős szerkezet működtetett. A bomba a barna Samsonite bőröndben volt, amit a raktér első részében helyeztek el, közvetlenül a gép törzsének kritikus pontján. A robbanás néhány másodperc alatt átszakította a gép oldalát, a kabinban pedig azonnal megszűnt a nyomás, ami gyakorlatilag pillanatok alatt apró darabokra tépte szét a gépet. Több szervezet is magára vállalta a merényletet, köztük az Iszlám Dzsihád és az északír Ulsteri Védelmi Liga nevű félkatonai szervezet is, de egyik bejelentés sem bizonyult hitelesnek. A tragédia után derült ki, hogy mindössze tizenhat nappal a robbantás előtt egy arab akcentussal beszélő férfi telefonon figyelmeztette a légitársaságot egy közelgő támadásra. A fenyegetést nem vették komolyan. A nyomozás hamar túlnőtt Skócia határain. Bekapcsolódott az FBI, a CIA, a brit MI5 és MI6, valamint számos európai ország rendvédelmi szerve is. Az áldozatok ugyanis 21 országból származtak, közülük 189-en amerikai állampolgárok voltak, ezért az Egyesült Államok történetének addigi legsúlyosabb terrorcselekményeként kezelték az ügyet. A nyomozók hónapokon át próbálták visszakövetni a bomba útját. Apró bizonyítékokból rakták össze a képet: egy megégett ruhacímkéből, néhány vezetékdarabból, egy időzítő áramköri lapjának maradványaiból és a bőröndben talált ruhákból. Ezek a nyomok végül Máltára vezettek. A nyomozás szerint a robbanószerkezetet egy olyan poggyászba rejtették, amit eredetileg a máltai Luqa repülőtéren adtak fel úgy, hogy nem tartozott hozzá utas. A bőrönd Frankfurtba került, ott automatikusan átrakták a Londonba tartó járatra, majd a Heathrow-n minden további ellenőrzés nélkül felkerült a New Yorkba induló Pan Am 103-as gépre. Ez a láncolat később alapjaiban változtatta meg a nemzetközi poggyászkezelési szabályokat: a legtöbb országban ezután vezették be azt az előírást, hogy utas nélküli poggyász nem kerülhet repülőgépre. Egyre hangsúlyosabbá vált a líbiai szál A bomba szerkezetének vizsgálata végül Líbiára terelte a gyanút. A szakértők szerint az időzítő egy olyan elektronikai alkatrészt használt, amiből korábban több darabot is a líbiai hírszerzés szerzett be. Emellett a Máltán vásárolt ruhák is olyan üzlethez vezettek, ahol a tulajdonos később azonosítani vélte azt a férfit, aki a robbantáshoz használt ruhadarabokat megvette. A nyomozásnak ugyanakkor geopolitikai háttere is volt. Az amerikai hírszerzés kezdetben nemcsak Líbiát, hanem Iránt is vizsgálta, mint lehetséges elkövető országot. Ennek oka az volt, hogy néhány hónappal korábban az amerikai haditengerészet tévedésből lelőtte az Iran Air 655-ös járatát, az incidensben 290 civil vesztette életét. Több elemző elképzelhetőnek tartotta, hogy a Pan Am 103-as felrobbantása erre válaszul végrehajtott bosszúakció volt, amit iráni támogatással vittek végbe. Mások úgy vélték, Moammer Kadhafi líbiai vezető állhatott a háttérben, válaszul az Egyesült Államok 1986-os líbiai légicsapásaira, amiket egy nyugat-berlini diszkó elleni terrortámadás után rendeltek el. A hivatalos vizsgálat végül az utóbbi verzió mellett tette le a voksát. 1991 novemberében a brit és az amerikai hatóságok vádat emeltek két líbiai állampolgár, Abdelbaszet Ali Mohamed al-Megrahi hírszerző tiszt és társa, Al-Amin Khalifa Fhimah ellen. A líbiai vezetés azonban éveken át megtagadta a kiadatásukat. Kadhafi politikai indíttatásúnak nevezte a vádakat, és azt állította, hogy országának semmi köze sem volt a merénylethez. A patthelyzet miatt az ENSZ súlyos szankciókat vezetett be Líbiával szemben, az Egyesült Államok pedig kereskedelmi embargót alkalmazott. Az ország egyre jobban elszigetelődött, ami végül tárgyalóasztalhoz kényszerítette Kadhafit. 1999-ben Líbia beleegyezett abba, hogy a két gyanúsítottat kiadják egy különleges bíróságnak. A tárgyalást nem Skóciában, hanem a hollandiai Camp Zeist egykori katonai bázisán tartották, ahol skót bírák, skót törvények alapján jártak el. A több hónapig tartó per végén, 2001 januárjában Abdelbaszet al-Megrahit életfogytiglani börtönbüntetésre ítélték, míg Fhimahot bizonyítékok hiányában felmentették. Az ítélet azonban korántsem zárta le az ügyet. Több jogász, nyomozó és hozzátartozó is kétségbe vonta a bizonyítékok megbízhatóságát, és azóta is sokan vitatják, hogy valóban al-Megrahi volt-e a merénylet kitervelője, vagy csak egy sokkal bonyolultabb nemzetközi játszma bűnbakjává vált. A Netflix a nyomozásra koncentrál A történet most azért került ismét reflektorfénybe, mert a Netflix feldolgozta a tragédiát a hatrészes minisorozatban. Ez annyiból érdekes döntés tőlük, hogy 2025 év elején megjelent a Lockerbie: Az igazság nyomában című ötrészes brit minisorozat, ami Jim Swire és Peter Biddulph The Lockerbie Bombing: A Father's Search for Justice című, 2021-ben megjelent könyvén alapul. Az adaptációban a főszerepet Colin Firth játssza, aki dr. Jim Swire-t alakítja. A férfi lánya, Flora életét vesztette 1988-ban a Pan Am 103-as járata fedélzetén, a sorozat pedig azt mutatja be, hogyan indult éveken át tartó küzdelme az igazság felderítéséért. A netflixes Lockerbie ezzel szemben egy kicsit másra helyezi a hangsúlyt. Közel sem annyira személyes, sőt, szinte teljesen kerüli a hatásvadászatot. Magát a robbanást is visszafogottan mutatja be, inkább a kisváros lakóinak szemszögéből látjuk a kétség kívül pokoli végkifejletet. Az első részekből is látszik, hogy a készítők nem sokkolni akarják a nézőt, hanem érzékeltetni, milyen elképesztő pusztítást hagyott maga után a merénylet. Fotó: World Productions / Netflix A történet középpontjában a Connor Swindells (Szexoktatás) által alakított Ed McCusker skót nyomozó és Patrick J. Adams (The Madison) FBI-ügynök áll. Rajtuk keresztül követjük végig a hosszú és aprólékos nyomozást, ahogy szó szerint a semmiből próbálják felderíteni az ügyet egyetlen ruhacímkéből, vezetékdarabból vagy időzítőmaradványból. A sorozat jól érzékelteti, hogy a nyomozás éveken át tartó nemzetközi együttműködés volt, de érdekes módon kevésbé mélyül el a szereplők személyiségében, inkább a folyamatra helyezi a hangsúlyt. Talán pont ez a sorozat legnagyobb erőssége és egyben gyengesége is. Tisztelettel bánnak az áldozatokkal és Lockerbie lakóival, akik rengeteget tettek a családok segítéséért, de az egész kicsit tét nélküli, és alkalmanként túlságosan visszafogott marad. Kevés szó esik például arról, hogyan változtatta meg a tragédia a nemzetközi légi közlekedést vagy milyen geopolitikai következményei voltak a merényletnek. Így azoknak, akik nem ismerik részletesen az eseményeket, több fontos összefüggés is háttérben maradhat. Mindezek ellenére a Lockerbie: A Pan Am 103-as járata méltó emléket állít az áldozatoknak. Nem egy akciódús thriller, hanem egy lassú, nyomozásközpontú dráma, ami azt mutatja meg, milyen emberfeletti munkára volt szükség ahhoz, hogy a világ egyik legsúlyosabb repülőgépes terrortámadásának felelőseit végül bíróság elé állítsák. A sorozat ugyan nem ad minden kérdésre választ, de jól érzékelteti, miért a lockerbie-i merénylet a modern terrorizmus és a légi közlekedés történetének egyik legmeghatározóbb eseménye. https://telex.hu/g7/adat/2026/08/07/infl.text: Menü Kereső A magyar infláció kakukktojás Európában Adat A Mol Mészáros utcai üzemanyagtöltő-állomása 2026. június 18-án – Fotó: Szigetváry Zsolt / MTI Hajdu Miklós Uniós összehasonlításban is rendkívül alacsonynak számít a ma közzétett, éves alapon 1,2 százalékos júliusi magyar infláció. Sőt, még az inflációs trendek is különböznek Magyarország és Európa országai között: míg a magyar árak egyre lassabban emelkednek, addig a kontinens többi részén a drágulás üteme változatlan. Számokban: az eurózónában júliusban 2,9 százalékra nőtt az infláció, ami alapvetően az energiaárak 10 százalékos emelkedése miatt következett be. Ezzel szemben Magyarországon a háztartási energiáért csak 2,3 százalékkal, a járműüzemanyagokért pedig 1,6 százalékkal kellett többet fizetni éves összehasonlításban. Tavasz óta csökken az infláció mértéke Magyarországon, míg az eurózónában 3 százalék közelében ragadt. Az eurózónás szintet a magyar árindex még az iráni háború kitörését követően sem érte el, áprilisban is csak 2,1 százalékig növekedett. Lényeges azonban, hogy ebben az időszakban a magyar benzinkutaknak az üzemanyagokat a kormány által meghatározott, nyomott árakon kellett értékesíteniük. Alulnézet: a magyar üzemanyagárak jóval alacsonyabbak , mint a környező országok többségében, noha a tavasszal bevezetett árszabályozás júniusban megszűnt. A Mol valószínűleg a globális árak növekedését csak némi időeltolódással érvényesíti. Ez piaci anomáliákhoz vezethet , de az új kormánynak is az az érdeke, hogy ne legyen drágulás, mert az üzemanyagárak alakulása átpolitizált téma lett. Tágabb kontextus: a júliusban enyhén emelkedő euróövezeti infláció tovább erősítette azokat a várakozásokat, hogy az Európai Központi Bank újabb kamatemelést hajthat végre. A magas olajárak az inflációs nyomást egyre szélesebb körben fokozzák, ami szintén indokolhatja a szigorúbb monetáris politikát. Igen, de: a magyarországi kormányváltással kapcsolatos piaci optimizmusnak köszönhetően tavasszal a jócskán megerősödött forint szintén fékezte az olajár emelkedésének következményeit. A Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) középtávú inflációs célja 3 százalék, mindkét irányban egy százalékos toleranciasávval, így a mostani, váratlanul alacsony inflációs adat további kamatvágásokra ad lehetőséget. A forint most épp gyengülőben van, a piac ugyanis már elkezdett beárazni egy szeptemberi kamatcsökkentést . Ha fennmarad ez a tendencia , akkor a fogyasztók jobban megérezhetik az importált inflációt, és az üzemanyag-drágulást is nehezebb lesz megfékezni. Az alacsonyabb kamatok azonban csökkenthetik az államháztartás kamatkiadásait. Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! Legfontosabb Friss hírek

Beállítom Tarr Zoltán társadalmi kapcsolatokért és kultúráért felelős miniszter szerint sem a minisztérium, sem ő nem szól bele a közmédia mindennapi működésébe. A miniszter szerint a parlament által megválasztott megbízott vezető végzi a közmédia átvilágítását egy néhány fős csapat élén. Arról is beszélt Tarr, hogy ezzel párhuzamosan a múlt héten elindult a széles körű szakmai párbeszéd, amelynek során különböző szakmai és érdekvédelmi szervezetek, szakemberek mondhatják el gondolataikat a közmédia átalakításáról. A miniszter azt kérte, hogy mindenki küldje el az észrevételeit, javaslatait a közmédia megújítására azon az online felületen keresztül, amely hamarosan megnyílik. https://hungarytoday.hu/medieval-festiva.text: Medieval Festival in Szeged Celebrates John Hunyadi’s Victory at Belgrade A medieval festival will be held on Saturday beside the Franciscan Church in Szeged, where cultural programs, medieval weapons and combat demonstrations, traditional dances, and children’s activities will commemorate the 570th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade, the organizers announced. The event was launched in 2006, on the 550th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade, by staff members of the cultural center of the Franciscan monastery in Szeged’s Lower Town. Their aim was to create a celebration honoring John Hunyadi’s victory over the Ottomans and, alongside the many national days of mourning, to also pay tribute to Hungary’s great historic victories. In the summer of 1456, the crusaders led by Saint John of Capistrano stopped near the Franciscan monastery in Szeged, at what is now Mátyás Square, on their way south. The location therefore has a direct connection to the historic events commemorated by the ‘Belgrade Victory Days.’ Participants of Szeged’s only cultural program dedicated to reviving medieval traditions, which has now been held for more than two decades, will gather on Saturday morning at Klauzál Square in the city center. The lively procession, featuring musicians, drummers, and flag bearers, will then make its way to the Franciscan Church and monastery in the Lower Town, where visitors will be able to enjoy live role-playing, a children’s knight tournament, the interactive “Dragon Trail” game, a knight-themed craft workshop, and a falconry demonstration. Visitors will be able to admire costumes and weapons at close range and experience what life was like in the military camps of King Matthias Corvinus’s famous Black Army. Alongside martial arts displays, knightly duels, and demonstrations of medieval weapons and warfare, members of historical reenactment groups will organize dance events and concerts. Thanks to the Historical Society of Marót, visitors will also learn what firearms were used during the Ottoman period. The program will conclude after sunset, with a fire show and fire duel by the St. Longinus Historical Society instead of fireworks. The following morning, a ceremonial mass will be held at the Franciscan Church in honor of the 570th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade. The Christian Hungarian forces led by John Hunyadi inflicted a crushing defeat on the army of Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II on July 22, 1456. In 2011, the Hungarian Parliament declared the date a national day of remembrance for the Siege of Belgrade. https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/artic.text: George Russell Mercedes Hungary 'They look very strong' – Russell wary of Ferrari threat in Hungary as Mercedes struggle in Friday practice Ferrari headed both sessions on Friday, while Mercedes failed to show competitive one-lap pace in Hungary. Jul 24, 2026 5:45pm UTC George Russell believes that Ferrari "look very strong" having dominated Friday practice ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix, while Mercedes struggled for performance. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton each finished fastest in both of Friday's one-hour sessions in Budapest, with the tight, twisty confines of the Hungaroring expected to suit the Scuderia's car this weekend. Despite leading both the Teams' and Drivers' standings, Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli failed to challenge the leading times in either session. "It was quite a strange day out there I think for everybody," said Russell, who finished P5 in both sessions. "It's an amazing track to drive but they've resurfaced half the track, super bumpy. "Our single lap [pace] didn't look great, the long run looked more competitive but what we feared with Ferrari seemed to the case. They look very strong." Russell ended the day only P5 in both sessions Russell admitted that he "trusted in the team that everything has been resolved" after a software issue denied him maximum power at the previous round in Belgium, but that in general "we've got work to do as a team, Ferrari are a good step ahead of everyone right now." Antonelli, who leads Russell by 50 points and Hamilton by 45, had a delayed start to proceedings on Friday, as his Mercedes was being driven by the team's Third Driver Fred Vesti in FP1. Once in the car for FP2, the Italian finished P13 having been unable to complete a Qualifying run, with his first effort halted by a red flag after Franco Colapinto crashed, while he suffered an oversteer moment on his second flying lap. ‘Toughest battle I’ve had psychologically’ – Russell opens up on title fight struggles ahead of Hungarian GP Antonelli struggled to put a flying lap together in FP2 after missing the day's first session Despite the setbacks, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord was confident the team would be in the mix come Qualifying tomorrow as they look to continue a 100% pole record in Grands Prix this season. "We hope we can fight for pole, we've been competitive at every type of circuit this year," he said. "I know there's a certain narrative that certain circuits favour us and others will favour them. "We've seen generally other teams swing back and forth a reasonable amount but I think we've been pretty consistently fighting up there, at the front and able to compete for pole at every race, so that has to be our target for tomorrow." Europe Romania Shoots Down Drone That Breached Its Airspace Two Romanian Air Force F-16 aircraft and two Italian Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft were scrambled to monitor the drone incursion. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print A Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down a drone that breached Romania's airspace on July 24. U.S. Air Force/Senior Airman Christopher Campbell Timothy Frudd 7/24/2026 | Updated: 7/24/2026 0:00 X 1 A Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down a drone that breached the country’s airspace on July 24, marking the first time Romania has done so despite dozens of previous airspace incursions. The Romanian Defense Ministry said its radar surveillance system “detected an aerial target” on Friday morning about 12 miles east of Sulina, a town in Tulcea County, Northern Dobruja, Romania. It said the target, which was later identified as a drone, penetrated the country’s airspace. The drone incursion follows a series of violations of Romanian airspace, including a drone crash in May that left two people injured in an apartment building. There have been repeated breaches of airspace on NATO’s eastern flank during the war between Russia and Ukraine. In response to Friday’s drone incursion, two Romanian Air Force F-16 aircraft assigned to the 86th Air Base and two Italian Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, deployed to the 57th Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base, were scrambled to monitor the situation. The two Italian fighter jets had been on NATO Air Policing duty prior to the incident, according to the defense ministry. The Romanian Defense Ministry confirmed that one of the F-16 fighter jets engaged the drone with an air-to-air missile and shot it down over an unpopulated area near Padina, Buzau County. Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said Friday was the first time a drone had been intercepted and destroyed in Romanian airspace. Related Stories Allies to Reinforce Air Defenses Along NATO Eastern Flank After Russian Drone Incident, Says Romania Day in Photos: Russian Drone Explodes in Romania, Bogota Metro Test Run, and Israeli Strike in Lebanon “This morning, around 11:00 a.m., a Romanian pilot in an F-16 aircraft shot down a drone that had entered our country’s airspace,” Romanian President Nicusor Dan said in a statement posted on X on July 24. “The area was uninhabited, so the pilot was able to fire without any risk involved. Currently, teams from institutions with relevant responsibilities are investigating the area to provide all the details about the incident.” Toiu credited the successful downing of the drone to the dedication of the F-16 pilot, the quick response of the Romanian military, and close coordination with the Italian Eurofighter aircraft. “This multinational combined effort underlines how NATO is ready and able to react to any potential air threats, 24/7, to safeguard our territory and protect our people,” NATO’s Allied Air Command said in a statement following the incident on July 24. The command said an investigation was launched after the drone was shot down. It also noted that the downing of the drone came as Romania, NATO, and other nations had been actively obtaining ground-based interceptors to strengthen defense capabilities. In a statement on social media, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Friday’s drone incursion marked another violation of the eastern part of European airspace. “I commend the Romanian military for their swift and effective response, safeguarding our shared security,” she said. “Strengthening defence and deterrence along our Eastern border remains a top priority.” Gen. Gheorghita Vlad, the Romanian army’s chief of staff, said on Friday that Romania had not yet identified the origin and purpose of the drone. He indicated that the drone appeared to be a recognized type of attack drone but said it was too soon to form conclusions. “Visually, the pilots reported the drone looked to be a Shahed type,” he said. The Shahed attack drones, which were designed by Iran, have been repeatedly used by Russia during its war with Ukraine. In May, the Romanian Defense Ministry said a Russian drone entered Romania’s airspace and crashed into an apartment building. Two people were injured in the drone crash. The defense ministry said the incident occurred while Russia was launching drone attacks on infrastructure and civilian targets in Ukraine near the Romanian border. In June, the Romanian government confirmed that its allies were prepared to help the country reinforce air defenses along the eastern flank of NATO. Toiu said the Russian drone incursion in May accelerated efforts to strengthen the country’s defenses. “Our top priority is to ​increase capabilities,” Toiu said. She added, “There is a common understanding that we need to strengthen the eastern flank, not just in Romania. This is a conversation we’re having with the Baltics and all countries on the eastern flank.” The leaders of NATO’s eastern member nations issued a joint statement in May highlighting the need to consolidate NATO’s air defenses against airspace violations. “Repeated airspace violations on the Eastern Flank underscore the urgent need to continue strengthening NATO’s air and missile defence, including against [unmanned aircraft system] threats,” the leaders said. The best seller among shotguns in the United States is the 12 gauge pump gun with a 30-in. full-choke barrel. It is what the customers demand and, naturally, what the manufacturers supply. Such a gun is all right for deliberate pass-shooting at ducks at from 45 to 60 yd. And when fixed up with a special straight stock and ventilated rib, it is also a fine weapon for trapshooting. But pass-shooting at ducks and trap shooting account for perhaps 10 percent of the shotgun shells expended annually in the U. S. The humble cottontail, which is usually found in the brush at ranges of around 20 or 25 yd.—and which zigs and zags through the cover like a mad thing—is the No. 1 shotgun target in this country. Then there are the bobwhite and several sorts of Western quail, John Pheasant, woodcock, grouse of various kinds, and what not. Even decoyed ducks are generally taken at from 25 to 35 yd.—and for that shooting the hunter needs a full-choke gun with 30-in. barrels about as much as he needs a 10-ton truck to take Susie to the movies. Then by accident I made a discovery. I had got my brand-new bride a little 20 gauge Ithaca double with 26-in. barrels. Came a day when she wasn’t feeling right pert. The vagrant notion to try her gun came over me, so I laced on a recoil pad to lengthen the stock and went out to a brushy spot where I knew several large coveys of quail hung out. In fact, I’d been bombarding them with my Model 12 Winchester pump , and its full-choke 30-in. barrel had little effect on them. To my astonishment I found I could hit them quite neatly with the 20. I could get on them before they ducked behind a bush, follow them and cut them down when they tried to zig. I made one run of five straight, something I’d never done before in my life. The larger the gauge, of course, the more a barrel can be opened up. A modified 12 gauge puts as many shot pellets into a 30-in. circle at 40 yd. as a full-choke 20, and a 12 patterning 40 percent (about Skeet No. 1) throws 1 1/4 oz. of shot into as dense a pattern as a 20 gauge bored modified does with 1 oz. of shot. The common belief that a 20 gauge throws a smaller pattern than a 12 of the same boring is erroneous. The 20 simply throws a thinner pattern. We are a logical people—we think. We shake our heads in astonishment when told that the Hindus starve for protein while India is overrun by sacred cows. We chuckle at the quaint superstitions of the Navajo and Apache Indians, who refuse to eat wild turkey or trout. Yet we arm ourselves with smoothbores which, for 90 percent of our shooting, handicap us almost as much as if we went into the uplands with a 20-lb. weight tied to each foot. How come? Why this strange fixation on long-barreled, slow-handling, full-choke guns? Outdoor Li The average gunner is still sold on the ancient myth — a hangover from black-powder days—that the longer the barrel the “harder” a gun shoots. I get a stream of letters telling me about the marvelous ranging qualities of some fantastic old cannon or other, one with a 36 to 40-in. barrel, and described as the hardest-shooting gun in the community, capable of killing single ducks at 125 yd. Actually the standard 12 gauge load —3 3/4 drams of powder and 1 1/8 oz. of shot—reaches maximum velocity in a 30-in. barrel. The maximum loads— containing 3 1/4 drams of progressive burning powder and 1 1/4 oz. of shot— reach maximum velocity in a 32-in. barrel. But (and here’s the catch) velocity loss when a barrel is cut below maximum is only 6 ½ to 7 1/2 foot seconds for each inch amputated. The difference, then, between the velocity delivered by a clumsy, slow-handling 30-in. barrel and that of a fast-handling 26-in. barrel is only about 30 foot seconds—and there’s that much difference among shells from the same box fired in the same gun. A man could use a 30-in. barrel and a 26-in. barrel alternately until the cows came home and never discern any difference in killing power, penetration, or necessary lead. Another myth that needs exploding is the commonly held belief that a long barrel will pattern better than a short one. Within practical limits barrel length has nothing whatsoever to do with pattern. Pattern is determined by the degree of constriction (choke) at the muzzle and by the construction of the shot shell itself. I have patterned many a gun with a 26-in. barrel that gave patterns running 75 percent or better. There is nothing wrong with the long barrel for pass-shooting at waterfowl or for flight-shooting of doves. The long barrel tends to steady the swing and give more precise aim. However, the gun with the shorter barrel will do about as well if it is properly stocked and balanced. The momentum of the long-barreled, muzzle-heavy gun deters a man from slowing or stopping his swing prematurely, and probably that is its greatest virtue. But despite the virtues of the longbarreled gun for special purposes (and even these are open to argument) it is a pretty sad instrument for most shooting. On the duck flyway the gunner sees his bird coming a long way off. He has time to make a mental calculation as to lead, to track his target, pass it with the gun swinging, and fire. The trapshooter knows where his bird is coming from. He has his gun mounted at his shoulder, his cheek on the comb. He has only to swing up with his target, get ahead of it, and shoot with the gun swinging. On the other hand, the upland gunner usually doesn’t know exactly where his bird is coming from. He has to get on it fast and shoot fast. When a cock pheasant comes thrashing out of the brush behind him and heads for the trees, he has to get on it—now. He must be able to make a lightning-fast change of direction when a quail starts to curve around the tree or when a cottontail zigzags from one brush pile to another. For work of this sort the long-barreled gun is sluggish, unwieldy, and much too slow. Outdoor Life I grew up with such cannons. One of my first shotguns was a Winchester Model 97 pump with a 32-in. full-choke barrel. I was a rifle nut and I shot this ponderous old blunderbuss like a rifle. Give me plenty of time and something was liable to get hit. Doves flying innocently to roost or water, or ducks flying incautiously low, were my meat. But quail were something else. Where there was no brush and I could take my own sweet time, I wasn’t too bad. Complicate matters with some brush and trees, though, and I was sunk. I decided that for some mysterious reason I was just naturally attuned to doves and ducks, but that quail had my number. Then a great light dawned upon me. Presently I discovered a sucker who had a 20 gauge L.C. Smith that weighed about 6 pounds. He told me he couldn’t hit anything with it because 20 gauge guns aren’t powerful enough—that it didn’t shoot hard because the barrels were too short. What he was looking for, he said, was a good old 12 gauge with a 30-in. fullchoke barrel. Trying to keep my eager voice from trembling, I asked him if he would swap for my 12 gauge pump and give me 10 bucks to boot. He would. I grabbed the 20 gauge and the sawbuck and ran. ( He couldn’t hit anything with the 12 gauge either. He simply could not shoot, but I didn’t tell him that.) I’ve found it exceedingly important, in any upland hunting I’ve ever done, to have a fairly light gun. It’s also important that it be rather short of barrel, for a light, short gun handles fast. I know of nothing that weighs more than an extra pound—or even half a pound— in a shotgun. I have a fine pair of Winchester Model 21 doubles—a 12 gauge and a 16. Each has 26-in. barrels and stocks are exactly the same. The 12 weighs 7.2 lb.; the 16, 7 lb. The 16 seems much lighter than the 12. I often ask visitors to heft the two guns and estimate the difference in weight. Guesses run from 1 to 3 lb. The duck hunter can sit in his blind and wait for the ducks to come into the decoys. Trap and skeet shooters have only to lug their guns from the clubhouse to the firing line. The upland gunner, though, must carry his shotgun many miles in the course of a hunt. When I hunted desert quail in Arizona, I’d walk from 10 to 20 miles during the day. A grouse shooter from New England tells me he probably walks 3 miles for every shot he gets at a ruffed grouse. In Idaho and Washington I have on occasion shot the limit of three cock pheasants after walking only a few hundred yards, but far more often I’ve climbed and walked for miles. The heavier the gun, the wearier the hunter. For upland hunting that requires a lot of hiking a gun weighing 7.2 lb. is about as much as anyone should carry. One of 7 lb. is better, and he who latches onto a 6-lb. gun is lucky —if the gun throws enough shot and if he’s used to it. The short-barreled gun is livelier, faster-handling, and quicker-pointing than the long-barreled one. To me a double with 26-in. barrels is exactly right. The weight is between the hands and the gun comes up fast. For upland hunting even a pair of 28-in. barrels on a double seems a bit sluggish. I do most of my skeet shooting with a Remington Model 11-48 automatic with ventilated rib and a 26-in. barrel. It swings smoothly and beautifully, and I can break two or three more targets out of each 100 (or so I tell myself) than I can with any double. But the skeet shot knows when his bird is coming out, where it is going. Before he shoots, his feet are in position. And before he calls for the target, he does about 75 percent of the job of mounting his gun. The overall length of my 11-48 is just under 46 inches, while the overall length of my doubles is 43. For upland shooting, that fine Remington has just 3 in. too much barrel on it. For most field shooting I can do about as well with it as I can with a double, but on the tough snapshots—when a quail is zipping behind a bush or a big rooster is about to get over a ridge— I’m a little behind with it. With the shorter, handier double I’d have my bird centered. The difference lies, of course, in the receiver of the automatic, something which the double does not have. Stick a barrel of even moderate length on the end of a long receiver and your gun is overlong. For another Remington automatic, a little 20 gauge, I have two barrels—one 26 in. long and bored for skeet, the other 28 in. and bored modified. I’m going to have a variable-choke device put on the modified barrel to give an overall length of 23 in. Then I’ll really have an upland gun. A short barrel often has a good deal of muzzle blast. The hunter next to it in a duck blind wouldn’t love the man shooting it, and at traps the shooters to the right and left would cry out bitterly. But that is no skin off the nose of the upland gunner, who does not shoot cheek by jowl with anyone else. How should the upland gun be bored? That depends. The man who hunts grouse in heavy timber or bobwhite quail in the brush or follows the elusive cottontail—that man needs as wide a pattern as he can get. Skeet boring, which will usually cover from 28 to 32 in. at 25 yd., is about right for fast, short-range shooting. It’s also good for anyone with enough self-control not to shoot at over 30 yd. or so. It is no good at all for the man who shoots at everything that gets up, because beyond 30 yd. a lot of birds will get away wounded, even though they’ve been fairly centered. Read Next: Best Over/Under Shotguns Outdoor Life It is routine to recommend improved cylinder boring for upland game, but the term covers a multitude of patterns. To one manufacturer, an improved-cylinder barrel is one that patterns 35-40 percent. To another it’s one that patterns 50 percent. With the new shells with wadless crimps and gasproof overpowder wads, many guns marked improved cylinder pattern from 55 to 65 and sometimes 70 percent. As a rule, guns bored improved cylinder on the continent but used with the latest American ammunition won’t miss modified patterns by much. Read Next: Best Shotguns for Bird Hunting One American improved-cylinder gun patterns consistently from 50 to 55 percent; another covers as much area at 25 yd. as its maker’s Skeet No. 1 barrels. But at short ranges this particular improved cylinder throws a pattern with a denser center that carries out farther and gives clean kills at ranges where the Skeet No. 1 boring would only feather. The sloppy gun pointer in the uplands should use a wide-open bore and not shoot beyond its range. The sharp gun pointer can use more constriction and tighter, smaller patterns. Probably the ideal, all-round upland boring is one that gives 50 percent patterns at 40 yd. It’s easier to hit with such patterns at short ranges than with full-choke patterns, yet they’ll reach out and kill to 40 yd.—which is long range in the uplands. This 50 percent pattern is called quarter choke because in a 12 gauge it is often reached with a constriction of only 10 points (.010 in.), whereas in the old days 40 points’ constriction was considered necessary for full-choke performance. Very often this ideal 50 percent pattern is reached with barrels marked improved cylinder, sometimes with barrels marked modified. Actually, it is about the best all-round boring for the sporadic shooter, since most gunners do not have the skill to hit regularly at over 40 yd. anyway. For my part, I do more shooting with a double-gun bored modified and improved modified (60 and 68 percent) than with anything else. I like to reach out and knock down the occasional wild pheasant that runs ahead of a dog and gets up at 35 or 40 yd. Modified will nail them! Actually, though, 90 percent of all upland game is killed within 30 yd., and for that you want skeet or improved-cylinder boring. The 12 gauge gun tends to be a bit on the heavy side to be ideal for upland shooting, even if it’s a modern repeater with light alloy steel and dural receiver. My Remington Model 11-48 skeet gun weighs 7 3/4 lb., for example. A Remington Model 870 pump-action skeet gun in the rack weighs slightly less, 7 /12 lb., which is what my 12 gauge Winchester Model 21 double weighs. A Remington Model 11-48 skeet gun in 20 gauge with ventilated rib and 26-in. barrel weighs 7 lb. on the button. The 20 gauge, on the other hand, is a weapon only for the expert upland gunner, since it cannot be opened up quite as much as the larger gauges and requires sharper pointing. Bored quarter choke and improved modified, or even modified and full, it is a delightful and deadly weapon with 1 oz. of shot. I have a low-down, sneaking hunch that the queen of the upland guns is the 16 gauge, the gun that performs like a 12 and kicks and carries like a 20. About as near a thing to an ideal allround gun that I can imagine is a 7lb. 16 gauge bored quarter choke and modified—or, if a man is a pretty sharp pointer, even modified and full. Don’t let anyone tell you that a 16 bored modified is much behind a modified 12 in range; it isn’t. I have killed many pheasants at 45 yd. with a modified 16— and they didn’t move an inch when they hit the ground. I have killed plenty of ducks at 50-55 yd. with full-choke 16’s. The last two roosters I shot were a double. Four came boiling out of a brushy draw. I made a right and a left and the birds fell 43 and 48 yd. from the gun. The .410 and 28 gauges are like the 20, but more so; they simply cannot be opened up enough. I have shot a lot of grouse with a .410 and I have broken some pretty fair skeet scores with a 28, but neither is an ideal upland gun by any means. Admiral was nominated this week to serve as the next leader of U.S. Army Europe and Africa. (Anthony Heatley/U.S. Army) By JOHN VANDIVER STARS AND STRIPES Published July 24, 2026 · STUTTGART, Germany — Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral was nominated this week to serve as the next leader of U.S. Army Europe and Africa. Admiral, whose nomination was announced Thursday by the Pentagon, would also serve as the leader of NATO land forces in Europe. He currently serves as the commander of III Corps and Fort Hood in Texas. The nomination called for Admiral’s reappointment to the rank of lieutenant general in line with the Pentagon’s decision to downgrade USAREUR-AF’s headquarters to a three-star command . Prior to leading III Corps, Admiral served as the Army’s director of force management and before that commanded the 3rd Cavalry Regiment. The Army’s mission in Europe has been in transition since the departure of Gen. Christopher Donahue , who relinquished command earlier this month. Widely regarded as one of the Army’s most innovative leaders, Donahue put in his retirement papers in June. His exit became a point of contention, with backers saying he was forced into retirement by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The Defense Department never publicly addressed the circumstances surrounding Donahue’s retirement. If confirmed, Admiral will come to the job with experience commanding at numerous levels. He also will lead at a time when the Army’s mission in Europe is adapting as the Pentagon adjusts force levels on the Continent. Among the recent moves was the Pentagon’s decision to cancel the deployment of a Fort Hood-based armored brigade to Poland. At the same time, the Pentagon and Polish leaders have been in talks about increasing U.S. troop presence in that country in other ways. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has said it will reduce its troop presence in Germany by about 5,000, but it hasn’t fully detailed how that will be accomplished. Army Europe John Vandiver covers U.S. military activities across Europe and Africa. Based in Stuttgart, Germany, he previously worked for newspapers in New Jersey, North Carolina and Maryland. He is a graduate of the University of Delaware. Vatican Weighs Papal Trip to Ukraine The Holy See’s foreign minister said it is evaluating the timing and conditions for a possible visit to the country by Pope Leo XIV. Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, the Holy See’s secretary for relations with states and international organizations, meets with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on July 20, 2026. (photo: Embassy of Ukraine to the Holy See) Victoria Cardiel/ACI Prensa/EWTN News Vatican July 24, 2026 The Vatican will study the conditions needed for a possible trip by Pope Leo XIV to Ukraine, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher said following a six-day pastoral and diplomatic mission to the war-torn country. Archbishop Gallagher, the Holy See’s secretary for relations with states and international organizations, said the possibility of a papal visit was among the questions he heard most frequently during his stay. “Almost everyone I met asked me that question. My answer is very simple. The Holy Father takes this invitation very seriously,” Archbishop Gallagher told Vatican Media in Kraków, Poland, before returning to Rome. “For our part, we will continue to study the conditions necessary to determine the right time and the most appropriate way for such a visit to bear the greatest possible fruit for Ukraine and for peace in the world,” he said. Archbishop Gallagher spent six days in Ukraine, which has been at war since 2014 and has endured Russia’s full-scale invasion since February 2022. He held political, institutional and Church meetings and took part in several pastoral events. He met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on July 20. Zelenskyy expressed gratitude for the Holy See’s continuing support for Ukraine amid the war with Russia. The principal purpose of Archbishop Gallagher’s visit was to participate in celebrations marking the 35th anniversary of the restoration of the Latin Catholic Church’s structures at the Marian shrine of Berdychiv. Thousands of faithful attended the celebrations July 19. Archbishop Gallagher said Ukrainian authorities had expressed appreciation for the Holy See’s support. “In our meetings with the authorities, we encountered profound gratitude for the Holy Father’s appeals and his words, and that is a source of encouragement for us,” he said. “They feel supported by the closeness shown first by Pope Francis and now by Pope Leo. This encourages the Holy See to renew its commitment to dialogue with the international community and with the Russian authorities, and to continue its humanitarian efforts, such as the mission entrusted to Cardinal Matteo Maria Zuppi, who continues working for the return of children, prisoners and civilians.” Pope Leo XIV has received several official invitations to visit Ukraine. Zelenskyy renewed the invitation during a conversation with the Pope on Good Friday. During that exchange, Pope Leo expressed his closeness to the Ukrainian people amid the suffering caused by the war and emphasized the urgency of ensuring humanitarian assistance. He also expressed his hope for an end to hostilities and a just and lasting peace with Russia. A Just and Lasting Peace Asked about the prospects for a ceasefire, Archbishop Gallagher said he had seen a strong willingness on the Ukrainian side to work toward that goal. “During these days I have seen a strong determination on the Ukrainian side to work towards that goal. It is difficult for me to say whether this can be achieved in the immediate future, but we must continue to work in that direction,” he said. “At the same time, as we saw at the shrine of Berdychiv — and as the history of this remarkable place of Marian devotion reminds us, renowned for many reported healings — we should never rule out the possibility of a miracle.” Archbishop Gallagher also reflected on what he had witnessed during the mission. “For me, this has been a profoundly positive experience. Beyond the logistical effort and the long journey required to reach Ukraine, it has allowed me to touch the reality of today’s world with my own hands,” he said. “We must remember that not everyone lives as we do in Italy or in my native England. There is a dark and troubling reality in our world today. We must not give in. In our own way, we too are called to strive, doing our part with the means available to us, in order to build peace.” Cardinal Zuppi’s Humanitarian Mission Archbishop Gallagher’s visit followed Cardinal Matteo Maria Zuppi’s second mission to Ukraine as Pope Leo XIV’s special envoy. The archbishop of Bologna completed four days of meetings in Lviv and Kyiv focused on prisoner exchanges, the return of Ukrainian children taken to Russia, and the delivery of humanitarian assistance. Cardinal Zuppi met civil and religious authorities, officials responsible for prisoner exchanges and relatives of military personnel and civilians being held in Russia. Among his principal meetings was an encounter with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, who thanked the Holy See for its humanitarian efforts and requested its support in achieving a comprehensive and lasting peace. Sybiha also raised Kyiv’s concerns about civilians detained in Russian territory and called for a humanitarian corridor to assist thousands of people in the Russian-occupied communities of Oleshky and Hola Prystan in the Kherson region. Prisoners were a central focus of the mission. Proposals discussed included a possible comprehensive exchange of prisoners of war, continued efforts to locate missing people, and measures to facilitate the return of civilians. The parties also discussed the situation of Ukrainian children taken illegally to Russia, an issue in which the Holy See has been involved for years through diplomatic and humanitarian initiatives. Another topic was the protection of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has recently been damaged amid attacks connected to the war. Ukrainian authorities consider its preservation and restoration a priority. This story was first published by ACI Prensa, the Spanish-language sister service of EWTN News. It has been translated and adapted by EWTN News English. https://brooklyneagle.com/404797/estonia.text: Estonian pleads guilty to selling electronics to Russia DOWNTOWN BROOKLYN – AN ESTONIAN MAN admitted in Brooklyn federal court on Thursday to his role in a scheme to illegally export over $1 million in sensitive electronic components to Russia, according to Joseph Nocella Jr., U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York. Andrey Shevlyakov pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit export violations, faces up to 40 years’ imprisonment, and will forfeit $1.5 million to the government. Shevlyakov had been added to a list of persons prohibited from acquiring items from the U.S. without the Department of Commerce’s permission. Using shell companies, Shevlyakov deceived suppliers and bought sensitive technology anyway. He then shipped the goods – including components used in communications, avionics, missiles and electronic warfare systems – to Russian defense contractors and government agencies. In one instance, Shevlyakov placed an order with a U.S. company for sensitive electronic components, but the company refused to sell to him. Shevlyakov then canceled his order, only to place it again days later under a false name. Shevlyakov was also involved in making deliveries, crossing from Estonia into Russia over 100 times between 2010 and 2016, according to border records. Additionally, Finnish border authorities once caught him with €70,000 worth of electronics hidden in his vehicle, the U.S. attorney’s office said. ✰✰✰ Subscribe to Continue Reading Sign In Explore https://www.planetf1.com/news/fia-max-ve.text: Max Verstappen has had a few skirmishes with the FIA over the course of his F1 career The FIA has confirmed that Red Bull driver Max Verstappen will face no further action after an incident with Williams’ Carlos Sainz in practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix. Verstappen was summoned to the stewards on Friday following an incident with Sainz in the early stages of FP1. Max Verstappen escapes FIA action after Carlos Sainz investigation Want more PlanetF1.com coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google for news you can trust Verstappen encountered a slow-moving Sainz on the approach to Turn 12, forcing the Red Bull driver to abandon a lap. He then appeared to retaliate by deliberately slowing on the exit of the corner to the Turn 13 hairpin, obstructing Sainz and the Audi of Gabriel Bortoleto. Verstappen found himself under investigation for erratic driving, requiring the four-time world champion to visit the stewards after FP1. Max Verstappen vs Isack Hadjar: Red Bull head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying records between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates With Sainz insisting that he was ‘not in any way affected’ by Verstappen slowing down on the exit of Turn 12, however, the stewards opted against taking further action. The stewards’ report read: “The Stewards heard from the drivers of Car 3 (Max Verstappen) and Car 55 (Carlos Sainz) and the team representatives and reviewed video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. “On the approach to turn 12, Car 3 had to move off the racing line to avoid Car 55 which had slowed unexpectedly on the racing line. “The Driver of Car 3 then slowed significantly at turn 12 and gesticulated to the driver of Car 55 to mark his frustration that he had been impeded by Car 55. “The driver of Car 55 then overtook Car 3. “The driver of Car 55 said that he was not in any way affected by Car 3 slowing at turn 12. No other car was affected. “The Stewards therefore determined to take no further action.” As reported by PlanetF1.com , Sainz was given a warning for his role in the incident despite drawing attention to an issue with his team radio communications at the time. Verstappen remains without a victory in the F1 2026 season entering the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend. The 28-year-old has been limited to just three podium finishes this year, recording a best result of second place at Red Bull’s home race in Austria. Verstappen also finished third in Canada and Belgium. Although he is officially under contract until the end of the 2028 season, it is widely believed that a clause in his contract will allow him to leave Red Bull if he is lower than second in the drivers’ standings at the summer break. Verstappen currently sits seventh, trailing second-placed Lewis Hamilton by 68 points with just 25 available in Hungary, the final race before the August shutdown. PlanetF1.com revealed last month that Verstappen is in advanced talks with McLaren over a move for 2027. However, it is unclear if he will commit to leaving his current team. https://www.planetf1.com/news/adrian-new.text: Adrian Newey observing in the Aston Martin garage Adrian Newey suggested that Lance Stroll ’s suspected rear suspension failure in Hungary was not related to the Aston Martin AMR26 upgrade package. Newey therefore described it as a “very unexpected” failure as Aston Martin begins its opening phase of developing the AMR26. Newey also confirmed that Honda is investigating the cause of vibrations, which were reported by Fernando Alonso, and could be seen on the data. In terms of pace, there were encouraging signs for Aston Martin. Adrian Newey addresses Stroll red flag and Honda review Want more PlanetF1.com coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust. There is a palpable buzz surrounding Aston Martin at the Hungaroring. At last, the team has sent its B-spec AMR26 into action. In terms of performance, it was a promising opening act. Alonso recorded a P13 finish in FP1. He slipped to 19th in the second hour of practice, but to be right in the mix with Cadillac remains a marked step forward. It was a more frustrating Friday on Lance Stroll’s side of the garage. Stroll triggered the red flags when he spun out of FP1. Aston Martin reported a suspected rear suspension failure. Stroll did not appear in FP2, as extensive work continued on his car. Adrian Newey, Aston Martin team principal and design chief, addressed the situation in Friday’s team leaders’ press conference. The area of failure in question was not a part of Aston Martin’s 16-piece upgrade, Newey confirmed. “Everybody is feverishly trying to understand exactly what went wrong and what happened as we speak, and it’s only once we have an understanding that we can comment on what we do next,” Newey told PlanetF1.com and others. “The area involved was actually not being changed. We are short on spares because the cladding and so forth is different. So there are some minor changes in that area. In that sense it was very unexpected. “As I say, until we have an understanding, it’s difficult to comment further.” Newey was also quizzed on a couple of Alonso team radio snippets. Alonso was urged to stay away from the kerbs before Stroll’s incident. Alonso also flagged up engine vibrations down the main straight at one stage in FP1. Newey explained both situations, confirming that Honda has launched an investigation into Alonso’s report. “So the first question, staying away from the kerbs, that’s purely because we are acquiring aero data,” said Newey. “When you’re trying to acquire aero data, you don’t want the disruption of kerbs thrown in, the inconsistency that corrupts the data. “The oscillations, yes, that’s really a question for Honda. They can see it on the data, and they are working on the solution.” More on Aston Martin from PlanetF1.com Aston Martin confirms ‘different direction’ as $1million question answered Upgraded Honda engine set to debut in Hungaroring run Teething issues are inevitable with such a substantial development package. Honda will soon throw its hat in the ring. As reported by PlanetF1.com on Thursday, Honda is set to debut its upgraded engine in a Hungaroring filming day, during the week following the Hungarian Grand Prix. The engine is due to be bolted into the AMR26 at the Dutch Grand Prix. Additional reporting by Thomas Maher Want to be the first to know exclusive information from the F1 paddock?
