https://www.ynetnews.com/article/sygwhsm.text: The case involving the smuggling of weapons from Ukraine, which were seized in November 2025 in a truck at the border crossing between Moldova and Romania, continues to widen and may now involve a rabbi. According to reports in Moldovan and Russian media, based mainly on a court ruling published as part of the legal proceedings, the name of Rabbi Pinhas Zaltzman, who presents himself as the chief rabbi of Moldova, was mentioned several times in testimony and investigative materials. However, the ruling does not determine that Zaltzman committed any offense, and he strongly denies any connection to the case. The affair began in November 2025, when Romanian customs authorities stopped a truck that had arrived from Moldova carrying advanced weapons, including anti-tank and anti-aircraft systems, RPG launchers and drone parts. The driver said then that “the destination of the shipment is Israel,” raising questions. Now, after the publication of parts of the ruling in the case of one of the defendants, it has emerged that one of those involved, Alexei Piankovsky, claimed in his interrogation that Zaltzman had asked him to transfer equipment from Ukraine to Moldova and later to Israel. According to Piankovsky’s testimony, Zaltzman described the items as “leftovers” from humanitarian equipment or as medical equipment intended for repair, not as weapons. The ruling noted that in mobile phones seized as part of the investigation, investigators found conversations between some of the defendants and Zaltzman, as well as photos of weapons and photos from his phone. Here too, the document does not determine the meaning of the findings and does not attribute criminal responsibility to him. The spokesman for Moldova’s Prosecutor’s Office for Combating Organized Crime refused to confirm or deny whether Zaltzman has any status in the case, saying only that “the investigation continues against several people whose identities are not being disclosed at this stage.” Alongside the legal reports, sources in Moldova’s Jewish community claimed that Zaltzman himself has not been seen in the country for many months. According to them, his last visit was in October 2025, and he has not returned to Moldova since, including during Hanukkah, Purim and Passover. The same sources also claimed that the Jewish community recently appointed Rabbi Menachem Mendel Axelrod as chief rabbi of Moldova. Zaltzman himself rejected the claims outright, saying he remains the chief rabbi of Moldova. “This is an old affair, with which I have no connection whatsoever," he told ynet. "Among the people quoted in the article is a Jewish criminal who sometimes came to pray at the synagogue. The attempt to drag my name into the incident is ridiculous and has no connection to reality. As part of my activities in recent years, I have had the privilege of greatly assisting tens of thousands of Jews, whether refugees from Ukraine or any refugee who needed help, regardless of origin or background. “In this framework, I worked extensively in the field of assistance, without any compensation and in accordance with the law,” Zaltzman continued. “The attempt, from the beginning, to turn this activity of mine into an attempt to smuggle weapons is a cynical exploitation by marginal political elements within the Jewish community, in place of an open-door policy of assistance to every Jew. There are countless witnesses who can testify to that. I am sorry that such a marginal, biased and false publication is being echoed in the Israeli press. All my life I have acted according to the law and out of a sense of mission to save Jews, and I will continue to do so.” The case continues to be handled in courts in Moldova and Romania. Some of the defendants have been released from custody, one admitted to the charges against him and was sentenced to a suspended prison term, and the investigation into additional suspects is still ongoing. According to Moldova’s Jewish community, Zaltzman is not the chief rabbi and is attributing to himself a role that is not his. “He was never elected or appointed to this position by the authorized bodies. He has no mandate to represent the community. The role he attributed to himself does not correspond to a position that has been recognized or approved institutionally and does not reflect the administrative structure of the organization’s leadership,” according to a statement issued by the community. In November 2025, Romanian customs authorities arrested a Moldovan citizen who was transporting in his truck an arsenal of heavy weapons, including anti-aircraft missile systems, anti-tank rockets and components for suicide drones. The driver declared at the time that the shipment was bound for Israel, but the shipping details have raised many doubts among politicians in Moldova, who believe the weapons came from Ukraine as part of a global smuggling chain.

https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/.text: Romania says it shot down another Russian drone in its airspace July 26 (UPI) -- Romania said Sunday it shot down a Russian drone over its territorial waters in the Black Sea, marking the the third such incident in a week and prompting the NATO member to summon Russia's ambassador. Defense Minister Radu Miruța said a Romanian Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcon aircraft shot down a drone that had penetrated into Romanian airspace near the delta of the River Danube in the Black Sea. The drone was first detected by radar outside Romanian airspace before continuing without authorization to a point above Sulina, Romania, Miruta said in a statement . Five minutes later at 10:13 a.m. it was shot down over the water. "Romania's safety is not defended with slogans. Congratulations to the pilots and ground support teams!" he said. "Each such incident confirms that Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine continues to generate risks beyond Ukrainian borders." Foreign Minister Oana Toiu added that Bucharest has summoned the Russian ambassador and will weigh whether to lodge a diplomatic protest over the trio of recent incidents. An initial investigation has revealed that a drone shot down on Friday "is of the Shahed type, used by the Russian Federation in the war of aggression against Ukraine," Toiu said . "It is inadmissible and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romania's airspace, which is, at the same time, NATO airspace and European Union airspace. "Such actions are unacceptable, and we treat them with the utmost seriousness, alongside our allies," she said. Romanian President Nicușor Dan similarly congratulated the pilots who carried out the missions and criticized Moscow for its "continued violation" of Romanian airspace. Prior to Sunday's latest incident, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha urged allies to craft a "comprehensive deterrence package" against Russia over its violations of Romanian airspace, calling them "a clear demonstration of the Kremlin's complete disregard for international law, national sovereignty, and European security. "The response must match the scale of the threat," he said . "We need a comprehensive deterrence package for Ukraine and Europe: stronger sanctions, maximum pressure on Russia, and a joint effort to shield Europe's skies from Russian terror." https://www.thedailybeast.com/putin-melt.text: World Putin Melts Down in Front of Stunned Sailors After Canceling Parade TALK THERAPY The Russian leader’s show of strength comes as his carefully managed image increasingly crumbles. Wiktoria Gucia Reporter Updated Jul. 26 2026 4:56PM EDT / Published Jul. 26 2026 4:50PM EDT Comments Vladimir Putin scrapped Russia’s Navy Day parade over fears of Ukrainian strikes and then raged to a group of sailors about a revenge fantasy and Soviet dictator Josef Stalin. After canceling the parade—which was set to feature around 200 warships sailing along the Neva River in St. Petersburg—the president opted for a televised meeting with Navy personnel. In an apparent bid to save face, he angrily predicted that Ukraine would ultimately fall apart, claiming that Russia had actually been the only “guarantor” of Ukraine’s “territorial integrity.” Apart from the eastern regions of Ukraine that Moscow has tried to claim as its own, Putin declared the western regions “a gift from Stalin” and claimed they would “sooner or later” return to Hungary, Romania, and Poland. The 73-year-old leader sounded somewhat defeated as he admitted that such a “return” would not happen immediately, suggesting it could take “a year, or two, or maybe even ten or fifteen” before everything would “historically fall into place.” Russian President Vladimir Putin visits the Main Admiralty to meet with commanders on Navy Day in Saint Petersburg, Russia, July 26, 2026. Vyacheslav Prokofyev/via REUTERS The claims about Ukraine’s western regions are a recurring part of the Kremlin’s bogus historical narrative that Putin has repeatedly used to try and justify his war. The move came as Putin’s war faces a growing backlash at home, with a months-long Ukrainian drone campaign targeting Russian oil infrastructure crippling parts of the country’s refining capacity, worsening fuel shortages, and stoking frustration among some of the Kremlin’s most loyal supporters. Putin Gets Spectacularly Ambushed After Leaving His Bunker DANGER ZONE Allison Quinn In a separate video address recorded from the safety of his office, Putin told sailors that Russia’s “naval forces are capable of effectively accomplishing the full range of tasks assigned to them.” The Russian leader also sought to project strength toward the West, boasting that the navy was “constantly developing,” including its nuclear strike capabilities. Putin’s display of confidence before Navy personnel, some of whom appeared less than convinced by his remarks, came just days after an uncomfortable public setback in which Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev used a meeting meant to highlight Russia-Kazakh ties to publicly undermine the Kremlin leader. Putin Left Out in the Cold as Trump Gushes Over New BFF SAD FOR VLAD Leigh Kimmins In remarks broadcast by state-controlled media, Tokayev said he had been receiving signals from both Europe and the United States about the war and had already discussed them with Putin. He then delivered a striking assessment, saying that “the nature of this conflict is not entirely clear,” which appeared to leave the Russian president visibly uncomfortable. The meltdown also comes amid growing frustration inside Russia, where Ukrainian strikes on warehouses belonging to Wildberries—the country’s equivalent of Amazon—have sparked anger among small business sellers as their financial losses pile up. Many sellers have expressed their frustration online. @fliginskikh/ Instagram “We’re already getting screwed over from every direction as it is,” cosmetic brand founder Svetlana Dodo said in an Instagram video , saying she had lost around 1 million rubles—about $12,800—after Ukrainian strikes set warehouses ablaze, destroying billions of dollars’ worth of inventory. Last Sunday, Vladimir Solovyov, one of Putin’s most prominent television propagandists, began his evening program by acknowledging that “things are difficult.” Putin, in comments to Russian sailors on Sunday, appeared to try and dismiss the growing public outrage that has begun to seep out online, claiming that it’s “dangerous” to rely on information in “online communities” because there is too much “clutter.” Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed in a national address on Thursday that individuals close to Putin had contacted Kyiv and blamed the Russian leader personally for starting the war and the heavy losses Russia has suffered. https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2026/07.text: Menu Search Latest Profile English Contact | About | International Committee of the Fourth International ( ICFI ) Menu Search International Committee of the Fourth International ( ICFI ) Latest Profile Fourth International Socialist Equality Party IYSSE About the WSWS Contact Donate More than 375,000 people have been driven from their homes and holiday accommodation in France and Spain as the wildfires produced by Europe’s third heatwave of the summer sweep across a continent enduring what is the worst heatwave season ever recorded. The figure is climbing inexorably towards 400,000 with the city council of French city Bordeaux considering a “total evacuation if needed”. Smoke and flames rise as a wildfire advances near La Adrada, Ávila province, Spain, Friday, July 24, 2026 [AP Photo/Manu Fernandez] A heat dome over Europe has driven record temperatures in many countries. At the late-June peak, temperatures ran 14-18°C above normal across much of the continent. The heat has not relented since. As the latest fires took hold a temperature of 48.4 °C was recorded at Casteltermini in Sicily on July 18—the highest recorded temperature in Europe so far during this heatwave. On Thursday temperatures reached 44 °C across southeastern interior Spain and the Guadalquivir Valley. According to interior minister Laurent Nuñez, France saw what was “probably” the biggest peacetime civilian evacuation it has ever seen. Over the weekend authorities ordered the total clearance, by land and sea, of the Gironde region of the south west—one of the country’s main holiday destinations—and the port city of Bordeaux with a metropolitan population of 850,000 began drawing up plans for its own evacuation. By Sunday more than 220,000 people had been evacuated from the path of the main forest fire in southwest France as almost 98,000 hectares burned nationally, a record. The fire that began near Saumos in the Gironde on Wednesday generated its own weather, with Sébastien Berge, head of the Gironde firefighters’ union, saying his members were “overwhelmed” by a fire front stretching more than 20km. On Sunday, Nuñez said the fires “remained extremely violent, unpredictable” as they edged towards Bordeaux. Around 44,000 fled the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast, its only access road threatened by the flames, with boats ferrying hundreds off the piers. At Biscarrosse to the south, evacuees included a children’s summer camp and a care home for the elderly. Jean Mazodier, 86, evacuated from his forest home at dawn, told Le Monde : “Everything’s burned. It’s like losing a child.” By the weekend the fire had turned towards Bordeaux, with evacuation orders issued across a widening span of suburbs along with the city’s airport, as around 55,000 people were cleared from villages on the city’s approaches overnight. Mayor Thomas Cazenave said the fire was “at the gates of the metropolitan area” and the city council was studying scenarios up to a total evacuation. Sixty-eight firefighters had been injured tackling the fires in the south-west. More than 1,500 French soldiers and 1,700 additional security personnel have been deployed, with an A400M military transport plane joining water bombers. Sunday’s finale of the Tour de France in Paris was shortened after security forces were redeployed. President Emmanuel Macron activated the European Union’s civil protection mechanism, securing aircraft and personnel from Croatia, Portugal, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, with Germany sending helicopters and rescue teams. That the head of state of one of the world’s largest economies must appeal across the continent for aircraft in an emergency forecast for months is an admission that no capitalist government across Europe maintains the means to protect its population. Evacuees are housed at the Bordeaux Exhibition Centre in Bordeaux, France, after having to leave their homes outside town due to the raging wildfires, Sunday, July 26, 2026 [AP Photo/Caroline Blumberg] In Spain, a national emergency was declared Thursday over wildfires for the first time ever, with more than 90,000 people told to flee. Such a declaration has been made only once before, during the nationwide blackout of April 2025 . On Saturday evening the interior ministry said a man had been found dead in his car in a ravine near Valencia. Three firefighters have lost their lives; one in Italy and two in France. Two wind-driven fires in the Ávila and Madrid provinces merged into a single blaze, moving towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Oliva, around 50km west of the capital. In response, operational command transferred to the military’s emergency unit. Nearly 30,000 people were evacuated across the Madrid region, with further evacuations near Toledo and in Castellón in the east. Madrid’s regional emergency chief, Carlos Novillo, admitted that the fire was “at its peak and currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain”. Regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso called it “the worst wildfire in our region’s history.” El Mundo reported some 24,000 hectares burned in the Madrid region and 21,000 in Ávila. Spain, too, requested aircraft through the EU mechanism. In Italy, more than 40,000 hectares have burned nationally since the start of the year, an 81 percent increase on the recent average. Wildfires had been raging for days across Sicily, where temperatures topped 40C and gusts of hot wind fanned the flames. In midweek, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officials, with the help of water-bombing aircraft, were deployed on the island to at least 50 fires the regional head Renato Schifani said. The fires spread this weekend from Sicily to the mainland. On Sunday a large blaze on the Gargano promontory in Puglia reached the coast, with more than a thousand tourists evacuated from beaches by boat. In Sicily, civil protection again raised its highest fire alert for the provinces of Palermo and Trapani. In Greece, firefighters responded to 50 rural and forest fires across multiple regions in 24 hours. To Vima reported on Thursday that most were brought under control in their initial stages by ground crews and aerial units. The largest operations were at Zoniana, in the regional unit of Rethymno on Crete; Afidnes in Attica; Ano Kerasovo near Agrinio; Kalligata on the island of Kefalonia; Imero Pefko in Pikermi; and Perachora near Loutraki. Attica (containing the capital Athens), Evia and Rhodes were placed under a red-code alert for very high fire risk. The engulfing of much of southern Europe by forest fires, worse than any before, is the result of world governments’ failure to do what is needed to restrict carbon emissions and global heating, compounded by decades of defunded forestry and civil protection. It is not just in the hotter climates that fires have broken out, but also in the north from the UK to Norway. Britain, the sixth largest economy in the world, possesses no aerial firefighting capability of any kind. In the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland, a blaze burning since July 15 has required more than 500 firefighters to tackle it. Scottish National Party First Minister John Swinney has asked Andy Burnham’s UK Labour “government for military assistance in aerial support... and we await a response.” North Wales and the Upper Severn are the first parts of Britain to declare a drought, having received just 3 percent of its average July rainfall, with a fourth heatwave forecast for the coming week. An analysis published this week by the World Weather Attribution consortium found the evaporative conditions drying out the continent were made 80 times more likely by global heating in western Europe and 40 times more likely in the east. On Friday, World Health Organization Europe head Hans Henri P. Kluge warned, “As climate change drives a warming world, we need to prepare for more frequent and intense wildfires.” Since 2022, the number of wildfires has risen by 57 percent across the WHO European Region. Portugal and Spain have suffered a 100 percent increase in wildfires this year compared with 2025. According to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), last year alone, around 2.2 million hectares burned, while 254,388 hectares had already been destroyed by July 22 this year. In the days since, the destruction has significantly worsened. France, with Paris playing a central role, is the most visited country in the world receiving more than 100 million annual foreign visitors. The response of the French state to the ongoing social catastrophe was that nothing should impact the bottom line, with Foreign Office minister Éléonore Caroit telling the BBC Saturday that tourists should not cancel their holidays. “I’m in Paris and nothing is happening [!], and most other regions are OK,” she said. This was less than two weeks after fire had torn through some 2,000 hectares of the Fontainebleau forest just south-east of Paris, forcing the evacuation of 1,000 people and compelling water-bombers to scoop from the Seine to protect the capital region for the first time in its history. As the WSWS reported on July 14, European mortality monitoring body EuroMOMO had by then attributed roughly 10,600 deaths to this summer’s heat, with an analysis by Politico identifying 14,000 excess deaths in six countries—Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain and the UK—during the June heatwave alone. This excluded deaths in other heavily impacted countries such as Italy, Portugal and Greece. The World Health Organisation estimates extreme heat has killed some 200,000 people in Europe in four years, deaths it said were for the most part “entirely preventable.” They are not prevented because society’s resources, controlled by the super-rich capitalist class and governments which serve their interests, have been allocated elsewhere. The same governments now appealing to one another for water bombers against the flames are pouring hundreds of billions into rearmament. Six of Europe’s leading oil companies made $21.7 billion in profits in the first quarter of this year, 43 percent up on 2025. https://djmag.com/news/tomorrowland-gene.text: Tomorrowland is benefitting the economy in the Belgian capital of Brussels, despite the festival being held in the town of Boom, around 27 kilometres away. As reported by Flanders news site VRT NEWS , Tomorrowland has 43 official partner hotels in Brussels. The Brussels Hotel Association (BHA) estimates that festival-goers are responsible for an estimated 60,000 hotel overnight stays in Brussels during Tomorrowland. Brussels’ Hotel Le Plaza on the Adolphe Maxlaan reported being fully booked, with 1,000 festival-goers staying at the hotel. The space hosted a special make-up service for attendees, with hotel director Laurent Dekeef telling Belgian station BX1 that despite the hotel’s traditional nature, it was “trying to extend the Boom experience right up to the doors of the Plaza”. Elsewhere, Belgium’s main flyer Brussels Airlines reported hosting nearly 25,000 festival-goers from 106 different countries across 409 flights, an increase of 10,000 on 2024. The airline offers seven official Tomorrowland party flights, which feature a live in-flight DJ, from locations such as Ibiza, Barcelona and Prague, with over 1,000 passengers signing up for the special trips. It was recently reported that residents in Boom and other local towns were making thousands of euros providing services to Tomorrowland attendees. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: A Chinese national took her own life in a centre run by Secure Journeys, an Australian subsidiary of US-based prison multinational MTC. Illustration: Victoria Hart/Guardian design View image in fullscreen A Chinese national took her own life in a centre run by Secure Journeys, an Australian subsidiary of US-based prison multinational MTC. Illustration: Victoria Hart/Guardian design Australian immigration and asylum China expresses ‘grave concern’ as internal documents reveal suicide warning before death in Melbourne immigration detention Exclusive: Serious questions raised about whether Chinese citizen was properly monitored at centre run by US prison giant Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Christopher Knaus and Ariel Bogle Sun 9 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 11.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US private prison company running Australia’s immigration system was warned that a newly detained Chinese citizen expressed suicidal ideation and had a history of self-harm less than 24 hours before she died by suicide in a Melbourne detention centre, internal documents show. The death has raised serious questions about whether the detainee was properly monitored and whether she was placed in an appropriate room, given her state of mind. It has also triggered an intervention from Australia’s biggest trading partner, Guardian Australia can reveal. Escapes, fires, stabbing: catastrophic security failures revealed in Australia’s immigration detention network Read more The Chinese embassy has confirmed it has “lodged solemn representations and expressed grave concern to the Australian side” about the circumstances of the death. “China will closely follow the case and safeguard the safety and legitimate rights and interests of Chinese citizens,” an embassy spokesperson said. China’s public intervention creates a fresh headache for the home affairs minister, Tony Burke , who is already furious about a string of security lapses involving the government’s new immigration contractor, Secure Journeys, a local subsidiary of the US-based prison multinational Management and Training Corporation. In May the Guardian revealed that a series of failures had allowed the escape of high-risk detainees, caused ill-equipped staff to be stabbed and hospitalised and triggered multiple investigations, one of which warned that MTC’s “minimalist staffing model” was putting workers and detainees at risk. Burke took the extraordinary step of hauling in the global president of MTC for a face-to-face dressing down in September 2025, just six months after the company was awarded the $2.3bn onshore immigration detention contract. On 10 July Australian Border Force issued a short statement saying a detainee had been found dead in the Melbourne immigration detention centre that morning. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The detainee was a Chinese citizen in her mid-30s who had been picked up the day before for allegedly overstaying an English-language studies visa, internal documents seen by the Guardian show. She had no criminal history. The ABF transferred her into the custody of Secure Journeys on the afternoon of 9 July. The ABF made clear to Secure Journeys that she had previously attempted self-harm and had “recently thought about self-harm/suicide”, the documents show . She was found hanging in her room in the Broadmeadows residential precinct, part of the Melbourne immigration detention centre, early the next morning. Victoria police are investigating the death, which they described as non-suspicious. The coroner’s court of Victoria said it had directed police to prepare a brief of evidence. If you have something to share on this subject, you can contact us confidentially using the following methods. Secure Messaging in the Guardian app The Guardian app has a tool to send tips about stories. Messages are end to end encrypted and concealed within the routine activity that every Guardian mobile app performs. This prevents an observer from knowing that you are communicating with us at all, let alone what is being said. If you don't already have the Guardian app, download it ( iOS / Android ) and go to the menu. Select ‘Secure Messaging’. SecureDrop, instant messengers, email, telephone and post If you can safely use the Tor network without being observed or monitored, you can send messages and documents to the Guardian via our SecureDrop platform . Finally, our guide at theguardian.com/tips lists several ways to contact us securely, and discusses the pros and cons of each. Illustration: Guardian Design / Rich Cousins There were 360 reported incidents of threatened and actual self-harm across Australia’s onshore immigration detention network between July 2025 and March 2026, according to parliamentary records. There have been at least two deaths this year. A Secure Journeys spokesperson said the company offered its “deep condolences to the family and friends of the female detainee” but could not comment further due to the investigation. “Secure Journeys’ commitment to maintaining safe and secure operations, as well as both staff and detainee welfare remains our top priority,” the spokesperson said. The Department of Home Affairs offered sincere condolences to the woman’s family and friends. “Due to our privacy obligations to the deceased and the ongoing investigation into this matter, it would not be appropriate to comment further,” a spokesperson said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion China experts described the embassy’s statement as “firm but not excessive”. The Australia-China Relations Institute’s director, Prof James Laurenceson, said the fact that representations had been made and the embassy had expressed “grave concerns” showed it was taking the death seriously. But Laurenceson said he didn’t read the embassy’s statement as “excessively aggressive”. Labor plans migration cuts as Tony Burke pulls out of major speech Read more “It is the case that Australia and China have been trading tersely worded diplomatic statements more frequently in recent months over everything from Taiwan, China’s maritime claims in the South China Sea, its cyber operations, the Jimmy Lai case, Darwin Port, and more,” he said. “But I am not convinced that China’s statement in this case should be interpreted as some sort of diplomatic slap back for Australian complaints about Chinese actions in other contexts.” MTC’s performance in running Australia’s onshore detention network has triggered multiple investigations, including by the federal work safety regulator Comcare. Internal documents show Comcare has set up a dedicated inspection program to scrutinise immigration detention, citing an “increase in notifiable incidents, the severity and the profile of the reported incidents involving the [contractor]”. The regulator privately warned the department this year that it had received numerous reports of “serious injury or illness to both workers and others (detainees)”, “self-harm ideations and death involving detainees” and “detainee on detainee violence”. One of Comcare’s key concerns is that the risk-assessment system used in the centres is not effective and is putting staff and detainees at serious risk of violence and other harms. Understaffing has been a key concern since MTC took over. A March report by the National Preventive Mechanism, an independent monitor of places of detention, reported that “critically” low staffing levels were compromising the centres’ safety. The understaffing is also causing seriously ill detainees to miss medical appointments because MTC lacks workers to escort them to health centres. * Do you know more? https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Rukhsar Ahmed is the owner of a former restaurant, the Gujjar Palace, near Manchester’s curry mile. Photograph: Supplied View image in fullscreen Rukhsar Ahmed is the owner of a former restaurant, the Gujjar Palace, near Manchester’s curry mile. Photograph: Supplied UK news Pakistani grooming gang suspect ‘refuses to give date for return to UK’ Rukhsar Ahmed was recently elected an MP in Pakistan while on bail over alleged child rape in 1990s Manchester Shah Meer Baloch and Rajeev Syal Sun 9 Aug 2026 11.41 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 12.38 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A grooming gang suspect released on bail in the UK and then re-elected as an MP in Pakistan has reportedly declined to say when he would return to face rape charges. The Guardian disclosed that Rukhsar Ahmed, a former Pakistan state minister, was arrested at Manchester airport in July 2024 on suspicion of raping and trafficking at least two underage girls from care homes in the city’s Rusholme area during the 1990s. He was released on bail and flew to Pakistan nearly two months ago, missing an appointment at a police station after telling officers he was too unwell to fly back to the UK. He was elected an MP for prime minister Shehbaz Sharif’s centre-right Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz party days later. He did not respond to requests for a comment when approached by the Guardian last week. View image in fullscreen Rukhsar Ahmed. Photograph: Supplied It emerged on Sunday that Ahmed, 61, had been located in his office in Khari Sharif, a village in Mirpur district. According to the Mail on Sunday, he told a reporter he would fly back to Britain to meet his bail conditions, but declined to give a date. “Everything is with my legal team in Manchester and London, they told me I can’t discuss this,” he told the newspaper. “What they done, this media in the United Kingdom and Europe, is out of order. I have not been convicted of anything nor charged for anything, so what is going on? I don’t want to discuss it, because if I discuss it, things may go wrong.” Asked directly whether he had raped two underage girls, he refused to answer, telling the reporter: “You are doing wrong now, I told you not to talk to me like this … please don’t talk to me like this, I told you I have nothing to do with it, OK.” Ahmed published a statement on his Facebook account on Friday. It read: “I categorically deny all the allegations against me and will address these matters through the appropriate forums. On legal advice, I will not comment further while these matters remain ongoing.” Ahmed was a minister in various state governments from 2006 until he lost his seat in 2021. The Guardian understands that Greater Manchester police (GMP) had wanted to restrict Ahmed’s ability to travel abroad as part of his bail conditions, but a judge rejected tougher measures in July 2024. Ahmed was arrested at Manchester airport on 18 July 2024 in relation to past child sexual abuse allegations linked to the Rusholme area, where he lived for many years. According to the report, he received a string of visitors in his office. He is the owner of a former restaurant, the Gujjar Palace, near Manchester’s curry mile. The ongoing investigation relates to allegations from several women about sexual abuse of children at care homes in the early 1990s, when Ahmed was in his late 20s. He is understood to be expected to answer police bail in the next six weeks. If he does not attend, GMP may issue a warrant for his arrest or take steps to extradite him. The Guardian has approached Ahmed for comment again. Richard Scorer, the head of abuse law at Slater and Gordon who has acted in many Manchester grooming gang cases said: “Rusholme has regularly featured in grooming gang investigations over the past 30 years, with many cases involving allegations of children being abused in and around the area. “Not all of those allegations have been adequately investigated. I hope that a comprehensive investigation is taking place here”. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: The analysis underlines that US rightwing actors are seeking to influence the UK and boost their position on X in moments of disorder. Composite: Guardian Design/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The analysis underlines that US rightwing actors are seeking to influence the UK and boost their position on X in moments of disorder. Composite: Guardian Design/Getty Images The far right Most X accounts posting about Belfast and Southampton unrest were based outside UK Exclusive: Analysis shows 55% of accounts were located overseas – and seven of 12 most-read posts came from US Carmen Aguilar García , Michael Goodier , Pamela Duncan and Dan Sabbagh Sun 9 Aug 2026 10.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 13.16 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google More than half the accounts that posted on Elon Musk’s X about the rioting in Belfast and the civil disorder in Southampton in June were based outside the UK, an analysis by the Guardian can reveal. Of the 8,672 accounts whose combined posts about the events exceeded 1,000 views, just 45.3% were shown as from the UK, according to the social media platform’s own location function. One in six (16.8%) came from the US, 4.5% from Ireland, and about a quarter from all European countries other than the UK. Seven of the 12 most-read tweets about Belfast and Southampton came from the US – including one from Musk himself and two other US “alt-right” commentators – while an eighth was linked to North America. The analysis underlines that US rightwing actors are seeking to influence the UK and boost their position on X in moments of disorder – an exploitation of flashpoint events that has only intermittently attracted political attention in Britain. Q&A Methodology Show The Guardian collected 43,000 tweets mentioning Belfast, Southampton, Henry Nowak or Vickrum Digwa posted on X during the period of the unrest in both cities. This covered the period from 2 June to the end of 3 June for Southampton and from the evening of 8 June to the end of 9 June for Belfast. For X accounts whose combined tweets reached more than 1,000 views, we extracted their location and the number of times they have changed their username as shown in the “about this account” tab. Using a large language model (LLM), the team first classified which posts were directly related to the protests in Belfast and Southampton, and then categorised them as containing explicit or implicit racist language or anti-immigration comments. For those about Belfast, we also classified tweets as containing calls inciting to violence. A team of three people manually verified more than 5,500 posts, statistically testing the accuracy of the model to be robust and in line with academic standards. Nearly a third of all 43,000 posts on X relating to the two incidents contained racist or anti-immigration comments. Almost one in 10 relating to Belfast contained calls for violence or paramilitary or vigilante action. Imran Ahmed, the chief executive of the Centre for Countering Digital Hate, said the data demonstrated that X had become “a weapon of choice” for hostile foreign actors seeking to manipulate shocking and divisive content. Their goal, he added, was “to amplify local tragedies and crises, intensify racist narratives, and incite violence in communities they have never set foot in and to whom they have no real connection.” A post from Musk after the life sentencing of the killer of 18-year-old Henry Nowak, who had been falsely accused of racism by police after being stabbed in Southampton, has been viewed more than 28m times. “Legacy mainstream media, same ones who wrote about George Floyd millions of times, are dead silent about Nowak,” Musk posted shortly before 3pm on 2 June, in effect promoting his own platform at a time of heightened tension and disorder in the Hampshire port. View image in fullscreen Elon Musk posted about race and immigration in the UK twice as often as he did about SpaceX in the run-up to the aerospace company’s IPO in June. Photograph: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters Eleven police officers were injured on the night of 2 June in Southampton as people claiming to protest over Nowak’s murder marched to the site of his death. This followed a rally, addressed by the far-right activist Tommy Robinson, outside the city’s main police station. Musk is based in the US and has not visited the UK since November 2023. A Guardian analysis last month found he posted about race and immigration in the UK twice as often as he did about SpaceX in the run-up to the aerospace company’s initial public offering in June. Security experts including Fiona Hill, a former adviser to the US and UK governments, have warned that the UK is a soft target for online manipulation by overseas actors because it does not take the idea of civil, or “psychological”, defence seriously. Dr Julia Ebner, a researcher at the Institute for Strategic Dialogue and the University of Oxford, said flashpoint episodes such as in Southampton and Belfast had become “strategic events” for far-right actors seeking to amplify and exploit them. “They are using the UK as a negative example, smearing the UK to promote their own narratives of western civilisational decay or social collapse,” Ebner said. “But the other purpose is to influence UK politics, and European politics more widely,” using crisis moments to “promote a strong, strengthened far-right wave across the world”. Four of the top 12 most-seen tweets came from UK accounts: two were by the leader of the Restore Britain party, Rupert Lowe, whom Musk has endorsed; another was from GB News, while the most popular, with 37.6m views, was written by the “anti-woke” rightwing political commentator Konstantin Kisin . Other accounts located in the US were anonymous, though familiar. @EndWokeness posted a blurry still image of a black man attacking a white man in Belfast on 8 June, saying the full video was “too graphic” to post. It attracted 16.3m views. The assault, a stabbing in which the victim, Stephen Ogilvie, lost an eye, prompted three nights of racially motivated rioting targeting non-white people in Belfast. An asylum seeker from Sudan was charged with attempted murder and at least 23 people were arrested. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters Preview latest after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen A vehicle set alight during riots in Belfast in June. Photograph: Peter Morrison/AP The @EndWokeness account, which has 3.9m followers, was cited by a parliamentary committee after it amplified a false claim that the 2024 attack in Southport, in which three girls were killed, was carried out by a Muslim man. The account has been linked by an open source analyst to Jack Posobiec, a rightwing influencer who promoted the Pizzagate conspiracy, a false accusation that leading US Democrats were engaged in satanic child abuse at a child-friendly pizza restaurant in Washington DC. Another leading poster was the US rightwing influencer Benny Johnson, who accused the New York Times of writing nothing about Nowak and thousands of pieces about the murder of George Floyd in Minneapolis in 2020 – though Nowak was murdered in the UK. The analysis of the most-viewed accounts did not reveal any posts from Russia or China – both countries that have been behind online disinformation campaigns – though it is possible that posters successfully disguised their locations using virtual private networks (VPNs). X shows location data for most profiles, inferred by the platform from user IP addresses, though government accounts are excluded. Last November, after the feature was introduced, X’s then head of product, Nikita Bier, said it was more than 99% accurate . When it was launched, it revealed that some pro-Scottish-independence accounts were based in Iran. But there were signs of inauthenticity in popular posts. Two of the top most-seen tweets came from the US-based C3 (@C_3C_3) account, accusing “legacy media” of not reporting about the Nowak case. Its profile picture is a baby wearing a Make America Great Again cap; the username has changed 14 times previously. One UK account, which tweeted at least six times about the murder of Nowak, with almost 3,800 combined views, had changed its name more than 400 times. NewsSceneUK – subsequently changed to BritifyFooty – wrote in one tweet about the “huge crowd of patriots outside #Southampton Police Station”. Accounts posting from overseas that changed their usernames more than 20 times included one in Kenya that wrote after the Belfast stabbing: “When the state fails to protect people, the streets find their own language.” Another, from Europe, described the Nowak case as “a globalized, calculated and malicious evil” affecting “every White person and every White nation”. Close to a third – about 13,000 – of the Belfast and Southampton tweets, whether from the UK or abroad, were racist or anti-immigrant, according to the Guardian analysis. When analysed separately, a quarter of the posts that were only about Southampton were racist or anti-immigrant, compared with a third of those that were only about Belfast. One UK-based poster, writing a day after the Belfast stabbing, claimed they hoped the attacker was British-born because “race is the issue, not immigration status”. The post registered 2m views. Valerie Wirtschafter, an expert on online foreign influence operations from the Brookings Institution, a US thinktank, said she believed violent events such as those in Belfast and Southampton were “a point of exploitation” in which “outside agitators” had an opportunity to make a disproportionate impact. Their position was helped by X and other social media companies cutting content moderation, she said, but in particular by “algorithms and how they collide with the basic cognitive processes of humans. We are more attracted to things that are shocking.” Explore more on these topics The far right X Elon Musk Far right Far right (US) Internet Belfast news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.theguardian.com/education/20.text: John and Katie Meehan have worked with the Lullaby Trust to strengthen safety and regulation of nurseries in England. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian View image in fullscreen John and Katie Meehan have worked with the Lullaby Trust to strengthen safety and regulation of nurseries in England. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian Early years education Parents of baby girl killed at nursery fear unsafe sleeping ‘rife’ in sector across England Katie and John Meehan say responses to campaign they launched after death of daughter Genevieve must be ‘wake-up call’ Josh Halliday North of England editor Sun 9 Aug 2026 09.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 09.36 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The parents of a nine-month-old girl who died after being placed in an unsafe sleeping position at nursery said they feared poor practice may be “rife” across England. Genevieve Meehan suffocated when she was strapped face down to a beanbag for an hour and 37 minutes at a nursery in Cheadle Hulme, Stockport, in May 2022. Kate Roughley, the nursery’s deputy manager, was jailed for 14 years in 2024 after being found guilty of manslaughter. One of Roughley’s colleagues was later jailed for the “deplorable” treatment of other babies in her care. Genevieve’s parents, Katie and John Meehan, have led a campaign with the charity the Lullaby Trust to strengthen safety and regulation of nurseries after a series of high-profile abuses. The sector has come under intense scrutiny in recent months after the cases of Vincent Chan and Nathan Bennett , nursery workers who sexually assaulted children in their care. View image in fullscreen Genevieve Meehan, who died in May 2022 at nine months old. Photograph: Greater Manchester Police/PA Chan was jailed in February for 18 years for molesting young children in a campaign of sexual abuse that was described as “every parent’s worst nightmare”, while Bennett was jailed in March for 24 years for raping and abusing young children in his care. Another nursery worker, Kimberley Cookson, was jailed in April over the death of 14-month-old Noah Sibanda, who had been physically restrained face-down with a blanket over his head while being put to sleep. As a result of Genevieve’s parents’ campaign , childcare settings in England will be banned from September from putting babies under 12 months to sleep in anything other than a cot. Ofsted, the regulator, will triple the number of unannounced inspections – adding an extra 3,000 visits a year, boosted by an additional £8m from the government – and inspect nurseries every four years instead of six. Each visit will scrutinise sleeping policies. Katie Meehan, 42, said she was “really shocked” by the extent of unsafe sleeping practice that had been revealed when nurseries wrote privately to the government about the planned changes this year. Some reported leaving babies to sleep in pushchairs “due to space limitations”, according to details shared with the Department for Education (DfE). Others put infants to sleep outside, adopting “forest school models or Scandinavian practices”. By law, nurseries are required to follow NHS safer sleep guidance – which includes laying the baby on their back in a cot or Moses basket – however, in the rules from September, the government will state: “Babies aged one year and under must only be placed to sleep in a cot.” Katie Meehan, who is working closely with the government and Ofsted, said the responses suggested unsafe sleeping may be “rife” across England and that they were a “wake-up call” for the regulator and officials. Some nursery owners said they would be forced to reduce the number of infants they take as a result of the new rules. Several raised concerns that this will ban smaller beds, such as dream coracles, which take up less space than a cot and have been widely adopted in recent years. John Meehan, 40, said he was concerned some nursery owners – many of whom are backed by private equity firms – were potentially putting profit before safety. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines UK Get the day’s headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morning Preview latest after newsletter promotion “There are lots and lots of people out there who just want to do their absolute best and they go into that industry because they want to look after children,” he said. “But my impression from some of the responses is that they are taking too many children and there is a money incentive for them to do so, and that is a real concern.” Ministers are now considering whether to introduce mandatory CCTV to all nurseries in England , one of the key aims of the campaign. Olivia Bailey, the former early years minister who spearheaded the latest reforms, is understood to have been very persuaded by the arguments for mandatory CCTV. Katie Meehan said she was disappointed that Bailey lost her role in the reshuffle when Andy Burnham became prime minister. However, she is hopeful Burnham will take up the reforms, having met Genevieve’s family this year when he was mayor of Greater Manchester. She said Burnham was particularly supportive of their call for mandatory CCTV – which was crucial in securing Genevieve’s killer’s conviction – and that he had told them: “Genevieve was a child of Manchester and she was failed. We’ve got to make sure it doesn’t happen again.” The DfE said: “What happened to Genevieve was a tragedy, and her parents’ campaigning has already changed practice across the country. We will keep going until no family goes through what theirs has. Nurseries, vets and shops: the sectors where private equity plays a big role Read more “The vast majority of settings do a brilliant job, and the response to our updated guidance showed a sector that wants to get this right. But settings have long been legally required to follow NHS safer sleep guidance, and that is why we are working with the Lullaby Trust to make those expectations unambiguous, so there can be no excuses for unsafe practice.” Sir Martyn Oliver, the chief inspector at Ofsted, said: “No parent should have to endure what Katie and John have been through. They have shown remarkable bravery in pursuing change following their daughter’s tragic death. “We welcome the DfE’s additional funding for more frequent inspections, including thousands more without notice visits. We’re also strengthening our inspection practice so that safe sleeping in nurseries and with childminders is now a mandatory part of every inspection and will be reported on for parents to read.” Explore more on these topics Early years education Crime Ofsted Childcare Children Parents and parenting Child protection news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed Education Schools Teachers Universities Students

Photograph: Richard Drew/AP New York Captain charged after woman and her five-month-old die in New York boat capsizing Manuel Hernandez charged with 13 counts of reckless endangerment after boat overturned in New York harbor Eric Berger Sun 9 Aug 2026 10.47 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 13.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The captain of a boat that capsized in the New York harbor on Saturday evening has been charged following the deaths of a 27-year-old woman and her five-month-old daughter. Manuel Hernandez, 46, was arrested and charged with 13 counts of reckless endangerment in the early hours of Sunday morning, a New York police department spokesperson told the Guardian. Police responded to a 911 call at 10.25pm by deploying a helicopter unit to the scene, where divers then found the woman and baby in the water, the spokesperson said. The two victims, whom the NYPD named as Sara Sanchez and her daughter Antonella, were then transported in critical condition to NYU Langone hospital in Brooklyn, where they were pronounced dead. “On Saturday, August 8, 2026, at approximately 2225 hours, police received a 911 call reporting an overturned vessel in the vicinity of Liberty Island, within the confines of the 1st Precinct,” the NYPD said. “The NYPD’s Harbor Unit, SCUBA Team and Aviation responded to the scene.” A dozen other people were rescued from the vessel before the police arrived, and later transported to hospitals, according to the spokesperson. “We are deeply saddened by the tragic loss of life last night, and our thoughts are with the victims’ family and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time,” said Captain Doreen McCarthy, the US Coast Guard sector New York commander. “We are extremely grateful for the heroic, swift actions of our partner agencies and Good Samaritan vessel who assisted in rescuing survivors from the water.” Associated Press contributed reporting Explore more on these topics New York US crime news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/09/over-.text: China's east coast has been preparing for the storm's arrival in recent days, with work and transport services suspended in some areas along its predicted path.The centre of the typhoon moved over the coastline near Yuhuan City in Zhejiang Province at about 5:30 pm (09:30 GMT), China's National Meteorological Centre said in an online post.Maximum wind speeds near the centre were more than 150 kilometres per hour at the time it made landfall, the NMC said. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250 to 500 mm of rain.Authorities relocated more than 900,000 residents from the city of Wenzhou and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.Nearly 1,400 flights in and out of Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled on Sunday, state broadcaster CCTV reported.Hangzhou's airport in nearby Zhejiang province saw 270 inbound and outbound flights cancelled, the report said.Heavy rain, strong windsThe effects were felt as far away as Hong Kong on China's southern coast, where the weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9°C, caused by warm air pushed over the city by Typhoon Dolphin.With the storm "moving towards the vicinity of Zhejiang and moving inland, its outer subsiding air will persistently bring extremely hot weather to the territory today to Tuesday", the Hong Kong Observatory said.Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain and strong winds to Japan's Okinawa before reaching China.Seven people in Okinawa suffered minor injuries, including a man aged over 100 who was blown over by gusts, fell to the ground, and hit his head, according to the island's government.By Sunday afternoon, 5,290 households in Okinawa were without electricity, according to regional utility Okinawa Electric Power.In Taiwan, dozens of ferry services were suspended, and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds to the island's north on Sunday.Red alert issuedChina's NMC issued a red typhoon alert — its most severe warning — on Sunday morning, forecasting "extraordinary torrential rain" in some areas of central and eastern Zhejiang.Heavy precipitation is also expected to fall in Shanghai and parts of Fujian, Anhui and Jiangsu provinces through Monday afternoon, it said.Typhoon Dolphin was expected to weaken after making landfall while moving in a northwesterly direction over eastern China.In Fujian, nearly 99,000 people were relocated from "risky areas" on Saturday evening ahead of the storm's arrival, state news agency Xinhua reported.Services on more than 200 ferry routes were suspended in Zhejiang and Fujian, Xinhua said. Work on offshore projects was halted, while 474 construction vessels had been called to port by Friday morning, Xinhua said.Some train services in affected areas were also suspended on Sunday to ensure passenger safety, state media reported.Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme heat events more frequent and more intense worldwide.Typhoon Dolphin's arrival in China comes two weeks after Typhoon Noul lashed southern Guangdong province, declared by authorities at the time as the strongest storm to hit China this year.Three people were killed, and hundreds of homes were damaged by Typhoon Noul in the Philippines before it reached China.

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/09/13-ki.text: Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes overnight that killed civilians and injured many others on both sides, local authorities reported.Large-scale Russian missile strikes on Ukrainian cities have become almost routine in recent weeks, with Moscow exploiting Ukraine’s critical shortage of interceptors for the US-made Patriot systems — the sole air defence weapon in its arsenal able to shoot down ballistic missiles.In the latest attacks, Ukrainian drones killed five people and injured two dozen others, including a four-year-old boy, in Russia’s border region of Belgorod, according to the regional administration.Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says four people were killed in the Kyiv capital region, a three-year-old boy and his grandparents, in one strike, and later another fatality was reported in a separate strike, also on civilian infrastructure.“More pressure is needed — new sanctions that will prevent Russia from producing these ballistic missiles. And our people absolutely need more protection. Anti-ballistic systems, interceptor missiles for Patriot, SAMP/T, NASAMS, and HAWK systems, as well as our F-16s,” wrote Zelenskyy in a post on the Telegram messaging app.In Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, Russian missiles struck a high-rise apartment block in the Saltivskyi district, killing three people and injuring 37, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov.At least six other deaths were reported in strikes on other frontline cities, including Sumy, Kherson and Donetsk in the eastern industrial Donbas region.Eight more people were injured in Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa after “dozens of missiles and drones” struck the city and surrounding region, according to local administration head Oleh Kiper.Ukrainian officials say 13 people were killed and approximately 90 others were injured in Russian attacks over the past 24 hours.Zelenskyy has for months lobbied other countries, especially the United States, to send Ukraine more Patriot systems, made scarcer by the Iran war, arguing they are crucial for defending civilians.Failing that, Zelenskyy wants to make Patriot ammunition in Ukraine or get approval from Elon Musk to use his Starlink satellite communications system to guide strikes inside Russia that can hit its missile launchers.Meanwhile, Kyiv has kept up long-range drone strikes against Russian energy infrastructure, as well as the country’s largest online retailer, Wildberries, and other targets deep inside Russia, sparking a fuel crisis.Russia’s defence ministry on Sunday claimed its overnight strikes hit drone warehouses in the Kharkiv region, as well as fuel depots and stores of other materiel belonging to Ukraine’s armed forces at the port of Odesa.It said its forces had shot down 153 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday, including over Russian-occupied Crimea and the Black and Azov seas.In Russia's Belgorod region, authorities said Ukrainian drone strikes damaged 29 apartment blocks and five private houses, as well as administrative buildings and unspecified “commercial facilities.”Debris from Ukrainian drones also fell on two enterprises and a private home in the Russian city of Novorossiysk, mayor Andrey Kravchenko said on Sunday.A major fuel terminal is located at Novorossiysk that links Kazakhstan's oil fields to markets around the world, and which has previously been a target for Ukrainian strikes, as Kyiv looks to suffocate the Kremlin’s energy sector, which it believes to be the financial arm of its invasion.

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/09/yemen.text: A medical source in Mokha, held by Yemen's internationally recognised, Aden-based government, said three civilians and eight military personnel had been killed in the Houthi attacks.A further 32 individuals were wounded, six of them civilians, the source added, explaining that all the civilian casualties had been a result of strikes on Mokha's port.Two military sources with the government forces earlier confirmed that at least eight troops had been killed in the strikes and more than 40 personnel were injured.The Houthis' military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted "Saudi enemy" troops and equipment in the area with missiles and drones.A years-long truce in Yemen's civil war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government appeared to collapse last month as fighting between regional allies of the United States and Iran flared.The breakdown of the UN-backed 2022 accord came as the rebels announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and the kingdom's oil infrastructure, in parallel with Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.Oil refinery strikeEarlier, Saree said the Houthis had struck an oil facility on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast after the Gulf kingdom's energy ministry said it had extinguished a fire at the Jazan site.He added that the attack on the facility operated by Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil firm Aramco was launched in response to incursions by drones from the Gulf monarchy into northwest Yemen.The two military sources with the Aden-based government confirmed the Houthis attacked Mokha with several waves of missile and drone barrages.One of the two military sources said the Houthis also targeted pro-government forces and installations outside Mokha and sites on islands near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the shipping chokepoint at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.The same military source said some locations targeted by the Iran-backed group housed Saudi troops but no casualties had been reported among military personnel from the Gulf kingdom.Residents in Mokha confirmed they heard blasts in the area, with one saying they "heard explosions from drones and air defences over the port and city".Another resident said they heard "six consecutive explosions" at the port.The Houthis control vast swathes of Yemen, including the capital Sanaa and areas on the border with Saudi Arabia's Red Sea provinces.The Yemeni threat to shipping and Saudi oil facilities came as Iran pressed its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, now the central flashpoint between Tehran and Washington amid efforts to end the Middle East war begun by the US and Israel in February.

https://www.dw.com/en/syria-says-deal-ag.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IWmG Assad's 2024 ouster was a blow to Russia's influence in the region [FILE: December 2024] Image: Leo Correa/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Syria and Russia have agreed on the future management of Russian bases on the country's Mediterranean coast. Russia used the bases to provide military support to former Syrian leader Bashar Assad during Syria's 13-year civil war that ended in 2024 . The Syrian Foreign Ministry announced Sunday that the two nations had signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) after 18 months of negotiations . The deal effectively means Russia will no longer have military outposts in the Arab country. Syria says the strategic Mediterranean bases will become joint training centers [FILE: December 2024] Image: Adrien Vautier/Le Pictorium/IMAGO What will happen to Russia's military bases in Syria? Syria will take over management of the Hmeimim airport and the commercial berth at Tartus port, Syria's Foreign Ministry said. State media cited the ministry as saying that the bases would be converted into "joint training and capacity-building centres, within new arrangements that preserve mutual interests." The facilities will be gradually integrated into the country's civilian administration. The transition is expected to be completed within three months, the ministry said. Russia has yet to comment on the agreement. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani visited Tartus port on Sunday Image: SANA/AFP Russia trying to build relations with post-Assad Syria During the civil war in Syria between 2011 and 2024, while Assad was president, Russia was Syria's main ally and military backer. Assad was overthrown in December 2024 , and now lives in exile in Moscow. Current Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa led an alliance of Islamist rebel groups that fought against government forces during the war. Assad's ouster in 2024 dealt a major blow to Moscow's influence in the region. Russian President Vladimir Putin has been trying to build ties with Syria's new leadership to protect the future of the only two official Russian military bases located outside the former Soviet Union. Al-Sharaa has met with Putin in Moscow twice since coming to power in January 2025. During his last trip, Putin said, "much has been accomplished in terms of restoring our interstate relations." The Syrian government has been demanding that Moscow extradite Assad. https://www.politico.eu/article/israel-r.text: Israel rejected a U.S.-backed peace plan for Gaza Sunday, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu saying that Israel will not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas has been “genuinely disarmed.” In dismissing the 15-point plan drawn up by U.S. President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace , Netanyahu also said that as long as he is prime minister, “a Palestinian state will not be established” in Gaza or the West Bank. The peace plan announced by the White House at the end of July would require Hamas to disarm and relinquish its governance in Gaza, while Israel would be required to withdraw its military forces from the territory. Advertisement Advertisement Hamas has said that it would begin disarming, but in recent days an Israeli official said the country still had “serious security concerns.” The rejection is a blow to peace negotiations the Trump administratoin has been brokering since September. The U.S. president had described the plan, now rejected by Israel, as a “critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government” and giving Israel “the security it deserves.” Israel appears unlikely to pull back significant forces or make other concessions ahead of legislative elections scheduled for October. Netanyahu faces a tough reelection battle, with his far-right coalition partners urging him to keep up the pressure on Hamas and leave forces in Gaza. Opponents also accuse him of failing to prevent the Oct. 7, 2023, attack when Hamas-led militants attacked Israeli communities, killing about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking 251 others hostage. Israel responded with a punishing military offensive that has killed more than 73,000 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. Netanyahu said on Sunday that he is now in discussions with U.S. officials about how to move forward. “They have ideas, some of which are acceptable to us and some of which are unacceptable to us, and we know how to stand up to these things,” he said.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwye.text: Image source, Google By Ruth Comer Published 2 hours ago Two drones were spotted over a military base in western Germany just days after an explosive-laden device was found at Leipzig airport. Germany's armed forces (Bundeswehr) confirmed they were seen on Thursday evening at a base in Mechernich, near Bonn, reportedly housing components for US-made Patriot air-defence systems. A spokeswoman for the Bundeswehr Joint Force Command said military police were deployed to the site before the matter was handed over to local police. It is the latest instance of drones being spotted near military bases or airports in European nations supporting Ukraine in its war with Russia, on which suspicion has fallen. Moscow has consistently denied any involvement. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told newspaper Bild on Sunday that Germany had become a regular target of "destabilising" attacks. "We're not at war, but we are the daily target of hybrid warfare," he said. Germany is currently investigating how a drone laden with explosives was able to reach a runway at Leipzig/Halle airport, which is used by Nato, the Germany military and serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines. The Bundeswehr declined to comment on the ongoing investigation when asked by the BBC on Sunday about the suspected origins of the drones spotted above Mechernich. The local police force has been contacted for comment. German media reports that the base has a storage facility for equipment âand spare parts used to maintain the Patriot missile batteries. The air-defence systems have become crucial to Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian ballistic missiles since Moscow's full-scale invasion began in 2022. However, President Volodymyr Zelensky this week pleaded to allies for further supplies, warning that Ukraine was running out of interceptor missiles. After initially offering Ukraine license to make Patriots in early July, US President Donald Trump last week denied any such agreement. A spate of drone sightings in European airspace last year left the continent on high alert, prompting the EU to discuss a continent-wide "drone wall" of air defences. Some European officials have blamed Russia for these drone sightings, claims Moscow has previously described as "absurd". https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c935.text: Image source, Getty Images By Grace Eliza Goodwin Reporting from New York Published 9 August 2026, 16:19 BST Updated 1 hour ago The operator of a boat that overturned near the Statue of Liberty, killing a woman and a baby, has been arrested and charged with reckless endangerment, New York police said. Officials said a large search and rescue operation was launched after the incident near New York Harbour on Saturday night. A nearby vessel rescued 12 people from the water before police arrived, the US Coast Guard (USCG) said. New York police divers later found a 27-year-old woman and a five-month-old girl, who were transported to a nearby hospital where they later died. The names of passengers and the specific cause of the incident have not been released. Around 22:25 local time (03:25 BST), police received a 911 call reporting an overturned boat in the waters near Liberty Island, which houses the iconic statue. The rescue involved two Coast Guard boats, four fire department boats, two police boats and a police helicopter, the USCG said. The survivors of the incident are all reported to be in stable condition, the agency added. The investigation into the incident is ongoing, officials said. The boat's operator, a 46-year-old Manhattan resident, faces 13 counts of reckless endangerment, officials said. Coast Guard investigators are also determining whether the boat was illegally chartered. An illegal charter is any passenger-for-hire vessel operation that does not have required credentials, safety equipment, and certificate of inspection. "We are extremely grateful for the heroic, swift actions of our partner agencies and Good Samaritan vessel who assisted in rescuing survivors from the water," said Capt Doreen McCarthy of the USCG.
