Állítólag Hollandiából becsempészett kokainnal üzletelt. Miután kiengedték, halálos fenyegetéseket kapott, így a Politico szerint először Irakba, majd Törökországba menekült. A svéd hatóságok ezzel egy időben több nagy bandavezért is elkaptak, Majid pedig úgy volt vele, hogy ő a megfelelő személy, hogy betöltse az utánuk maradt űrt. Eleinte Uppsalában építette ki a hálózatát, ami aztán tovább terjeszkedett. 2023-ra már közel egytonnás drogszállítmányok felett rendelkezett a svéd média szerint. Ő maga „Kurd róka” (angolul Kurdish fox) néven híresült el, tehát róla kapta az angol nevét a Foxtrot is. 2023-ban Majid már Törökországban élt, de hiába kérte a kiadatását a svéd kormány, nem adták át nekik a bandavezért. Ekkoriban a két ország között a skandináv ország NATO-tagságának ügyében is diplomáciai feszültség volt, Majidot ráadásul védte a török állampolgársága, amit pénzért vásárolt magának. A letartóztatását az is akadályozta, hogy a svéd titkosszolgálat akcióiról információt szivárogtattak a bűnbandának – valószínűleg néhány török diplomata jóvoltából. A maffiózó azért nem bízta a véletlenre: még abban az évben Iránba menekült, és valószínűleg ma is Teheránban tartózkodik. Rawa Majid – Fotó: Swedish Police Diamant Salihu, a svéd SVT műsorszolgáltató oknyomozó újságírója három éve vizsgálja a Foxtrotot és kapcsolatait. Szerinte ezen a ponton változott meg jelentősen a csoport tevékenysége. Amellett, hogy a maga drogügyleteit onnan irányítja, a maffiavezér már az iráni rezsim meghosszabbított karjaként is működhet: a svéd rendőrség úgy véli, hogy a koppenhágai izraeli nagykövetség elleni kézigránátos támadást is a Foxtrot segítségével szervezték le. „Alkut kellett kötnie azért, hogy szabadon élhessen Iránban, azzal a feltétellel, hogy ő és hálózata a rezsimnek dolgozik” – mondta róla Salihu a BBC-nek . A Foxtrot így már nemcsak a maga ellenségeit, hanem iráni disszidenseket és ellenzékieket is célozhat. Ugyan Teherán kategorikusan tagadja , hogy bármilyen kapcsolatban állna a bandával, de az Egyesült Államok és az Egyesült Királyság is az iráni kapcsolatok miatt vezetett be szankciókat, és tavasszal az európai titkosszolgálatok a terrorfenyegetettség miatt kifejezetten ráálltak a banda levadászására – erről itt írtunk bővebben . Hogyan lehet viszont Iránból irányítani egy svédországi bűnszervezetet? Nos, a Foxtrot módszerei sokban hasonlítanak a DZ Mafiáéra – vagy inkább fordítva. A lényeg, hogy a csoportok sokszor kallódó kiskorú elkövetőket szerveznek be a közösségi médián keresztül bérgyilkosnak. Nem meglepő, hogy az Arte riportja szerint 2024-ben az aktív bandatagok 13 százaléka kiskorú volt, néhányan közülük 13-14 évesek. A nyomozók szerint a rájuk bízott feladat minden szakaszát, a toborzástól a fegyverek átadásán át a végső kivitelezésig távolról, digitális kommunikáción keresztül bonyolítják le, általában titkosított üzenetküldő appokon. Az Europol ezt „Erőszakszolgáltatás”, angolul rövidítve VaaS-módszernek nevezi. „Tudatosan egyre fiatalabb tinédzsereket toboroznak, mert ők nem gondolnak a lebukás következményeire, és hajlamosabbak vállalni a kockázatot” – mondta Diamant Salihu, a svéd SVT műsorszolgáltató oknyomozó újságírója a BBC-nek. Elmondása szerint olyan összegeket ajánlanak a tiniknek, ami megváltoztatná az életüket. Ezután jön a bökkenő: az újoncokat letartóztatják, mielőtt begyűjthetnék a pénzt, a banda fejesei pedig mennek tovább anélkül, hogy bepiszkították volna a kezüket. „Egyáltalán nem érdekli őket, ha a tinédzsereket elkapják. Mert amikor elkapják őket, nem kérhetik a pénzt, amit felajánlottak nekik, és nem is látunk példát arra, hogy kifizették volna ezeket a fiatal gyilkosokat” – mondta Salihu. A tizenéves Tábornok, a 47-es Ügynök és „1” A Foxtrot működését jól példázza Atilla Azimov esete. A 18 éves norvég fiatalt egy másik tinédzseren keresztül szervezte be a svéd maffia. A 17 éves toborzót a kiskorúsága miatt nem nevezhette meg a sajtó, de Generalen, azaz Tábornok néven emlegetik. A Norvégiában élő Azimovnak pénzt ígértek egy leszámolásért cserébe, ő pedig az instrukciók alapján 2025 februárjában átment Svédországba. Célpontja, a 20 éves Murad Abdelkader a McDonald'sban dolgozott diákmunkásként, és épp hazafelé tartott, amikor Azimov a sötétben elkezdett rá lövöldözni. Már a földön feküdt, amikor fejbe is lőtték. Az áldozatnak semmi köze nem volt semmilyen bűnszervezethez, összetévesztették valakivel. Azimov végül egy vasat sem kapott a gyilkosságért, a hatóságok viszont elfogták, a bíróság pedig életfogytiglani börtönbüntetésre ítélte. Atilla Azimov a svéd rendőrség által kiadott fotókon – Fotó: Swedish Police De nagyon hasonló az a nagy-britanniai eset is , aminél végül nem történt meg a gyilkosság. A napokban ítélték el Johannes Natlandot, akit szintén Norvégiából szervezett be a Foxtrot. A tinédzser jólétben és kényelemben nőtt fel, újságíró szülők gyerekeként. Focistának készült, de 13 évesen kábítószerfüggő lett, paranoid késztetései voltak, pszichotikus állapotba került. Járt pszichiátrián és rehabon is, majd rövid ideig problémás gyerekeknek fenntartott intézetben élt. Ott került összeköttetésbe egy másik tinédzserrel, aki összehozta a Foxtrottal. A Natlandot megbízó tini szintén Tábornok volt, aki először csak annyit írt neki: „270K egy angliai gyilkosságért”. Ez a norvég koronában megadott összeg átszámolva közel 9 millió forintos ár lett volna. Az üzenetben azt ígérték , hogy a bérgyilkosságot vállaló embert azonnal kicsempészik az országból, a rendőrséget pedig lefizetik, hogy ne nyomozzanak körültekintően. Váltig állították, hogy semmi sem mehet félre, a fiatal pedig belement az ajánlatba. Ezután tovább referálták egy 47-es Ügynök nevű felhasználóhoz, aki Signalon keresztül segített neki leszervezni az utazást. Ő foglalta le neki a repülőjegyet, és segített neki a sürgősségi útlevél megszerzésében. Már a határőrség is gyanúsnak tartotta a fiút a gyorsított útlevéleljárás, a készpénz és a retúrjegy hiánya miatt. Végül mégis beengedték, mert csak 3 nap múlva indult volna visszajárat Norvégiába a manchesteri reptérről. Natlandnak ezután egy „1” nevű férfi adta meg az instrukciókat, a videójátékok küldetéseit idéző, játékosított formában. Küldött neki egy térképet és videókat, amelyek megmutatják, hol találja meg a huddersfieldi erdőben elrejtett fegyvereket és egy lopott kocsit. Egy másik videó azt szemléltette, hogy hogyan fér hozzá egy elrejtett pénzes táskához, amiből finanszírozni tudja a küldetést. Natland ezután kényelembe helyezhette magát egy huddersfieldi szállodában. Persze nem tudott ellenállni a kísértésnek, hogy videókat küldjön a barátainak a fegyverekről, az ágyán szétterített előlegről. Közben a 47-es még írt neki egy üzenetet: „Holnap sok dolgunk lesz”. Csakhogy ekkorra Tábornokot már őrizetbe vették az oslói reptéren. A 17 éves épp egy norvég rendőr 14 éves fiának meggyilkolását próbálta megszervezni. Egy 15 és egy 17 éves fiút toborzott a késeléses támadás végrehajtásához, de a 15 éves értesítette a rendőrséget. Amikor letartóztatták, a nyomozók megtalálták a huddersfieldi gyilkossági terv részleteit a telefonján. Natlandot így még azelőtt elkapták a brit hatóságok, hogy elkövette volna a bűncselekményt. Azt se tudta egyébként, hogy kit kellene megölnie. A brit terrorelhárítás a mai napig nyomoz ebben az ügyben. A bíróságon gyilkosságról szóló összeesküvés vádjában találták bűnösnek Natlandot. Hogy pontosan mi lesz az ítélet, az októberben dőlhet el. A 17 éves Tábornokot viszont a BBC szerint májusban ítélték el, és 14 éves börtönbüntetését tölti. Róla kiderült, hogy 3 éve gyermekotthonban élt, onnan dolgozott be a bűnbandának. Vannak kisebb sikerek a banda elleni küzdelemben Az Europol külön létrehozott egy osztagot, az Operatív Munkacsoport (OTF) GRIMM-et, hogy kezeljék a problémát. Nem véletlen kellett bevonni az európai bűnüldöző szervet: a VaaS-módszert ugyanis láthatóan sok esetben arra használják, hogy országokon átívelően vezényeljenek le leszámolásokat. A munkacsoportban jelenleg 11 országot vizsgálnak, ahol ezt az ügymenetet használják: Belgiumot, Dániát, Finnországot, Franciaországot, Németországot, Izlandot, Hollandiát, Norvégiát, Spanyolországot, Svédországot és az Egyesült Királyságot. Stefan Hector, a svéd országos rendőrfőkapitány-helyettes azt mondta, hogy folyamatosan bővítik együttműködésüket más országokkal, és igyekeznek megmutatni a szervezett bűnözőknek, hogy a világon sehol sem érezhetik magukat biztonságban. Az OTF GRIMM a megalakulása óta eltelt 15 hónapban már ért el sikereket, ha áttörésről nem is lehet beszélni. Az európai rendőrség több mint 280 letartóztatást hajtott végre, köztük néhány kulcsfontosságú gyanúsítottat is elfogtak. Az egyik legnagyobb kapás Ali Shehad Ahmed letartóztatása volt, akit a 47-es ügynöknek tartanak. A brit rendőrség szerint ő kifejezetten közel áll Majidhoz. A férfit az iraki kurd Szulejmánijja városában vették őrizetbe, és folyamatban van a kiadatása Svédországba. Mohamed Mohdhi a svéd rendőrség által kiadott fotón – Fotó: Swedish Police Májusban Mohamed „Moewgli” Mohdhit, a svéd rendőrség által a Foxtrot „központi szereplőjeként” jellemzett volt rappert tartóztatták le Tunéziában. Júniusban egy svéd bíróság életfogytiglani börtönbüntetésre ítélte Poya Shafie-t, akit Majid egyik legközelebb álló embereként tartanak számon, miután Irakban letartóztatták. „Nem fogunk meghátrálni. Ha veszélyt jelentenek a svédekre, egyenként elkapjuk őket, akkor is ha külföldön vannak” – jelentette ki májusban Ulf Kristersson svéd miniszterelnök. Egyelőre nem világos, hogy a letartóztatások milyen mértékben rontották a Foxtrot működési képességét, tekintve, hogy a szervezet feje még mindig Iránból irányíthat. „Még mindig aktív. És amíg ez a hálózat aktív, attól tartok, továbbra is látni fogjuk az iráni rezsim ellenségei elleni támadásokat” – mondta Salihu. Az sem biztató jel, hogy más csoportok – köztük a Foxtrot riválisa, a Dalen Network és a DZ Mafia is – átvették a kiskorúakat bevonó VaaS-módszert. Svédországban emiatt aktív vita folyik arról, hogy a kormány 14 évre csökkentené a büntethetőségi korhatárt, és több kiskorút küldene börtönbe, mint korábban. https://nypost.com/2026/07/27/world-news.text: See more of our coverage in your search results. Add The New York Post on Google Attorneys for social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate will meet with federal prosecutors in Miami on Monday to work out a schedule for the potentially monthslong process of fighting extradition to the United Kingdom, where the brothers are accused of rape and sex trafficking . A date for a bond hearing will likely be set during the status conference, along with other important dates like deadlines for filings and a formal extradition hearing. The Tates made a brief court appearance two days after their July 18 arrest . 4 Andrew and Tristan Tate after being arrested in Miami at an IBA Bear Knuckle Fights event at James L Knight Center by US Marshals. BACKGRID They aren’t required to attend Monday’s conference, and their attorneys said Friday that the Tates didn’t plan to be there . They’re being held in federal detention across the street from the courthouse. The Tates promote wealth, male dominance and misogyny through their social media empire and are among the world’s most polarizing internet personalities. The former professional kickboxers, who have dual US and UK citizenship, have millions of social media followers and are vocal supporters of US President Donald Trump. Explore More Sudden death of California law student studying abroad linked to popular weight loss shot Hitler’s $42M Luger — the ‘most valuable pistol on Earth’ — at center of sensational court battle Iran airs rare clip of supreme leader — but here’s why it does nothing to dispel dire health rumors The White House has said the brothers shouldn’t expect any help from the president. Asked Thursday whether the White House would intervene in the extradition process, press secretary Karoline Leavitt flatly rejected the idea. “No, we’ve already answered that question,” Leavitt said. The Tates’ attorney, Joseph McBride, said after last week’s hearing that they should remain in the US. 4 Attorney Joseph McBride speaks to the news media following a court hearing for his clients Andrew and Tristan Tate after they were arrested to face rape and sex trafficking charges against them in the United Kingdom, Monday, July 20, 2026, in Miami. AP Photo/Marta Lavandier “We are of course objecting to extradition because Andrew and Tristan are innocent,” McBride said. “They’ve never done nothing wrong. They shouldn’t be extradited for crimes they did not commit.” McBride said the extradition attempt is politically motivated and suggested the case involved former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s decision to step down, though he provided no details. Prosecutors in Britain said the new charges relate to four new accusers and were brought after authorities received evidence from police in Bedfordshire, in southeastern England. 4 In this courtroom sketch, Andrew and Tristan Tate appear with their attorneys before Judge Lauren Louis in Miami federal court, Monday, July 20, 2026, in Miami. AP The allegations, which span from 2010 to 2017, include rape, assault, trafficking and offenses relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” McBride said none of the latest accusers have been identified. The brothers are already charged with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012 and 2015. 4 Andrew Tate, left, watches his brother Tristan speak, outside a police station in Voluntari, Romania, May 21, 2025. AP Photo/Vadim Ghirda The new allegations are the latest in a long-running international legal saga involving the Tates that has spanned the US, Britain and Romania. The brothers have repeatedly denied wrongdoing. The brothers moved to Romania in 2016 and were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations, and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems. Travel restrictions were lifted last year, and they flew to Florida. Andrew Tate, 39, became known a decade ago when he was a contestant on the UK reality television show “Big Brother.” He was booted from the show when a video appeared to show him assaulting a woman. He has amassed over 10 million followers on X but has been banned from other platforms, including YouTube, TikTok and Instagram, for violating hate speech guidelines. He has made widely condemned comments, such as saying women who are sexually assaulted should bear some responsibility for the attacks and sharing graphic descriptions of how he might attack women. The Tate brothers have consistently denied allegations of abuse and human trafficking, claiming their violent and misogynistic statements have been taken out of context or were intended as jokes. https://www.merimbulanewsweekly.com.au/s.text: Vienna may not be the exact geographic centre of Europe on the map but it's pretty close, making it a perfect stepping-off point to other Euro capitals such as Prague and Budapest, only hours away by train. But don't rush to venture out of the Austrian capital - it boasts a vibrant cultural scene and some of the greatest historical architecture on the continent. The modern architecture is not bad either, as the bold shapes of the new 48-storey Danubeflats skyscraper attest. The A by Adina Vienna Danube Hotel, which opened in April last year, occupies the first five floors of the tower and is part of the revitalisation of this former industrial area along the Danube River, a 15-minute drive from downtown. The hotel is in the Donaustadt district. On one side is the Harry Seidler-designed Wohnpark Neue Donau apartments, and on the other, the Reichsbrucke bridge. Two U-Bahn subway stations are a 10-minute walk away - by far the easiest way to arrive. Car access involves a confusing series of underground ramps, which took my taxi driver three valiant attempts just to find the entry. The serviced-apartment hotel has lavish contemporary styling throughout. A by Adina is the first property in Euripe by Australian company TFE Hotels and the warm tones remind me of the natural landscapes of Australia, with some retro styling adding personality. Lottie's restaurant has an industrial feel with polished concrete, timber finishes and exposed piping, while the walls of windows showcase views of the Danube and city skyline. There are 120 rooms, ranging from studios to two-bedroom apartments, and all include a full kitchen. I'm in a 70-square-metre one-bedroom apartment with an enormous terrace. I'm travelling with only a carry-on bag and the bonus is the washer-dryer, in which I run a cycle while relaxing on a comfy sofa in a bathrobe. There are giant TVs in both the bedroom and the living room, and the Dreamcatcher king-sized bed lives up to its name - I sleep solidly, with blackout curtains keeping the 5am sunrise at bay. Lottie's has a bar and small-plates menu offering contemporary cuisine and a "touch of Australian flavours". Breakfast starts at 6.30am with both a generous buffet and a la carte options. But as good as the light scrambled eggs are, how can you start a day in this city without at least a strudel? Bar food is available from 5pm, and while the menu is small, the Karaage Crispy Chicken and Bao Buns are winners. A good way to wind down the day is with a signature Old Fashioned cocktail on the bar balcony, shaped a little like the bow of a ship. A sundeck runs the length of one side of the building, and at the pointy end is a heated infinity pool - perfect for catching the sunshine in the afternoon. Off the pool is a high-tech gym, probably one of the largest I've seen in a hotel, with machines, free weights, saunas and steam rooms. There's no shortage of parks nearby with a riverfront walk, the expansive Donaupark and Danube Island all a stroll away. For a trip to the local shops, it's a 30-minute walk to a Westfield, while downtown attractions are a 20-minute subway ride. Vienna is stunning and seeing it from a new perspective in this revitalised area adds another element to the experience. The writer was a guest of the hotel and travelled courtesy of Scoot

https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/gov.text: The Budapest Times Government pledges dialogue with Hungarians abroad at Petőfi memorial inauguration It is the duty of the Hungarian government to represent the rights of Hungarians living beyond the borders, which also means that these rights cannot be diminished, Zoltán Tarr, Minister for Social Relations and Culture, stressed on Sunday in Fehéregyháza, Transylvania, at the inauguration ceremony of the restored and expanded Petőfi memorial site. At the settlement near Segesvár, participants commemorated the 177th anniversary of the Battle of Fehéregyháza (also known as the Battle of Segesvár), which took place on 31 July 1849, and held the inauguration of the Petőfi memorial site — restored with Hungarian state support — along with the opening of the new permanent exhibition. The commemoration began with a festive church service at the Unitarian church, where Unitarian Bishop István Kovács led the prayer, followed by a sermon delivered by Reverend László Szabó. In his ceremonial address — his first visit to Transylvania as minister — Zoltán Tarr spoke about support policy and stated that the support provided by the motherland in previous years would be reviewed, and that in cases of abuse the necessary legal measures would be taken. According to the minister, the previous government used Hungarians living beyond the borders to extend its ideological and political influence. “We must ask for forgiveness — on their behalf too — from every deceived — forgive the expression — hoodwinked and fear-ridden compatriot living beyond the borders,” he said. “We ourselves promise our fellow citizens consultation and dialogue, conversations — because this is what there was no opportunity for over the past year,” he said. He added that it is his conviction that the parties, through conversation, can arrive at the common ground needed to make the Hungarian nation strong, brave, and hopeful once again. Speaking about the Battle of Fehéregyháza, which also resulted in the disappearance of Sándor Petőfi, he said that the Hungarian nation has been able to move beyond every oppressive regime and historical low point, and he believed that 2026 represents an opportunity for a new beginning for the Hungarian nation. Hungarian history contains countless periods that serve as reminders of how brave, free, and capable of anything for their homeland the Hungarians are, and this bravery and freedom is the shared national foundation that has held the nation together even in the most difficult of times — and it is from this that the future the current government wants to build also draws its strength, he said. He also touched on the fact that while many people know Sándor Petőfi, few truly know who he really was, and that the new permanent exhibition attempts to step away from the statue, from the cult author, and to rediscover the greatness and value of his life’s work through the lens of his disappearance and death. Hunor Kelemen, president of the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (RMDSZ), expressed his gratitude to members of previous generations who had tended the Petőfi memorial site near Segesvár even when there were no resources to do so or when it was outright forbidden. In the case of Sándor Petőfi, there is a danger that the person disappears behind the cult, he suggested, and reminded those present that Hungary’s greatest poet wrote significant poems in Partium and Transylvania, and that the Petőfi cult also originated there. “It was in Transylvania that he found love, and it was here that he fell in battle for his other love — freedom,” he recalled. He warned that freedom remains fragile in the 21st century as well, and that its preservation always depends on the contemporary generation: it must be defended and passed on. Freedom is always a matter of decision, courage, and recognition, and the Hungarians of Transylvania choose it whenever they stand up for their rights, build institutions, and refuse to let others decide on their behalf. There is no freedom without human dignity, and where the freedom of the individual is diminished, so too is that of the community, he said. In Transylvania, freedom means living it not against others, but together with them, he stressed. According to Ferenc Péter, president of Mureș County Council — which maintains both the Mureș County Museum and the Fehéregyháza museum operating as one of its subsidiary units — the task of the Petőfi Museum is to authentically preserve the poet’s legacy and make it comprehensible to future generations. Its renovation is the result of cross-border cooperation, “because Petőfi’s legacy cannot be confined within administrative borders,” he said. According to Petra Török, director of the Petőfi Literary Museum, which participated in the project as a partner, the new permanent exhibition also pays tribute to those heroes “who were not given a grave in the nation’s cemetery.” She recalled the heroes who died in the battle near Segesvár and their widows, and spoke about how the exhibition also presents material relics uncovered on the former battlefield. https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/otokar.text: Otokar begins Romanian-built COBRA II deliveries News Economy July 27 2026 09:55:04 Otokar begins Romanian-built COBRA II deliveries Deliveries of COBRA II 4x4 tactical wheeled armored vehicles produced entirely in Romania have begun for the Romanian Armed Forces, marking a new phase in Türkiye’s largest-ever single armored land vehicle export project. The program covers 1,059 COBRA II vehicles ordered by Romania. Following the delivery of vehicles manufactured in Türkiye, the first COBRA II units produced at the Automecanica Mediaș facility in Romania have now been handed over to the Romanian military. With serial production progressing as planned, Otokar ’s Mediaș facility has become the company’s manufacturing hub in Europe and its first production site within the European Union. The development gives Romania the capability to carry out all stages of production for a 4x4 armored vehicle rather than simply assembling imported components. More than 780 of the 1,059 vehicles ordered by Romania are scheduled to be produced in Mediaș over a five-year period. Around 300 vehicles have been delivered so far, while 216 units, including four new variants, are planned for delivery during 2026. Yusuf Fettahlıoğlu, General Manager of Automecanica Mediaș, said the Mediaș facility is expected to evolve into a regional land-systems hub capable of supporting future export opportunities within NATO and European Union defense programs, in addition to meeting the needs of the Romanian Armed Forces. The 140,000-square-meter facility has been equipped to NATO standards and operates according to the same production standards used at Otokar’s facilities in Türkiye. Since its introduction in 2013, the COBRA II has been selected by more than 20 users in 13 countries, including over 600 vehicles operated by NATO members. The vehicle is currently in service in 30 different variants worldwide. https://www.iefimerida.gr/english/greece.text: Greece's Foreign Ministry has expressed strong concern over repeated drone incursions into Romanian airspace, calling the violations a breach of international law and pledging full solidarity with Bucharest. "Greece expresses deep concern over the repeated incursions of unmanned aircraft into Romania's airspace," the ministry said in a post on X. "Any violation of the airspace and territorial integrity of a sovereign state constitutes a clear breach of international law and is unacceptable. We express our full solidarity with our EU partner and NATO ally, Romania." The statement did not specify the source of the drones or provide further details on the incidents. Romania, a NATO member bordering Ukraine, has reported multiple airspace violations in recent years attributed to drone debris and aircraft linked to Russia's war in Ukraine, prompting repeated protests from Bucharest and expressions of support from allies across the alliance. Greece's statement adds to a chorus of NATO members who have condemned airspace violations near the alliance's eastern flank amid heightened tensions over Russian military activity in the Black Sea region.

Europe Home page Europe 0 0 Euractiv: EU member states lift ban on imports of Russian sable fur 27 July 2026 11:13 (UTC +04:00) Imports of luxury Russian sable pelts may resume after EU member states lifted a ban that had only been introduced in April, Euractiv said, Ukrainska Pravda reports. The change was included in the latest package of EU sanctions against Russia agreed by Brussels last week. The European Commission justified the exemption by arguing that Russia dominates the global trade in sable pelts, leaving European manufacturers with very few alternative suppliers. "Apparently, it's very difficult to get them anywhere else," a senior EU official said. Italy and Greece, the two largest buyers of Russian sable pelts within the EU, pushed for the exemption, a European diplomat told the outlet. The sable is a small carnivorous mammal native to the forests of northern Asia. It is prized for its exceptionally soft fur and has long been sought after by Europe's luxury fashion houses. Russian sable coats can sell for tens or even hundreds of thousands of euros. According to Sojuzpushnina, Russia's only international fur auction house, Greek and Italian companies continue to rank among the leading international buyers of the fur, alongside Chinese and Russian firms. For example, Italian fur manufacturer Maurizio Braschi purchased the most expensive lot of sable at auction in September 2022 on behalf of Braschi, and again in May 2023 for a private client in Moscow, according to publicly available records from Sojuzpushnina. Meanwhile, imports of finished fur garments into the EU and exports of such products to Russia remain prohibited under sanctions introduced in 2022, alongside other luxury goods such as diamonds and caviar. In 2022, fur producers in Greece strongly opposed those sanctions, warning that they would amount to a death sentence for the industry. The exemption agreed last week restores access to raw Russian sable pelts, although exports of finished fur garments to Russia remain banned. The policy change comes as Brussels continues to consider the future of its own fur farming industry. An EU-wide ban on fur farming is being considered following a successful European Citizens' Initiative calling for an end to the practice across the EU as well as a ban on the import and sale of fur products. Only a handful of EU countries, including Spain, Greece, Hungary, Finland and Poland, still have fur farms in operation, although Poland has already adopted legislation to phase out the industry over the coming years. However, the European Commission has repeatedly postponed its decision, which had originally been expected in March. A draft proposal suggested that the Commission favours strengthening animal welfare standards instead of introducing a complete ban on fur production and import. After early F1 2026 pain for Aston Martin and Honda, hope arrived at the Hungarian Grand Prix as a 16-part upgrade for the AMR26 arrived. The results were positive. From comfortably last over recent rounds, Aston Martin got a car into Q2 courtesy of Fernando Alonso. During the Hungarian Grand Prix, Aston Martin went wheel-to-wheel with Williams, Alpine, and Haas as Lance Stroll finished 13th and Alonso 14th. That has helped lift the mood within the Aston Martin camp, especially as as the correlation between virtual and real world aligned for the upgraded AMR26. That correlation is important as it suggests that, going forward, Aston Martin can have confidence that future developments will yield the expected anticipated performance; not only for F1 2026 but into next year, too. The team has maintained a cautious outward approach despite positive early signs from the upgrades. Team owner Lawrence Stroll did though give a glowing review when speaking with Sky F1’s Martin Brundle ahead of lights out in Hungary. Conducting his iconic ‘grid walk’ segment, Brundle spotted and approached Stroll, who rarely gives interviews. “Lawrence, your car is going a bit better. Are you satisfied with the improvement with your car this weekend?” Brundle asked. Stroll confirmed: “Yeah, obviously we’ve made a very big step forward. One of many to come. So yes, very satisfied. “Thanks to all the hard work from all the boys and the girls at the factory to make it happen.” Stroll concluded that it was a “good start” to the recovery process for his team. https://www.romania-insider.com/veritas-.text: Education Business Views Verita's Strongest IB Results Yet and What the Diploma Is Really Teaching Students: 'The Goal Is Not Only to Acquire Knowledge, but to Think with Flexibility, Judgement, and Intellectual Curiosity' 27 July 2026 romaniainsider Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn As more Romanian families weigh international education options, the IB Diploma Programme stands out for combining academic breadth with independent research and critical thinking. Romania Insider spoke with Doria Draghiciu, Deputy Head of Secondary High School at Verita International School in Bucharest, about how the IB's inquiry-based approach differs from traditional education, how universities view the diploma, and the school's recent highlights, including its strongest IB results in recent years, with a cohort average of 32.2 points and one student scoring 44 out of 45. How does the IB's inquiry-based approach differ from more traditional models of education? Doria Draghiciu: The IB inquiry-based approach differs from more traditional models of education mainly in the way knowledge is constructed and used. In a traditional model, knowledge is transferred from the teacher to the student directly. The student uses it to solve some kind of exercise and is then assessed on whether they can reproduce that knowledge on a test. The IB does not reject knowledge taken in this way or direct instruction. In fact, strong inquiry cannot happen without subject knowledge. Where the IB differs is that it asks students to go beyond the acquisition of knowledge. Students are challenged to question, make connections, investigate and build models in unfamiliar situations, as well as reflect on the process of learning itself. In order to do this, the process starts from the practical experience and builds the abstract concepts afterwards. Students start with an applied example and find the general rules after identifying the patterns. In this sense, the role of the teacher is central and shifts from the traditional model. The teacher is still an expert and provides knowledge, explanation, feedback, and assessment, but the lessons are transformed into learning experiences that require students to be conceptual learners and independent thinkers. The goal is not only for students to acquire knowledge, but that they look at what they know with more flexibility, judgement, and intellectual curiosity. How do universities weigh the IB Diploma against A-Levels, AP, or national curricula in admissions decisions? Doria Draghiciu: Universities recognise the IB Diploma as a strong and challenging qualification, alongside A Levels, AP, and national curricula. Each system has its own strengths. A Levels allow students to specialise earlier, and AP offers flexibility, especially for students applying within the American system. At Verita, one of the reasons we value the IB Diploma is that it gives students both breadth and depth. Students study six subjects , so they continue to develop across languages, humanities, sciences, mathematics, and the arts or electives, while also going deeper in their Higher Level subjects. This means they do not close doors too early, but they still have the academic depth needed for competitive university courses. Through its Diploma Core , the IB also gives universities a fuller picture of the student. Through the Extended Essay (EE), students complete independent research. Through the Theory of Knowledge (TOK), they learn to question how knowledge is built and evaluated. Through Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), they engage with creativity, activity, and service beyond the classroom. So universities are not only seeing subject grades, but also evidence of research skills, critical thinking, time management, reflection, and balance. I would not frame the IB as better than every other system for every student. But I do think its advantage is that it prepares students very well for university life, not only because of what they study, but because of how they learn to think, manage work, and take responsibility for their own learning. How does Verita support students in their IBDP? Doria Draghiciu: At Verita, we support students in the IB DP through both academic and pastoral structures. Students have strong subject teaching, but they are also supported through Core time, TOK, CAS, Extended Essay guidance, mock exams, reflection meetings, academic tracking, university counselling, and individual follow-up. The DP is not only challenging because of the content. It is challenging because students have to manage deadlines, independent research, internal assessments, exams, CAS, and university planning at the same time. So our role is to help students understand the programme, plan ahead, and build the habits they need to manage it well. We also work closely as a team. Teachers, the DP Coordinator, the counsellor, learning support, parents, and students themselves are all part of the support system. Our aim is to help students become independent, but not isolated. They are expected to take ownership, but we give them the structures and guidance to learn how to do that. How do you involve parents in their child's DP journey? Doria Draghiciu: We involve parents by trying to make the Diploma Programme less mysterious. From the outside, the DP can look like just another school programme with final exams at the end, but it is much more layered than that. There are internal assessments, the Extended Essay, TOK, CAS, predicted grades, university applications, and deadlines that come at different moments across the two-year programme. So our role is to communicate clearly and early on, not only when something has gone wrong. We use parent information sessions , individual meetings, reports, emails, and follow-up conversations to help parents understand both the programme and their child's progress. I think parents are an important part of the DP journey, but their role is not to manage things for the student. Their role is to understand the pressure points, support routines at home, encourage balance, and help students become more independent over time. What were the school's highlights in the past academic year? Doria Draghiciu: The Class of 2026 delivered Verita's strongest IB Diploma results in recent years, marking the highest cohort average of 32.2 points. One student's near-perfect score of 44 out of a possible 45 points stands out as an exceptional achievement, placing them among the very top IB performers worldwide. One of the main highlights of the past academic year was our IB evaluation visit. It was an important moment for Verita because it allowed us to pause, reflect on the Diploma Programme, and look honestly at both our strengths and our next steps. The process confirmed many things we are proud of, especially our culture of care , our student support, and the way teachers work together around students. We also continued to strengthen the Core of the programme, especially TOK, CAS, and the Extended Essay. The TOK Exhibition was a real highlight this year. It was a hit with students, teachers, and the wider school community, and it gave students a meaningful opportunity to show how they are thinking about knowledge, perspective, evidence, and real-world objects. Another important highlight was the development of our university counselling programme, supported by the Dukes network, which has significantly improved the way we support students in thinking about pathways, careers, and university choices. This has made the process more intentional and has helped students and families have these conversations earlier and with more clarity. For me, the highlight is not a single event. It is seeing the programme become more intentional, more coherent, and more connected to who we are as a school. *This business view wast edited by Romania Insider for Verita. Fully operational since July 2024, the project benefits from a 25-year feed-in-tariff under Hungary’s “KÁT” scheme and is backed by a €35.5 million project finance facility. Closing of the transaction is expected until the end of 2026. PPC Group will have an option to acquire a co-located battery storage of 49.1MW / 196.2 MWh asset, subject to the project reaching Ready-to-Build (RTB) status. Greenvolt Power , one of the leading developers of large-scale wind, solar, and battery energy projects, and part of the Greenvolt Group, has signed an agreement to sell Kira, a 57.47 MWp solar PV park, located in Királyegyháza, southern Hungary, approximately 180 km from Budapest, to PPC Group, for a total consideration of €64.2 million . PPC will also have an option to acquire a 49.1MW / 196.2 MWh co-located battery storage project, subject to the project reaching Ready-to-Build (RTB) status, The solar PV project reached Commercial Operation Date (COD) in July 2024 and secured a feed-in-tariff (FiT) under Hungary’s 'KÁT' Scheme for a period of 25 years. It is also supported by a €35.5 million project finance facility with attractive margin conditions. 'Hungary has become a particularly active market for us, and this sale illustrates the strength of our platform in the country and our commitment to accelerating the energy transition in Central and Eastern Europe. Furthermore, this sale shows Greenvolt's ability to develop and deliver high-quality renewable energy assets across Europe ,' said João Manso NetoCEO of Greenvolt Group . 'This transaction reflects the growing confidence international investors place in the quality of our pipeline. Partnering with an investor of PPC's scale and ambition reinforces Greenvolt's positioning in Hungary, building on the momentum created by the recent inauguration of the Buj BESS,' said Spiros MartinisCEO of Greenvolt International Power . The buyer is a company of PPC Group, Greece’s largest power generation company, the country’s sole electricity distributor and largest power supply provider, which has been pursuing the expansion of its business portfolio in the Balkans and Central and Southeastern Europe over the past three years. The sale comes only weeks after Greenvolt inaugurated the Buj BESS, Hungary’s largest standalone battery energy storage system currently in operation, with 99.8 MW / 288.6 MWh of capacity. Together, the two milestones underline the pace and scale of Greenvolt Power’s activity in the Hungarian market and its role in supporting the country’s energy transition. Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Chinese industrial group Sany is considering opening a heavy machinery factory in Ghimbav, Brașov County, where it plans initially to assemble cranes, excavators, and other construction equipment, local publication Bună Ziua Brașov reported. According to the report, Sany representatives met Ghimbav mayor Ionel Fliundra on July 22 to discuss the conditions for the investment and the support the local administration could provide. The company is reportedly seeking to acquire an existing 20,000-square-metre industrial hall, allowing production to begin by the end of 2026. Mayor Fliundra told the company that the local administration would provide all support permitted under Romanian law. He also highlighted that Ghimbav has among the country's lowest property tax rates, a policy aimed at attracting investment. The mayor added that the area where the planned factory would be located is included in an infrastructure modernisation programme, which envisages the rehabilitation of Sânzienelor Street and the extension of water and sewage networks. The reported manufacturing project follows earlier plans by Sany to expand its presence in Romania's renewable energy sector. Chinese media reported in April that the group, through its Singapore subsidiary, was preparing an investment programme worth more than EUR 1 billionn in Romania. The project includes the development of two photovoltaic parks with a combined installed capacity of around 1.6GW in Uivar, Timiș County, a 2.34GWh battery energy storage system and a data centre with capacity of up to 70MW near Timișoara. If confirmed, the Ghimbav facility would mark Sany's first manufacturing investment in Romania and would complement the group's planned renewable energy projects in the country. iulian@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Pingan Yang / Dreamstime.com ) Read next 24 July 2026 Business Romanian manufacturer TeraPlast inaugurates polyethylene pipe factory in Spain Normal Business Chinese group Sany reportedly considers heavy machinery factory in central Romania 27 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? https://www.newsandstar.co.uk/news/26409.text: Business People Carlisle New market stall serving up Hungarian food in Carlisle By Matthew Graham Reporter Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A NEW market stall is serving up European flavours with a twist. Nokedli, a Hungarian street food stall, is now open inside Carlisle 's Market Hall serving up homemade Hungarian pasta and customisable salads and fries. Father-daughter team Laszlo (Les) and Szilvia Varga, who run the family-owned business, chose the location for its central location. More choices for customers (Image: Supplied) Szilvia Varga said: "Since moving to Carlisle eight years ago, the Market Hall has always been one of our favorite places for food. "It’s such a central and historical hub for the city and with recent renovations it’s only become a greater asset. "So when looking for a venue, it really was a ‘why not here’? question than a ‘why should we?’ question." The pair serve up nokedli, a Hungarian noodle dish that is lighter than traditional pasta and can be paired with a choice of sauces and toppings. Flavours include tomato, cheese, garlic mushroom, and butter and herb, with protein options such as chicken, steak, halloumi, or mushrooms. Customers can build their own bowl or choose from a set menu, with new specials featured weekly. For those looking for something different, noodles aren't the only option on the menu. They also serve customisable salads and fries, and drinks from a selection of canned drinks. They are currently exploring the addition of a coffee machine. Szilvia said: "The different flavours and opportunity to customise. "Nokedli is a versatile meal that can be mixed with different sauces and toppings. "So you can always have something new." The stall is open from Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 3pm. Some of the dishes on offer (Image: Supplied) All dishes are served in takeaway bowls, and lids are available for those who want to enjoy their meal elsewhere. The team have plans to expand the menu and introduce offers in the coming months. Szilvia said: "We definitely have a few ideas brewing in our pot. "We have our weekly specials and will be hosting online polls to see what people are most interested in. "The specials range from traditional Hungarian dishes (like lángos) to other cuisines, like chili con carne. "We are also looking into meal-deal offers, such as adding side salads with your main meal. "Desserts may also be in the works." The business encourages customers to follow updates and specials through social media or by stopping by the stall in person. Photograph: BC Wildfire Service/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Firefighters would traditionally get a break during nightfall, as cooler air would slow the burning, but this is no longer the case. Photograph: BC Wildfire Service/AFP/Getty Images Canada Canadian government steps in as ‘out of control’ wildfires force thousands to flee British Columbia battling 102 fires day and night across province, as breakneck speed hampers firefighters’ efforts Olivia Bowden in Toronto Sun 9 Aug 2026 14.20 EDT Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 00.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Canada’s federal government has announced it will provide urgent assistance to British Columbia after an onslaught of unprecedented fast-moving wildfires that killed one person and forced about 22,000 people to flee their homes in frantic evacuations. A total of 102 wildfires were raging across the province on Sunday, of which nearly half were categorised as “out of control”, according to the BC Wildfire Service. Of those fires, 78 ignited during the past week. The entire community of Summerland, about 30 miles (48km) south-west of the city of Kelowna and home to about 12,000 people, was evacuated overnight on Saturday, along with a further 8,000 people around nearby Peachland. About 10,000 others have been told to prepare to evacuate at a moment’s notice. Anette Boulet was among residents who fled Summerland along Okanagan Lake in British Columbia. As she and her family left around 4.30am Saturday, their home was shrouded in smoke. “You couldn’t see barely. It was just dark, and the ridge, the ridge of fire just coming towards you,” said Boulet, who evacuated to a centre in Penticton. “There’s no words to express it, the fear.” In a social media post on Sunday, Eleanor Olszewski, Canada’s minister of emergency management and community resilience, said she had “approved a request for federal assistance from British Columbia to provide shelter and accommodations for people who have been forced to leave their homes”. “I have tasked federal officials, led by the government operations centre at Public Safety ‌Canada, to work with the province to ensure support reaches those who need it most,” she ​said. Map Efforts to battle the Bald Range wildfire have been hampered by the breakneck speed of its spread. The blaze was first detected late on Friday evening, and grew within hours to more than 40 sq miles (100 sq km) – nearly twice the size of the island of Manhattan – as it raced nearly nine miles toward Okanagan Lake. The province’s premier, David Eby, declared a state of emergency late on Saturday, telling reporters that the blaze had been “like a bomb going off.” Cliff Chapman, BC Wildfire Service’s director of provincial operations, said the prolonged hot and dry weather the province has faced this summer had resulted in “explosive” fire conditions never seen before. Lightning caused by thunderstorms forecast this week could make the situation still worse, he said. Residents were shaken awake in the middle of the night to flee their homes. Jennifer Pascoa, who lives in Summerland, told the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation that she had begun to pack when she saw flames licking the nearby mountains. “It happened so quickly. We came home from the beach, we saw the plume of smoke, and then within an hour, the sky was covered in dark, black clouds,” she said. The British Columbia Wildfire Service said 10 standard helicopters and one night-vision helicopter were involved in the response. Thousands told to evacuate in British Columbia as wildfire grows The Royal Canadian Mounted Police, the country’s federal police force, said an 80-year-old woman died while trying to escape the wildfire that forced evacuations in the Okanagan Lake region. Mike Flannigan, a professor of wildland fire at Thompson Rivers University in Kamloops, BC, said the rapidity of the fires’ spread was indicative of increasingly extreme blazes springing up in Canada and the US. Southern BC and the pacific north-west in the US had had little to no rain in the past six weeks, leaving the regions “bone dry”, he said. “You walk through the forest, it crunches; if you look sideways, you start a fire.” These conditions were being driven by human-caused climate change, he said. “We’re seeing higher intensity fires today than the past … the shorter the timeframe, the more challenging it is.” Before this decade, fire agencies’ policy was that if a blaze was 20km (12 miles) away from a community, there was no cause for immediate concern. The ferocity and speed of these fires meant that such calculations no longer held, said Flannigan, warning that all homes in at-risk regions should have an emergency kit ready to go. “If a fire can run 60km in a day, you should be worried about it,” he said. The Bald Range fire was also an example of how fires could metastasise through the night, he said. Traditional firefighting practices would usually give firefighters a break during nightfall, as the cooler air would slow the burning. “That’s not the case any more. The fire roars through the evening, through the night, and we’re seeing this more and more,” he said. Drought and the sheer power and size of the fires during the day allow them to keep momentum even in the dark. Fire management agencies in BC and Alberta now fight fires after dark using night-vision helicopters. Current conditions indicated that the fire season in BC and the US states of Washington and Oregon could extend into the autumn, Flannigan said. “It looks grim … there’s no rain,” he said, adding that, like California, Canada may begin to have “fire years” instead of a summer fire season. “I’m scared for the coming weeks.” In the US, crews in Washington that for over a week have been fighting three wildfires that began burning in the Spokane area continued clean-up near containment lines. None of the fires were growing, officials said. The fires have damaged or destroyed about 920 structures. Earlier in the week a man was arrested and charged with intentionally setting the biggest of the three Spokane-area blazes. 1:12 Typhoon Dolphin batters parts of east and south-east Asia – video Extreme weather Typhoon Dolphin: more than a million people evacuated in China as record rainfall dumped on Shanghai Authorities warn that days of intense rain could trigger widespread flooding and landslides as storm moves north and further inland Yu-chen Li in Taipei Mon 10 Aug 2026 00.55 EDT First published on Sun 9 Aug 2026 23.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google More than a million people were moved to safety across eastern China by Sunday evening as powerful Typhoon Dolphin made landfall amid fears torrential rain would cause flooding and landslides. Wenzhou, a coastal city in Zhejiang province, said it relocated more than 900,000 people and opened more than 1,500 emergency shelters. In neighbouring Fujian, 98,900 people were moved from high-risk areas. Hong Kong records hottest day ever as Typhoon Dolphin fuels heatwave Read more In Shanghai, 215,600 people were moved from areas considered at risk by Sunday evening, substantially higher than an earlier figure of 30,300. A weather station in central Shanghai recorded nearly 313mm of rain in the 24 hours to 7am on Monday, its highest 24-hour rainfall in more than 150 years of records. Another station in the city recorded nearly 400mm. The hashtag “Shanghai turns into the sea” began trending on the Chinese social media platform Weibo, as videos circulated showing streets flooded around the Wukang Mansion, one of the city’s best-known tourist landmarks. The average rainfall recorded across Zhejiang from Friday evening to Monday morning reached 173mm, reportedly surpassing the levels seen during previous major typhoons including Lekima and Bavi. Dolphin weakened rapidly to a tropical storm by 5am on Monday. But as the storm continued to move northwards and farther inland, heavy rain was forecast across large parts of eastern and central China , extending north into Shandong and affecting Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Shanghai. Authorities maintained an orange alert for heavy rain and warned that days of intense rain could trigger widespread flooding and landslides through Wednesday, urging people to stay indoors during the heavy downpours. Forecasters in China predicted some areas could see 200-400mm (7.9–15.7 inches) of rainfall over the coming days. View image in fullscreen A temporary shelter in Hangzhou, where thousands of people were evacuated because of Typhoon Dolphin. Photograph: VCG/Getty Images The storm forced Shanghai’s two airports to cancel more than 1,300 flights. Public transport services, including many local trains, have been suspended in the financial hub. Zhejiang’s Ningbo international airport, about 150km south of Shanghai, will resume flight operations from midday (0400 GMT) on Monday. But the airport warned some journeys may yet be delayed or cancelled. Provincial capital Hangzhou resumed subway services on Monday morning, after halting some train operations on Sunday. Elsewhere, Dolphin fuelled intense heat over Hong Kong on Sunday, pushing the city to its highest ever temperature of 36.9C . The extremely hot weather was expected to continue into Tuesday, officials said. In Taiwan, ferry services were suspended and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds on Sunday. Dolphin earlier swept through Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and ⁠cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings. In the Philippines, the typhoon did not make landfall in the country’s north but intensified the seasonal monsoon rains, which flooded many areas of the main northern Luzon region, including around Manila. Scientists say global warming has made extreme weather more likely, including more powerful typhoons. Photograph: Avalon/Universal Images Group/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Scientists suggest this summer has been ‘a clear example’ of climate breakdown intensifying extremes that reinforce each other. Photograph: Avalon/Universal Images Group/Getty Images Extreme heat World’s seas have hit hottest temperature on record for July, say scientists Average sea surface temperature outside polar regions was highest on record for July, beating previous high in 2023 Ajit Niranjan Sun 9 Aug 2026 22.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The world’s seas were hotter last month than in any July on record, scientists have said, as devastating heat struck western Europe . Sea surface temperatures hit record highs for July on the Atlantic coast and western Mediterranean, the EU’s Copernicus climate change service found, with severe marine heatwaves roiling Europe’s seas. Globally, the average sea surface temperature outside the cold polar regions was the highest on record for the month, beating the previous July record set in 2023. World’s oceans losing their greenness through global heating, study finds Read more Surface air temperatures around the world in July 2026 were marginally cooler than July 2024 – by just 0.01C – leading scientists to consider the two months as the joint-second warmest Julys on record. Western Europe has experienced its hottest June-July period on record, data shows, with “exceptional” heat driving wildfires that devastated swathes of the Mediterranean. The first two summer months of 2026 were 2.79C hotter than usual, the Copernicus said on Monday, beating the previous record set four years ago and reflecting the “exceptional persistence of heat” since the season began. Central Europe is reeling from a heatwave in which national temperature records fell in a handful of countries including Austria and Slovakia. It is the latest in a scorching summer that has dried out vegetation and primed the continent to burn. Samantha Burgess, a climate scientist at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, said this summer had been “a clear example” of climate breakdown intensifying extremes that reinforce each other. July temperatures per year “[As] persistent high-pressure systems trapped heat over western Europe, the extreme temperatures also amplified widespread drought,” she said. “As soils dry out, they lose their ability to provide natural cooling, allowing heat to build more readily.” Supercharged by fossil fuel pollution, a string of heatwaves have hit Europe since the end of spring, with particularly brutal heat at the end of June expected to have resulted in more than 10,000 deaths. Copernicus said widespread dryness observed in May and June intensified last month, with exceptionally low rainfall and soil moisture in much of western Europe. Across the dry regions, which include France, Spain, and parts of Germany and the UK, low river flows hit water supply, irrigation and power plants, including in countries downstream. Short of cooling water, two coal-fired power plants were forced to shut in Poland last week, as well as Hungary’s sole nuclear power plant, for the first time in its 44-year history. Heat and drought are among the biggest environmental threats to Europe’s economy. Early estimates for this summer suggest the June heat cost grain farmers €2bn in lost crops. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Down to Earth The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential Preview latest after newsletter promotion The longer-term damage can eclipse short-term losses, economists warn, particularly if droughts persist over many years. The mega-drought of 2015-18 cost Europe €439bn, a new working paper led by the CMCC European Institute on Economics found, with high but short-lived hits to agriculture and low but persistent impacts on manufacturing and construction. The researchers argue that conventional methods substantially underestimate drought-related economic losses as they fail to capture the years after. Marta Mastropietro, a researcher at CMCC and the Polytechnic University of Milan, and lead author of the study, said: “Even a single dry year causes real economic damage, but a persistent drought is different: its effects can compound across sectors and keep accumulating for years afterward. “That intersection between compounding and long-lasting impacts is what conventional impact estimates tend to miss.” About half a million hectares have burned across the EU since the start of the year, data published by the European Forest Fire Information System shows, accompanied by above-average pollution as burning vegetation spews thick smoke. The hot, dry and windy conditions that make it harder to battle blazes has set new records for severity for this time of year. Víctor Resco de Dios, a professor of forestry engineering at the University of Lleida, said: “Climate change is creating increasingly favourable conditions for the development of mega-wildfires. “The good news is that through vegetation management and urban planning we can largely mitigate the problem,” he said. “However, we must be clear about one thing: what seems extreme to us today will be remarkably benign in a few decades if we continue to fail to take the necessary adaptive measures.” Explore more on these topics Extreme heat Oceans Europe news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: The religious right stormed the restricted area in July, apparently with the support of Benjamin Netanyahu. Photograph: Ilia Yefimovich/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The religious right stormed the restricted area in July, apparently with the support of Benjamin Netanyahu. Photograph: Ilia Yefimovich/AFP/Getty Images First Edition newsletter Israel Monday briefing: How the new phase of confrontation at al-Aqsa signals a challenge to the status quo In today’s newsletter: ​Jerusalem’s most volatile site has again become a flashpoint, with Arab states and former Israeli officials sounding the alarm over Benjamin Netanyahu’s complicity Hettie O'Brien Mon 10 Aug 2026 01.45 EDT Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 01.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. In late July, Itamar Ben-Gvir, West Bank settler and far-right extremist minister of security in Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, joined a group of more than 2,000 Jewish extremists to storm al-Aqsa mosque compound, Jerusalem’s most sensitive holy site. The far-right group has been doing this for years. Ben-Gvir has made series of visits to the site over the last three years, eroding norms and inflaming tensions. Jordanian officials have recently warned that it could be at risk of an “imminent” Israeli takeover. With national elections scheduled in October, and many eyes still firmly on Gaza (this weekend, Netanyahu rejected a US-backed 15 point plan for peace), the Israeli government appears to be racing to expand Israeli settlements and accelerate ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in the West Bank and East Jerusalem before its mandate expires. For this morning’s First Edition, I spoke to our senior international correspondent, Julian Borger , about the latest incursions, and how Israeli extremists are trying to create a new reality in Jerusalem. That’s after the weekend roundup. Weekend roundup UK politics | Sadiq Khan has called on the government to commit to revamped climate action and to reduce the UK’s reliance on oil and gas, as the UK endures a summer of drought, wildfires and heatwaves. US politics | The US Senate voted to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general in a win for Donald Trump, who will now have his one-time personal attorney sitting atop the nation’s law enforcement apparatus. US-Israel war on Iran | Iran has issued tough new demands for reopening the strait of Hormuz, as a deal to open the strategic waterway remained out of reach on Saturday. Russia-Ukraine | Up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed in Russia, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said . On Saturday, Turkey called for a “moratorium” on attacks by Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea after a series of strikes on civilian ships there World news | The alleged leader of the Kinahan organised crime group was extradited from Dubai on Sunday and met by a huge security operation in Dublin, marking the end of a global game of cat and mouse with European, US and Gulf authorities. In depth: ‘To erect structures, even if they’re temporary, is a red rag to a bull’ View image in fullscreen One of the most contentious places on earth. Photograph: Tamir Kalifa/Getty Images The al-Haram al-Sharif site in Jerusalem’s old city, known to Jews as the Temple Mount, is one of the most contentious places on earth. It’s governed by a fragile agreement that gives Muslims exclusive rights to pray and worship there, while Jews pray at the Western Wall below. But Israel’s messianic right, which has gained a powerful foothold in Netanyahu’s coalition government , is fixated on the site as a symbol of its political project. Their vision of building a new Jewish temple on one of Islam’s holiest sites – once a fringe idea – has become increasingly widespread. Since 2023, Jewish religious extremists have made numerous visits to the 35-acre compound which is home to both al-Aqsa mosque and Dome of the Rock, the holiest sites for Muslims in Jerusalem and one of holiest sites for Muslims in the world. “At first, you had groups of perhaps 20 Jews, mostly settlers, who were escorted by the police to the far wall of the compound to pray discreetly,” Julian tells me. “If you were just a casual visitor, you wouldn’t necessarily see them”. Over the last two years, however, the groups have grown bigger and more audacious. On 23 July, they sang the national anthem, and prayed and performed rituals in the centre of the compound, while Israeli police – who report to Ben-Gvir, who was in attendance – set up tents to provide shade to the worshippers. “To erect structures, even if they’re temporary, is a red rag to a bull,” Julian says. “The longstanding fear is that Israelis would knock down the Dome of the Rock or the mosque, or rebuild a [Jewish] temple on the site. And these tents were part of a gradual attempt to push the boundaries.” Eight Arab nations swiftly issued a joint statement condemning “mass incursions by settlers led by extremist Israeli ministers”. Last Wednesday, the Jordanian authorities, who administer the site, held an emergency meeting of Arab and Islamic nations to discuss these risks, and afterwards, the Jordanian authorities condemned Israeli violations and warned that they constituted a “blatant provocation” to Muslims worldwide. “All they can do is issue strong statements, saying, ‘don’t do this’,” says Julian. The Waqf, the Jordanian-appointed foundation that manages the site, is “defenceless”, he explains. In the run-up to Ramadan this year, Waqf sources told the Guardian that five of its staff had been detained by the Shin Bet, Israel’s counterintelligence service. Meanwhile, Israeli police have begun actively recruiting extremist activists to serve in the Temple Mount Unit, the force responsible for policing the compound. According to Haaretz , the deputy commander of the police’s Temple Mount Unit published a callout to officers on social media and in WhatsApp groups associated with West Bank settlers. “Anyone who wants to take part in implementing sovereignty is welcome to contact me,” he wrote. Why is the site so significant? The site’s history is constantly enlisted in attempts to justify the present. Muslims know the raised compound in the south-east of Jerusalem as al-Haram al-Sharif (the Noble Sanctuary), or simply al-Aqsa, after the mosque located at its southern edge. Next to the mosque, at the centre of the compound, is the Dome of the Rock, one of the oldest surviving Islamic places of worship. It’s on this site the prophet Muhammad is said to have ascended to heaven. At the base of the compound is the Western Wall, a section of retaining wall that survived the destruction of the second Jewish temple in 70CE. The Temple Mount is also the holiest site in Judaism , the site of two temples which were built and then destroyed by invaders in ancient times. Access to the site has been delicately managed for centuries. After the six-day war in 1967, when Israel captured East Jerusalem from Jordan, the Israeli government agreed that Jordan would continue to be the site’s custodian. Since then, the “status quo”, as it is known, has sought to prevent violent conflict by circumscribing the rights of Muslims and Jews to access the compound. While Jews are permitted to visit the site at specific times, they cannot pray there. Many Jews opt not to visit the site, out of fear of treading on holy ground while ritually impure. “The status quo represented a historic compromise. Jews got the Western Wall. Muslims got Haram al-Sharif,” Julian says. “But the site has always been a detonator, sitting right there in the centre of the old city, with strong religious beliefs crammed together in a small area.” How has this erupted in the past? It’s not uncommon in the region for holy sites to be carefully managed with intricate arrangements. Elsewhere in the Old City, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre is divided up between six Christian denominations, with its keys held by two Muslim families. At the Cave of the Patriarchs in the occupied city of Hebron, a mosque and synagogue share one building. Past Israeli moves to challenge the status quo at al-Haram al-Sharif have been incendiary, sparking deadly violence. In 2000, then Israeli opposition leader and future prime minister Ariel Sharon made a visit to the site in an attempt to demonstrate Israeli sovereignty, sparking a chain of events that helped ignite the second intifada. More recently, Hamas gave the name “ al-Aqsa flood ” to its attack on Israel in October 2023 that killed 1,200 Israelis and triggered the war on Gaza, claiming it was provoked by Israeli violations at the Jerusalem mosque. What’s the end goal of these incursions? Some Jewish extremists have begun marching under the temple flag – a star of David overlaid with a picture of the (as yet nonexistent) third temple they hope to build. “You see these flags on the bulldozers that are flattening neighbourhoods in Gaza, and soldiers wearing patches with a picture of the third temple on them,” Julian says. The rise of the third temple movement comes at a time of surging attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank , with the scale of violence prompting urgent calls for intervention from the heart of the Israeli establishment. Earlier this year, dozens of Israelis , including two former prime ministers, former heads of its security services and former judges, signed a “final warning” threatening legal action against their government over its support for “Jewish terrorism” in the occupied West Bank. They argued the actions of the government had isolated Israel internationally and put its security at risk. “There’s a feeling that the far-right side of Netanyahu’s government is now creating unnecessary, long-term security problems for Israel,” Julian says. That extends to attempts to change the status quo at al-Aqsa. Netanyahu has publicly backed Jewish prayer at the site, claiming that changes pushed by Ben-Gvir were coordinated with him . “This isn’t the stuff of radicals any more,” Julian says. “It has government approval.” The week to come Wednesday | A partial solar eclipse will be visible across the whole of the UK, with the south-west of England getting the best of British views. Parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain will experience a total eclipse. Thursday | Clacton-on-sea residents will vote in the byelection Nigel Farage triggered last month, with the Reform leader taking on 33 mostly novelty candidates. Results are expected early Friday. Thursday | The Office for National Statistics will publish UK GDP figures for the second quarter of 2026.
