Liliana PÃ©rez Ocampo and her family escaped moments before their home was rocked by a 7.4 magnitude quake on Monday. "At first, we thought it was just a mild tremor like the ones that usually happen in Colombia, but when more than 30 seconds passed and everything was shaking harder, we realised it was an earthquake," the mother-of-four told the BBC World Service. Her family, including two young children at school, are safe. "In the end, material things can be replaced," she said. "The most important thing is life, and we have that." With at least 169 people killed, this has been the strongest earthquake to hit Colombia in the 21st Century, according to the country's Geological Service. More on this story. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8en.text: Image source, Anadolu Agency/Getty Images Image caption, Protesters hold cardboard figures with ropes round their necks during a rally against the death penalty in Beirut, Lebanon in October 2013. By Samantha Granville Beirut Published 3 hours ago Lebanon's parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, a move that would make it the first country in the Middle East to formally end capital punishment. A majority of MPs in the 128-seat parliament backed the measure on Tuesday, while Hezbollah's parliamentary bloc voted against it. The legislation will now go to the cabinet before being passed to President Joseph Aoun for signing. The government has already expressed its support for the measure. Lebanon has not carried out an execution since January 2004, although courts have continued to hand down death sentences. Rights groups estimate that more than 78 people remain on death row. Under the new legislation, capital punishment will be replaced with life imprisonment with hard labour. However, the legislation does not yet set out in detail how the new sentence would be enforced. Hard labour is already written into Lebanese law but has rarely been implemented in recent years. The country's financial crisis and overcrowded prisons have limited the authorities' resources and capacity. The latest legislation follows years of campaigning by civil society groups and lawyers for the removal of capital punishment from Lebanese law. "We cannot solve a crime with a crime or end violence with violence," Oragit Younan told the BBC. As co-founder of the Lebanese Association for Civil Rights, she led a nearly three-decade campaign to abolish the death penalty in Lebanon. "We are in a war, and people [have been] killed every day, so even in this situation, we can fight, we can struggle for human rights, and we can win. We can be a model for others," she said. Tuesday's vote in parliament follows more than two decades of a de facto moratorium on executions. An execution required a decree signed by the president, prime minister and justice minister - but no such decree has been signed since 2004. Under Lebanese law, the death penalty could previously be imposed for some of the country's most serious offences, including aggravated murder, certain terrorism-related crimes resulting in death, treason, espionage and offences against state security. Previous attempts to abolish the death penalty have failed, including legislation introduced in parliament in 2004 and a proposal from the justice ministry in 2008. Lebanon's move comes as the use of the death penalty remains contested elsewhere in the Middle East. Jordan resumed executions in June, carrying out its first since 2017. In Israel, its parliament has approved legislation that allows for the expansion of the circumstances in which capital punishment can be imposed. Israeli MPs passed a new law in May to impose the death penalty and conduct public trials for those involved in the Hamas-led attacks and mass hostage-taking in Israel in October 2023. Elsewhere, the UN human rights chief has said he is alarmed by the rise in executions in Iran, with capital punishment continuing to be used "to instil fear among the population and suppress dissent". In Iran, at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests, UN human rights chief Volker TÃ¼rk said earlier this month. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/clye.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, AndrÃ¡s Baka served for 17 years as the Hungarian judge at the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg By Nick Thorpe in Hungary Published 22 minutes ago Hungary's parliament has elected AndrÃ¡s Baka, 73, a respected judge and former head of the Supreme Court, as head of state. The Hungarian president is a largely figurehead role, but Baka's rule promises to be tempestuous. His task will be to monitor Prime Minister PÃ©ter Magyar's efforts to dismantle the interlocking economic and political powerhouse established by former Prime Minister Viktor OrbÃ¡n. He will also oversee the writing of a new constitution, to replace OrbÃ¡n's constitution of 2011. "We cannot build the new Hungary on revenge," AndrÃ¡s Baka told Parliament, after he was elected by 140 votes to 6. "The majority of society now feels a sense of liberation and hope. Others feel disappointment and uncertainty," he said. "In a democratic society, this is not an anomaly, but a natural state of affairs." All 51 MPs belonging to OrbÃ¡n's party Fidesz walked out of the chamber before the vote, in protest against the ousting of their favourite, TamÃ¡s Sulyok, from the post last month . In his speech, AndrÃ¡s Baka promised the broadest possible debate on the creation of a new constitution. Since taking office in early May, the new Magyar government has lost no time attacking OrbÃ¡n's legacy. Twenty-seven laws have been passed, and two amendments to the constitution. The states of emergency - migrants, Covid, and war in Ukraine - which OrbÃ¡n used to govern by decree, were all cancelled. The Sovereignty Protection Office, which the Fidesz government used to attack critical journalists and NGOs, was abolished, and an National Asset Recovery and Protection Office was established, with sweeping powers to investigate and prosecute individuals accused of stealing state funds under the former government. Fidesz accuses the Tisza government of establishing a "tyranny". Ironically, they removed Baka from his post as president of the Supreme Court in 2011, for attempting to stop them undermine the rule of law. Public service radio and TV have been off air since 9 July , as news programmes are revamped. The stated aim is to restore their independence, from their Fidesz-era role as government propaganda organs. Other key changes came under Amendments 16 and 17 of the constitution, limiting the prime minister to two terms in office, and MPs to three. The ability of the Constitutional Court to oversee acts of parliament, taken away by Fidesz, was also restored. If the Tisza majority expects Baka to be a tame president, they may get a rude awakening. In a BBC interview before he was asked to take the post, he made clear he opposes the limitation of MPs' terms as an intrusion on the right of voters to freely choose their representatives. Baka served for 17 years as the Hungarian judge at the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. "I am not a political man," he told the BBC last month. "I got involved in politics through my professional, legal way of thinking." Baka was elected today as a transitional figure. Under the constitutional amendment which made his presidency possible, the new president will likely only be in place until the new constitution comes into force - or for maximum of five years. Speaking to parliament on Tuesday, Baka made it clear that he intended to push back against the Hungarian tendency to trust in powerful leaders. "The state is not there for itself," he said, at the end of his speech. "It is there for the people." Related topics Hungary More on this story What does new Hungarian PM PÃ©ter Magyar stand for? https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckg9.text: Image caption, Images of the damaged vessel have been verified by the BBC By Yolande Knell ,Â Middle East correspondent Â and Â Michael Sheils McNamee Published 11 August 2026, 14:35 BST Updated 3 hours ago Four people have reportedly been killed in an attack on a small cargo ship in the Red Sea suspected to have been carried out by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, the internationally recognised government of Yemen has said. If confirmed, it would be the first deadly strike by the group on a vessel since the US and Israel started a conflict against Iran. Yemen's transport ministry said the ship was hit with three ballistic missiles, south of the port of Mocha, causing a fire on board and resulting in the deaths of four crew - three Pakistanis and one Indonesian. The Houthis began attacks on shipping last month - announcing a naval blockade of Saudi ports. They have not admitted carrying out the attack. The conflict in the region has been ongoing since the end of February, punctuated by a faltering ceasefire which was meant to lead to a deal to end the war. It has whipped up regional tensions, with the Houthis also attacking Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and oil facilities, in parallel with Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz - the vital waterway where a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit. The attack comes after a years-long truce in Yemen's civil war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government collapsed last month. The Houthis control much of north-western Yemen, and frequently clash with the government. The government operates out of Aden in the south, due to the capital Sanaa being held by the Houthis. Social media images examined by BBC Verify appear to show a damaged cargo ship in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which sits at the inlet of the Red Sea, off the coast of Yemen. In its statement, the Yemeni government said the ship had been carrying food, and that the attack on a commercial vessel marked an escalation in approach from the Houthis. In an earlier statement, maritime risk management company Vanguard said the Yemeni Navy deployed to assist the vessel and came under fire. This resulted in three others being injured. Close-up pictures show the vessel is named Tihamah which, according to ship-tracking platform MarineTraffic, is in the Red Sea off Warner Point. Vanguard has identified the ship as sailing under the flag of Tanzania, while shipping website MarineTraffic says it is owned by an Egyptian operator. In its statement, Yemen's ministry of transport referred to Tihama as a "Yemeni commercial ship", while earlier reports in Iranian media referred to it as "Saudi-affiliated". The pictures of the vessel, which were shared by Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency, have been verified as new and show no signs of AI-generation. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/11/magy.text: Menü Kereső Kijött a közlöny: augusztus 19-től új köztársasági elnöke van Magyarországnak Belföld Weiler Vilmos Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Kedden este megjelent a Magyar Közlöny idei 109. száma , amely egyetlen országgyűlési határozatot tartalmaz: azt, amely szerint Országgyűlés Baka Andrást választotta Magyarország köztársasági elnökévé. A határozat elfogadásakor lépett hatályba, az államfő azonban csak augusztus 19-én lép hivatalba. A közlöny vonatkozó része így néz ki: Forrás: Magyar Közlöny Baka Andrást, a Legfelsőbb Bíróság volt elnökét kedden 140 igen, 6 nem és nulla tartózkodás mellett, titkos szavazással választották meg Magyarország köztársasági elnökévé. A Fidesz és a KDNP már korábban közölte, hogy nem vesz részt az új államfő megválasztásában. De ki is Baka András, aki egy ilyen éles és konfliktusos helyzetben veszi át az államfői posztot? Baka András az emberi jogi, kisebbségi jogi kérdések kutatója. Neve akkor vált különösen ismertté, amikor 2011-ben jogellenesen eltávolították a Legfelsőbb Bíróság éléről, miután bírálta az Orbán-rendszer igazságszolgáltatás átalakítására vonatkozó terveit. Baka András 1952-ben született Budapesten. 1978-ban az ELTE Állam- és Jogtudományi Karán szerzett jogi doktorátust, majd több mint húsz éven át a Magyar Tudományos Akadémia (MTA) Állam- és Jogtudományi Intézetének tudományos kutatójaként dolgozott, később az Államigazgatási Főiskola főigazgatójaként tevékenykedett. 1991 és 2008 között két cikluson át volt az Emberi Jogok Európai Bíróságának bírája. Az 1980-as évektől az Egyesült Államok több egyetemén volt vendégprofesszor, és többször hívták meg előadni Franciaországba és az NSZK-ba is. Baka a rendszerváltás utáni első parlamenti ciklus elején, 1990–1991-ben az MDF országgyűlési képviselője volt, de a pártba nem lépett be. Szakszervezeti múlttal is rendelkezik: 1988–1990 között a Tudományos Dolgozók Szakszervezetének (TUDOSZ), 1989–1990 között az Értelmiségi Szakszervezeti Tömörülésnek (ÉSZT) volt az elnöke. Baka 2016 júniusában jogerősen pert nyert az Emberi Jogok Legfelsőbb Bíróságán. A testület megállapította, hogy Baka András főbírót azért menesztették idő előtt személyre szabott jogalkotással a tisztségéből, mert szakmai minőségében nyilvánosan kritizálta a bíróságok függetlenségét veszélyeztető lépéseket. Később az Európa Tanács Miniszteri Bizottsága felelősségre vonta a magyar államot azért, mert 2016 óta nem hajtotta végre a Baka kontra Magyarország ügyben hozott strasbourgi ítéletet. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/08/11/neme.text: Menü Kereső Kedden a hannoveri repülőteret kellett lezárni egy azonosítatlan drón miatt Külföld Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Egy drón miatt keddre virradó éjszaka leállt a légi forgalom a hannoveri repülőtéren. A futópályákat, valamint a reptér körüli légteret több mint két órán keresztül időszakosan lezárták. A hannoveri repülőtér az NDR közszolgálati csatornának azt közölte, hogy 3:44 és 5:20 között több rövid idejű lezárásra is sor került. Egyes időszakokban mindkét futópályát érintette a korlátozás. Az incidens miatt hat utasszállító járat késéssel indult, egy tehergépet pedig másik reptérre irányítottak át. A Spiegel egy belső rendőrségi jelentésre hivatkozva azt írta, hogy az esettel kapcsolatban nem zárható ki a hibrid tevékenység. Ugyanakkor a dokumentum szerint nem világos, hogy van-e összefüggés a múlt heti lipcsei drónincidenssel . A Spiegel által idézett jelentés szerint a szövetségi rendőrség figyelmeztető rendszerei nem érzékelték a drónt. A német légi forgalmi irányítás szintén nem tudta bemérni az eszközt. A repülőtér munkatársai azonban többször is látták a drónt. A jelentés szerint ebből arra lehet következtetni, hogy nem kereskedelmi forgalomban kapható, hagyományos modellről volt szó. Ezt az a körülmény is alátámaszthatja, hogy az eszköz körülbelül két órán keresztül a levegőben maradt. Az NDR megkereséseire sem a szövetségi, sem a hannoveri rendőrség nem válaszolt. A beszámoló szerint a nyomozást időközben a rendőrség államvédelmi osztálya vette át. A lipcsei incidens után Alsó-Szászország belügyminisztere, Daniela Behrens kifogásolta, hogy a szövetségi kormány nem tervezi saját drónelhárító rendszer telepítését a hannoveri repülőtérre. Alexander Dobrindt szövetségi belügyminiszter tájékoztatása szerint Észak-Németországban csak a hamburgi repülőtéren tervezik drónelhárító rendszer kiépítését. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/08/11/oros.text: Menü Kereső Találsz egy férfit, meghal, kapsz 8 milliót. Sokan csinálják így, szokásos eljárás lett Külföld Legfontosabb Friss katonasírok az oroszországi Jefremov városában 2023 márciusában – Fotó: Natalia Kolesnikova / AFP Nyilas Gergely Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „És ha megölik a maguk férjét, mit tegyenek? Mintha máskor nem halhatnának meg. Hát, pénzt kapnak!” – Oroszországban három éve még magyarázkodnia kellett Pavel Rakov kapcsolati tanácsadónak, amikor arról beszélt férjezett asszonyoknak, vőlegényre vágyó nőknek, hogy milyen előnyük származhat abból, ha kedvesük a frontra megy Ukrajna ellen harcolni. Ma már kevésbé kellene magyarázkodnia: az orosz–ukrán háború ötödik évére egész iparág épült a frontra vonulók fizetésének és haláluk esetén a kártérítési pénznek a megszerzésére: csak időben kell házasságot kötni. Az orosz közbeszédben őket nevezik fekete özvegyeknek. Ennek is vannak azonban fokozatai. Van, aki csak sikeresen ismerkedik, de olyan is van, aki hadsereget átszövő korrupciós kapcsolatok révén utána is tud nyúlni a katonának, befolyásolva a túlélési esélyét. „Találsz egy férfit az SZVO-ról. Meghal, kapsz 8 milliót. Sokan csinálják így, szokásos eljárás lett, vesznek belőle valami olcsó kis lakást. Ez egy üzleti modell” – osztotta meg tapasztalatait Marina Orlova ingatlanügynök az Oroszországban különleges katonai műveletnek nevezett háború rövidítését használva. „Vannak rá coachok, jogászok. Erkölcsi akadály nincs, ha pénz van.” Halottpénz 2022 őszén Oroszországban részleges mozgósítást rendeltek el – ezt egyszer merte megtenni a Kreml, de a társadalmi elutasítás kockázata miatt azóta a magas fizetést ígérő toborzásra épít. Azt viszont nem lehet kizárni, hogy a szeptember 20-i formális, de mégsem teljesen tét nélküli parlamenti választások után ezt ismét elrendelik, Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök szerint az ukrajnai titkosszolgálati információk is erről szólnak. A mozgósítással együtt akkor életbe léptették a gyorsított házasságkötést lehetővé tévő szabályozást: hirtelen mozgósított fiatalok ezrei nősültek meg. Ez még nem a fekete özvegyek időszaka volt, hiszen a mozgósítás váratlan volt, ezeket a házasságokat jellemzően egymást valóban ismerő párok kötötték. A gyorsításra módot adó szabályozás azonban érvényben van azóta is, így jelentek meg a fekete özvegyek, akikkel a katonák a szerződéskötés előtt vagy már a szolgálat ideje alatt, az eltáv vagy a sebesülés miatti lábadozás idején kötnek házasságot, akár egyetlen nap ismeretség után. Jekatyerina a negyedik férjét harmadik férje temetésén ismerte meg. Az előzővel sem élt túl sokat, mert a férfi szerződésesnek állt, és néhány hónap múlva meghalt a fronton. A nőnek egy hónappal korábban még sikerült meghatalmazással hozzáférést szereznie a férje számlájához, így már a halála napján leemelte a szolgálatért addig összegyűlt 2,5 millió rubelt (kb. 10 millió forintot), majd a halál hivatalossá tétele után megkapta az ötmillió rubeles kártérítést is. A férfi anyja a bíróságon támadta meg a döntést, mondván, a házasság nem volt valódi, érdemben nem éltek együtt. Első fokon az özvegynek adtak igazat, így az ügy most a másodfokú döntésre vár. Eközben a temetésen megismert negyedik férj anyja hasonló igénnyel fordult a bírósághoz. Az ő fia Jekatyerinát rövid ismeretség után vette el, és másnap már ment is vissza a frontra. Néhány hónap múlva ő is eltűnt a fronton. Holttest nélkül a nő még fél évig semmiképp sem számíthatott juttatásra, de ő számított az elsődleges jogosultnak. Hogy megkapja-e, kérdés, mert az év végén az előző férj ügyében mégis gyanúsítottá vált a meghatalmazás alapján leemelt 2,5 millió rubel miatt. Ugyanígy eljárás indult egy 38 éves nő ellen, aki a fronton meghalt 60 éves férje után tartott igényt a pénzre. Kiderült, hogy a házasságot egy hamis terhességi igazolás nyomán kötötték, a férj felnőtt fia végül elérte, hogy a pénzt ne a semmiből megjelent feleség kapja. A nőt most hat év börtön fenyegeti, mert az ügyészség szerint a hamis terhességi igazolással csalást követett el. A legtöbb ügy azonban általában polgári peres eljárásban zajlik a „fekete özvegyek” és a halott katonák korábbi családjai között. Újoncok búcsúznak hozzátartozóiktól egy moszkvai toborzóközpontban a 2022-es részleges mozgósítás idején – Fotó: Sefa Karacan / Anadolu Agency / Getty Images Ezek az ügyek ma már mindennaposaknak számítanak, bár így is van, amelyiket jobban felkapja a sajtó. Például Angelina Varjuhina ügyét, aki talán az életet élvező instafotóinak sokaságával tűnt ki a fekete özvegyek sorából. De talán azzal is, hogy rövid életű férje az ukrán hadsereg által Oroszország területén hosszú hónapokig fenntartott kurszki kiszögellést felszámoló, ezért a Kreml által kiemelt hőstettként tálalt „ csővezeték-akcióban ” halt meg. Georgij Kosztirko 2024 augusztusában vette el Varjuhinát, októberben már nem is beszéltek, miután a férj családja szerint a nő fotói alapján nem úgy tűnt, hogy a feleség a szó morális értelmében is házasságnak tekintené a kapcsolatot. Igaz, Varjuhina nyilvános instája alapján ez nem egy fél óra alatt lezavart házasságkötés volt, hanem méretét tekintve valódi esküvő, amelyet másfél éves ismeretség előzött meg. Az orosz sajtó mégis tényként kezeli, hogy a nő legalábbis számításból ment férjhez. Ám amilyen könnyű megkötni a házasságot, olyan nehéz felbontani, Kosztirko a frontról ezt még kevésbé tudta érvényesíteni. Végül 2025 februárjában kimondta ugyan a bíróság, hogy a házasság március 25-től már megszűnik, ám Kosztirko március 9-én meghalt. Varjuhina igyekezett özvegysége jogán érvényteleníteni a válásról szóló döntést, igényt tartva a halott férj után járó juttatásra. A bíróság azonban a katona édesanyja mellé állt, így Varjuhina elesett az özvegyi juttatásoktól. Azaz a pénzt az édesanya kapja. Ezek az ügyek azonban minden elemükben súlyos társadalmi értékzavart jeleznek: elvégre, miközben gyászoló anyák, feleségek szerepelnek a halott katonák körüli vitákban, valójában az Ukrajna ellen indított támadó háborúba önként, magas fizetésért hadba vonulókról és a pénzért ezt támogató szülők, rokonok, feleségek marakodásáról van szó. Az állam teremtette meg a helyzetet A Vlagyimir Putyin által indított háború a társadalmi mobilizáció meghatározó elemévé vált. Arról ebben a cikkünkben olvashat bővebben, hogy az orosz elnök milyen ideológiát körít és milyen szerepet szán a háborút megjárt, akár börtönből amnesztiáért cserébe a frontra vonuló katonáknak. A szolgálat jellegétől függően 100-300 ezer rubel közötti fizetések, a szerződéskötéskor felvehető egyszeri juttatás százezreknek jelentett vonzó alternatívát, főleg azoknak, akik a hátrányos régiókban, érdemi képzettség nélkül legfeljebb a 27 ezer rubeles minimálbérre számíthatnak, ha van munkájuk egyáltalán. Nemcsak nekik vonzó, hanem családjuknak vagy épp azoknak, akik az Oroszországban csak különleges katonai műveletnek nevezhető háború résztvevőire, orosz rövidítéssel SZVO-s partnerre pályáznak. „Keresem az én kis SZVO-skámat, Kszenyija, 28”, „Szeretem a virágokat és a szusit, kedves vagyok és okos, keresem a saját SZVO-somat, Inga, 32” – hasonló hirdetések sokaságát lehet találni az orosz közösségi oldalak társkereső csoportjaiban. A cikk elején idézett társkapcsolati tanácsadó arról is beszélt a női hallgatóságnak, hogy mi a teendő, ha a férfi nem akar a frontra menni. „Menjenek maguk a hadkiegészítési parancsnokságra és mondják, hogy én tudok megfelelő férfit. Mondják meg a nevét, lakcímét, munkahelyét” – javasolta nevetést aratva. Igaz, később azzal védekezett, hogy a mondatot kiragadták a kontextusából, valójában egy kérdésre válaszolt, hogy mi a teendő, ha a partner haszontalan alkoholista, aki csak terhére van az egyedül gürcölő feleségnek. A lényegen azonban ez nem változtat: az állam a felemelkedés ígéretét adta meg a háborúval. A seregbe jelentkezőnek is, halála esetén pedig a családnak – vagy annak, aki épp jókor kötött házasságot a katonának állóval. Ezt Putyin még a gyászoló anyák előtt is remek érvnek gondolja. „Van, aki csak teng-leng, észrevétlenül telik el az élete. Élt, nem élt, mindegy is. De az önök fiai éltek. Értik? Ők elérték a céljukat. Nem hiába távoztak az élők sorából” – mondta az elnök. A bizarr vigasztalás az egyenlőtlen helyzetben bejön: a fiukat, férjüket gyászolók nem győznek köszönetet mondani Putyinnak , talán az elismerő szavak és talán a pénz miatt is. Fekete öves fekete özvegyek A frontra jelentkezéstől anyagi felemelkedést remélő katonák befűzésére építő iparágnak van azonban egy sokkal szervezettebb változata is, amelyhez a hadsereget átszövő korrupciós hálózat is kell. Alekszandr Poliscsuk a 60-as gépesített dandárnál volt zászlós tavalyi letartóztatásáig. A gyanú szerint a dandárhoz tartozó egység könyvelőnője, valamint egy őrmesteri rangban lévő kolléganője Poliscsuk feleségével közösen legalább két férfit szervezett be a hadseregbe, majd hozta nekik össze a házasságokat. A feleség szerepét a könyvelőnő és az őrmesternő vállalták, egyiküknek ehhez előbb valódi férjétől is el kellett válnia . A cél az volt, hogy a meglehetősen képzetlen és ami még fontosabb, elsődleges örökösök nélküli fiatal férfiak bevételeit megszerezzék a házasság és az ennek alapján adott meghatalmazások révén. Haláluk esetén a védelmi minisztériumtól és az állami biztosítótól összesen 13 millió rubelre (kb. 52 millió forintra) is jogosultak voltak a feleségek, akik elosztották a pénzt Poliscsukékkal. Ebben a két esetben csak a fizetéseket és egyéb juttatásokat, mert a két katona az eljárás elindításakor még biztosan életben volt. A háború orosz áldozatainak emlékfala 2026 februárjában – Fotó: Hector Retamal / AFP A házasságra a bakákat itt nem feltétlenül a szerelem illúziója vette rá, hanem az az ígéret, hogy katonai kapcsolataik révén a feleségek biztosítják, hogy ne kelljen részt venniük a legveszélyesebb bevetésekben. Ez viszont azt jelenti, hogy az ellenkezőjét is el tudják érni. Erről, ha nem is fekete özvegyekhez kötve, de az egyes egységek parancsnokainak esetében már a Kreml-párti katonai bloggerek is beszéltek: szerintük rendszerré vált, hogy az alárendelt katonák nagyobb eséllyel kerülnek az első vonalba, ha nem fizetnek zsebbe közvetlen felettesüknek. Mindenki cinkos „Ezek az összegek mindenkit felbolygatnak. A katonáknak, a nőknek, a hadkiegészítésnek, mindenkinek a legfontosabb motivációja a pénz. Az államnak a jóra kellene ösztönöznie. Nálunk a rosszra ösztönöz” – mondta a jelenségről Jevgenyij Sztupin. A jogász emlékeztetett arra, hogy az ország lakossága alapvetően szegény, sokakat nyom a hitel vagy épp a hitelképtelenség. Ebben a helyzetben az állami propaganda központi eleme a toborzáshoz a pénz, a milliós összegek mindenütt látványosan virítanak az utcai plakátokon. Szerinte ez az erkölcstől elszakadó kapzsiság a társadalom minden rétegében megjelenik és erősödni fog. Szerinte ennek jele a fekete özvegyek megjelenése is. Vannak ugyan velük szemben indított hatósági eljárásokról szóló hírek, de az igazi visszhang nem ez: „Az emberek készek pénzért harcolni, készek a pénzért harcba küldeni gyerekeiket, férjeiket. Nincs társadalmi tiltakozás. Van egy olyan érzésem, […] hogy a fekete özvegyekről inkább irigykedve beszélnek” – mondta Borisz Pasztuhov. A Londonban élő politológus szerint Putyinnak egyelőre megvan a lehetősége arra, hogy a pénzzel motiválva toborozzon, bár kérdés, hogy ez elég-e ahhoz, hogy havonta 40 ezer újabb embert vonzzon be a frontra és még nagyobb kérdés, hogy ezzel képes-e változtatni a fronton inkább stagnáló és az orosz erőket is kifárasztó helyzeten. Pasztuhov szerint az ország gazdaságához mérten ezek az egyéni szinten vonzó összegek aprópénzt jelentenek – de arra épp elegek, hogy rendszer épüljön rájuk, amíg a társadalom nagyobb része perspektívát, nem pedig zsákutcát lát benne. Mindeközben az orosz hadsereg halottakban és súlyos sebesültekben mérve becslések szerint közel másfél millió embert veszített, anélkül, hogy eredeti katonai céljait, Ukrajna kapitulációját vagy Ukrajna teljes fekete-tengeri partvidékét vagy legalább a Donbasz egészét megszerezte volna. https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2026.text: Prague’s rare 70 mm IMAX draws thousands of Europeans for Nolan’s 'The Odyssey' PRAGUE (AP) — With Christopher Nolan’s highly anticipated “The Odyssey” recording impressive sales around the globe, thousands of Europeans have used it as a new and unexpected reason to visit Prague. The Czech capital has a movie theater that's among the few dozen in the world equipped with the coveted 70 mm IMAX screen to watch the first feature made entirely with IMAX film cameras. “It completely changed my experience about the movie," said Nicolas Walak from Poland, who also saw the movie before on a normal screen before viewing it in Prague. "Everything was great. It was a great movie.” Czech cinema adapts to meet demand for rare IMAX format There are only 41 70 mm IMAX screens worldwide, with most in North America. Montpellier in France and the Belgian capital, Brussels, are the only other two in the European Union countries. Britain has another three. To meet massive demand, the Czech branch of the Cinema City offers four to five screenings a day, one starting after midnight, and the majority are sold out. Film fans from about 15 European countries, from Scandinavia to Spain, have been coming to watch “The Odyssey” in Prague, Cinema City said. Their number reached 22,000 by Monday, it said. The 70 mm IMAX film presentation is Nolan's preferred format. The Oscar-winning filmmaker calls it the “best possible experience.” Moviegoers travel up to three days to Prague Daniel Jung drove with his two teenage sons, Felix and Leo, for three days from Norway through Denmark and Germany "just to see this movie. Tomorrow, we’re going back.” Leo was in touch with Cinema City by email half a year before the July 16 premiere and followed the cinema operator on Instagram. He managed to book the tickets immediately after they became available. “We were in the 11th row, right in the middle. We had the very best seats,” Leo said, calling the effort “absolutely worth it.” “It’s just so big. We come from Norway, the screens we have are much smaller,” he said. “Now, we watched it in this huge format. I will always remember this experience.” Felix said they had a good time on the way, visiting some places in Germany, but it would be worth it even if they just drove straight there. Few IMAX left because of costs and other challenges Due to the cost and other challenges, productions made using large format film are rare. The IMAX cameras are heavy and new versions with reduced noise had to be developed to be usable for making “The Odyssey.” The film print sent to theaters is so big — weighing some 300 kilograms (661 pounds) and 18 kilometers (11 miles) long — that it has to be delivered to theaters in parts. The movie and the projector have to be in a climatized room and the projectionists need to be approved by IMAX for the job. As movie theaters around the globe were acquiring digital IMAX equipment around 2008, the Cinema City decided not to get rid of the original analog projector in Prague. It was placed in a corner for three years until 2012 to screen Nolan’s “The Dark Knight Rises.” It was used to show several others, including Nolan's “Interstellar” in 2014 and “Oppenheimer” three years ago. “We’re really grateful to him for that,” projectionist Tomáš Vyšinský said about his predecessor who saved the equipment. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/gen.text: NATO Member Romania Shoots Down Stray Drones From Ukraine War After Years Of Incursions July 28, 2026 8:00 pm No Comments Since Russia’s full invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the war has repeatedly spilled across Romania’s border as drones violate the airspace of the neighboring European Union and NATO member. Now Romania is trying something new to stop the incursions: shooting down the drones. Romanian pilots shot down the first of three drones in as many days from F-16 fighter jets starting Friday as Russia intensified attacks against Ukraine near the border. After determining the drones were of Russian origin, Romania summoned Moscow’s ambassador in protest and expelled a Russian diplomat on Monday. Drones have crossed into Romanian territory multiple times from Ukraine to the north and east, including in May when a drone injured a mother and child after crashing into an apartment block in the eastern town of Galati along the Danube River. Romanian authorities largely responded by scrambling jets, collecting debris, erecting fallout shelters near the border and frequently admonishing Moscow for its war spilling into its territory. Romania and Poland also acquired the MEROPS system, which fires short counter-drones to take down incoming stray drones, following a spate of incursions along NATO’s eastern flank late last year. Drones have crossed into the territories of multiple EU countries, but have been a persistent problem for Romania’s leadership in the capital Bucharest. At least 19 have entered Romania’s airspace this year, while there have been 50 cases of drones or drone fragments identified on its territory since the war started in 2022, according to Romania’s Ministry of National Defense. Romanian President Nicusor Dan on Sunday congratulated the Romanian pilots for downing the drones and blamed Russia for the incursions. “It is unacceptable and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romanian airspace,” he said. Romania shifts the approach to stray drones Despite passing legislation last year to shoot down drones in its airspace, which was strongly opposed by nationalist political parties, Romania has avoided shooting them down until now. Romanian military analyst Radu Tudor said the May drone incident in Galati may have “changed something in the Romanian authorities’ mentality” in how to approach the issue. “This was somehow a kind of psychological trigger, in order to say: ‘OK, enough is enough,’” Tudor said. “Until now, it probably was an Allied decision in NATO not to respond with firepower, because it was somehow a danger of escalation.” “I think it’s not only a change of attitude of Romania, I think it’s a change of attitude in NATO,” he added. Before the three interceptions over the past week, Romanian pilots also shot down a stray Ukrainian drone above Estonia in May. Romanian pilots and planes are based in Lithuania to provide broad strike capabilities for NATO. “They saw so many signals that Russia is trying to provoke NATO,” Tudor said. “Romania is the only NATO country who shot down four drones on the eastern flank — three on Romania and one in Estonia.” The message sent to Moscow mirrors a statement by NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at the organization’s summit in Ankara, Turkey, earlier this month: “‘Don’t play with us’.” Russian diplomat expelled In response to the drone incursions, Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Russia’s ambassador in Bucharest on Monday and presented him with fragments of a drone, saying Moscow “bears exclusive responsibility for all these grave incidents.” The ministry also expelled a member of the Russian mission, who was given five days to leave the country. “The Russian side learned what they already knew: the drones downed on Romanian territory belong to them,” Foreign Minister Oana Toiu wrote in a post on X. “Drone fragments recovered by the Ministry of National Defence and the ongoing prosecutor investigation confirm their Russian origin beyond any doubt.” The Russian embassy in Romania responded in a statement posted on its Facebook page, saying Russia “has never directed and does not direct combat drones” to Romanian territory and denied the allegation as “completely unfounded.” “An unprovoked expulsion of a Russian employee will not go unanswered,” the embassy said. Tactical shift to down errant drones Cristian Popovici, the Romanian defense ministry’s head of public relations and a former air defense officer, said tactics have been developed to eliminate errant drones. “We recorded more than 100 attacks with drones near our border with Ukraine, and many of them resulted in debris or even drones that penetrated our airspace,” he told The Associated Press. “Our pilots and our air force, we developed the tactics, procedures, and now we can face and we can eliminate this threat.” The change began when Romanian pilots shot down a drone over Estonian airspace and from that point the military applied “lessons learned” and had a “100% rate success in three days with three drones,” Popovici said. Despite the new approach to stray drones, Popovici said Romania does not plan to become entangled in the war between Russia and Ukraine. “We are in a peacetime, we are not involved in this fight,” he said. “If Russia wants to escalate with NATO, it’s up to them. I’m not sure it’s a wise move now.” (AP) Leave a Reply You must be logged in to post a comment. (Photo by Wojtek RADWANSKI / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski has warned that mounting economic and military pressure on Russia could make Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin increasingly dangerous, saying Moscow should end its “criminal misadventure” in Ukraine “before it’s too late.” “The Russian economy is beginning to suffer. Russians can’t pretend that it’s an external, special military operation anymore,” Sikorski said in an interview with TVP World’s On the Record program on Tuesday. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . But Sikorski cautioned against interpreting Russia’s growing difficulties as meaning the threat from Moscow is disappearing. “A sick man with a gun is still a man with a gun,” he said. “That’s why we are spending so much money on defense, in order to convince Putin that any conflict with Poland would cost him even more dearly than his criminal war with Ukraine.” Advertisement The Polish foreign minister said Putin’s “desperate” situation could push him to do “something risky,” as speculation grows over whether Moscow could seek to escalate the war before possible negotiations. Could Russia expand the war beyond Ukraine? Asked about warnings that Russia could eventually expand the conflict further west, Sikorski acknowledged the debate over whether some of those fears have become exaggerated. But he made clear that Warsaw cannot afford to assume Putin will behave rationally. Other Topics of Interest US Senate Delivers Overwhelming 86-12 Bipartisan Backing for Russia Sanctions as Zelensky Watches Zelensky’s Capitol visit coincides with a decisive push to squeeze Moscow’s energy revenues and raise the cost to Russia of continuing the war. “If Putin does something irresponsible, like the invasion of Ukraine, we will respond – definitely, ourselves,” Sikorski said. “His capabilities are clearly less than we had thought, but his intent is even worse.” That assessment, he suggested, is based partly on what the war has revealed about the limits of Russian military power compared with expectations before the full-scale invasion. At the same time, Sikorski argued that Putin’s intentions have proven more aggressive than many Western governments anticipated. Advertisement “He clearly doesn’t have a realistic picture of the geopolitical situation and his prospects,” Sikorski said. He described Putin as “clearly misinformed,” arguing that a Russian leader with an accurate understanding of Moscow’s situation would have greater reason to seek a deal. “The question is whether Putin is ready for a deal,” Sikorski said. Escalate before de-escalating? Sikorski was also asked about the possibility that Russia could intensify the war precisely as preparations for eventual negotiations accelerate – effectively attempting to escalate before de-escalating. The discussion also turned to the risk of further Russian escalation, including broader use of North Korean troops and a possible new mobilization drive after Russia’s September elections. Sikorski said North Korean forces are already part of Moscow’s war effort under the military treaty between Russia and North Korea. He noted that the Kremlin claims the Ukrainian territories it occupies are Russian territory – a position Moscow could use to justify deploying North Korean troops there under the agreement. “That’s a very nasty example of collaboration between two authoritarian countries,” Sikorski said, questioning what Pyongyang is receiving in return for the losses suffered among North Korean personnel. Advertisement He also challenged the assumption that another Russian draft would automatically strengthen Moscow’s forces. Conscripts, he argued, are fundamentally different from contract soldiers who voluntarily sign up to fight, making a new mobilization potentially more politically and militarily risky for the Kremlin. For Warsaw, the larger concern is therefore not simply whether Moscow has enough military capacity for another major escalation, but whether a Russian leadership under increasing pressure could nevertheless decide to take a dangerous gamble. Sikorski said the possibility that Putin “may be desperate and may do something risky” should not be dismissed. Russia weaker than feared, but still dangerous The comments underline an apparent paradox in Poland’s assessment of Russia after more than four years of full-scale war. Moscow has failed to demonstrate the level of conventional military power many Western governments feared before February 2022. But for countries on NATO’s eastern flank, that does not automatically translate into greater security. Instead, an economically strained Russia facing continued Ukrainian resistance and growing pressure on its energy sector could become less predictable. Advertisement Sikorski’s warning comes as Poland continues to invest heavily in its armed forces and deterrence against Russia, with Warsaw portraying those expenditures as necessary to ensure that Moscow understands the cost of any confrontation with a NATO member. Sikorski welcomes shift in Washington Sikorski also pointed to what he sees as an encouraging shift in Washington’s approach to the war. “The fact the US has now recognized that Ukraine has cards and made extraordinarily successful efforts to level the playing field is a good sign,” he said. His comments came as Zelensky visited Washington on Tuesday for the funeral of late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham, one of Ukraine’s most vocal supporters in Congress. Zelensky also held a private meeting with US President Donald Trump at the White House, where the two discussed efforts to revive negotiations with Russia and Ukraine’s push for an agreement allowing it to produce Patriot missile interceptors domestically. ‘Honor’ Graham with Russia sanctions Sikorski specifically called on Trump to follow the change in rhetoric with stronger economic measures against Moscow. He said he hoped Trump would “honor” Graham by finally adopting additional sanctions against Russia. The US Senate on Tuesday was preparing to begin consideration of a bipartisan Russia sanctions package that Graham had spent his final days trying to advance. The legislation is aimed particularly at reducing the energy revenues that continue to finance Moscow’s war. The meeting marked Zelensky’s first visit to Poland since the two countries’ diplomatic fallout over a military unit’s honorary UPA title in June. by Kyiv Post | July 29, 2026, 10:06 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk addresses the press at the end of the meeting of state leaders of the European Group of Five (E5) and the NATO Secretary General, on June 24, 2026. (Photo by Ludovic MARIN / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in Lublin on Wednesday, July 29, marking his first trip to Poland since the historical dispute over a military unit’s title strained ties between the two countries earlier in June. Zelensky detailed the meeting in a statement on Telegram, saying the talks covered bilateral relations, defense cooperation, and the safety of Ukrainians seeking refuge in Poland amid Russia’s full-scale invasion. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Zelensky said “protecting our cities and communities from brutal Russian strikes” remains a top priority, with anti-ballistic defense standing out as the most urgent. “Our cooperation strengthens both our region and all of Europe,” Zelensky continued, adding that “Ukraine’s security and protection also mean Poland’s security and protection.” Advertisement A visit clouded by months of tensions The Lublin meeting comes after weeks of strained relations between Kyiv and Warsaw , triggered by Ukraine’s decision to grant an unit of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) the honorary title “Heroes of the UPA,” a reference to the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which Poland blames for the mass killings of Polish civilians in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia during and after World War II. Critics have framed the dispute as ultimately serving Russia’s interests, arguing that the focus should shift from historical grievances to the present threat Moscow poses to NATO and Europe, rather than allowing old wounds to divide them. Other Topics of Interest Ukraine to End VAT Exemption on Imported Goods Bought via Foreign Marketplaces Ukraine’s government says the change would align Ukraine with EU rules, although the new tax regime would not start before 2027. Wednesday’s meeting confirmed both sides are working to move past the diplomatic fallout. On July 17, Zelensky announced a five-point plan aimed at strengthening ties with Poland, pledging to grant the country access to Volhynia files . Defense and refugee on the agenda Zelensky said he briefed Tusk on the outcome of recent diplomatic engagements in Washington, during which he met US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office at the White House on Tuesday, July 28. He discussed Patriot missile production with Trump, focusing mainly on the Washington-granted license which would allow Ukraine to manufacture the systems domestically. Advertisement Around the same time on Tuesday, Zelensky announced discussions on joint weapons production with Lockheed Martin . On July 23, joint cooperation with Raytheon was unveiled as well. However, no specific timeline for launching production was given, nor were further details about the proposed arrangement disclosed. Beyond military matters, Zelensky said the leaders addressed the wellbeing of Ukrainian refugees living in Poland. “It is important that Ukrainians who left their homes and found shelter in Poland feel safe,” he wrote. Hate crimes surge amid diplomatic fallout Following the dispute between Kyiv and Warsaw, hate crimes against Ukrainians living in Poland have increased. Several attacks were recorded in recent weeks, including an assault on a couple and separate incidents involving teenagers targeted on multiple occasions. The rise in hostility comes as a new poll suggests eroding Polish support for Ukraine on several fronts. According to a survey conducted Wednesday, July 29, 52% of Poles oppose backing Ukraine’s bid for EU membership, while 65% reject the idea of sending Polish troops to help oversee a postwar ceasefire. Advertisement On military aid tied specifically to the UPA dispute, opinion is more evenly split – 44% favored suspending support over the row, compared with 41% who wanted assistance to continue. Trustee Eric Ungaro said at the meeting that the trustees had approved several projects and purchases earlier in the year despite warnings from Fiscal Officer Paul Canter, who said they may come close to their yearly budget. “We knew we were going to be running tight, cause in Poland Township, we don’t carry over $5 million like the state; I mean, they’re in the billions, we just run our budget late, and we do what we have to do,” he said. The township is projected to overspend by $1,678 at the end of the year according to their 2027 tax budget. Ungaro says the first thing trustees did upon learning of a deficit was to discontinue projects that had not yet begun. One of the purchases was a new police cruiser that trustee Edward Kempers suggested they return. The trustees also dismissed seasonal workers for the time being. “We have to do something, I don’t know if it’s personnel… I’m guessing from this point forward, we’re buying nothing that is not essential for the safety of our community,” Kempers said. The idea of a police levy arose during discussions, though one has not passed in the Township for 30 years. Canter tells 21 News that one of the biggest reasons for the deficit is the way the police department is funded. Currently, the Poland Township Police Department is partially funded by the Township’s general fund, while the other portion comes directly from local property tax revenue. The trustees do not plan to fill any vacant positions in the police department, and part-time workers are expected to reduce hours. Trustee Frank DeMain, who attended the meeting virtually, says that there is no guarantee that a levy would pass. “If we put a levy on and they vote it down, in my opinion, the residents are saying ‘Hey, we want you to do less with less or as much as you can with less’,” he said. Canter says that the township has yet to receive real estate tax revenue from the county due to changes to property tax laws that have delayed advanced collections. He adds that the township was required to fill out a tax budget for the first time in 20 years due to new state laws. Previously, the county had waived the requirement for townships to fill out tax budgets in the middle of the year. The Poland Township Trustees did not take any action at Tuesday’s meeting after Trustee Frank DeMain was unable to attend in person. Ungaro tells 21 News the trustees plan to hold another special meeting next week to discuss the financial situation and possibly make cuts. ​ Download the WFMJ app for your Apple or Android smartphone or tablet to get our push alerts as news happens. Popcorn and Inspiration ‘Madame Curie’: Radiating Resilience This drama tells how a scientist and her husband work together to make great scientific discoveries. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Pierre and Marie Curie in the laboratory, circa 1904 and come to life in a 1943 film. Public Domain Rudolph Lambert Fernandez 7/28/2026 | Updated: 7/28/2026 0:00 X 1 NR | 2 h 4 min | Drama | 1943 Since the early 20th century, the world’s vastly improved understanding and use of radiation has transformed several fields, from medical imaging and cancer therapy to atomic energy. The heavily fictionalized biopic, “Madame Curie,” traces that back to the pioneering 19th-century discovery and study of radium and radioactivity by scientist Marie Curie, and her husband and colleague, Pierre. Impoverished Polish student of physics, chemistry, and mathematics, Marie Sklodowska (Greer Garson) excels at Paris’s University of Sorbonne. Finding her too reclusive for her own good, Prof. Jean Perot (Albert Bassermann) introduces her to a similarly shy, scientifically minded Frenchman, Dr. Pierre Curie (Walter Pidgeon). They conduct their respective experiments in Pierre’s lab. Marie Curie (Greer Garson) in her lab, in "Madame Curie." Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Intrigued by Dr. Henri Becquerel’s (Reginald Owen) discoveries, Marie becomes engrossed in examining how pitchblende gives off rays even independent of the sun. Pierre starts to share her obsession. Lab work blossoms into love, then marriage. Marie gives up her dream of returning to Poland to teach and stays in Paris. Together, they brave the scientific establishment’s prejudice against women leading scientific discovery. Marie braves potentially cancerous burns from prolonged radiation exposure. Through a back-breaking process of trial and error, she discovers a new element: radium. Related Stories ‘Madame Curie’: The Radiance of Shared Discovery Scientists: From the Great to the Lesser Known After four years, having started by processing eight tons of pitchblende, the couple runs over 5,000 sequences of crystallization, distilling out element after element, before isolating radium. They then start to unlock the phenomenal power of radiation. Marie Skłodowska Curie, circa 1920. Public Domain Director Mervyn LeRoy understands the laboratory is a lonely place, prone to silence and seriousness, and wary of impetuousness. Its unglamorous setting, tuned to repeated failure and only rare success, is perfect for the studious, even the socially awkward. Sensitively, he shows how Marie and Pierre, hiding themselves in work, end up finding each other. Poster for "Madame Curie." Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Respect and Warmth Does LeRoy overdo the romance? Perhaps. But he rightly intuits that had there not been a deep bond of respect and warmth between the real-life duo, they couldn’t have collaborated as effectively as they did. He even allows a tinge of humor to lighten the otherwise abidingly grim mood. Once, while toiling away in his dank, drab lab, Pierre presents Marie with one of the first copies of his new book. But with the flourish he lends that gesture, he might as well be brandishing a bouquet. Not to be outdone, Marie reacts as if admiring a fresh cut of flowers. Slowly, she reads out the book’s title: On Symmetry in Physical Phenomena, Symmetry of an Electric Field and of a Magnetic Field. Pierre’s face glows, as if he’s struck a home run. (L–R) Marie Curie (Greer Garson), Jean Perot (Albert Bassermann), Pierre Curie (Walter Pidgeon), and Dr. Becquerel (Reginald Owen), in “Madame Curie.” Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pidgeon brings his usual gravitas to this performance, reflecting Pierre’s admiration for his wife’s critical thinking, resourcefulness, and eagerness to learn from failure. Garson and her famously upturned eyebrow carry the film by projecting Marie’s spirit of originality alongside her morbid self-doubt and simmering despair. In one scene, Marie is reeling from a shocking turn of events. Garson brings such a sense of devastation to Marie’s bearing, that she sits unblinking, in a single take, for a full four minutes. This is while fellow-actor Bassermann is pacing the room, trying to inspire Marie with an impassioned speech on the virtues of resilience. Unsurprisingly, Garson’s Best Actress Oscar nomination was one of the seven nominations this film secured. Nobel Scientist The real-life Marie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person to win a Nobel twice, and the only person to win a Nobel in two distinct sciences: physics and chemistry. The Curies were the first duo to win a Nobel as a married couple. Marie Skłodowska Curie, circa 1920. Public Domain Marie refused to patent their discoveries so that the global scientific community could freely build on their research. Today, radioactivity is measured using the “curie” unit, named in their honor. Good scientists like Thomas Edison or Louis Pasteur become great not by dedicating a mere year or two but by their entire lives to truth-seeking. Importantly, in a speech she delivers here, Marie frames scientific inquiry as a quest for truth. Why does she feel science possesses great beauty? It allows for seemingly inconsequential individuals to grasp an element of truth that, together with what others uncover, reveals a greater, higher truth. Where does science’s “spiritual” strength lie? It lies in its power to cleanse the world of evils: ignorance, wars, poverty, disease. In a plea to her audience of scientists that at once radiates power and humility, Marie urges them to do as she and Pierre had done their whole lives, “Look for the clear light of truth.” You can watch “Madame Curie” on HBOMax, YouTube TV, and Hulu. ‘Madame Curie’ Director: Mervyn LeRoy Starring: Greer Garson, Walter Pidgeon Not Rated Running Time: 2 hours, 4 minutes Release Date: Dec. 15, 1943 Rated: 3 stars out of 5 What arts and culture topics would you like us to cover? https://www.perthnow.com.au/news/dna-bre.text: Fresh evidence has been uncovered in the search for the identity of a man who was found dead in bushland more than 20 years ago. The man’s body was found at Echo Point, Katoomba in the Blue Mountains on June 4, 2004. He remains unidentified, despite extensive investigations across the past 22 years. An advanced DNA analysis has now given police a clearer depiction of the man’s appearance and background, with new digital images released as detectives renew their appeal for information. The man – often referred to as the ‘Echo Point man’ – is now believed to have been of Latvian or Middle European descent and more than 60 years old at the time of his death. Police describe him as being caucasian in appearance, about 178cm tall and of a medium build, with light grey hair and frontal baldness. Detectives also believe the man was suffering significant eyesight problems, releasing an image of a handwritten note as part of their investigations. “To whom it may concern. Eyesight absolute s —t,” the note reads. “Unable to work any longer. No cure I’m told!” The man was wearing a blue button shirt with a red cardigan, cream jacket, blue corduroy pants, a black belt, and brown work boots when his body was found. Detectives have developed detailed images of the man’s build, face, and the clothing he was last wearing, and hope this new information will enable them to finally identify the man. Superintendent John Nelson said police were urging anyone with information about a man missing since the early 2000s, possibly with Latvian or Middle European heritage, to contact investigators. “Despite extensive inquiries over many years, this man’s identity remains unknown,” he said. “Police understand this may be a difficult subject, but identifying this man is about dignity, respect, and providing answers to family who may still be searching.” Anyone with any information regarding this case is urged to contact investigators attached to Blue Mountains Police Area Command or Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.

(Reuters/Mario Anzuoni) SPONSORED ARTICLES How logistics industry experts plan to ‘move forward’ after COVID-19 Reasons why Filipinos love Korean culture and products Why Batangas is the destination for budget-friendly family holidays Apple TV’s first San Diego Comic-Con Hall H panel previewed five upcoming titles ‘Matchbox’ follows reunited childhood friends in a life-size car adventure ‘Dark Matter’ Season 2 centers on loss and belonging, creator says Next ‘Silo’ chapter shows characters trying to breach a long-sealed door SAN DIEGO — Apple TV revved audiences up for “Matchbox The Movie” at its San Diego Comic-Con debut on Saturday with a high-octane trailer that paid homage to the classic miniature Mattel toy cars. The panel unveiled first-look footage showing a group of childhood friends reunited as adults and thrust into an action-packed adventure involving life-size Matchbox cars. John Cena, who plays former soldier Sean, said he performed some of his own stunts and was “scared for his life” throughout filming. Joking about the intensity of the action, he said his castmates reassured him they would find him a fresh pair of pants if needed. The cast, who filmed in locations including Budapest and Slovakia, reflected on their favorite shooting spots. “My favorite location? Hall H,” Cena said, referring to Comic-Con’s famous venue. The movie, which begins streaming on October 9, is produced by Apple Studios, Skydance Media, and Mattel Films. Fresh start on ‘Dark Matter’ The “Dark Matter” panel revealed new footage from Season 2 of the series, premiering August 28. Created by Blake Crouch and based on his 2016 novel, the series stars Joel Edgerton as physicist Jason Dessen, who travels between alternative realities. After the events of Season 1, Dessen and his family seek a fresh start. “Imagine your home’s been taken away. You’ve lost all your friends,” Crouch said, describing the new season’s themes of loss and the search for belonging. The panel also offered an early look at “Neuromancer,” the upcoming sci-fi series based on William Gibson’s 1984 novel. Created by Graham Roland, the cyberpunk drama follows a former hacker and a street samurai who join forces for a high-stakes heist. The series premieres on Apple TV on January 22. Another highlight was the action-comedy “Mayday,” starring Ryan Reynolds as a U.S. Navy pilot named Troy. First-look footage showed Troy and Nikolai, played by Kenneth Branagh, being pursued by the KGB as they scrambled for survival. The film begins streaming September 4. Horror series “Widow’s Bay” debuted footage from its Season 2, arriving in 2027. The show’s first season, released in 2026, earned 19 Emmy nominations. The preview featured Tom Loftis, played by Matthew Rhys, trapped in a narrow crawl space. A mysterious figure approaches, ultimately revealing himself as a violent clown in what turns out to be a nightmare. Loftis is the widowed mayor of the superstitious town of Widow’s Bay. The panel concluded with footage from “Silo” Season 3, which premiered on July 3. Set in a dystopian future where 10,000 people live inside a 144-level underground silo, the series stars Rebecca Ferguson as engineer Juliette Nichols. Comic-Con attendees saw characters attempting to open a sealed door that had never been breached, as the new season explores more of the silo’s secrets. —Reporting by Danielle Broadway; Editing by Rod Nickel Interaksyon ‘Ted Lasso’ returns to the pitch with a new challenge on Apple TV Apple aims for better and more entertainment offerings, executive Cue says ‘Severance,’ ‘The Penguin’ lead nominations for TV’s Emmy awards ‘Severance’: What the hit show can teach us about cybersecurity and human risk Apple losing over $1 billion a year on streaming service, the Information reports ‘Shogun,’ ‘The Bear’ pile up nominations for TV Emmys Woman draws flak for brushing teeth while dining at coffee shop Filipino Catholics celebrate 401 years of ‘Buen Suceso’ devotion From legal action to ‘thank you’: Apple David edits post hinting at suing critics Marcos proposes P7.2 trillion budget for 2027 Do we really need 10,000 steps a day? ‘That amount of trash is systematic’: Trash-covered river in Baclaran sparks concern Philippine peso loses most among Asian currencies

http://www.bjreview.com.cn/China/202607/.text: Home | China | Opinion Governance Pacific Dialogue Fact Check Voice | World | Business | Lifestyle | Video Wisdom Without Borders Pacific Dialogue Through Their Eyes Real People, Real Lives On the Scene My China Eye | Multimedia Photography Infographics | Documents | Special Reports | Xinjiang Today Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Slovak President Peter Pellegrini, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, on July 28 (XINHUA) Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Slovak President Peter Pellegrini in Beijing on July 28. China stands ready to join hands with Slovakia in forging a strategic partnership that features mutual respect and trust, equality and mutual benefit, as well as stability and resilience, Xi told Pellegrini, who is on a state visit to China. Xi stressed that mutual respect for each other's development paths and a firm commitment to friendship and cooperation have been the foundation for the sound and rapid growth of China-Slovakia relations. China commends Slovakia for upholding the one-China principle and will continue to work with Slovakia to accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, he said. He called on the two countries to tap the potential for collaboration in emerging sectors and frontier fields, including clean energy, digital economy, robotics and AI, to create new highlights in bilateral cooperation. The two sides should broaden cooperation in culture, sports, tourism, youth and subnational exchanges, and make it easier for people to travel between the two countries, he said. Xi said China and Slovakia should safeguard the UN-centered international system and the international order underpinned by international law, jointly promote an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and contribute to building a community with a shared future for humanity. China has always viewed the EU as a partner and develops its ties with the EU with sincerity and goodwill, Xi said, calling on Slovakia to play a constructive role in promoting the sound and steady growth of China-EU relations. Noting that Slovakia values the strategic partnership with China, Pellegrini expressed the expectation for more outcomes in cooperation in economy and trade, AI, digital economy, robotics and new energy. He added that Slovakia welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest there. As an EU member state, Slovakia is willing to actively promote cooperation between the EU and China and the proper settlement of differences through dialogue and consultation, said Pellegrini. Slovakia is willing to work with China to uphold multilateralism, safeguard the purposes of the UN Charter and international law, and promote regional and world peace and stability, he said, adding that his country is willing to closely coordinate with China to strengthen global governance of AI. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Pellegrini. A welcome banquet was also held for him around noon.

https://www.perthnow.com.au/news/crime/h.text: Police at the scene before the search for the baby boy was called off later on Wednesday. (HANDOUT/SOUTH AUSTRALIA POLICE) Credit: AAP Police sent to mum's home hours before family tragedy Robyn Wuth and Eleanor Wilson AAP 29 July 2026, 10:59am Copy link Share story The gruelling search for a missing baby has been abandoned, as police confirmed the child's mother visited police the day before her body was found alongside her toddler's in a suspected double murder-suicide. The bodies of Helena Wright, 36, and her 23-month-old daughter were found in waters near Cape Northumberland on South Australia's southeast coast on Monday after police were alerted to an empty car with its engine left running. On Wednesday afternoon, police called off a three-day search of land and sea for Ms Wright's three-month-old son, who also vanished on Monday. "Based on expert advice and available information, the infant could not have survived the period of time that has elapsed, either in the water or on land," a SA Police spokesperson said. Prevailing weather conditions forced emergency vessels out of the water for much of Tuesday and limited search efforts on the shoreline and clifftops, "significantly" reducing the likelihood of finding the baby, police said. "The reality is, after three days, the chances of finding the baby alive are zero," Superintendent Trent Cox said on Wednesday. "We've been unable to ? launch water assets. We've been able to get the SES aerial drone up," he said, adding that experts had advised against deploying an underwater drone in the dangerous conditions. Despite calling off the search, authorities will continue to monitor the shoreline over coming days in the hope they can retrieve the baby's body. Authorities continue to investigate exactly how the tragedy unfolded, after revealing on Wednesday they were treating the incident as a murder-suicide. Ms Wright was originally from Estonia and had been living in Compton, a small locality outside Mount Gambier about 26km north of Port MacDonnell. Police have confirmed she attended Mt Gambier Police Station the day before the tragic incident, where she spoke to police. A call from a friend led police to conduct a welfare check at her home about 9.30am on Monday, but the home was empty. Less than two hours later, at 11.15am, police were alerted to an abandoned car left with its engine left running near Cape Northumberland. The bodies of Ms Wright and her toddler daughter were recovered from the ocean on Monday. The pair was found below the cliffs and retrieved with help from local fishermen. A coronial investigation is now underway, with a report to be prepared for the coroner. Police have spoken to the woman's husband, the father of the children, and say the deaths are being treated as a suspected murder-suicide. Earlier, officers said there was no information to suggest anyone else was involved in the incident. SA Premier Peter Malinauskas said the tragedy had shocked the community to the core. ''If it involves children, that breaks your heart ? particularly when we know there was a two-month-old baby missing. That's hard to get your head around," he said on Tuesday. Major Crime detectives and specialist forensic officers remain at the scene as investigations continue. https://www.christiandaily.com/news/roma.text: (Photo: Unsplash) Leaders representing major Christian denominations in Bihor County, Romania, have issued a joint declaration affirming the dignity of every human being while upholding traditional biblical teaching on marriage. Its publication came a day before the Oradea Pride march on Saturday (July 25). The statement, titled "On the Dignity of the Human Person," was signed by Orthodox, Roman Catholic, Greek Catholic, Reformed, Pentecostal, and Baptist leaders in the region. It sought to outline a unified Christian perspective on human identity and sexuality amid ongoing public debates in western Romania. "In the context of public debates and demonstrations touching upon some of the most sensitive dimensions of human existence, we, representatives of the religious denominations in Bihor County, feel it is our duty to express our vision - not to impose it nor to condemn individuals, but out of a responsibility to testify, with respect and love, to the truth about humanity," the statement reads. The leaders unequivocally affirmed the intrinsic value of all individuals, stating that every person is created in the image of God and therefore "possesses a dignity that can neither be negotiated nor lost.” "No one has the right to hate, despise, or turn a fellow human being into an adversary," the declaration said, noting that judgement belongs strictly to God. Addressing the theological foundation of human identity, the statement rejected reducing a person's existence solely to sexuality or passing desires. "Christian teaching has always affirmed that the practice of homosexual relations is incompatible with the order of creation, like any other use of sexuality outside the communion between a man and a woman united through Holy Matrimony," the leaders wrote, adding that this doctrine stems not from hostility, but from the conviction that God knows the true purpose of human existence. The statement also contained an acknowledgment of past shortcomings within the Church, calling ministers to humility. "We acknowledge that, not infrequently, we failed to welcome such wounds with the delicacy of the Gospel," the text reads. "There were moments when sterile rigors took precedence over parental embraces, and harsh responses came faster than benevolent listening." Calling on believers to respond to cultural shifts "without hatred, without verbal violence, without irony, and without contempt," the declaration urged Christians to bear witness with gentleness, warning that "truth without love becomes cruelty, and love without truth turns into a simple endorsement of error." The declaration was signed by P.S. Sofronie (Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Oradea), P.S. László Böcskei (Roman Catholic Bishop of Oradea), P.S. Virgil Bercea (Greek-Catholic Bishop of Oradea), P.S. Bogdán Szabolcs János (Reformed Bishop), Pastor Ioan Moldovan (President of the Pentecostal Community of Oradea), and Pastor Mihai Micula (President of the Baptist Community of Oradea). https://vietnamnews.vn/politics-laws/179.text: Permanent Deputy PM receives Lithuanian Foreign Minister HÀ NỘI — Permanent Deputy Prime Minister Phạm Gia Túc received Lithuanian Minister of Foreign Affairs Kestutis Budrys in Hà Nội on Tuesday, saying that ample potential and room remain for cooperation between the two countries. Hailing the outcomes of Budrys’s talks with Vietnamese Minister of Foreign Affairs Lê Hoài Trung, Túc called his guest’s official visit a contribution to the traditional friendship between the two countries as well as the substantive development of the Việt Nam-EU Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. He suggested them expand ties across all fields, with a focus on enhancing political trust through mutual visits and meetings at all levels, particularly high levels. They should maximise existing cooperation mechanisms, boost economic, trade, and investment connections by effectively leveraging the EU-Việt Nam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA), strengthen business linkages, and expand cooperation in areas matching Lithuania’s strengths such as the digital economy, financial technology, energy (LNG infrastructure, renewable energy, grid development, and network synchronisation), seaports, maritime transport, logistics, and science – technology, the host said. Việt Nam stands ready to create optimal conditions for Lithuanian enterprises to explore the market and make long-term investment in the country, the Deputy PM affirmed. Túc called on Lithuania to continue voicing strong support for the remaining EU member states to swiftly ratify the EU-Việt Nam Investment Protection Agreement (EVIPA) and to advocate the European Commission's early removal of the "yellow card" warning on Việt Nam's seafood exports, particularly during Lithuania's rotating Presidency of the Council of the EU in the first half of 2027. He also proposed that the two sides expeditiously finalise the legal framework for cooperation, including the agreements on the avoidance of double taxation, visa exemption for official passport holders, education, training, and labour, while stepping up people-to-people exchanges. On this occasion, he requested that Lithuania continue creating favourable conditions for the Vietnamese community residing in the country, enabling them to fulfil their role as a bridge of friendship between the two nations. For his part, Budrys conveyed Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda’s invitation to Party General Secretary and State President Tô Lâm to pay an official visit to the European country at an early date. He also conveyed greetings and an invitation from Lithuanian PM Mindaugas Sinkevicius to PM Lê Minh Hưng. The minister spoke highly of Việt Nam's impressive development achievements, its increasingly important role in ASEAN, and the progress in Việt Nam-EU relations. Lithuania attaches great importance to its relations with Việt Nam and is ready to act as a bridge for promoting ties between Việt Nam and the EU, he affirmed, stating that during its upcoming rotating EU Presidency, Lithuania will prioritise the implementation of EU cooperation projects with Việt Nam, particularly in energy and transport infrastructure through the Global Gateway initiative. Agreeing with his host’s opinions, Budrys said Lithuania wishes to expand cooperation with Việt Nam in trade, investment, energy, cybersecurity, logistics, and agriculture, noting that it will send a business delegation to Việt Nam to explore cooperation and investment opportunities. In addition, he asked the two sides to promote labour collaboration, student exchanges and cultural ties reaffirming his country’s support for the EVIPA and the early lifting of the IUU fishing "yellow card". During the meeting, both host and guest emphasised their commitment to strengthening their countries’ coordination and mutual support at the United Nations and other multilateral forums, as well as to advancing ASEAN–EU relations. They reaffirmed the importance of maintaining peace, stability, security, safety, and freedom of navigation and overflight, and resolving disputes by peaceful means in accordance with international law, particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). — VNA/VNS Politics & Law Việt Nam, Netherlands eye stronger cooperation in trade, technology and innovation Politics & Law Top Vietnamese leader attends inauguration of Việt Nam House, meets Vietnamese community in Australia Politics & Law Việt Nam, Australia seek to forge stronger bonds Politics & Law Việt Nam sends condolences to Colombia over earthquake losses Politics & Law Việt Nam–Australia Joint Statement on Economic Resilience Cooperation Politics & Law Việt Nam–Australia Joint Statement on Deepening Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Politics & Law Draft law proposes greater autonomy for HCM City and special-class cities Under the proposal, HCM City and cities officially classified as special-class urban centres would be eligible to apply special development mechanisms and policies.
