https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/ma.text: McHenry County Marine veteran, 48, identified as woman killed in Fox River DUI boat crash "She would go above and beyond for anyone, there was no one like her, the most selfless and kind person you would ever meet," said Michelle Macias, Jablonska's sister. By Randy Gyllenhaal and Izzy Stroobandt • Published July 28, 2026 • Updated on July 28, 2026 at 10:26 pm BOOKMARKER NBC Universal, Inc. The woman killed by a speeding boater on the Fox River is remembered by family as a selfless and kind Marine veteran. Randy Gyllenhaal reports. The 48-year-old woman who was struck and killed by a speeding boater on the Fox River over the weekend is remembered by her family as a selfless and kind U.S. Marine veteran who served her country after immigrating to Chicago from Poland. Magdalena Jablonska was out on the Fox River on Saturday with her family when 45-year-old boater Richard Stevenson slammed into the vessel they were on from behind at 80 mph, according to authorities. Stevenson was both drunk and speeding when he crashed into them, prosecutors said. Stream NBC 5 for free, 24/7, wherever you are. WATCH HERE Jablonska was killed in the crash and her dog and fiancé were both injured. "She would go above and beyond for anyone, there was no one like her, the most selfless and kind person you would ever meet," said Michelle Macias, Jablonska's sister. Macias said Jablonska joined the Marines "straight out of high school" and "never [did] anything for herself, always for everybody else." Jablonska was a big fan of dogs and often "loved the shelters for the puppies," her family said. They are now raising money for animals in the wake of the devastating loss and hope that Stevenson will be held accountable in court. "We are giving our hopes and faith they will do right by her so nobody else gets hurt," Macias said. Local Northwest Indiana 20 minutes ago ‘Stay put': Entire town in northwest Indiana without power after severe storms Severe Weather 42 minutes ago ‘We've got a mess': Rolled over semis, downed power lines block part of Indiana interstate Stevenson, who worked for the prominent Bolingbrook-based Stevenson Crane Company that is owned by his family, is facing charges of aggravated DUI and reckless homicide after the crash, records show, and prosecutors say his blood alcohol content was twice the legal limit when he sped his high-powered pontoon in a slow zone. Prosecutors called him a "ticking time bomb" because of his history of DUI charges dating back more than 20 years, including two previous DUI convictions, three reckless driving convictions, three fleeing and eluding police convictions and four misdemeanor speeding convictions, according to court records. They also said witnesses described how he had picked up a bucket of Fireball whisky bottles and was drinking them as he drove. He allegedly stopped later at a bar for two more shots. They say that after the crash, Stevenson admitted to another witness that he was drinking and that his life was over. He stayed on the scene and was later taken to a hospital where he allegedly refused blood and urine tests, according to prosecutors. “We offer our sincerest condolences to the victims’ families and loved ones. Yesterday, Richard Stevenson's employment with the company in the equipment sales department was terminated. He held no leadership role," Stevenson Crane Company said in a statement. Stevenson was ordered to be detained until trial , and his next court date is set for August. Lake County Sheriff John D. Idleburg released a lengthy statement on Tuesday regarding the crash, stating in part: "Like so many in our community, I am frustrated and saddened by the reckless, dangerous, and inexcusable and preventable actions of a boater on the Fox River whose actions claimed one life and critically injured another person last weekend. The victims were people simply enjoying time on our recreational waterways. Our hearts go out to the victims and their families, and we are hoping for the recovery of the person critically injured." https://isp.netscape.com:443/news/world/.text: News Home U.S. World Entertainment Money Politics Sports Science Health Odd News NATO member Romania shoots down stray drones from Ukraine war after years of incursions BUCHAREST, Romania (AP) — Since Russia’s full invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the war has repeatedly spilled across Romania's border as drones violate the airspace of the neighboring European Union and NATO member. Now Romania is trying something new to stop the incursions: shooting down the drones. Romanian pilots shot down the first of three drones in as many days from F-16 fighter jets starting Friday as Russia intensified attacks against Ukraine near the border. After determining the drones were of Russian origin, Romania summoned Moscow’s ambassador in protest and expelled a Russian diplomat on Monday. Drones have crossed into Romanian territory multiple times from Ukraine to the north and east, including in May when a drone injured a mother and child after crashing into an apartment block in the eastern town of Galati along the Danube River. Romanian authorities largely responded by scrambling jets, collecting debris, erecting fallout shelters near the border and frequently admonishing Moscow for its war spilling into its territory. Romania and Poland also acquired the MEROPS system , which fires short counter-drones to take down incoming stray drones, following a spate of incursions along NATO’s eastern flank late last year. Drones have crossed into the territories of multiple EU countries , but have been a persistent problem for Romania's leadership in the capital Bucharest. At least 19 have entered Romania’s airspace this year, while there have been 50 cases of drones or drone fragments identified on its territory since the war started in 2022, according to Romania's Ministry of National Defense. Romanian President Nicusor Dan on Sunday congratulated the Romanian pilots for downing the drones and blamed Russia for the incursions. “It is unacceptable and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romanian airspace,” he said. Despite passing legislation last year to shoot down drones in its airspace, which was strongly opposed by nationalist political parties, Romania has avoided shooting them down until now. Romanian military analyst Radu Tudor said the May drone incident in Galati may have “changed something in the Romanian authorities’ mentality” in how to approach the issue. “This was somehow a kind of psychological trigger, in order to say: ‘OK, enough is enough,’” Tudor said. “Until now, it probably was an Allied decision in NATO not to respond with firepower, because it was somehow a danger of escalation.” “I think it’s not only a change of attitude of Romania, I think it’s a change of attitude in NATO,” he added. Before the three interceptions over the past week, Romanian pilots also shot down a stray Ukrainian drone above Estonia in May. Romanian pilots and planes are based in Lithuania to provide broad strike capabilities for NATO. “They saw so many signals that Russia is trying to provoke NATO,” Tudor said. “Romania is the only NATO country who shot down four drones on the eastern flank — three on Romania and one in Estonia.” The message sent to Moscow mirrors a statement by NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at the organization's summit in Ankara, Turkey, earlier this month: “‘Don’t play with us’.” In response to the drone incursions, Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Russia’s ambassador in Bucharest on Monday and presented him with fragments of a drone, saying Moscow “bears exclusive responsibility for all these grave incidents.” The ministry also expelled a member of the Russian mission, who was given five days to leave the country. “The Russian side learned what they already knew: the drones downed on Romanian territory belong to them,” Foreign Minister Oana Toiu wrote in a post on X. “Drone fragments recovered by the Ministry of National Defence and the ongoing prosecutor investigation confirm their Russian origin beyond any doubt.” The Russian embassy in Romania responded in a statement posted on its Facebook page, saying Russia “has never directed and does not direct combat drones” to Romanian territory and denied the allegation as “completely unfounded.” “An unprovoked expulsion of a Russian employee will not go unanswered,” the embassy said. Cristian Popovici, the Romanian defense ministry’s head of public relations and a former air defense officer, said tactics have been developed to eliminate errant drones. “We recorded more than 100 attacks with drones near our border with Ukraine, and many of them resulted in debris or even drones that penetrated our airspace,” he told The Associated Press. “Our pilots and our air force, we developed the tactics, procedures, and now we can face and we can eliminate this threat.” The change began when Romanian pilots shot down a drone over Estonian airspace and from that point the military applied “lessons learned” and had a “100% rate success in three days with three drones,” Popovici said. Despite the new approach to stray drones, Popovici said Romania does not plan to become entangled in the war between Russia and Ukraine. “We are in a peacetime, we are not involved in this fight,” he said. “If Russia wants to escalate with NATO, it’s up to them. I’m not sure it’s a wise move now.” ___ McGrath reported from Leamington Spa, England. 07/28/2026 06:29 -0400 © Copyright The Associated Press. All rights reserved. https://globalvoices.org/2026/07/29/runn.text: Running from Russia, running from hate: A trans girl’s flight to survival Isabelle. Image courtesy of author. This post is part of Global Voices’ July 2026 Spotlight series, “ Statelessness .” This series offers insight into the issue of statelessness and how it hinders people’s freedom of movement, educational opportunities, political access, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here . For the last two years, Russia has been rated last in LGBTQ+ rights by ILGA-Europe , the European branch of the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association. For transgender people living in Russia, this translates to a life of risk, danger, and often exile. Global Voices spoke to Isabelle, a transgender woman from Magnitogorsk, Russia ab0ut her experience in Russia, her eventual decision to flee the country for her own safety, and the tumultuous European asylum process. Magnitogorsk is a large industrial city in the Urals. It is a so-called monocity: the entire community is based around one industrial plant, the Magnitogorsk Metallurgical Plant, where steel is produced. The community only exists because the plant exists. As in most places in Russia, apart from some communities in bigger cities, people tend to be very homophobic. Isabelle shared: I realized I was a trans girl around the age of 16–17, though at that time I didn’t know what this meant. I didn’t dare to transition because I was living in a dorm in Magnitogorsk, and it was scary: Society in Russia, especially in smaller cities, is quite unfriendly, let’s put it that way. In the summer of 2022, with the help of Center T , I received a ‘diagnosis’ and officially started hormone replacement therapy: back then it was still possible. Then, gradually, things started getting banned, and eventually everything was prohibited completely with the ‘ law banning gender transition ’ in 2023. C enter T is an NGO from Russia that has been helping trans people and their families since 2020. In March 2026, it was declared an “extremist organization” in Russia. Assigning extremist status means anyone directly connected to the organization is criminally liable, including those employed by it or listed among its founders. Under the logic of the Russian authorities, a case can be opened against anyone who “participated” in the activities of such organizations. This means that donations to the organization, providing consultations for the project or within its initiatives, any form of assistance, and even a simple approving comment on social media, may be treated as crimes. Since this political attack, Center T issued a warning on their social media channels urging their followers to take precautions, delete everything, including reposts, likes, and any queer imagery on their profiles, and be ready to run from the country. However, they have continued supporting trans people in Russia, anonymously, now mostly on issues of how to leave the country or help a person in crisis. Isabelle said: Since then, the situation has only gotten worse every year. I was repeatedly insulted on the streets (long hair and small breasts were enough to look at least androgynous, which already made you a target in modern Russia). I lived in Moscow and in the small town of Nytva (Perm region). Already in 2013, the anti-LGBTQ+ campaign was so pronounced that some experts suggested it had become part of the nation’s DNA, the official ideology and strategic narrative of the government and the country. It has also led to more murders and torture of LGBTQ+ people. Isabelle explained how the situation in Russia deteriorated, and why she eventually decided to flee the country and seek asylum: I could no longer live [in secret], so I started running social media using my pronouns (she/hers). I understood that I could be imprisoned for that, and in the realities of Russia, for me, that would be a death sentence. I realized I could no longer stay in Russia because it wasn’t safe (both in everyday life and politically). I started looking into what I could do and found out that I could apply for asylum in Spain. I began learning Spanish and got in touch with Russian-speaking organizations. I tried to get a visa in September 2025, but it was denied, so I decided to use the Balkan route. That was quite an adventure. Me and two other trans people, we went to Serbia, and crossed the bridge to Croatia. Spain was my destination from the start: it’s known as one of the safest places in Europe for trans people. We passed through Croatia and were registered by the police there, but Croatia is not safe for LGBTQ+ people from Russia: there’s serious everyday discrimination , and they don’t recognize the danger we face. We couldn’t stay, so we continued toward Spain through Hungary , a small town near the border, from where we planned to fly to Spain. All EU countries can legally grant refugee status or subsidiary protection to LGBTQ+ people fleeing Russia when the person can show a well-founded fear of persecution because of their sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, or sex characteristics. Under EU asylum law, approved LGBTQ+ claims are generally treated as persecution of a “particular social group.” But no EU state grants refugee status automatically just because someone is LGBTQ+ and Russian. Practically, LGBTQ+ Russians often aim for countries with more developed asylum practices and support networks. Spain is especially well regarded by the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association (IGLA) Europe as a 2026 asylum destination because it is the only country where sex characteristics are expressly included in positive asylum-related measures. For many queer Russian asylum seekers, the process of seeking safety can be a long and harrowing experience. Isabelle shared: In Hungary, before our flight to Barcelona, we were detained by Hungarian police, and we spent 50 days in a Hungarian immigration detention center. To be honest, at first it was horribly scary. For the first two days we were promised that everything would be OK. But we were handcuffed, and slept on benches in common rooms at the airport detention center. But then we were even more terrified when we went to Nyírbátor close to the border in Hungary, and they brought us to a real jail. There were nine police officers and only three of us queer persons. Maybe it would have been easier for Hungary actually, and cheaper, to accept refugees than to pay for all these security measures to detain queer people and put them in jail. At least I was put on the floor where there were women and families (men, women, and children), not the floor for men only. Still, I had been harassed in this jail but did not dare to file a complaint because all I wanted to do was to get out of there. Interestingly, we have met a lot of awesome people here. Because it is immigration jail, there were people from all over the world: Iran, Russia, Chechnya, and many others. After two months, because things are slow over there, they received a confirmation from Croatia that they would accept us back (for the process of asking for refugee status). So we were sent back to Croatia. From there I eventually managed (it was a very, very stressful 30 hours) to reach Spain in December 2025. The whole journey, thus, took almost three months. I applied for asylum as an LGBTQ+ person in January 2026 in Spain. When I got to Barcelona, I was a bit in shock that the local LGBTQ+ NGOs could not or did not want to help me. At first I went to ATHACHI NGO (which is supposed to help LGBTQ+ refugees) and asked for help to get the hormones I needed for my continuing transition, and they never gave me any advice or anything — never called me back. The same situation happened with other organizations, Red Cross and CAER [the Spanish Commission for Refugees] . Fortunately, I could buy the medicine in pharmacies because they took pity on me and did not ask for prescriptions. Overall, it is a difficult situation for all refugees: you need to find an apartment, register there and only then can get into the national medicine system. However, it is very difficult to find a place to live where you could also register when you are a refugee. But the organizations do not help to find a solution. They also gave me and some people I know, also LGBTQ+ refugees, wrong and harmful legal advice. For instance, they advise people to go back to Croatia. But Croatia does not accept that LGBTQ+ people are in danger in Russia, and are actually sending them back. And I am a very public person, I have a popular Instagram blog which is serving to give support and advice to Russian-speaking trans people. I have around 3 million views per 30 days but because the blog is open and not private (I want all the trans people who need support to be able to find it), I get hundreds of threats and hateful comments from the people in Russia. One person promised that if I ever came back, he would cut my head off. It is simply impossible for me to go back to Russia now. So now I am waiting on my decision of refugee status in Spain. Isabelle’s Instagram blog is a safe, positive, and joyful corner of the internet: She shares her love of life and optimism. Despite her harrowing ordeal, she continues to share her happiness with the world and, in her own cheerfu l way, educates the public about the rights of transgender people. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: The best practice for investigating potential bodies inside things like wheelie bins and suitcases is not to open it, but to x-ray it, an expert says. Photograph: Kevin Frayer/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The best practice for investigating potential bodies inside things like wheelie bins and suitcases is not to open it, but to x-ray it, an expert says. Photograph: Kevin Frayer/Getty Images Australian police and policing A ‘body’ found in a suitcase was actually a sex doll. How did NSW police get it so wrong? Officers – correctly – may not have fully unzipped the bag containing the lifelike doll to avoid destroying evidence, one expert says Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kat Wong Tue 11 Aug 2026 21.03 EDT Last modified on Tue 11 Aug 2026 21.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Revelations that a “body” found inside a suitcase was actually a sex doll may have been embarrassing for police, but experts say officers followed the correct procedure. New South Wales police on Sunday were called to Oallen, a town near Goulburn, after two members of the public found a suitcase containing what they believed to be human remains, dumped on the side of the road. A police statement released on Sunday said the body was believed to be female, and the bag was sent to the forensic medicine laboratory. ‘Body’ found in suitcase near Goulburn was actually lifelike doll with ‘bruises and grazes’ Read more But after forensic examinations on Monday morning, it was confirmed the “body” was actually a life-like doll dressed in clothes that had hair, a nose piercing, markings that resembled bruises and grazes. While former NSW police officer Vincent Hurley said the discovery was “amusing in hindsight”, investigators had done the right thing. “Police have been blamed over the years, and rightly so, for tunnel vision,” Hurley, a criminologist, told Guardian Australia. “Can you imagine if it was a real body and they just go unzip the bag and say, ‘we’ll have a poke’? “They did the right thing, it’s embarrassing, yes, but they followed procedure.” When police arrive at a reported crime scene, they generally try not to contaminate it, Hurley said. This means they may not have unzipped the bag the entire way to confirm a potential body, because doing so could destroy any fibres or blood that may have been on the zipper. The best practice for investigating potential bodies inside things like wheelie bins and suitcases is not to open it, but to X-ray it, Paola Magni, a Murdoch University forensic science associate professor, said. Even after realising they had a doll, forensic examiners likely would have had to fully continue inspecting it for traces of evidence like semen or other DNA in case it was associated with another suspicious case. “It’s a doll, but if it’s connected to another crime, they can use that opportunity to link it to something suspect,” says Magni, an expert in decomposition. “Any potentially suspicious situation has to be treated with the best practice in forensic investigation. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion “They did the right thing, they investigated it step-by-step.” Hurley also said objects like sex dolls could be “incredibly lifelike” and noted the bodies of real murder victims were often found in confined places like car boots, suitcases and barrels. “It’s not unusual to be in a suitcase, it’s just unusual that it turned out to be a plastic doll,” he said. Crimes around sex dolls are generally rare, but in Australia possessing a child-like sex doll is an offence and police have previously charged people after intercepting air cargo found to contain such items. However, the one discovered on Sunday is not believed to be childlike and police investigations into it have concluded. At her press conference on Monday, Superintendent Linda Bradbury maintained police had “no regrets”. “Our police have undertaken the processes that we do to maintain integrity in such serious crime, to a T, and I do commend people for that,” she said. Bradbury also confirmed the members of the public who discovered the suitcase had made the right decision by pulling over, peeking inside, and calling as soon as they believed it was something suspicious. Victorian parliament has voted to abolish group voting tickets (GVTs) to elect its upper house. The state was the only remaining jurisdiction with the system, in which voters can only choose one party above the line on the ballot paper, with their preferences then allocated by the party if it’s knocked out during counting. GVTs have been criticised by experts including Antony Green because they allowed backroom deals between parties to flourish, enabling some candidates to get elected with only a minuscule number of primary votes. The electoral amendment (miscellaneous matters) bill 2026, which passed the upper house 33 votes to 4, will replace GVTs with a new above-the-line voting system that requires voters to number at least five groups in order of preference. Those preferences will then flow to candidates in the order they appear below the line for each party or group. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Catering trucks are parked near Air Force One as the motorcade carrying Donald Trump arrives following the Nato summit at Ankara international airport on 8 July. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP View image in fullscreen Catering trucks are parked near Air Force One as the motorcade carrying Donald Trump arrives following the Nato summit at Ankara international airport on 8 July. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP Donald Trump Trump’s Air Force One deception faces scrutiny over ‘decoy’ passengers Journalists and others were allowed to fly on presidential jet despite security threat while Trump was spirited away Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email Joseph Gedeon and David Smith in Washington Tue 11 Aug 2026 20.33 EDT First published on Tue 11 Aug 2026 17.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Democrats called on Tuesday for a congressional briefing over a stunning charade in which Donald Trump was secretly spirited to a different plane than the one the public and press believed he was travelling on. Critics now question why reporters and the public had been deliberately misled. When US intelligence allegedly found a credible threat that Iran plotted to kill him last month, Trump left Air Force One in a catering truck, an episode first reported by the Washington Post and also by the New York Times. While the president was reportedly snuck out the side door of the plane, more than a hundred aides, officials and reporters were kept onboard to fly towards Britain, without being told there was a threat to their lives. “It appears that the idea was we can reduce the danger to President Trump by offering up 100 or so people to be killed by the Iranians in his place,” said Steven Cash, executive director of the Steady State and a former CIA intelligence officer and senior adviser to the Department of Homeland Security’s intelligence branch. Trump reportedly hid in catering container to board secret flight in Turkey amid Iran threat Read more Richard Blumenthal , a Democratic senator for Connecticut, called the operation “unprecedented and surreal” and “downright scary” on CNN. “There has to be a congressional briefing because it involves not just the safety of the president. “I want to know what precautions were taken to make sure that all of the passengers on that Air Force One, which was judged too dangerous for the president to fly on, what precautions were taken to keep the staff and reporters on that plane safe?” The White House had publicly said the president would fly to Britain onboard Air Force One – albeit an older version instead of the new Qatari-gifted aircraft. In reality, Trump boarded the presidential jet in full view of television cameras before being spirited away minutes later and transferred to an air force C-32A. The deception was sufficiently elaborate that journalists travelling with the president – and some White House staff – believed Trump remained onboard Air Force One. Reporters were instructed to keep the shades over their windows closed during the flight. The C-32A carrying Trump flew to RAF Mildenhall in Britain, arriving at about 10.20pm. The older Air Force One and the travelling press pool arrived minutes later. Photographers subsequently captured Trump descending from the presidential aircraft, apparently after he had been secretly reunited with it. Trump then greeted troops at the base before boarding the newly refurbished Boeing 747 donated by Qatar and flying on to Washington. Ned Price , a former deputy to the US ambassador to the UN, said he did not begrudge any White House taking extraordinary measures to protect the president but the current administration had perpetuated an “outright lie” for weeks and turned reporters into “unwitting conspirators”. Price, an ex-special assistant to President Barack Obama on the national security council, added: “There was a way to do this where they didn’t need to lie. They could have enlisted the travelling press pool, who would have very willingly, I am certain, not reported on certain security arrangements. “Once all was said and done and the president was safely in the UK or back at Andrews air force base, they could have said, ‘This is what we did and this is why we did it,’” Price added. “But they feel no compunction to the truth. They feel no loyalty to the truth. Instead it’s just an effort over the past month to lie and to mislead.” Journalists also raised concerns. Jake Tapper, an anchor on CNN, tweeted : “Obviously the life of the president is paramount, and previous White Houses have used deception to protect the president’s life. But no officials I’ve spoken to have ever before heard of using an AF1 full of WH staff and journalists as a decoy during an imminent threat.” And Jose Zamora, Commitee to Protect Journalists’ regional director for the Americas, said the administration had a responsibility to ensure reporters weren’t exposed to unnecessary danger. “Reporters should be informed of credible security threats so they can make informed decisions about their safety,” he said. “Transparency should be the norm for any administration, particularly when safety is at stake.” 2:13 Trump ‘secretly switched planes via catering truck’ amid Iran threat | Deconstructed – video The White House has not directly confirmed the details of the operation. Its communications director, Steven Cheung, instead told the Post the president faced numerous threats and that officials used “every tool at our disposal” to protect him. The revelation sheds new light on an abrupt decision that had already raised questions about the security of the Qatari aircraft. Trump had flown the newly refurbished jet to the Nato summit – its first international journey – but unexpectedly announced that he would instead use the older Air Force One on the first leg of his return journey. At the time, Trump said the new aircraft was being flown to Mildenhall so US troops stationed there could inspect it. The New York Times and CBS News subsequently reported that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a possible attack on Trump or his aircraft amid the escalating conflict with Iran. During the summit, the US military was conducting major strikes against Iran, adding to fears of Iranian retaliation. The new account suggests that the threat was taken more seriously than previously understood. Not everyone is convinced the threat justified what happened next. “From the Iranian perspective, pulling off an attempted targeting of presidential aircraft at this depth would be extremely implausible; it would require close-in clandestine operators with man-portable anti-air systems,” said Ankit Panda, the Stanton senior fellow in the nuclear policy program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Panda said it was not clear there had been a specific, credible threat within Turkey itself, though presidential security routinely plans around “known unknowns”. “Iran doesn’t have surface-to-air missiles that could target an aircraft taking off from Ankara,” said Dr Jeffrey Lewis, a distinguished fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute. Iran could in theory strike a plane on the runway with a ballistic missile, he said, “but that seems very unlikely”. His guess: US officials were worried about “a terrorist-like attack using a man-portable air defense system,” such as a Chinese-made QW-12 or FN-16, or a North Korean version of the Russian Igla. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion James Jeffrey, a former US ambassador to Turkey and deputy national security adviser under George W Bush who is now a distinguished fellow at the pro-Israel Washington Institute, said the secrecy around moving Trump to another aircraft pointed to serious intelligence behind the threat. “This is very unusual, and indicates that they had very good intelligence of a threat, and that they did not trust the aircraft that he was in,” said Jeffrey, who has extensive experience traveling onboard Air Force One. Jeffrey said he believed the intelligence may have come from Israel, which has extensive intelligence capabilities focused on Iran. While Israeli officials sometimes seek to “not only inform but influence” US policy, he said they would not risk fabricating a threat involving the president’s safety. “They wouldn’t play with something as serious as the president’s safety,” Jeffrey said, adding that any such warning would prompt the US government to verify the intelligence, gather more information about the threat and follow up on it.” Trump himself appeared to hint at the security concerns when reporters questioned him about why they had been ordered to keep their window shades closed. “You’re probably on a dangerous flight,” he said. “But if I go, you go. Right?” Asked later whether there had been a credible Iranian threat against Air Force One, Trump said: “Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you.” The operation has nevertheless prompted questions about the decision to deceive the press corps and the public, particularly after the White House continued to maintain the cover story. “The way to mitigate the threat included offering up the remaining people on Air Force One as an unwitting decoy,” Cash said. What was unclear, he added, was the order of operations – whether Trump’s team waited until he was safely away before letting the rest of the plane take off, or sent it up not knowing. If officials had simply announced Trump wasn’t onboard once he had landed safely, he said, they could have accomplished most of what they wanted without anyone remaining in the dark. “It really does sound like they were intended to serve as a decoy.” Cash pointed to Intelligence Community Directive 191 , the government’s “duty to warn” policy, which requires intelligence agencies to alert people who are the specific, credible target of a threat of killing, serious injury or kidnapping – including, he said, journalists and civilians, not just officials. “If there’s intelligence collected that shows that a human being or a group of human beings are in danger, they need to be warned,” Cash said. “The question is: were the people who remained on the plane warned? If not, it violated ICD 191.” The directive, adopted by the director of national intelligence in 2015, does allow waivers when a warning would compromise sources, methods or operations – but Cash said he knew of no exception written for using people as decoys. “Probably because nobody ever thought that anybody would come up with the idea.” Others defended the operation. Ari Fleischer, a former White House press secretary under President George W Bush, said that if the report was accurate, the Secret Service, air force and White House deserved credit for protecting the president. “If there’s a credible threat against any POTUS, their job is to protect him,” he wrote on X . The extraordinary journey echoes an operation carried out by Bill Clinton in 2000, when the former president secretly flew into Pakistan onboard an unmarked executive jet while Air Force One was used as a decoy. But Matthew Hoh , a senior fellow at the Eisenhower Media Network and Iraq war combat veteran, described the Trump incident as unique. “If it was a credible threat and they allowed Air Force One to take off thinking it was going to be shot down or whatever was going happen, they saw the pilots, the air crew, the White House staff, the journalists as all being expendable, dispensable, meaningless,” he said. “There’s a lot of implications here with this story that help us understand this administration better or maybe reinforce the understanding we already have of this venal and vainglorious White House.” Explore more on these topics Donald Trump Trump administration US politics news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.dw.com/en/drone-attack-hits-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IewM The Zawiya oil complex west of Tripoli was hit by explosives-laden drones, sparking fires at the site of Libya's largest refinery Image: Mahmud Turkia/AFP Advertisement Libya 's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said Tuesday that fires at a fuel storage facility had been quickly brought under control after a drone attack. The Zawiya oil complex west of Tripoli is home to the country's largest refinery and has been the scene of repeated armed clashes between warring factions fighting for primacy in the country since the fall of former strongman leader Moammar Gadhafi in 2011. What happened in the drone attack on Libya's Zawiya oil refinery? Monday's attack by an as yet undeclared actor targeted the Zawiya Oil Refining Company with explosives-laden drones, causing a tank containing about 4.5 million liters (1.2 million gallons) of gasoline to collapse after a fire. Owner Brega Petroleum Marketing said the fires had been brought under control far faster than expected, with engineers telling Reuters news agency that damage had been limited, though operations were interrupted. In a statement on X, Abdulhamid Dbeibah, Libya's internationally recognized prime minister, wrote that the crime of targeting civilian infrastructure would "not go unanswered." Libya's UN-recognized Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah condemned the drone attack on the Zawiya oil complex, saying the targeting of civilian infrastructure would "not go unanswered" [FILE: October 13, 2022] Image: Yousef Murad/AP Photo/picture alliance "The use of drones to strike vital facilities," wrote Dbeibah, "is not a random incident, but rather an organized and dangerous act that requires a firm response to protect the state and its institutions and prevent its recurrence." Officials from Libya's electricity provider said two further drones targeted the Zawiya power plant early Tuesday morning, with one hitting the fire-fighting system but causing no damage. What is the security situation in divided Libya? Libya has remained divided since the 2011 uprising that toppled Gadhafi. Dbeibah's UN -recognized government is based in Tripoli in the west, while eastern and parts of southern Libya are controlled by the Libyan National Army (LNA), a military force led by commander Khalifa Haftar. Amid those tensions, the LNA said its head of military intelligence, Fawzi al-Mansouri, was killed in a car bombing in Benghazi on Monday night. According to the LNA, an explosive device attached to al-Mansouri's vehicle detonated as he left a mosque. Authorities have not identified those responsible. Khalifa Haftar commands the Libyan National Army (LNA), which controls eastern Libya and parts of the country’s south [FILE: September 5, 2024] Image: Abdullah Doma/AFP/Getty Images Khaled Haftar, one of Khalifa Haftar's sons, said an investigation had been opened, adding that initial "indicators point to a despicable terrorist tactic," according to AFP news agency. His office later said authorities had arrested a "terrorist cell" in Benghazi that was allegedly preparing acts of sabotage, but did not say whether it was linked to al-Mansouri's killing. Al-Mansouri was a prominent military figure close to the Haftar family and had played a key role in fighting jihadist groups in eastern Libya. How has Libya's political division affected oil production? The split between dueling administrations has stunted the country's oil producing progress and kept foreign investors wary as rival sides clash over control of the oil revenues that pour into the Central Bank of Libya. In 2024, a standoff over control of the bank slashed the country's oil exports by more than half. Libya holds Africa's largest proven oil reserves, yet has struggled to return to pre-2011 production levels of 1.6 million barrels per day. June production hit 1.44 million barrels per day, the highest output levels since 2013, but far short of its target of 2 million barrels per day. https://www.dw.com/en/unesco-2-4-million.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Ievm A father teaches his children at home in Afghanistan, where access to education remains severely restricted for girls [FILE: August 6, 2026] Image: AFP Advertisement Around 2.4 million girls in Afghanistan have been denied access to secondary education since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, UNESCO said Tuesday. The figure has risen by about 200,000 since last year and could reach nearly four million by 2030 if the ban remains in place. "Afghanistan remains the only country in the world where girls and women are formally banned from secondary and higher education," Hoda Jaberian, UNESCO’s program coordinator for education in emergencies, said. "Five years is not a temporary interruption in a child’s education. It is clearly almost an entire secondary school cycle." Why are Afghan girls banned from secondary schools and universities? The Taliban seized power on August 15, 2021 , as US and NATO forces withdrew after two decades of war . They initially assured the international community that women would be allowed to continue studying. Taliban fighters took control of Afghanistan's presidential palace in Kabul after President Ashraf Ghani fled the country [FILE: August 15, 2021] Image: Zabi Karim/AP/picture alliance But secondary schools were closed to girls in March 2022 . Women were barred from universities in December that year . The Taliban described both measures as temporary, but they remain in force. The authorities say they respect women's rights in line with their interpretation of Islamic law and Afghan culture. They have also insisted the issue is a domestic matter. Restrictions extend beyond education. Women face limits on employment and movement and have been barred from public parks, gyms and beauty salons. The UN has described the broader system of restrictions as “gender apartheid.” Russia is the only country to formally recognize the Taliban administration. What has happened to girls' education since the Taliban takeover? UNESCO says the restrictions have reversed two decades of progress. Girls had very limited access to schooling in 2001. By 2021, nearly one million were enrolled in secondary education. "Afghanistan had made really major progress in expanding girls’ access to education," Jaberian said. "But unfortunately, much of that progress now has been completely reversed." UNESCO has called for the immediate and unconditional restoration of girls' and women's right to secondary and higher education. The agency continues to support community-based education as well as literacy and skills programs, often held in community spaces or facilitators' homes. How is the Taliban ban affecting Afghanistan's economy? UNESCO estimates that excluding women from secondary and higher education could push around 600,000 women out of the workforce by 2066. The restrictions could also cause cumulative income losses of 9.6 billion US dollars and increase the risk of early marriage. The ban is also worsening a shortage of female teachers. UNESCO expects Afghanistan to face a deficit of more than 11,000 qualified female teachers by 2030. "Many teachers have left the country and those who were in the system are banned from continuing teaching," Jaberian said. She added that restrictions on women teaching boys had left some pupils with unqualified male teachers or no teachers at all. How severe is Afghanistan's wider education crisis? Afghanistan's education system is facing problems far beyond the ban on girls. More than two million primary school children are already out of school for other reasons. More than 90% of 10-year-olds cannot read a simple text, while the national literacy rate stands at 37%. Many schools are overcrowded and poorly equipped. Nearly half lack water, sanitation or heating. Natural disasters, including earthquakes and floods, have forced around 1,000 schools to close since 2021, adding further pressure to the country's education system [FILE: November 5, 2025] Image: Sayed Hassib/REUTERS The system is also under pressure from people returning to Afghanistan. Three million people returned in 2025 alone, either voluntarily or forcibly. More than seven million have returned or been forced back since 2023. Natural disasters have added to the crisis. Earthquakes , floods and other disasters have forced around 1,000 schools to close since 2021, UNESCO said. Edited by: Saim Dušan Inayatullah Don't let the algorithm hide the news. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c20d.text: Figure caption, Watch: Moment powerful earthquake shakes Colombia and crumbles buildings By Michael Sheils McNamee Published 6 hours ago Rescue workers in Colombia are working against the clock to free survivors trapped in buildings and under rubble following Monday's powerful earthquake. More than 180 people have been confirmed dead - most in the cities of Cali and Pereira. The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) on Monday and was felt across an enormous area, stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia - with fresh aftershocks still being felt on Tuesday. While the official death toll remains 181, an aggregated figure gathered from local officials puts it higher - potentially at more than 240. A state of emergency has been declared by President Abelardo de la Espriella. Giving an update on Tuesday from Pereira, one of the worst hit cities, President Espriella said as well as those killed, almost 2,600 had been injured, and almost 200 people remain missing. He also reported that more than 1,100 homes had been destroyed, and more than 8,000 had been damaged. Overnight on Monday into Tuesday, several people several people spent the night outdoors in cities like Pereira and Cali - either due to their homes being destroyed, or fear of further collapses. Across the country, dozens of larger buildings have also collapsed. In Cali, a city of 2.2 million people where there have been 95 deaths, a unified command post has been set up to co-ordinate the rescue effort. On Tuesday, Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder said that 239 people remained trapped, with 949 injured and 45 buildings which have either completely or partially collapsed. Several of the upper floors of one of the city's hospitals, some dedicated to paediatric care, collapsed, leaving some patients trapped. In Calima, a neighbourhood in the north of Cali, four children died after a section of the Gimnasio Calima school collapsed. The mayor of the municipality, Antonio Cadavid, stated that other children ended up with serious injuries, with a total of 30 children were referred to care centres. To combat threats of looting, he has also ordered a curfew, coming into effect at 20:00 local time, and lasting until 06:00 on Wednesday morning. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Firefighters in Cali have worked to pulled survivors free from rubble Image source, Reuters Image caption, Rescuers searched for survivors at the site of a collapsed building in Cali Further tremors were felt in Cali on Tuesday - part of a pattern of aftershocks across the country, with more than 70 having taken place since Monday's earthquake, according to Colombia's geological service. According to the agency, two earthquakes of magnitude 3.6 occurred early on Tuesday. The first was in San JosÃ© del Palmar and the second in Santander. In Pereira, 79 people have died according to the city's fire department. The city has implemented a car-free day to allow the search to go ahead, with citizens urged to comply. Footage from the city has shown the massive scale of the rescue effort, with hundreds of volunteers working to remove rubble and free trapped survivors. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Large numbers of volunteers joined the effort to free survivors in Pereira Hours after the earthquake hit Pereira, a resident of the Parque Industrial neighborhood, near the city's airport, told BBC Mundo about the shock being experienced in the area. "It's impossible to get around the city center. In BolÃ­var Square (the city's main square), at least one building collapsed. Furthermore, there are structures where buses and trucks are trapped, and people are afraid those structures will collapse as well," he said. "We're all in shock. It was really awful." Jorge Eduardo Rojas, mayor of Manizales, said five people had been killed in the city. Sixty buildings in Manizales had partially or totally collapsed. Cautioning about further aftershocks, Rojas urged the public not to share chain messages or social media posts from unknown sources, as they "may contain false or unverified information... which could cause greater concern and alarm among the public". On Tuesday, help and support continued to be offered to Colombia from the international community. A statement from a spokesperson for UN Secretary-General, AntÃ³nio Guterres, stated that he "expresses his solidarity with the people and government of Colombia" and that it working to support the government's response. Spain's Foreign Minister, JosÃ© Manuel Albares, reported that 164 Spaniards were still missing. At the moment, he added, there are no reports of injuries or deaths of its citizens. The Donald Trump administration, which backed President Abelardo de la Espriella in his successful election earlier this year, announced this afternoon a donation of $15.5m (Â£11.5m) to Colombia. Offers of help have also come from Ecuador, Brazil, El Salvador, and Venezuela. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvg8.text: Image source, US Central Command Image caption, Centcom says its helicopter fired two hellfire missiles on the Panama-flagged ship By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 11 August 2026 The US military says one of its helicopters has fired missiles to disable "the steering gear" of a cargo ship attempting to violate the US blockade of Iranian ports. In a statement, US Central Command (Centcom) says its MH-60 aircraft on Tuesday fired two hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged M/V Vela Nova vessel, as it attempted to transit the Gulf of Oman. Centcom said it acted after "the ship's civilian crew ignored repeated warnings from American forces". The vessel "is no longer transiting to Iran", it added. Iran has not commented. The US has been enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports, following failed attempts to end the war it and Israel started on 28 February. Tehran retaliated by launching attacks on Israel and US-allied states across the Gulf. It has also effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz - a key oil shipping waterway. A fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit the strait before the war and prices have fluctuated wildly since then. Mediators have so far failed to bring the sides to an agreement on reopening the strait - and, since the latest ceasefire collapsed in June, both the US and Iran have exchanged fire intermittently. In its statement on X, Centcom said M/V Vela attempted to sail to an Iranian port without naming it. It also did not say whether there were any casualties or injuries. It says the US blockade "remains in full effect", adding that as of 11 August Centcom has "redirected 55 commercial vessels attempting to run the blockade, disabled 3 non-compliant vessels, and boarded 2". In a separate development on Tuesday, Yemen's internationally recognised government said six people were killed and 10 injured in strikes by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on a cargo ship in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they hit a vessel carrying Saudi military equipment. It appears to be the first deadly attack by the group on a ship since the war began. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/clye.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, A woman wades through floodwaters outside her inundated house at a village in Assam's Sivasagar By Soutik Biswas India correspondent Published 2 hours ago Well past midnight on 19 July, as floodwaters surged through a village in India's northeastern state of Assam, Bornali Baruah and her husband were trying to save his 97-year-old mother. Almost bedridden, Lokada Duarah could not walk. There was no boat, no rescue team and no neighbour available to help. So they lifted her onto a makeshift raft made of banana trunks, and carried her through the rushing water towards safety. "Everyone was trying to save themselves," Baruah says. An hour later, she says, the three of them reached a shelter camp on a national highway some distance away from their house in Charing village in Sivasagar district, one of the worst flood-affected districts. The water was three to four feet deep and the current so strong that they had to move slowly, holding each other's hands and using sticks to steady themselves. By then, Baruah's home was disappearing beneath the flood. The water would eventually rise to about five feet inside it. Image caption, Baruah quit journalism to concentrate on animal husbandry The scene in Charing was part of a much wider disaster unfolding across Assam. The latest figures put the death toll from floods at 100, with 10 districts and 456 villages affected and about 140,000 people impacted. Fifty-two relief camps have been set up. Overall, the floods have affected nearly 1.2 million people across 25 districts, damaged more than 19,000 houses and left more than 75,000 people in 252 relief camps. The floods have been particularly severe in parts of Upper Assam, where villages like Charing that do not usually flood have been inundated. For Baruah, 40, the shock is especially profound. "This is the first flood we have experienced in this area in our lifetime," she says. Baruah has lived in Charing since birth, and her ancestors lived here before her. She recalls hearing about a major flood in 1950, long before she was born, but nothing like this had happened during her lifetime. Her home sits in a landscape criss-crossed by rivers, though none runs immediately beside it. The single-storey, eight-room house is about 25km (15 miles) from Sivasagar town; the Brahmaputra is roughly 20km away, the Dikhow 12km, the Jhanji 10km and the Mitong just 5km. Image caption, A 97-year-old Lokada Duarah was carried onto a banana tree trunk and taken to safety after floodwaters rose around her home Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, A boy uses a makeshift banana raft to navigate floodwaters in Assam She had never imagined the water would reach her doorstep. But when it did, the flood threatened not only her home, but the livelihood she had spent years building. Baruah was once a full-time journalist. In 2016, she left the profession to take up animal husbandry, and three years later was named Assam's 'Best Livestock Farmer'. Her farm grew to around 300 goats, 500 ducks and 1,000 chickens, along with fish. The flood destroyed much of it. She says she lost most of her goats, 300 ducks, 300 chickens and a sizeable amount of fish, as well as the machine she used to make animal feed. Furniture, laptops, vehicles and the family's collection of books were also destroyed. None of her livestock was insured. "There is no insurance system here for livestock, especially goats," she says. The first warning came on 17 July, when the Jhanji river began to rise. Two days later, the Dikhow and Mitong spilled into surrounding areas as the Brahmaputra and its tributaries swelled rapidly. Several rivers breached their embankments, Baruah says, sending powerful currents through towns and villages. About a day after the water began rising, she and her family abandoned their home. By then, the water inside the house was four feet deep. They spent the next 10 days in a relief camp. Image caption, Baruah and her family abandoned their home nearly a day after the water began rising For five days in the camp there was no electricity or mobile connectivity and Baruah could not even charge her phone. The government provided the family with a relief kit containing rice, lentils and cooking oil. Help also came from strangers at the camp. A young woman whom Bornali had never met, helped with food, cleaning and looking after her 60 surviving goats. Another took responsibility for treating and feeding animals that had fallen ill. But why did the water reach a place that Baruah says had never flooded before? Dhrubajyoti Sahariah, a professor of geography and director of the Centre for Brahmaputra Studies at Gauhati University, says flooding itself is natural in the Brahmaputra Valley, a lowland region in Assam. What has changed is the "frequency, intensity and severity of floods well beyond historical norms". The Brahmaputra, one of the world's largest multi-channel rivers, ranks among the top five globally for both water discharge and sediment load. Much of that sediment comes from Tibet, where the river originates. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, A family shelters inside a tent in Sivasagar district, among more than 5,000 people lodged in 252 relief camps Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Amit Giri holds a photo of his father, Siv Sankar Giri, who died in the floods, outside their damaged home in Sivasagar. He is among 100 people killed in the floods. As it enters Assam's vast floodplains, home to some 28 million people and hemmed in by hills, it slows and deposits sediment, fuelling erosion and floods. Flooding is an annual feature of life in Assam, but some years are far worse: the 2004 floods alone affected 12 million people and killed 251. In the recent floods, Sahariah says, continuous heavy rainfall in Upper Assam and neighbouring Nagaland's Mon district triggered severe flooding and large-scale silt deposition in Sivasagar, Charaideo and Jorhat. Sahariah says floods are reaching areas once spared because more people have settled on active floodplains, forests have been cleared, mining and hill-cutting have increased sediment in rivers, and roads, bridges and other infrastructure have been built without adequately accounting for the region's hydrology. Yet Assam cannot manage the Brahmaputra on its own. Many of its tributaries originate in the surrounding hill states, while flood-control measures are largely planned within Assam. "What is needed is basin-scale planning," Sahariah says, along with greater coordination between states and better understanding of the rivers' changing geography. For Baruah, however, the science has become painfully personal. Image caption, Only 60 of Baruah's goats survived the floods She has returned to the area around her flood-damaged home. For now, she and her family are staying at a neighbour's house nearby, hoping to move back into their own home within a week. Baruah says she does not intend to leave Charing. Moving away, she says, requires economic and social circumstances that her family simply does not have. So she is beginning to think about how to live with a threat that was, until now, largely absent from her life. She says that if heavy rain comes again, she would need to raise the house higher, perhaps by building up its foundation. She is not yet sure how she would manage it or pay for it. The family would also need a raised platform where they could retreat to safety, and they would stock food and drinking water in advance. Baruah is learning to live with the possibility of more floods â and to prepare for them. Did she feel like a climate refugee? "No. If we regain our economic and mental strength, life will return to the way it was before." "We will have to learn to coexist with the floods." Az elődöntőjében övé volt a második legjobb nevezési idő, de sikerült felülírnia a papírformát. Az pedig végül titokban a valódi Air Force One-ként repül a megszokott gép után. Ilyen forgatókönyvet leginkább filmekben lehet látni, az amerikai sajtóban megjelent beszámolók szerint azonban pontosan ez történt, amikor Donald Trump július 8-án hazaindult Ankarából, a NATO-csúcstalálkozó után. Az amerikai elnököket védő Secret Service az elmúlt évtizedekben többször is használt csaligépeket és páncélautókat, ha a fenyegetés szintje azt megkövetelte. A legismertebb eset 2000-ben történt, amikor Bill Clinton akkori amerikai elnök Pakisztánba repült, és az amerikai hírszerzés attól tartott, hogy Oszama bin Laden terrorszervezete, az al-Kaida merényletet kísérelhet meg ellene. A beszámolókban megjelent taktikához hasonló manőver Trumpnak sem volt újdonság, miután a 2024-es elnökválasztás alatt kampánystábja tett már hasonló lépéseket iráni fenyegetések miatt. Úgy tudni, most is iráni merényletveszély miatt volt szükség a fokozott biztonsági intézkedésekre. Az ankarai esetről több lapnak is beszámoltak források, a Fehér Ház pedig nem cáfolta, hogy megtörtént. A CBS szerint viszont a Trump-kormány több tisztviselője is kifogásolta, hogy szigorúan titkos taktikák és módszerek szivárogtak ki a nyilvánosságba, ami a jövőben nehezebbé teheti az amerikai elnökök védelmét. Ételszállító teherautóban vihették át a gépek között Trump július 6-án érkezett meg Ankarába, a NATO-csúcsra, ahova Air Force One-ként az új, Katartól kapott gépet használva utazott. Amikor két nappal később hazaindult, már nem az új gépbe szállt be, hanem a régibe, amelyet korábban rendszeresen kritizált. Az erről készült felvételen látni lehetett, ahogy az elnök a New York Times akkori beszámolója szerint szokatlanul gyorsan felment a géphez tolt lépcsőn, integetett, majd beszállt a gépbe. Nagyjából öt perccel később egy, a másik oldalon álló catering teherautó elindult a géptől. Az élelmiszer-szállításra használt, megemelhető rakterű teherautóban ekkor már ott volt az Egyesült Államok elnöke is – írta meg először a Washington Post, aminek értesüléseit először a New York Times , majd később a CBS News és a CNN is megerősítette, névtelenül nyilatkozó amerikai tisztviselőkre hivatkozva. A teherautó, amibe Trump állítólag több munkatársával együtt szállt be, a gépnek a sajtó munkatársai és a kamerák által nem látható oldalán volt. A Post cikke szerint a teherautóval egy másik amerikai kormányzati géphez vitték az elnököt. Ott megemelték a rakodóteret, így jutott be Trump titokban a másik repülőgépbe, amelybe Pete Hegseth amerikai védelmi miniszter a rendes lépcsőn át szállt be. A gépet, egy C–32A típusú, átalakított Boeing 757-est magas rangú kormányzati tisztviselők utazására szokták használni. Az általában az elnök különgépeként használt eredeti repülő megtévesztésként az Air Force One hívójelet használva Nagy-Britanniába repült, a fedélzetén az elnök útjáról tudósító újságírókkal és Trump több munkatársával együtt, akik mind azt hitték, hogy az elnök is velük utazik. Mivel az Air Force One valójában annak a gépnek a hívójele lenne, amin ténylegesen az elnök tartózkodik, ebben az esetben titokban a C–32A töltötte be ezt a funkciót. A Mildenhall légibázisnál elsőként az új, Katartól kapott gép szállt le, majd az ott videózó planespotterek felvételei szerint nagyjából négy órával később az elnököt titokban szállító C–32A, pár perccel később pedig az Air Force One-nak hitt csaligép. Azt nem lehet tudni, hogy Trumpot hogyan sikerült titokban visszacsempészni ez utóbbi gépre, ami körül a CNN szerint a szokásosnál nagyobb biztonsági készültség volt. Trump végül erről szállt az új, Katartól kapott elnöki gépre, és azzal repült vissza az Egyesült Államokba. Ételszállító teherautó a régi Air Force One-ként használt Boeing mellett, indulás előtt az ankarai Esenboğa repülőtéren, 2026. július 8-án – Fotó: Saul Loeb / AFP A régi gép jobb? Az akkori beszámolók mind arról szóltak, hogy Trump a régi különgépén repült el Ankarából. Az elnök erre akkor azt a magyarázatot adta, hogy „a régi idők kedvéért” repül a megszokott géppel, valamint azért, hogy az új gépet meg tudják nézni a Mildenhall légibázison szolgáló katonák. A New York Times, majd a CBS News azonban azt írta, hogy biztonsági okokból, a Secret Service kérésére használták a régi gépet, mert a Katartól kapott és az elnöki használatra sietve átalakított új gépnek nem voltak még megfelelő védelmi eszközei. Július végén pedig már a CBS és a Times is arról számolt be, hogy valósnak ítélt iráni fenyegetések álltak a gépcsere hátterében. Mindkét médium értesülései szerint a Katartól kapott és nagyjából négyszázmillió dolláros költséggel átalakított új gépen nincsenek olyan fejlett rakétaelhárító rendszerek, mint a régi repülőn, és az amerikai légierő lapnak nyilatkozó egykori tisztviselői meglepőnek nevezték, hogy Trump azt külföldi utazásra használta. Ráadásul az iráni háború alatt az Iránnal szomszédos Törökországba, amit korábban az iráni rezsim elvétve rakétákkal támadott. Szakértők a Timesnak azt mondták, hogy két évbe is beletelik egy új gép felkészítése az elnöki használatra, és akár egymilliárd dollárt is felemészthet. A Trump-kormány nyomozást indított a géppel kapcsolatos kiszivárogtatások miatt, és idézéseket nyújtottak be a Times több újságírójával szemben. Híváslistákat akartak tőlük megszerezni, de később visszavonták a kereseteket, miután a bíróság megkérdőjelezte azok törvényességét. A Fehér Ház kommunikációs igazgatója, Steven Cheung akkor közleményben védte meg az új gépet: szerinte csúcstechnológiás és magas szintű biztonsági funkciói vannak. Ahogyan azt az elnök nemrégiben kijelentette, számos olyan ellensége van Amerikának, amelyek őt vették célba; „mi pedig minden rendelkezésünkre álló eszközt – beleértve a figyelemelterelést és a megtévesztést is – felhasználunk e fenyegetések kezelésére” – mondta. A katari gépet ezután azért továbbfejlesztették . Az akkori közlemény most újra a figyelem középpontjába került a figyelemelterelés és megtévesztés szavak használata miatt. A legújabb hírekre reagálva, miszerint Trumpot ételszállító teherautóval csempészték át egy másik gépre, a Fehér Ház szó szerint Cheung korábbi közleményét adta ki újra, az egyetlen különbség az volt, hogy a két szó hiányzott belőle. Az amerikai sajtóban megjelent beszámolók szerint egy Iránnal kapcsolatba hozható valós fenyegetés hatására reptették ki mindenki elől rejtve Trumpot Ankarából. A Times értesülései szerint pár óra alatt dolgozták ki a tervet, miután tisztviselők valósnak ítélték a fenyegetést, ami nem a katari gép ellen irányult, hanem bármilyen repülő ellen, ami az elnököt szállítja. A megtévesztési tervről csak pár kormányzati tisztviselő tudott, köztük Dan Caine tábornok, a vezérkari főnökök egyesített tanácsának elnöke, valamint Pete Hegseth. Trump az első elnöksége óta iráni célpontnak számít, miután elrendelte az iráni Forradalmi Gárda akkori nagy hatalmú vezetője, Kászim Szulejmáni ellen Irakban végrehajtott légicsapást. Graff amerikai történész és újságíró cikke szerint évtizedek óta követik az elnököket, létezésük nyílt titoknak számít. De nem csak gépekből vannak csalik, a Secret Service-nek több hasonló páncélautója is van, hogy ne lehessen mindig tudni, az elnök melyikben utazik. A „csaliautón” is ott vannak az amerikai zászlók, és az elnöki pecsét , sőt, még a rendszáma is ugyanaz : 800-002. Clintont 2000-ben a repülőtéren például hat ugyanolyan kinézetű limuzin várta, amelyek sorrendet cseréltek, miután elhagyták a repülőteret a város felé. Emellett az elnököket szállító Marine One hívójelű helikopter is több másikkal együtt szokott repülni, hogy megnehezítsék az esetleges támadók dolgát. Amikor pedig Trump a kongresszusba utazott évértékelő beszédére, biztonsági okokból több ugyanolyan konvoj indult el a Fehér Házból. The complaint was filed against an unknown perpetrator after reviewing the former prime minister’s most recent contracts with her company relating to managing his social media profiles, which came to a total of 4 billion forints (around €11 million) in public funds over several years. Kaminski confirmed that the payment increased over the four years, but she said the government failed to mention that this was to keep pace with inflation. She further argued that it is also misleading to emphasize that Triton Communications only had five full-time employees, because the work actually involved more than 30 people in total. Fanny Kaminski accepts that the new government is reviewing its predecessor’s contracts. “However, I refuse to accept that in the process, they are trying to cast suspicion on a law-abiding Hungarian company by using cherry-picked figures, omitting facts, and using misleading insinuations,” she stated. A kérdés tehát nem az, hogy műszakilag lehetséges-e hűtőtornyokat építeni egy VVER-440-es erőműhöz. A nemzetközi példák alapján egyértelműen igen. A valódi kérdés inkább az, hogy miért nem történt ez meg az elmúlt évtizedekben. Wagner Ernő írásának fontos érdeme, hogy a paksi alacsony vízállás ügyét nem pillanatnyi üzemeltetési zavarként, hanem hosszabb távú vízgazdálkodási problémaként értelmezi. Ebben teljesen igaza van. Helyesen mutat rá arra, hogy a Duna medersüllyedése, a kisvizes időszakok gyakoribbá válása és az energetikai infrastruktúra sérülékenysége nem egymástól független jelenségek. A következtetésnél azonban el kell választani egymástól két külön kérdést: a Duna vízgazdálkodási problémáját és a paksi erőmű hűtéstechnikai sérülékenységét. Ez a különbség döntő: a vízlépcső a folyó működését változtatja meg az erőmű igényeihez szabva, míg a hűtőtorony az erőművet igazítja hozzá a folyó természetes korlátaihoz. A logikai hiba – véleményem szerint tehát – az, hogy a helyi, erőművi hűtéstechnikai sérülékenységből automatikusan országos folyószabályozási program következik. A vízlépcső tehát Paks üzembiztonsági kérdéseire adható, leginkább túlzó és drága megoldás. Az „ágyúval a verébre” közmondásos esete. Paksnál a közvetlen probléma az, hogy az ország legfontosabb villamosenergia-termelő létesítményének hőelvezetése túl nagy mértékben függ a Duna nyári kisvízi és magas vízhőmérsékleti állapotától. Ezt a függést oldani kell és nem adottságként kezelni. Másként fogalmazva: a döntő kérdés nem az, hogy miért nem tettünk több ezer tonna betont a Dunába, hanem az, hogy miért nem épült ki időben olyan zárt vagy részben zárt hűtési rendszer, amely csökkenti a Duna vízállásától és vízhőmérsékletétől való függést. Wagner úr joggal hangsúlyozza, hogy Paksnál a medián vízállás hosszú távon jelentősen süllyedt párhuzamosan a bevágódással, és hogy a jelenség már a paksi bővítéshez kapcsolódó korábbi hidrológiai háttértanulmányokban is megjelent. A 2003-as rekordalacsony vízállás óta pedig minden szakembernek nyilvánvaló kellett volna hogy legyen a hűtőtorony fontossága. Több mint húszévnyi mulasztásról beszélünk. A mulasztás intézményi halogatásként írható le – „majd az utódom megoldja” –, illetve presztízsberuházásokra (például stadionokra) költötték a forrásokat. A kelet-közép-európai technokrata gondolkodás egyik visszatérő tévedése, hogy a rendszerszintű problémát látványos műtárgyban szereti megjeleníteni. A beton könnyen kommunikálható. Át lehet vágni előtte egy nemzeti színű szalagot, bele lehet állítani a kamerát, és az intézkedés kézzelfoghatóvá válik. A vízgazdálkodási rendszer sérülékenysége azonban nem mindig ott oldható meg, ahol a legnagyobb műtárgy épül. Sokszor éppen fordítva: a valódi megoldás kevésbé látványos, de célzottabb, olcsóbb és kisebb külső ökológiai kockázattal jár. Ettől függetlenül a vízlépcsők és duzzasztók kérdését nem lehet igazolni azzal, hogy „máshol is vannak”. A duzzasztók súlyos környezeti hatásokkal járhatnak, különösen síkvidéki, kis esésű folyószakaszokon. A duzzasztás megváltoztatja a folyó sebességviszonyait, hordalékszállítását, hőháztartását, oxigénviszonyait és élőhelyi mozaikosságát. Felvízi oldalon feliszapolódást okozhat, alvízi oldalon pedig a hordalékhiány miatt tisztavíz-eróziót, vagyis medermélyülést és partalámosást válthat ki. A nemzetközi szakirodalom általános megállapítása szerint a gátak megszakítják a hordalék és a tápanyagok természetes hosszirányú kapcsolatát, a nagyobb szabályozó műtárgyak pedig különösen erősen feldarabolják a vízgyűjtőket. A nagymarosi vízlépcső esetében – ha elkészült volna – a tisztavíz-erózió nem elvont kockázat lett volna. Az alvízi medermélyülés éppen azokat a kavicsos, jó vízvezető földtani rétegeket érinthette volna, amelyekre a budapesti parti szűrésű csápos kutak és a szentendrei térség fúrt kútjai is támaszkodnak. Vagyis a duzzasztás nemcsak élőhelyi és hordalékgazdálkodási kérdés lett volna, hanem közvetlen ivóvízbázis-védelmi kockázat is. Azaz jelentősen rontotta volna Budapest és a Dunakanyar lakóinak vízellátását. A duzzasztás hatásai nem merülnek ki a természetes élőhelyek átalakulásában. A víz áramlásának lelassítása rontja a vízminőséget, növeli az algásodás kockázatát, és gyengíti a folyó természetes öntisztuló képességét. A hordalék felhalmozódása rendszeresebb és költségesebb kotrási munkákat tesz szükségessé, miközben a hordalékhiány a duzzasztó alatti szakaszokon fokozza a medereróziót, így növelve a partvédelmi és hídvédelmi beavatkozások költségeit. A halállomány és a természetes vízi környezet változásai érzékenyen érintik a horgászatot, valamint a vízhez kötődő turisztikai és ökoturisztikai szolgáltatásokat, csökkentve az ezekből származó helyi bevételeket. Ez pedig nem politikai jelszóval, hanem nyílt modellezéssel, független hatásvizsgálattal és több évtizedes üzemeltetési forgatókönyvekkel dönthető el. Érdemes itt külön elválasztani Wagner Ernő írását a tágabb közbeszédben gyakran megjelenő leegyszerűsítésektől. A szerző nem, de a populáris közbeszéd állítja azt, hogy egy dunai vízlépcső önmagában megoldaná a Homokhátság vagy a Sárrét vízhiányát. Ez fizikai értelemben téves. A víz nem folyik felfelé. A térségi vízpótlás külön csatornarendszereket, szivattyúzást, tározást, de még inkább talajvíz-visszatartást, tájhasználati változást és ökológiai szempontból is értékelhető tájhasználatot igényelne. Ezt nem lehet néhány dunai műtárggyal helyettesíteni. A paksi ügyben ezért a fogalmi tisztázás a legfontosabb. A vízlépcső elsősorban folyógazdálkodási és környezetvédelmi kérdés. A döntéshozatalnál azt kell mérlegelni, hogy a medersüllyedés, a kisvízi állapotok, a mellékágak kiszáradása és a hajózási problémák kára hogyan viszonyulna egy duzzasztómű gazdasági, hidromorfológiai, ökológiai és tájképi káraihoz. Ez legitim szakmai vita. De nem ugyanaz a vita, mint az, hogy a paksi erőmű hűtését miért nem tettük évtizedek alatt kevésbé Duna-függővé. Ha ezt a két kérdést összekeverjük, akkor a vita rossz irányba fordult. A vízlépcső látványos, nagy, technokrata válasz. A hűtőtorony kevésbé látványos, de célzottabb válasz. És a piszkos anyagiakat is érdemes fontolóra venni: egy hűtőtorony darabja körülbelül 10 millió eurós nagyságrend (durván 35 milliárd forint), és négy kellene belőle. A vízlépcső több százmilliós nagyságrend felett található. Szóval bekerülési költségét tekintve is jelentős különbség van e két megoldás között. Paks sérülékenysége tehát nem bizonyíték arra, hogy Magyarországnak sürgősen vízlépcsőt kell építenie. Inkább annak bizonyítéka, hogy egy stratégiai fontosságú erőmű hűtési rendszerét nem igazítottuk hozzá időben a Duna ismert hidrológiai és klimatológiai változásaihoz. A vízlépcső kérdése maradjon ott, ahová tartozik: a Duna jövőjéről, a medersüllyedésről, a hordalékról, az árterekről, a mellékágakról, a hajózásról és a természetvédelmi mérlegről szóló nyílt szakmai vitában. Paks esetében viszont a valós, arányos és olcsóbb megoldás elsőként nem a folyó átalakítása, hanem az erőmű hűtési rendszerének korszerűsítése lenne. Másként: nem a Duna tartozik Pakshoz.
