Photograph: Jeremy Davidson/Getty Images/iStockphoto US news Drone footage shows rare bird’s-eye view of stingrays off New York coast With wing spans up to 3ft, the shy cownose ray species typically arrive in Long Island waters in the warmer months Maya Yang in New York Wed 12 Aug 2026 06.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 12 Aug 2026 08.26 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Drone footage of dozens of stingrays in the ocean off New York has captivated beachgoers and marine enthusiasts, offering a rare bird’s-eye view of a species that scientists say has visited the area for decades. The footage was captured last Friday off the coast of Southampton on the Long Island peninsula by Joanna Steidle, a Hamptons-based professional drone pilot known for her aerial ocean shots . It shows cownose rays gliding through the water en masse near the surface. Describing the rays in a separate drone shot last week, Steidle said on Instagram: “While filming these I can feel my heartbeat and breathing align with their wings flapping....it is in these moments I feel completely connected and present.” The sighting raises the possibility that the species is migrating farther north and appearing in the area more consistently as ocean temperatures rise, or could simply indicate that increased drone use is making everyday wildlife activity more visible to the public, various experts said. Thousands of migrating stingrays spotted off New York coast The video appears to show hundreds of cownose rays swimming in a group that some refer to by the collective noun “fever”, as in a fever of rays. The species is a large, migratory elasmobranch , a subclass of cartilaginous fish, named for their distinctive high-lobed head resembling a cow’s nose. With wing spans stretching up to 3ft (1 meter), the shy and non-aggressive cownose ray feeds mostly on bivalves, including clams and other bottom-dwelling prey. The rays typically arrive in Long Island waters in the warmer months, following water temperatures that suit them as they migrate north from the Chesapeake Bay, the mid-Atlantic estuary, and other waters farther south. As ocean temperatures rise rapidly around the world, driven largely by climate change , scientists say, warmer waters could be contributing to changes in the timing and range of the rays’ migration. Speaking about the sighting, Dean Grubbs, associate director of research at Florida State University’s coastal and marine laboratory, said: “This occurrence probably does represent a northern shift in the migration due to temperature. Historically, there would be some cownose rays that would make it up to Cape Cod or so in small numbers during warm years, but the big schools would terminate the northern migration around Chesapeake Bay. Now, as ocean temperatures warm, the northern migrations of a lot of species are shifting further and further north.” Grubbs pointed to blacktip sharks as a precedent for a northward shift. While that species was rarely seen north of North Carolina in the 1970s, he said, it had become common in Virginia and Delaware by the 1990s and is now frequently found in New England during warm summers. Ryan Wallace, an assistant professor of environmental studies and sciences at Adelphi University, said cownose rays generally prefer water temperatures 70-79F (approximately 21-26C), meaning New York’s warm, coastal waters could drive them to migrate north earlier in the spring and remain in the region longer. “Water temperature kind of dictates that timing, and so that can then trigger – as the drone footage had captured – these large fevers, which can be hundreds, even thousands in some cases,” Wallace said. Cownose rays, however, are not new to Long Island. “The cownose rays are very common, often in very large groups, along beaches of Long Island, New York and Long Beach Island, New Jersey, in the surf and also in the quiet bay waters behind the barrier islands for at least the last 25 years,” said Thomas Grothues, associate research professor at Rutgers University, in New Jersey. “They are ‘newly’ discovered by beachgoers every year and are frequently mistaken for sharks because their wingtips protrude,.” Matthew Ajemian, associate research professor at Florida Atlantic University’s Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institute, said cownose rays have been documented in New York’s waters since the 1800s. While there may be more public sightings, he said, researchers must also consider how advances in drone technology have changed the way wildlife is observed by the general public and experts alike. “People are seeing them, I think, more frequently [in real life and online]. We also have to be aware of our observer bias too, because it’s so much easier for us to capture these types of things [nowadays],” Ajemian said, adding: “We have drone technology, which really helps with some of the capacity to see things that are relatively rare, although I guess the correct term for its abundance within New York is ‘uncommon’.” Echoing Ajemian, Kevin Weng, an associate professor at College of William & Mary Virginia Institute of Marine Science, said drones are particularly valuable for observing cownose rays from above, but researchers need to account for where and how often those observations are made. “Drones, amazing. What we need to understand is the distribution of observation effort,” he said. Still, researchers say drones offer a valuable new tool for studying cownose rays, especially when it comes to estimating their size and movement. “Drones are definitely giving us views and a perspective we haven’t seen before for a lot of species. Estimating population abundances for cownose rays is particularly difficult because they travel in such large schools. I think aerial drones may be a useful tool for estimating abundances of species like cownose rays that do spend a substantial amount of time near the surface,” Grubbs said. http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/12/pyong.text: North Korea conducted its second ballistic missile test in less than a week on Wednesday, South Korean media reports, in what is believed to be a protest against the upcoming military exercises between Seoul and Washington, which Pyongyang sees as a practice for an invasion.A ballistic missile fired from the North’s eastern coastal Wonsan area around 6 a.m. flew more than 700 kilometres, South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said.South Korea’s military condemned the test and warned it remains ready to repel any provocation by Pyongyang in cooperation with the United States. South Korea’s national security council called North Korean ballistic missile launches “acts of provocation” and urged the North to halt them immediately.The Japanese Defense Ministry also reported detecting the launch, saying the weapon landed in waters outside its exclusive economic zone, between the Korean Peninsula and Japan.Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi told reporters that Japan strongly protested the North Korean launch through their embassies in Beijing. “It’s a serious problem that affects the safety of the Japanese people,” he said.The launches, within days of each other, were seen as part of North Korea’s extended run of weapons tests as the country has refused to return to talks with the US and South Korea for years.It also came two days after South Korea and the United States announced they will kick off their annual large-scale military drills on 17 August to beef up readiness against North Korean threats.North Korea has previously responded to the Ulchi Freedom Shield training and other major South Korea-U.S. military exercises with provocative weapons tests and harsh rhetoric, although experts believe Pyongyang often uses its rivals’ military training as a pretext to boost its own testing activities. The US and South Korea have repeatedly said their training is defensive in nature.After last year’s Ulchi Freedom Shield training exercises began, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said the drills showed the US and South Korea’s “will to ignite a war” and claimed they have grown more provocative than before, which has prompted North Korea to respond with “proactive and overwhelming” countermeasures.Last week, on 6 August, South Korea, the US, and Japan detected the launch of a short-range ballistic missile from North Korea in what was the North’s first ballistic weapons testing activity since late June.Pyongyang didn’t confirm the reported launch, though it usually releases details of weapons tests a day later.

https://www.dw.com/en/short-on-us-patrio.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IetU Eight batteries for US Patriot interceptor missiles are stationed across Ukraine, but President Zelenskyy is looking elsewhere for missiles Image: Jens Büttner/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Russia is increasingly relying on ballistic missiles for its attacks on Ukraine — precisely the weapons that Ukraine 's armed forces depend heavily on Western support to ward off. However, the crucial US -produced Patriot interceptor missiles are often in short supply. How urgently does Ukraine need new Patriot missiles? Extremely urgently. While Ukraine has set up a well-functioning defense network against drones , its armed forces are reaching their limits when it comes to fending off Iskander-M ballistic missiles. One of the few weapons capable of countering such missiles is, above all, the Patriot system with its PAC-3 interceptor missiles. At the beginning of August, it became evident once again how patchy Ukraine's air defense has become. During a Russian attack on August 1, Ukraine could only intercept one of 27 ballistic missiles fired. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said this was due to the fact that there were practically no more Patriot interceptor missiles left for the eight batteries stationed across Ukraine. Three days later, according to Ukraine, Russia fired another 24 ballistic missiles as well as four Zircon hypersonic missiles, of which none were intercepted. Ukraine faces Patriot missile shortage To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The French/Italian SAMP/T is considered an alternative to the Patriot system. However, Ukraine owns only a few of those, and the required Aster-30 interceptor missiles are also in short supply. In addition, the more powerful new-generation SAMP/T NG will only gradually become available. Therefore, the system is not a European short-term alternative to Patriot. At the same time, Patriot deliveries are declining. According to Zelenskyy, Ukraine received only about one-third as many anti-aircraft missiles so far this year as it did in 2025. The war in the Middle East has further exacerbated the global shortage. Unlike at the beginning of the Ukraine war, the problem today lies less with launching facilities and more with Patriot ammunition. What are the dimensions of Russia's missile capabilities? Although exact Russian figures are not publicly available, there are numerous indications that Russia is ramping up its production. Moscow has, for example, significantly increased production of Iskander-M and Kinzhal ballistic and air-launched missiles. According to current estimates, it produces around 60 to 65 Iskander-M missiles per month alone, which amounts to more than 700 per year. Reports indicate there are apparently shipments from North Korea as well. According to Ukraine, Pyongyang has supplied Russia with some 150 ballistic missiles since the end of 2023. In addition, a North Korean missile unit that has recently been deployed to Russia could be equipped with up to 120 additional missiles. Ukraine calls on allies to help with air defenses To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video According to Ukraine's Defense Ministry, Russia launched 195 ballistic missiles of various types in July alone. Only 29 of them could be intercepted. Ukraine's military intelligence service estimates that Russia is currently capable of firing up to 100 ballistic missiles per month without depleting its stocks. In contrast, US missile producer Lockheed Martin supplied only 620 modern PAC-3 MSE interceptor missiles worldwide in 2025. The company plans to increase its annual production capacity to 2,000 units, but only as part of a seven-year program. Did the US allow Ukraine to build its own Patriots? According to defense intelligence platform Army Recognition, an average of only some 133 Patriot interceptor missiles have been delivered to Ukraine per year since the start of the war. Given the intensity of Russian missile attacks this isn't much, which is why another option is gaining importance in Kyiv : domestic production. In the wake of the NATO summit in Ankara in July, the Ukrainian government presented the matter as largely settled. Zelenskyy cited a political decision by US President Donald Trump to grant Ukraine licenses for the production of Patriot interceptor missiles. As recently as July 28, it was declared after a meeting of the two leaders in Washington that both presidents had had talks about the "implementation" of this decision. Will there be a Patriot deal? Zelenskyy visited the White House in late July Image: Selenskyj/Telegram Three days later, Trump caused confusion. The US had not yet approved Ukrainian production; it had to be "careful," Trump said, with this kind of technology transfer. Nonetheless, the talks are continuing. According to information from Reuters news agency, American and Ukrainian representatives are considering, among other options, a model in which components are produced in Ukraine and missiles are initially assembled in Germany . Kyiv's participation in the production of a new, less expensive Patriot missile is also under discussion. How quickly could Ukraine build Patriot missiles on its own? Not fast enough to solve the current problem of overburdening. Outgoing Ukrainian ambassador in Washington, Olha Stefanishyna, estimated that setting up production of Patriot missiles in Ukraine was a process that could take anywhere from 12 months to five years. A modern interceptor missile has numerous highly specialized components. A shortage of seeker heads, electronics or missile motors, for example, can limit the entire production. Until a domestic production is established, Kyiv is trying to obtain Patriot missiles more quickly. To this end, other customers are to pass on their shipments to Ukraine and get replacements at a later date. What's the status of Ukraine's own developments? Ukraine is no longer working alone on a system of its own, but is trying to set up a European-Ukrainian missile defense project instead. The program is known as Freya. The core of the system will be the FP7.X interceptor missile provided by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point. According to the company's CTO, Iryna Terekh, its architecture is based on Soviet designs for the S-300 and S-400 air defense systems. Today's missile, however, had only some 20% in common with its predecessors, Terekh said. Iryna Terekh, chief technical officer of Ukrainian arms manufacturer Fire Point, said the FP7.X interceptor missile is based on Soviet designs Image: Anna Pshemyska/DW Now involved in the project are, according to Fire Point, more than a dozen European arms manufacturers. Their goal is to develop an interceptor missile costing less than €1 million ($1.15 million), which would make it less expensive than the modern Patriot PAC-3 missiles ($5 million). However, this system will not be quickly available either. The Ukrainian side aims to have a prototype ready during the first half of 2027. This article was originally written in German. https://www.politico.eu/article/russia-k.text: Russian authorities said Ukraine’s overnight bombardment of the western Krasnodar region killed two people and injured at least 12. Andrei Kravchenko, mayor of the Russian city Novorossiysk, said the attack killed one child and injured eight people. Drone debris damaged four businesses and 21 residential buildings, including apartment blocks, he said. Krasnodar Krai regional governor, Veniamin Kondratyev, said on his Telegram channel that more buildings were damaged elsewhere in the region, killing one man and injuring four people. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attack on Wednesday but insisted that Kyiv’s forces had targeted the naval base in Novorossiysk, which he called “the last major stronghold of the Russian fleet in the Black Sea.” Advertisement Advertisement “Our Palianytsia jet-powered drones, Neptune missiles, and unmanned naval systems successfully struck the designated targets. Hits on air defense positions, piers, and seaport infrastructure have been confirmed,” wrote Zelenskyy on X . “The occupation fleet and all the infrastructure supporting it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues,” he warned Moscow. Russia’s defense ministry said the country’s air defenses had intercepted and destroyed 502 Ukrainian drones over several regions and the Black Sea overnight. Moscow has stepped up its missile attacks on Ukraine in recent months, killing dozens of Ukrainian civilians, while Kyiv has hit back at Russian targets, including oil refineries and warehouses belonging to Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries. Last week, an intercepted Ukrainian drone crashed onto a Russian beach , killing seven people and injuring 40.

https://www.politico.eu/article/andy-bur.text: LONDON — Prime Minister Andy Burnham will lead a meeting of the government's emergency committee Wednesday afternoon in response to ongoing heatwaves, droughts and wildfires across the U.K. COBR (Cabinet Office Briefing Room) meetings are convened during a crisis or emergency — and come as the record-breaking conditions take a severe toll on U.K. infrastructure. The crisis is an early test for Burnham, who came to office just last month. Advertisement Advertisement A Downing Street spokesperson said: “We know how challenging this summer is proving, particularly for firefighters tackling wildfires, farmers working in drought conditions, and NHS staff in busy A&E units. “We will continue to take the action needed to keep communities safe, protect water supplies, support farming communities and safeguard the environment.” Britons are this week bracing for their fifth heatwave of 2026, with some temperatures forecast to exceed 36C. The Met Office, Britain's national weather service, has warned that this summer is set to be the U.K.'s hottest since records began. More than two-thirds of England is now in drought after the driest July since records began in 1836. The whole of Wales is also in drought, and more than 27 million people across the U.K. are facing water restrictions including hosepipe bans. The U.K. is grappling with wildfires including at the New Forest national park in south England. The National Fire Chiefs Council responded to 458 wildfires last month, its busiest month on record. 'Snail's pace' The rival Green Party first demanded a COBR meeting weeks ago after a wildfire engulfed parts of Suffolk in eastern England. Green Leader Zack Polanski said Wednesday's meeting is “only a first step. This is a climate emergency which is leading to hundreds of deaths and stretching our firefighters, health staff and farmers to the limit. What we urgently need is concrete action.” Advertisement Advertisement Liberal Democrat Energy Spokesperson Pippa Heylings warned a COBR meeting alone “will not put out fires or protect our communities,” and said government is “moving at a snail’s pace.” Prior to today's COBR, the U.K.'s National Drought Group and Severe Weather Resilience Network have held regular meetings, and the government has also vowed to work with water companies to build nine new reservoirs for the U.K. — which built its last reservoir back in 1992. U.K. climate advisers have meanwhile spent much of the summer urging the country to up its game when it comes to adaptation for a warming world. The Committee on Climate Change, a government advisory body, said in May that cooling to protect from heat, “increased flood preparedness, and improved water management are the highest priorities.” “Deploying these adaptations at scale will help avoid loss of life – particularly amongst those most vulnerable to climate impacts – and unnecessary damage and disruption to people and to the economy,” it said. The U.K. has been “built to a climate that no longer exists,” Swenja Surminski, a member of the Climate Change Committee Adaptation Committee, told MPs in June. Additional reporting by Charlie Cooper. Advertisement Advertisement

https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/08/12/tran.text: Menü Kereső Kiderülhetett, hova menekült a körözött lengyel politikus, akinek korábban Orbánék adtak menedéket Külföld Aradi Hanga Zsófia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Transznisztriában, a Moldovától elszakadt, orosz megszállás alatt álló szakadár régióban tartózkodhat Marcin Romanowski volt lengyel igazságügyi miniszterhelyettes. Erről először a lengyel RMF FM számolt be . A rádió nem hivatalos forrásból úgy értesült, Romanowski a varsói kerületi bíróságra adott be hivatalos kérvényt, amelyben a lakhelyéül egy triaszpoli címet adott meg. A politikus azért fordult a bírósághoz, hogy garanciát kérjen arra, hogy ha személyesen megjelenik a lengyel igazságszolgáltatás előtt, akkor szabadlábon védekezhet. A varsói kerületi bíróság szóvivője megerősítette, hogy Romanowski augusztus 4-én kérelmet nyújtott be, amit továbbítottak az ügyészségre. Triaszpol Transznisztria fővárosa, a dokumentum alapján feltételezhető, hogy Romanowski ide menekült, miután július elején a magyar kormány visszavonta tőle az előző, Orbán Viktor vezette kormány által biztosított politikai menedékjogot. A lengyel politikus már a választások után elhagyta Magyarországot. Transznisztria hivatalosan Moldovához tartozik, egyetlen ENSZ-tagország sem ismeri el önállóságát. A Lengyelországban korrupcióval vádolt Marcin Romanowski 2024 decemberében menekült Magyarországra, és kapott politikai menedékjogot az Orbán-kormánytól. A lengyel ügyészség többek között közpénzekkel való visszaéléssel és korrupcióval gyanúsítja a nacionalista-konzervatív Jog és Igazságosság (PiS) párt politikusát. A lengyel ügyészség a napokban utasította el a kérelmét, hogy szüntessék meg ellene az előzetes letartóztatást, és ejtsék a vádak egy részét is. Ebben az ügyben érintett a korábbi igazságügyi miniszter, Zbigniew Ziobro is. Őt azzal gyanúsítják, hogy még a PiS kormányzása idején igazságügyi miniszterként szervezett bűnözői csoportot alapított és irányított. A szervezet a gyanú szerint akár több mint 150 millió złotyt (12,7 milliárd forint) is elsikkaszthatott. A korábbi lengyel igazságügyi miniszter jelenleg is körözés alatt áll Lengyelországban. Ziobro szintén Magyarországon bujkált, miután idén januárban menedékjogot kapott Orbán-kormánytól . Romanowskival együtt ő és a felesége is elhagyta az országot, miután Magyar Péter kilátásba helyezte, hogy a Tisza kormányalakítása után kiadják őket Lengyelországnak. Magyar korábban arra utalt, hogy Ziobro az Egyesült Államok felé távozott , Romanowski pedig Szerbia felé hagyta el Magyarországot. Ziobro kapcsán az RMF FM azt írja, Lengyelország július végén hivatalosan is kérte a kiadatását az Egyesült Államoktól. Arra, hogy Romanowski most az oroszbarát Transznisztriában bujkálhat, több lengyel politikus is reagált . „Úgy tűnik, új szokásunk van. A menekülés Transznisztriába, amelyet bizonyos mértékben Oroszország irányít. Azt hiszem, ezt nem is kell kommentálni” – mondta a rádiónak Cezary Tomczyk, a Polgári Koalíció védelmi miniszterhelyettese. Több lengyel parlamenti képviselő is arról írt a közösségi médiában, Romanowski lépése újabb bizonyíték arra, hogy a PiS orosz érdekeket szolgál ki, a politikust pedig hamarosan fel is használhatja az orosz propaganda. Romanowski nemcsak menedékjogot kapott az Orbán-kormánytól. A Direkt36 derítette ki , hogy a korrupcióval vádolt politikus a Fidesz-frakció egyik munkatársának lakásában lakott, és munkát is kapott a kormányközeli Alapjogokért Központnál, ahol Magyar–Lengyel Szabadság Intézet vezetője lett. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/12/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter: Döntött a kormány, fenékküszöbbel és annak kiépítéséig két elsüllyeszthető bárkával emelnék a Duna vízszintjét Belföld Nádor András Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Egy dunai fenékküszöb építésének azonnali megkezdését és ezzel párhuzamosan egy ideiglenes megoldás előkészítését rendeltük el – mondta Magyar Péter szerdai rendkívüli tájékoztatóján. Ideiglenes megoldásként két, potenciálisan elsüllyeszthető, 80 méteres bárkát fognak készenlétbe helyezni Paksnál. A beruházást a sürgőssége miatt kiemeltnek minősítette a kormány, hatmilliárd forintba fog kerülni. A miniszterelnök bejelentette: ha elkészül a fenékküszöb, akár egy méterrel is képes lesz megemelni a vízszintet a területen. „A kormány a mai helyszínbejárást követően a vízügyi, energetikai és védelmi szakemberek egybehangzó javaslata alapján meghozta a döntést arról, hogy haladéktalanul, már a holnapi napon megkezdjük a Duna két partjától, a paksi atomerőmű és Dunaszentbenedek település között egy Dunai fenékküszöb építését, első körben 35 ezer, majd 110 ezer köbméter kő felhasználásával.” A miniszterelnök szerint a beruházással „pár héten belül biztosítható, hogy a Dunai vízszint az atomerőmű hűtőcsatornájánál ne csökkenjen mínusz 90 cm alá, és ennek következtében Magyarország legfontosabb erőműve teljes kapacitással működhessen”. Bejelentette azt a kormánydöntést is, hogy „a várhatóan ismét rendkívül gyorsan apadó vízszint miatt” a fenékküszöb építésével párhuzamosan készenlétbe helyeznek Paksnál két 80 méter hosszúságú bárkát. „Szükség esetén készen állunk arra, hogy ezen két bárka irányított elsüllyesztésével rövid távon akár 20 centimétert emeljünk a Duna vízszintjén, hogy ezzel a végleges fenékküszöb elkészültéig is elkerülhető legyen a paksi erőmű teljes leállítása.” Magyar azt mondta, a két beavatkozás, a fenékküszöb építése és a bárkák készenlétbe helyezése egymást fogja kiegészíteni. Szerinte jelenleg ez a leghatékonyabb és legbiztonságosabb megoldás, és ezt támogatják a szakértők és a hatóságok is. A védelmi és kivitelezési munkálatok koordinálásával és irányításával Kádár Pál tábornokot, a Védelmi Igazgatási Hivatal vezetőjét bízta meg a miniszterelnök. A kormányfő szerint már ma este Paksra érkezik az ideiglenes megoldáshoz szükséges egyik 80 méteres bárka Mohácsról, és holnap már a második is itt lesz. Szerdán derült ki, hogy felterjesztéssel fordult a paksi önkormányzat a magyar kormányhoz, amelyben azt kérték, a megváltozott klimatikus viszonyok miatt a kormány vizsgálja felül a paksi atomerőmű hosszú távú biztonságos hűtővízellátását garantáló valamennyi lehetséges megoldást. Barnabás István, Paks alpolgármestere a felterjesztés tartalmáról azt mondta, az önkormányzat nem egy konkrét műszaki megoldást javasol, hanem a szóba jöhető javaslatok vizsgálatát, és az alacsony vízállásból eredő problémák megoldását kéri. Magyar Péter kedden közölte, hogy szerdán a paksi atomerőműben ülésezik a kormány . Szerdai posztjából derült ki, hogy a buszozó miniszterekkel ellentétben ő helikopterrel ment a kormányülésre. https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/08/12/tis.text: Menü Kereső Kellenek a magyar műholdak, de nem biztos, hogy a 4iG-vel: a Tisza-kormány felülvizsgálja a csoport állami gigamegrendelését Gazdaság Legfontosabb Jászai Gellért, a 4iG-csoport elnöke, Sárhegyi István, a Remred társalapítója és a 4iG Space and Technology Zrt. vezérigazgatója, Tessely Zoltán fideszes országgyűlési képviselő és Nagy Márton nemzetgazdasági miniszter elhelyezi az időkapszulát a 4iG Space and Technology űripari holdingvállalat gyártással foglalkozó portfólióvállalata, a Remred Zrt. martonvásári űrtechnológiai gyártóközpontjának alapkőletételi ünnepségén, 2024. május 6-án – Fotó: Vasvári Tamás / MTI Brückner Gergely Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Tanács Zoltán tudományos és technológiai miniszter nemrég bejelentette, hogy a magyar kormány a következő években 500 millió euró (mintegy 180 milliárd forint) értékben fektet be az IRIS² uniós fejlesztésbe. A betűszó az Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite rövidítése, és a műholdas ellenálló képességet, összekapcsolhatóságot és biztonságot szolgáló infrastruktúrát takarja, gyakorlatilag az Unió a Starlink európai alternatíváját szeretné stratégiai okokból kifejleszteni. Vagyis egy olyan rendszer készül, ami műholdak segítségével a világűrből szórhat gyors és megbízható internetet. A jelenleg háttérben hozzáférhető információk szerint a nagy fejlesztés zöme Belgiumban, az Aerospacelab nevű vállalatnál valósulhat majd meg, de sok minden nem nyilvános még a projektről. Így például az is kérdés, pontosan milyen lehetőségeket jelent majd a magyar hozzájárulás a hazai űrvállalkozások számára. A cél, hogy egy olyan uniós műholdalapú infokommunikációs rendszer jöjjön létre, amelynek révén a haváriák esetén is elérhető egy megbízható, nagy sávszélességű európai zárt kommunikációs csatorna. Ezzel összefüggésben az IRIS² számos kormányzati alkalmazást támogat majd, a válságkezelés (humanitárius segítségnyújtás), valamint a kulcsfontosságú infrastruktúrák összekapcsolása és védelme (biztonságos kommunikáció az EU nagykövetségei számára) területén. Igen ám, de ahogy arról a Hvg.hu beszámolt, Magyarországnak már van egy korábban megvalósított, hasonló tartalmú szerződése, hiszen a tőzsdén jegyzett 4iG-csoporttal kötött állami HUSAT-program 2030-ra valami ilyesmit ígért. Például dual-use földmegfigyelési műholdak gyártásáról szólt Magyarországon (a szeptember végén elkészülő martonvásári Remtech nevű gyártóközpontban), ahol 8 alacsony Föld körüli pályára szánt műhold készül. A Hvg.hu cikkében az szerepelt, hogy az új tervek fényében megszűnhet a 4iG-csoport kiemelt státusza az űriparban, miután a Tisza-kormány átalakítja a források elosztásáért felelős intézményeket. Ebben a cikkben annak jártunk utána, mi forog kockán, és milyen kimenetek lehetségesek a most zajló folyamatban. Témába vágó kérdéseinkre mind Tanács Zoltántól, mind a 4iG-csoporttól kaptunk válaszokat, a céggel folytatott háttérbeszélgetésen Sárhegyi István, a 4iG Űr- és Védelmi Zrt. vezérigazgatója és Zábori Balázs, a csoporton belüli űripari vállalat, a Remred technológiai igazgatója tájékoztatta a Telexet. A HUSAT-megállapodások Mint Tanács Zoltán a Telexnek elmondta, a 4iG Űr- és Védelmi Technológiák Zrt.-vel a magyar állam három, egymáshoz kapcsolódó szerződést kötött, ezek együttes, bruttó kötelezettségvállalási értéke 2,36 milliárd euró. Az utolsó két szerződés megkötésére, amelyek tovább bővítették a korábban megkötött szolgáltatási tartalmat, közvetlenül a 2026-os országgyűlési választás előtt került sor. Az első szerződést (telekommunikációs és földmegfigyelési szolgáltatás + előkészítő tevékenység) 2024. december 5-én kötötték a felek, és 2040. december 31-én fut ki, ennek értéke bruttó 1,669 milliárd euró. A második szerződés (áthidaló LEO telekommunikációs szolgáltatás) 2026. március 13-án született, ez 2031. december 1-jén fut ki, az értéke bruttó 311 millió euró. Végül a harmadik szerződés (bővített földmegfigyelési kapacitás) 2026. április 2-án keletkezett, 2034. június 1-jéig tart, és bruttó 381 millió euró az értéke. Ez így együtt még a mai árfolyamon, a szerződések megkötésének idejénél erősebb forinttal számolva is több mint 855 milliárd forintot jelent. Ráadásul Tanács Zoltán szerint „az állam által a 4iG-nek kiszerződött űripari szolgáltatások árbevétele egyes becslések szerint akár százszorosan is meghaladhatja a 4iG cégcsoport űripari szegmensének a szerződések megkötése előtti, néhány milliárd forintos árbevételét. Ez nyilvánvalóan nem egy szerves, piacilag megalapozott növekedést jelent képességekben, kapacitásokban.” A szerződések átvilágításán túl a jelenlegi kormány azt is vizsgálja, hogy a 4iG leszállítási képességei, potenciális külső beszállító partnerei mennyire adottak a sokéves szerződésben vállalt szakmai feladatokhoz. Kérdéseinkre a 4iG-t azt írta, „egyoldalú megközelítés a két éve létrehozott holding egyetlen éves árbevételét 15 évre szóló szerződések teljes értékével összevetni”. Álláspontjuk szerint a HUSAT-programhoz szükséges földi és űrinfrastruktúra beruházási igénye rendkívül magas, valamint a 4iG Űr és Védelmi Zrt. létrehozásakor nem új, tapasztalat nélküli vállalkozások kezdték meg működésüket: a holdingba olyan, 10-30 éves múlttal, jelentős árbevétellel, infrastruktúrával és nemzetközi referenciákkal bíró űripari társaságokat és képességeket szerveztek, mint a Remred vagy a Hungaro DigiTel (HDT), kiegészítve a 4iG több évtizedes informatikai, adatközponti és adatfeldolgozási kompetenciáival – közölték a Telex érdeklődésére. A 4iG szerint a csoport célja az volt, hogy ezeket az addig különálló képességeket integrálja, ezért nem mesterséges árbevétel-növekedésről, hanem nemzetstratégiai jelentőségű kritikus infrastruktúráról van szó, amely hosszú távon a magyar űripar nemzetközi pozícióját, valamint a magyar gazdaság- és iparfejlesztésben betöltött szerepét is meghatározhatja. A cég válaszában azt is ígérte, hogy partnerek lesznek: „állunk minden olyan vizsgálat elé, amely a HUSAT-szerződések jogi vagy szakmai megfelelőségét, illetve a vállalt szolgáltatások leszállításához szükséges képességeket vizsgálja”. Ugyanakkor furcsállják, ami történik, hiszen mint írták, az elmúlt időszakban nyilvánosságra hozták a saját űripari képességeik több tízmilliárd forintból megvalósuló fejlesztését, valamint a nemzetközi technológiai és beszállítói megállapodásaikat. Nézetkülönbség tehát bőven van, és hogy még összetettebb legyen a kép: Jászai Gellért, a 4iG Nyrt. vezetője augusztus elején az Egyesült Államokba utazott, és – mint a LinkedIn-profilján tudósított – fontos stratégiai együttműködésekről tárgyalt. A megbeszélések középpontjában egyebek között a HUSAT-program finanszírozása állt (J.P. Morgan, Export-Import Bank of the United States), illetve tárgyalás folyt a szakmai részletekről (Northrop Grumman). Vagyis leegyszerűsítve: itthon vizsgálat jön, ami potenciálisan veszélyeztetheti a meglévő szerződéseket, de a magáncég ettől függetlenül mintha menne előre a nemzetközi finanszírozásban is. Politikai konfliktus A Tisza-kormány és a 4iG viszonyáról amúgy is érdemes lenne beszélni. A 4iG az Orbán-érában kifejezetten mélyre ásta magát mindenféle, Magyarország számára kulcsfontosságú kritikus infrastruktúrába (távközlés, védelmi ipar, űripar), utóbbi kettőben amolyan nemzeti „prime” kívánt lenni, vagyis olyan magánvállalat, amely összefogja az elsősorban állami megrendelésekből álló szektor magánszereplőit. A szereplők egy része be is tagozódott alá, mások az egész modellt kárhoztatták, mert szerintük a 4iG-nél központosított forráselosztás miatt ígéretes hazai kkv-k maradtak ki a támogatott projektekből. Az új vezetés, vagyis a Tisza-kormány pedig egyelőre mintha se kiköpni, se lenyelni nem tudná a helyzetet. Időnként felbukkannak a nyilvánosság előtt olyan hatalmas értékű szerződések, amelyek az új állami vezetés számára láthatóan kellemetlen meglepetést jelentenek. Ezek némelyike a tőzsdén korábban bejelentett publikus szerződés, de olyanok is vannak, amelyeknek a puszta léte is titok volt eddig a közvélemény előtt. Ezekből a legismertebb az a 10 évre kötött védelmi informatikai megállapodás volt, amely 1311 milliárd forint értékben született, és amelynél egy 38 milliárd forintos előlegszámla várta az új kormányt. A 4iG-nek ezen kívül van egy hasonló méretű harcijármű-szerződése, és mint most megtudtuk, több műholdas szerződése is. Ebben az írásunkban az európai és a magyar műholdas szerződésekről írunk. Tanács Zoltán szerint Magyarországnak szüksége van korszerű műholdas kommunikációs és földmegfigyelési szolgáltatásokra, és a hazai űripar fejlesztésére. De szerinte ezt a korábbi kormány gyakorlatától eltérő módon nem egyetlen cégre építve szükséges fejleszteni, hanem a hazai kkv-k tucatjait bevonva, kihasználva az Európai Unió és az Európai Űrügynökség által kínált lehetőségeket. A 4iG képviselőinek fő gondolata szerint viszont az állam és a 4iG-csoport között megkötött, most vizsgálandó HUSAT-megállapodások az európai modellbe illeszkednek, és fontos nemzeti képességeket hoznak létre. Vagyis a cég azt mondja, a komplex távközlési, műholdirányítási és nagy felbontású földmegfigyelési szolgáltatásokat egyaránt tartalmazó HUSAT nem az IRIS² alternatívája vagy versenytársa, hanem annak magyar kiegészítője, mivel eltérő fókusszal és jellemzőkkel bír. A 4iG-nél végig azt hangsúlyozták nekünk, hogy a „prime” logikája pontosan ez: vagyis nem egy cég vesz részt a fejlesztésekben, hanem a program megvalósítását az integrátor csak összefogja, de a kkv-k, a kutatóintézetek és egyetemek bevonását lehetővé téve összehangolja tevékenységüket. Európa korábban a tudományos részre ment rá Szakadjunk el egy kicsit attól a hazai vitától, amiről még sokat fogunk hallani, és nézzük a nagy képet! Az űrszektornak két elkülönülő iránya van: az űrkutatás, amely a világűr tudományos vizsgálatát, valamint az alaptudományi és alkalmazott K+F-projekteket foglalja magában, robotos és emberes küldetésekkel egyaránt; az űripar, amely a technológiákra, az eszközökre, a gyártásra és a szolgáltatásokra fókuszál. A 2010-es évek végére a világűr stratégiai jelentősége alapvetően megváltozott. Az űr többé már nemcsak kutatási vagy technológiai kérdésként jelent meg, hanem a gazdasági versenyképesség, a kritikus állami szolgáltatások, a katonai műveletek és a geopolitikai befolyás egyik meghatározó dimenziójává vált. A NATO maga is deklarálta, hogy 5 műveleti védelmi területet és képességet fejleszt (ezek: a szárazföldi, a tengeri, a légi, a kiber és az űr). Közben megjelentek a magáncégek, a kereskedelmi űripar is, mint a SpaceX, a Planet Labs, a Maxar, az ICEYE, az Axiom vagy a BlackSky, és bebizonyították, hogy a korábban kizárólag állami monopóliumnak tekintett képességek kereskedelmi alapon is létrehozhatók. Az Egyesült Államok, Kína és Oroszország az elmúlt évtizedben egyaránt stratégiai fontosságúként tekintett a világűrre. Az Egyesült Államok létrehozta az önálló Space Force-t, Kína saját globális navigációs rendszert épített ki, miközben rendkívüli ütemben növelte műholdas és indítási kapacitásait, Oroszország pedig továbbra is jelentős katonai és felderítő műholdas infrastruktúrát tart fenn. Az európai űrtevékenység önmagában sokáig nem volt olyan jelentős, mint amit más nagyhatalmaknál láthattunk. Európa fejlődését hosszú időn keresztül alapvetően a tudományos együttműködés és a közös technológiafejlesztés határozta meg. Az Európai Űrügynökség (ESA) – amely nem EU-s, hanem összeurópai szervezet, és jelenleg huszonhárom tagállamot tömörít – megalakulása óta azon dolgozott, hogy az európaiak egyesítsék erőforrásaikat olyan képességek létrehozása érdekében, amelyeket önállóan csak a legnagyobb államok tudtak volna finanszírozni. Az ESA-nak voltak is szép fejlesztési sikerei, ilyen volt az Ariane hordozórakéta-család, a Columbus Orbital Facility, egy európai kutatómodul, a Rosetta űrszonda vagy a Mars Express, az ESA első bolygómegfigyelő küldetése. A szervezetnek Magyarország is tagja volt az elmúlt évtizedben, és az utóbbi időben még növelte is a hozzájárulását. Így évi 20-30 millió eurót fizetünk be az ügynökségnek, amelynek van egy „geo-return” nevű elve, ez alapján a tagállami befizetéseknek megfelelő összeg megy vissza a tagállamok sikeresen pályázó cégeihez. Emiatt a magyar cégek számára még mindig jelentős, szabadon megpályázható, versenypályázati forrás állna rendelkezésre. Ennek oka a magyar űrszektor éretlensége: Magyarország eddig csak alacsonyabb értékű projekteket tudott lehívni – mondta Zábori Balázs, a Remred vezetője erről a Telexnek. Mint a szakember mesélte, ő és társai, egykori BME-s fiatalok, a Magyar Tudományos Akadémia Energiatudományi Kutatóközpont égisze alatt indították el a később sikeressé vált Remred Kft. (később Remred Zrt.) nevű céget. Miután több nagy ESA-projekt is itthon indulhatott el, a kutatóintézeti spin-off olyan űrügynökségekkel dolgozott és dolgozik ma is együtt, mint az említett ESA, vagy az amerikai NASA, a japán JAXA, illetve a német DLR. Később a 4iG-csoport ebbe a cégbe fektetett be, és ennek bázisán kezdte el kialakítani a saját űripari képességeit. Mára ilyen profilú cég vagy részesedés a 4iG-csoportban a HDT műholdas távközlési szolgáltató, ami a tervek szerint a HUSAT műholdjainak irányítását végzi majd, továbbá a földi állomásokat üzemelteti, valamint a NADIR Geospatial Solutions Zrt., amely a földmegfigyelési adatok feldolgozásáért felel. Emellett van két külföldi érdekeltsége is a 4iG-nek: az izraeli SpaceCom 20 százaléka, illetve a cégcsoport 100 millió dollárral beszállt az Axiom Space Inc . amerikai cégbe is, ezért 5 százalék alatti tulajdont szerzett. Utóbbi társaság vitte fel Kapu Tibort is az űrbe. Az ő küldetésének voltak kutatási aspektusai is, de a szakemberek szerint az űrutazásnak elsősorban az volt a nagy értéke, hogy a társadalom érdeklődését felkeltette az ágazat iránt, és jelezte, hogy Magyarországról sem lehetetlen feljutni az űrbe (Farkas Bertalannak, illetve a magyar származású Simonyi Károlynak sikerült ez korábban). Észbe kaptak az EU országai Európa államai az utóbbi időben elkezdtek azon gondolkodni, hogy a közös projektek mellett miként tudnának egyedileg is sikeresek lenni – mondta Zábori Balázs. A 2022-ben kitört orosz–ukrán háború e felismerést drámai módon felgyorsította. A műholdas kommunikáció (Starlink-típusú megoldások) biztosította a kritikus állami és katonai kapcsolattartást, amikor a földi hálózatok megsérültek vagy megsemmisültek. A konfliktus egyúttal arra is rámutatott, hogy Európa jelentős mértékben külső szereplőktől függ. Az Európai Bizottság ezután egyre következetesebben kezdte alkalmazni a „nyitott stratégiai autonómia” (open strategic autonomy) fogalmát. A koncepció lényege, hogy Európa önállóan is bírjon képességekkel, ezt követve Franciaország, Németország, Olaszország, Spanyolország, Lengyelország, Finnország, Svédország, Norvégia, Belgium és egyre több kisebb európai ország is saját műholdas programokat indított. A modellek eltérők. Franciaország és Németország teljes spektrumú űrhatalom kíván lenni. Olaszország és Spanyolország katonai és polgári feladatokra is alkalmas dual-use modellt választott, Lengyelország a felzárkózó modell példaországa, Finnország és Svédország a legmodernebb NewSpace-vállalatokra (az űripar területén belül valamilyen új technológiával foglalkozó startupokra) fókuszálnak, végül Norvégia és Luxemburg azt bizonyította, hogy kisebb országoknak is lehet önálló űrprogramjuk. A releváns kérdés persze nem az, hogy Magyarország képes-e ugyanazt felépíteni, mint Franciaország vagy Németország (mert nyilván nem képes), hanem az, hogy valamelyik képességterületen lehet-e csatlakozni. A legnagyobb európaiak, vagyis az Airbus, a Thales Alenia Space, az OHB, a Leonardo, a Hisdesat, az ICEYE vagy a SES fejlődésének közös eleme, hogy mindegyik mögött megjelent a hazai kormányzati megrendelő. Stephen Watkins had been awarded sole custody of his boys two months prior to their disappearance. York Regional Police said, with help from her father, the accused took the boys following her court-ordered weekend with them in March 2009, crossing the border to New York before boarding a flight to Germany then Poland. In 2012, Ustaszewska Watkins’ father was convicted in Newmarket of helping her flee and received an 18-month conditional sentence, including a year under house arrest. He has since died. Watkins eventually tracked his boys down in Poland and petitioned a Warsaw court to return them to Canada. His request was denied when the court ruled the boys were fully integrated into Polish society. The Watkins boys, who are now in their 20s, remained in Europe for years. Their mother has now been ordered by the court not to communicate with them or their father. Ustaszewska Watkins is represented by defence lawyer Anthony Bryant. The allegations against the accused have not been tested in court.

http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27921.text: Big News Network.com Hungarian nuclear reactor temporarily shut down as Danube drops to record low BUDAPEST, July 29 (Xinhua) -- The third unit of Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant has been temporarily shut down as the Danube River dropped to record low amid prolonged drought and extreme heat, an official announced on Wednesday. Istvan Kapitany, Hungary's Minister of Economy and Energy, stated on social media that the reactor shutdown was executed in accordance with predetermined operational safety guidelines as river levels continued to fall. The water level of the Danube River in Budapest fell to a record low of 31 centimeters on Tuesday, according to Hungary's General Directorate of Water Management. The shutdown followed earlier curtailments at the facility, which comprises four units with a combined capacity of around 2,000 megawatts. The minister said the shutdown was part of a carefully prepared plan prioritizing operational safety rather than an unexpected emergency. The plant relies on the Danube for cooling water, making flow reductions necessary to meet environmental regulations regarding water temperature. The temporary electricity deficit will be compensated by domestic renewable energy sources and increased power imports, Kapitany added, reassuring the public that Hungary's energy grid remains stable. https://bmmagazine.co.uk/business/one-hu.text: Lithuanian law allows a bank to freeze a suspicious transaction for a maximum of 10 business days without formal law-enforcement action. If your business account stays blocked longer than that, with no explanation and no evidence of a criminal investigation, courts have repeatedly ruled the freeze unlawful – and ordered the bank to return the funds plus interest. Revolut, the London-founded fintech, provides its European banking services through a subsidiary licensed in Lithuania and supervised by the Bank of Lithuania and the European Central Bank. It is there, in Vilnius, that a recent set of figures has drawn scrutiny – and with them a question that will be familiar to any British business following the UK’s own debate over frozen accounts: how long may a bank withhold a customer’s money before the law requires it to be returned? Rolandas Kiškis, head of Lithuania’s Financial Crime Investigation Service (FCIS – the country’s Financial Intelligence Unit), recently gave the Lithuanian Parliament’s Budget and Finance Committee a telling statistic: the agency receives around 100,000 suspicious transaction reports a year, and a striking 80% of them come from a single market player – Revolut Bank. As the FCIS head himself noted, most of these reports are generated automatically, by a system that files a report the moment it detects the faintest hint of risk. Revolut’s explanation is straightforward: the bank serves 57 million customers across the European Economic Area, so it naturally generates proportionally more reports, and its transaction monitoring relies on AI-driven systems that respond to potential fraud in real time. For a UK readership the relevance is twofold. Revolut is a British-founded company that many in the UK use, so how frozen funds are handled within its European operations is of natural interest. More practically, a large number of UK businesses operating across the Channel – those with EU subsidiaries, euro-denominated accounts or European customers – hold money with institutions licensed not by the FCA but by regulators in Vilnius, Dublin or Amsterdam. Where such an account is frozen, it is the law of that jurisdiction, not UK law, that governs the customer’s rights. Anti-money laundering compliance is, without question, an important, legally mandated duty for financial institutions. But this statistic has another side, one rarely discussed in public: behind every automatically generated report there is often a real customer whose funds are frozen, whose account may be blocked, and who frequently receives no explanation for weeks, months, sometimes over a year. “In practice, a number of these situations have no legal basis at all, and courts are increasingly ruling in customers’ favour,” says Dr. Justinas Jarusevičius, a partner and attorney at Lithuanian law firm Motieka & Audzevičius. How Long Can a Bank Legally Freeze Your Money? The 10-Business-Day Rule Lithuania’s Law on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing – the national implementation of the EU’s anti-money-laundering framework – sets out a clear mechanism. When a financial institution identifies a suspicious transaction, it must suspend it and report it to FCIS within three business hours (Art. 16). From that point, the decision shifts to the state. FCIS has 10 business days to take the steps needed to confirm or dispel its suspicions. If, within that period, the financial institution receives no instruction to apply a temporary restriction on ownership rights under the Code of Criminal Procedure, the transaction must be resumed. In other words, a customer’s funds can lawfully stay frozen over a suspicious transaction for longer than 10 business days only once law enforcement has become involved and applied criminal-procedure measures – measures that can themselves be challenged in court. In practice, Jarusevičius says, a different scenario often plays out: the financial institution blocks the account on its own initiative, tells the customer only that “compliance checks” are under way, or offers no explanation at all, while the funds sit “under review” for months – with no FCIS instruction, no pre-trial investigation, no court order. In such cases, if the institution cannot point to a specific legal basis, the freeze is unlawful and the institution faces civil liability. Who Has to Prove the Freeze Was Justified? What the Courts Have Ruled A telling example is a dispute recently concluded against NIUM EU, UAB, an electronic money institution licensed in Lithuania, in which Jarusevičius’s firm, Motieka & Audzevičius , represented two business clients. In June 2022, the institution cut off the clients’ access to accounts holding close to EUR 490,000, without any warning. Their complaints went unanswered, not within the 15-business-day deadline set by the Law on Payments, nor afterwards: the first substantive response arrived more than six months later, and the actual legal basis for freezing the funds was never disclosed until the case reached court. On 6 June 2024, the Vilnius Regional Court, in civil case No. e2-1187-643/2024, ruled that the institution had failed to prove any legal basis for withholding the clients’ funds. The court rejected the institution’s defence, which relied on an instruction from a UK regulator addressed to the institution’s sister company: that instruction was neither binding on the Lithuanian entity in its dealings with its own clients, nor did it cover the claimants, who had no contractual relationship with the entities named in it. It was also significant that nothing in the case showed FCIS had ever been informed about the clients’ transactions at all, meaning the statutory prevention mechanism had never even been triggered. On 12 December 2024, the Lithuanian Court of Appeal, in civil case No. e2A-510-912/2024, upheld the first instance ruling and set out a rule with significant practical implications: in disputes of this kind, it is the financial institution that must prove it reasonably restricted the client’s account access and had the right to withhold the funds. A vague reference to AML law, or to a generic contract clause allowing the institution to suspend services “in accordance with legal requirements” is not enough – the institution must identify and prove the specific statutory provision, or the specific instruction from a competent authority, underlying its actions. This Court of Appeal case is not an isolated one. Lithuanian courts are currently hearing a number of similar cases in which clients of Lithuania-licensed financial institutions are seeking the return of funds held in their accounts but frozen by those institutions. The outcome for the clients was not just the return of their funds (the institution transferred most of it once it learned of the court proceedings) – the court also awarded 12.5% annual interest for the period between the filing of the case and the return of the funds, plus legal costs. What Should a Customer Whose Funds Are Frozen Do? Jarusevičius recommends three practical steps. First, demand a written explanation of the grounds for the freeze. Under the Law on Payments, payment service providers must inform customers about the blocking of a payment instrument and its reasons (with narrow statutory exceptions), and must review a written complaint and provide a reasoned response within 15 business days. Second, track the timeline. If more than 10 business days have passed since the transaction was suspended and the customer has received no information about any measures taken by law enforcement, the continued freeze is likely without legal basis. Third, enforce your rights. Consumers can turn to the Bank of Lithuania, which resolves disputes between consumers and financial market participants out of court. For business clients, the main route is litigation, where they can claim not only the return of their funds but also interest for the period the funds were unlawfully withheld. The case law above shows that the burden of proof in these disputes falls on the financial institution, and that a passive stance by the institution, failing to respond to complaints, failing to disclose grounds, is weighed by courts in the client’s favour. Clients often ask whether they have to simply wait for the bank to act first. They don’t, Jarusevičius says. Once the 10-business-day window has passed with no sign of law-enforcement involvement, the customer can send a formal legal demand and, if that goes unanswered, file a claim – there is no requirement to keep waiting indefinitely for the institution to volunteer an explanation. Prevention – Yes. Arbitrariness – No. The problem is not the filing of suspicious activity reports itself – that is a statutory, socially useful duty, and a high volume of reports does not by itself indicate wrongdoing. The problem arises when risk management turns into the indefinite withholding of customer funds without legal basis, without information, and without law enforcement involvement. Lawmakers struck this balance clearly: a suspicion gives an institution the right to suspend a transaction for days, not months. After that, it is for the state to decide, and if it doesn’t, the money must go back to its owner. As the volume of automated reports keeps growing, that rule only becomes more relevant. For UK businesses that hold funds with EEA-licensed institutions, it is a distinction worth understanding before, not after, an account is frozen. Justinas Jarusevičius is an attorney representing clients in financial services litigation, including the case against NIUM EU, UAB described above. Newsflash Newsroom , 29.07.2026, 19:51 Healthcare. Romania’s caretaker government has approved hiring procedures for over 6,850 positions in the public healthcare sector. The decision was made amid all-out strikes in the healthcare system, initiated on Tuesday by the Sanitas Federation in nearly 500 public hospitals across the country. Trade unions are unhappy with the serious staff shortage and with the draft unified salary law, which they claim will reduce the income of healthcare workers. Caretaker prime minister Ilie Bolojan says the strike is based on misinformation related to this bill and promises no incomes will be cut. Defence. The Chamber of Deputies in Bucharest on Wednesday adopted the bill to approve the SAFE loan agreement between the European Union and Romania and worth nearly 17 billion euros of investments in defence and strategic infrastructure. Signed in May, the agreement was passed by the deputies in its original form, without amendments. The bill will next go to the Senate, which will have the final say on the matter. Also on Wednesday, the Chamber of Deputies, acting as the decision-making body, passed a bill providing for a temporary and gradual reduction in the excise duty on diesel fuel. The measure will be in force for three months, but may be further extended. Endorsed by all parliamentary groups, it aims to reduce fuel prices at the pump. Drought. The entire Danube basin is faced with severe drought. In Romania, the water flow is three times lower than the average for this period, and experts say that in early August it will get very close to the all-time low of 1,400 cubic meters per second recorded in 1985. Irrigation restrictions are in force in the area, but water supply to the public is not affected. Due to the extremely low level of the Danube, Unit 1 of the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant was shut down as a precaution and disconnected from the national energy system on Tuesday. While the state-owned company Nuclearelectrica said it would also conduct a controlled shutdown of the plant’s Reactor 2 on Thursday. A Danube cruise ship with 186 passengers on board ran aground, with the tourists later taken to the Bulgarian port of Vidin while the ship remained stuck in a sandbar on the Romanian shore. Anthem. Military ceremonies were held on Wednesday in Bucharest and in military units across the country to celebrate the National Anthem Day. In a message on this occasion, president Nicuşor Dan says the anthem has preserved its force as a driver of social cohesion and acts as a common denominator of the Romanian identity, represented by citizens within the borders and by communities in the diaspora. National Anthem Day was proclaimed by law in 1998 and is celebrated every year on July 29. Romania’s anthem, Deşteaptă-te române (Awaken, ye Romanian), written by Anton Pann on lyrics by Andrei Mureşanu, was officially performed for the first time in 1848, in the city of Râmnicu Vâlcea, a landmark in national history to this day. Earthquake. The president of Romania Nicuşor Dan on Wednesday sent a message of compassion for the victims of the earthquake that hit Japan. “Deeply saddened by the loss of lives following the earthquake in Japan. My heartfelt condolences go out to the affected families, and I wish a speedy recovery to the injured. Romania stands by Japan in these difficult times,” the president said in a social media post. At least 13 persons died after a 7.1 earthquake struck southwestern Japan on Tuesday, where authorities are carrying out rescue operations and assessing the extent of the damage caused by collapsed buildings, fires, power outages and transport disruptions. Wildfires. A new unit of 40 Romanian firefighters left for France today to help fight wildfires. This is the third unit in the mission carried out by Romania within the framework of the European Union Civil Protection Mechanism. Romania has extended its participation in the firefighting support mission in France by two weeks. Until mid-August, Romanian firefighters will be ready to step in, at the request of the French authorities, alongside the other European teams taking part in the mission. https://pittsburghquarterly.com/articles.text: Archive Contact Subscribe Advertise About What Does America Mean to Me? Local leaders share their thoughts on the eve of the nation's 250th anniversary by PQ Staff 2026 Summer July 29, 2026 On the eve of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, we asked a group of leading Pittsburghers to consider and answer that question. We thank them for giving their thoughts on this important occasion. MARK WIEDMAN, PRESIDENT, PNC America represents the promise that where you start doesn’t have to define where you end. It’s a country built on reinvention, where each generation moves us closer to our ideals. Pittsburgh reflects that spirit. Once forged by steel and industrial grit, it helped build the backbone of the nation. Today, as a center of innovation, technology, and healthcare, it’s shaping what comes next. Different eras, same purpose: pushing America forward. America is opportunity, resilience, and the confidence that tomorrow can be better than today. MAGGIE HARDY, OWNER & CEO, 84 LUMBER To me, having grown up in western Pennsylvania with my father, who started 84 Lumber 70 years ago, America means opportunity. Being privately held, we have the opportunity to make a difference for each person we touch in our company, through our customers, associates, vendors, and partners. For example, during Hurricane Katrina (just one of many natural disasters), we were the first boots on the ground to offer support. As America approaches its 250th year, it is our mission to deliver the American Dream to our people, watch them grow, and become future leaders that drive America for the next 250 years. TAO HE, BOARD DIRECTOR, PITTSBURGH CHINESE CULTURE CENTER As a Chinese immigrant who has lived in Pittsburgh for more than 20 years, America still means opportunities that I never would have had while in China. In China, I was a janitor working at a hotel. In the U.S., I am a CPA working at an over-100-year-old accounting firm. America means faith, which I found in Pittsburgh, and this helped me find my identity and my purpose in life. America means another chance, that I can push the restart button after each failure. I can learn and grow from my failures. America means family, which I am building up with my wife and my beautiful son and daughter. America means that I can forever dream big, work hard and have another chance. Thank you for everything, America. Happy 250th birthday, America. Long live America! JEFF FINKELSTEIN, PRESIDENT & CEO, JEWISH FEDERATION OF PITTSBURGH For my family, America wasn’t just opportunity; it was survival. All four of my grandparents came to America from Europe in the early 1900s. One, my grandfather Irving, arrived alone in Boston at age 20 with little education and nothing promised. He learned a trade, worked with dignity into his 70s, and built a life rooted in freedom and opportunity. While his family members who remained in Latvia were murdered by the Nazis, his descendants were given a future here. Their survival is America’s promise. I still believe in that promise — as a proud American, and a proud American Jew. KANAK IYER, FOUNDING PRESIDENT, ASIAN AMERICAN CHAMBER OF COMMERCE PITTSBURGH The American Dream is why so many of us come here. Did I achieve it? Not in conventional terms. But I have lived life on my own terms — the freedom to pursue a scientific dream. Could I have done that in India? Not at that time; the resources didn’t exist. In America, as a 27-year-old immigrant, I had my “aha” moment in a remarkable laboratory, an opportunity for which I will always be grateful. What followed were challenges: learning how to navigate the system and confronting systemic barriers. Yet none of that stopped me. I became an entrepreneur before I even knew the word, built my own enterprise, and found my way back to science to pursue what once felt impossible. That is what America means to me: possibility, resilience, and opportunity. REV. PAUL T. ABERNATHY, CEO, NEIGHBORHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT America is, above all, an idea by which people of goodwill continually form a political union founded on values expressed through radical commitment to honor the God-given dignity of all persons. As Americans, we speak of this union not in the sense of land, ethnicity, language or religion, but rather, as laws that guarantee the free pursuit of beauty, truth and goodness for every human within our borders. As we celebrate the 250th anniversary of this nation, I pray that it is the idea of America far more than the history of America that guides us well into our future. DAN ONORATO, EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT, HIGHMARK HEALTH & FORMER ALLEGHENY COUNTY EXECUTIVE America is both a promise and a responsibility. It is the promise that where you start doesn’t limit where you can go. Growing up on the North Side of Pittsburgh, I saw how hard work, strong communities, and opportunity can change lives and revive places. America also represents a responsibility to serve others and build institutions that endure. In public service, I’ve learned that responsibility is all about listening, solving real problems, and caring for people when they’re most vulnerable. At 250 years, we continue to shape the promise of this great nation and bear the responsibility of making it better today and tomorrow than it was yesterday. https://www.salisburyjournal.co.uk/featu.text: Military Salisbury Forces Briefing: Defence Secretary Dan Jarvis in Estonia By David Falcke Share 0 Comments 5 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Estonia update During a visit to Estonia, the Defence Secretary, Dan Jarvis, met personnel deployed on Operation CABRIT and saw a range of capabilities in action, including the Archer artillery system, Army Rangers, drones, military working dogs and close combat survivability equipment. Defence minister visits 1 Royal Welsh. (Image: NATO) Over the past week, the 1 R WELSH Battlegroup has been on Exercise Bold Dragon, focusing on combined arms manoeuvre interoperability and working with French artillery soldiers, attended a live-fire exercise featuring the British Army's Archer self-propelled artillery system. British Military Working Dogs attached to the NATO Multinational Battlegroup Estonia featured at the Estonian Police Open Day to showcase the fantastic abilities of these four-legged friends. Sappers in Lithuania Sappers visit Vilnius in Lithuania. (Image: 22 Regt RE) Recently, 40 personnel from 22 Engineer Regiment deployed to Lithuania on Exercise SWINTON SUWALKI 26. The week-long terrain walk focused on the Suwałki Corridor, examining mobility, survivability, route reconnaissance, infrastructure assessment, and engineer support to operations. The exercise also included a valuable visit to the Lithuanian Engineer Battalion, who hosted the group and provided insight into their current and future capabilities. Gunners in Bavaria Rock climbing gunners. (Image: 26 Regt RA) 26 Regiment Royal Artillery recently travelled to Bavaria as part of an Adventurous Training package. Throughout the trip, personnel took part in a range of challenging activities, including rock climbing, Kletterstein, mountain biking, and hill walking. The package provided an excellent opportunity to develop resilience, teamwork, confidence, and leadership while operating in the demanding environment of the Bavarian Alps. Sappers at the seaside Over the past two weeks, the 22 Engineer Regiment Dive Team deployed on Ex PORTLAND DIVE in Weymouth, focusing on fast water diving operations. For three days, we trained the Ukrainian Dive Team, sharing specialist technique in underwater search schemes for fast water diving ops. It was a privilege to work alongside the Ukrainian divers, who are now looking to incorporate fast water diving into their own training syllabus - strengthening capability through shared knowledge, cooperation and interoperability. Polish exercise for Hussars The King's Royal Hussars Battlegroup, consisting of two Challenger 2 Squadrons, a Danish Leopard Squadron and an anti-tank Company from the Scots Guards, have been exercising alongside US and Polish forces on Ex DEFENDER Europe. Romanian Business News - ACTMedia :: Services | About us | Contact | RSS Home Daily Financial & banking Economic Companies Energy & Environment Romania-UK trade reaches GBP10.3 billion in 2025 Bilateral trade between the UK and Romania reached GBP 10.3 billion in 2025, up 4.9% from the previous year, according to the latest data published by the United Kingdom's Department for Business and Trade, quoted by the Romanian-British Chamber of Commerce (BRCC). British exports to Romania increased by 7% to GBP 3 billion, while imports from Romania increased by 4% to GBP 7.3 billion. Thus, Romania ranks 32nd in the ranking of UK's most important trading partners . Trade in goods continued to be supported by strong activity in industry and production. "Cars represented the main category of goods imported by the United Kingdom from Romania, to the tune of GBP 1.3 billion pounds, making up 30.4% of the total British imports of goods from Romania, after an annual increase of 18.4%. Other important categories included beverages and tobacco products, general industrial machinery and electrical equipment. British exports of goods to Romania were dominated by beverages and tobacco products, mechanical power generators and cars, which highlights the importance of already strengthened industrial supply chains and the potential for extensive sectoral cooperation," reads a BRCC press release. Also, British exports of services to Romania increased by 16.1% to GBP1.5 billion (50.5% of total UK exports to Romania). In this context, travel represented the most important category of services, with a share of 37.1% of British exports of services to Romania and 43.2% of British imports of services from Romania, followed by other services for companies and transport. "The latest figures mark a new increase in bilateral trade between the United Kingdom and Romania, confirming the positive trend in the economic relationship. The contribution of key sectors such as automotive, machinery and electrical equipment, along with the growing importance of services for companies, is particularly encouraging. These results provide a solid basis for future development and point to new opportunities for investment, innovation and sectoral partnerships. At BRCC, we will continue to connect companies, institutions and industry leaders, contributing to transforming this favourable evolution into concrete projects and long-term sustainable growth," BRCC Chairman Robert Uzuna is quoted as saying in the statement. In the British foreign direct investment segment in Romania, the stock stood at GBP 752 million at the end of 2024, down 19.9% year-on-year, indicating an opportunity to strengthen investment projects and long-term capital commitment. In contrast, Romanian and UK foreign direct investment increased by 22.2% to GBP 303 million. "Romania's overall economic trajectory reinforces its growing importance in the European landscape. The country's gross domestic product is estimated to reach USD 480.8 billion in 2026, which would place Romania 39th in the ranking of the world's largest economies. It is estimated that export activity supported approximately 2.6 million jobs in Romania in 2022, of which approximately 103,600 were supported by exports to the United Kingdom. The United Kingdom's market share in Romania stood at 2.2% in 2024, indicating additional expansion potential, especially in automotive, advanced manufacturing, industrial machinery, electrical equipment, business services and technology. The combination of the already consolidated industrial supply chains and the growing services component provide a solid basis for the development of a deeper and more integrated economic relationship between Romania and the United Kingdom," according to the organisation. The Romanian-British Chamber of Commerce is the main organisation dedicated to the promotion of bilateral trade and investment between the UK and Romania. Founded in 1998, the entity operates independently and has offices in London, Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca. Romanian Business News - ACTMedia :: Services | About us | Contact | RSS Home Daily Financial & banking Economic Companies Energy & Environment Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan on official visit to Bucharest on Thursday Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan will make on Thursday his first foreign visit since taking office, travelling to Bucharest for meetings with Romania's leadership, the Moldovan Government announced. His programme includes talks with President Nicusor Dan, acting Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, and the leadership of the Romanian Parliament. According to the Government in Chisinau, Tofan will hold a bilateral meeting with his Romanian counterpart, Ilie Bolojan, focusing on strategic projects of common interest, economic cooperation and regional security developments. The discussion will be followed by joint press statements. The agenda will also cover the status and acceleration of bilateral projects, with emphasis on transport and energy initiatives aimed at strengthening interconnection between the two banks of the Prut and addressing current challenges. According to the Romanian Government, the two senior officials will also address aspects related to the security situation in the region, against the backdrop of Russia's ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine, as well as the security and economic consequences of this war, with Bolojan expected to reiterate Romania's firm support for Moldova's accession to the European Union and discuss concrete forms of assistance and diplomatic and sectoral coordination to advance the process. In addition, the Moldovan prime minister will participate in a discussion session with representatives of the Bessarabian Businessmen's Club, focused on stimulating investment and supporting the business environment. The Canada Border Services Agency says officers apprehended what is believed to be 300 kilograms of methamphetamine and 80 kilograms of cocaine. It says officers stopped a commercial truck at the Coutts border crossing along the border on July 2. Suspected methamphetamine and cocaine seized by the Canada Border Services Agency from a commercial truck at the Coutts port of entry on the Alberta-U.S. border, on July 2, 2026, is shown in this composite of handout photos. Border officers arrested the driver and the drugs were handed over to the RCMP. The agency says officers in Alberta seized more than 1,300 kilograms of meth and cocaine last year. https://www.penbaypilot.com:443/article/.text: Visit our partners: Boothbay Register Wiscasset Newspaper Search form Wed, 07/29/2026 - 2:28pm Josephine Pitts McAlary Josephine Pitts McAlary A life very well lived ROCKPORT — Jojo McAlary passed away peacefully at Wingate Residences, in Haverhill, Massachusetts, her “home away from home” for the last two and a half years, surrounded by family and friends, after a short period of declining health on July 21, 2026. She was two weeks short of her 103 rd birthday. Born August 8, 1923 in New Orleans, Louisiana, the only child of Everett E. Pitts and Diana Wall Pitts (later Fogler). She lived in New Orleans until 1937 when the family moved back to the family home in Rockport, Maine. Jojo was in a class of nine that graduated from Rockport High School in 1940. She went on to attend Colby College, graduating in December 1943. She met her future husband, Frederick McAlary, at Colby College and they were married two hours after she received her diploma on December 12, 1943. Frederick, also a Colby graduate was in the U.S. Army at that time. He was soon deployed to Europe during WWII, not returning until the Fall of 1945. In his absence Jojo lived in Rockport, taught high school and gave birth to their first child, Diana. After being discharged from the Army, they moved to Bangor, Maine where Fred began a 38 year career with the Bangor Daily News. In 1947 they had a second child, Fred, Jr. In addition to bringing up her young family, Jojo was active with the womens’ group at St. John’s Episcopal Church, scouting clubs, Lionetts and Patawa Club. In 1963, she returned to teaching in the Math Department at Fifth Street Junior High School. In 1972 she transferred to Bangor High School where she taught algebra and geometry, was a class advisor and was very active many school activities. She and Fred both retired in 1985. After retiring they moved into the Rockport house that they had inherited from her parents which became their year-round home. Traveling annually became a passion; Europe to celebrate D-Day’s 50th anniversary, Australia, New Zealand, Florida and many Caribbean islands. In 2004, after several years of failing health Fred passed shortly after their 60th anniversary. Jojo decided that Rockport would remain her forever home where she was surrounded by many relatives and friends. She enjoyed daily walks to Rockport Harbor, frequent visits to the top of Mount Battie and being a long-time member of the Mid Coast Community Chorus. She was always ready to go anywhere with anyone that wanted to travel. Over the next 15 years among other adventures she: walked the Great Wall in China, rode an elephant in Thailand, ziplined over Victoria Falls in Africa, did a train trip across Canada, rode a camel Tunisia, fed the macaques in Gibraltar, hiked the glaciers in Patagonia, visited the Winter Palace in St. Petersburg, Russia, cruised the Amazon in Brazil, visited the Wailing Wall in Jerusalem, hot air ballooned in Turkey, also toured Ireland, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Croatia, Finland, Estonia, Singapore, South Africa and many other destinations. She fulfilled her world travel bucket list except travel to Antarctica. Jojo was predeceased by her husband, Fred, in 2004; her daughter, Diana Hicks in 2013; and her grandson Andrew Hicks in 2010. She is survived by her son, Fred McAlary and his wife Mary of Andover, Massachusetts; grandson Ryan and his partner Phil Coppola of Haverhill, Massachusetts; son-in-law Tony Hicks, of Leesburg, Florida; granddaughter, Jennifer Hicks of Brunswick, Maine; grandson Andrew Hicks and his wife Karen of Annapolis, Maryland; as well as five great-grandchildren. two great-great grandchildren, and a nephew, David McAlary. A Memorial Service will be scheduled in August in Rockport, Maine. Further details will be forthcoming. Condolences and memories may be shared at www.longfuneralhomecamden.com.
