https://www.breitbart.com/europe/2026/07.text: KYIV, Ukraine (AP) – A Russian ballistic missile and drone barrage across Ukraine overnight killed at least eight civilians, including children, and injured more than 50 others, officials said Thursday, and NATO scrambled its warplanes after one of the missiles crossed the country’s western border into Poland. The blitz expanded Russia´s almost daily bombardment of Ukrainian cities, including the capital of Kyiv where tens of thousands spent the night sheltering in subway stations, as Moscow apparently looked to exploit Kyiv´s critical shortage of Western-supplied anti-ballistic missile defenses. NATO said a Russian missile entered Polish airspace during the onslaught and landed in a rural area. It caused no injuries or damage but could deepen tensions between the military alliance and Moscow, as wary European countries fear the 4-year-old war could spill into their territory. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called it “yet another reckless act by Russia and a dangerous consequence of its war against Ukraine.” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it was “a very serious incident,” but added: “There are absolutely no reasons to believe that Poland was the target.” Russia’s barrage struck areas of Ukraine where weapons are believed to be stored and manufactured. Ukrainian long-range drones and missiles have battered Russia’s oil sector, causing a fuel crisis. The attack came two days after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with U.S. President Donald Trump and representatives of American defense companies as he pleads for swifter and bigger deliveries of Patriot air defense systems to stop Russia´s ballistic missiles. The Iran war has drained stockpiles of the U.S.-made interceptors. Trump has promised to grant Ukraine licenses to build its own Patriots, but production could take many months. “Given the critical shortage of air defense missiles from our partners, our warriors are accomplishing truly incredible things, demonstrating a very high level of professionalism,” Zelenskyy said on social media. “This Russian terror once again proves that protection against the Russian missile threat is the most important task when it comes to saving the lives of our people,” he said. Zelenskyy said at least 10 Ukrainian regions were attacked, with dozens of homes, businesses and infrastructure facilities destroyed or damaged. Russia launched more than 70 missiles, a significant number of them ballistic missiles, he said, and over 280 attack drones, of which more than 260 were intercepted. The Russian Defense Ministry said it targeted Ukrainian air bases, arms factories and military telecommunications and logistics facilities, including drone factories and storage depots, as well as plants for missiles, aircraft repairs, electronics and chemicals. In the Dnipropetrovsk region, the Russian attack killed six people and wounded 10, said Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, in a post on Telegram. Children were among the dead – a 6-year-old girl and boys aged 11 and 17 in the area of Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy’s hometown, Hanzha added. The children´s parents were killed in the same attack, but two more children were pulled alive from the rubble, Zelenskyy said. “It was an ordinary home, blown (to) smithereens by a ballistic missile,” he said on X. In Kyiv, Russian forces struck the capital with ballistic missiles, killing a 31-year-old man and wounding two others, the National Police press service said. More than 56,000 people sheltered in Kyiv´s subway stations overnight, according to the Facebook post from the metro system. A cruise missile attack struck the western city of Lviv, killing one person and wounding over 30, including children aged 6, 13 and 15, said Maksym Kozytskyi, head of the Lviv regional military administration. In the Poltava region, a drone hit warehouses, killing one person, said regional military head Vitalii Diakivnych. Russian forces also dropped three powerful glide bombs on an industrial zone in the southern city of Kherson, killing a 56-year-old man, local officials said. A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crossed into Poland overnight, violating NATO airspace, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X, calling it a clear demonstration that strengthening Ukraine´s air defenses would also guarantee wider European security. Responding to the missile alert, NATO forces in Poland scrambled two fighter jets, an attack helicopter and two other aircraft, and activated ground defenses, said Col. Michael O´Connell, the spokesperson for the alliance´s military command in Belgium. The missile quickly disappeared from radar, the Polish Armed Forces said. A helicopter flew to its last known location, where the crew discovered a probable impact site in a farming area in Lublin province, the command said. Investigators found fragments indicating that the object was a Kh-101 missile, Polish news agency PAP reported. Tusk had met with Zelenskyy in Lublin on Wednesday to discuss defense issues. NATO military commander Gen. Alexus G. Grynkewich told Poland´s Defense Chief Gen. Wieslaw Kukulan the military alliance “will continue to take all necessary measures to defend NATO territory,” O´Donnell said. Meanwhile, Russia´s Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 258 Ukrainian drones overnight. A depot belonging to Wildberries online retailer was set ablaze in Russia’s Penza region southeast of Moscow, in the latest strike on the company’s warehouses, Penza Gov. Oleg Melnichenko. Four people were injured and 200 workers were evacuated, he said, adding that about 100 firefighters were deployed. Wildberries also reported its warehouse in Sarapul in the Udmurtia region more than 1,000 kilometers (600 miles) from Ukraine, was struck by a Ukrainian drone and set ablaze. It said the workers had been safely evacuated. The Russian online news outlet Astra reported that another Wildberries depot in the Perm region in the Urals was also set ablaze by a Ukrainian drone strike. Regional authorities reported a Ukrainian drone attack but didn´t give information about the damage. Thursday´s attacks on Wildberries warehouses brought to 14 the number of the retailer´s depots struck by Ukrainian drones in under two weeks. Ukraine accuses Wildberries of supplying goods that can be used by the Russian military. Ukrainian drone units destroyed four more vessels belonging to Russia´s “shadow fleet” of sanctions-busting tankers, bringing the total to 205 since the operation began July 6, Robert “Madyar” Brovdi, commander of the Unmanned Systems Forces, said on his Telegram channel. https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new.text: A chilling case has emerged in South Australia, where a mother who died in a suspected murder-suicide visited a police station a day before the incident, according to South Australia Police. The bodies of 36-year-old Helena Wright and her 23-month-old daughter were found in the ocean west of Port MacDonnell on Monday (July 27, 2026).Wright, 36, visited the Mount Gambier Police Station on Sunday, July 26, where she spoke with police, authorities confirmed on Wednesday (July 29, 2026), according to The Guardian. On Wednesday, police said they had ended the official search for a missing three-month-old after “careful consideration”, saying the infant “could not have survived the period of time that has elapsed, either in the water or on land,” as quoted by The Guardian.Emergency crews were dispatched to the area on Monday after an abandoned vehicle with its engine still running was discovered at about 11.15 a.m. Wright, who was originally from Estonia, lived in Compton, a small locality outside Mount Gambier, about 26 kilometers north of Port MacDonnell.Authorities said Wright had visited a police station one day before her body was found. On the morning of the incident, at about 9.30 a.m., officers went to her home to conduct a welfare check after a concerned friend contacted police. No one was at the property when they arrived. Wright and her 23-month-old daughter were later located below the cliffs, with local fishers assisting in recovering their bodies.Investigators have spoken with Wright's husband, the father of the children, and said based on the evidence currently available, the matter is being investigated as a murder-suicide . Meanwhile, land and sea search operations were launched around Cape Northumberland near Port MacDonnell on the Limestone Coast in an effort to find the missing three-month-old infant. Comprehensive physical search efforts have focused on a sizable area of water and land, unfortunately the infant has not been found, police said on Wednesday, as quoted by The Guardian. Officers also acknowledged that hopes of finding the infant alive had faded. The reality is, after three days, the chances of finding the baby alive are zero, Supt. Trent Cox said earlier on Wednesday.Cox said rescue efforts had been complicated by extremely challenging conditions, preventing emergency vessels from entering the water for much of Tuesday and restricting search teams to the shoreline and clifftops. We've been unable to … launch water assets. We've been able to get the SES aerial drone up, he said, adding that specialists had advised against using an underwater drone because of the hazardous conditions.Police said they will continue to coordinate shoreline monitoring and inspections across the coming days . South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas said the tragedy had deeply shaken the community. If it involves children, that breaks your heart, he said on Tuesday.The matter has been referred to the coroner, who will examine the cause and circumstances surrounding the deaths. Police said there is no information to suggest that any person other than the mother and her two children were involved in this heart-breaking incident .

https://www.ynetnews.com/article/rjaexcf.text: An Israeli man in his 30s was stabbed early Tuesday at the Ozora music festival in Hungary, while two other Israelis were arrested in a separate incident on suspicion of attempting to sell drugs to an undercover police officer. Hungarian police arrested three suspects in connection with the stabbing. Authorities said the Israeli victim was hospitalized and that his condition had stabilized. Following the attack, police said they had increased their presence at the festival grounds and would continue carrying out heightened security checks with the event’s organizers to protect attendees. The three suspects are being investigated over their alleged involvement in a serious assault and on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm. It was not the first stabbing involving an Israeli at the festival. Last year, a 26-year-old Israeli was wounded on the final day of the event after allegedly being attacked by another Israeli. In a separate case, Hungarian authorities said police arrested three people at the festival on Monday, including two Israelis, after allegedly catching them selling drugs. One of the Israelis is a survivor of the Nova music festival massacre on October 7 and is believed to suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder. Attorney Mordechai Tzivin, who specializes in assisting Israelis arrested abroad, said he expected the detainees’ rights to be protected. “Based on my experience in Hungary, the young men are fortunate that the incident did not occur under the previous government,” he said. “It can be assumed that under the current political circumstances, law enforcement authorities will act in the accepted, independent and fair manner seen in European Union countries, free from pressure. This will presumably also be reflected in the protection of detainees’ rights.”

Opinion Academia The middle-income health trap When a country crosses the World Bank’s threshold from low- to middle-income status, it is deemed too rich to qualify for aid, even though it is not yet rich enough to cover its health costs. Share this article Change text size Gift Premium Articles to Anyone I n the lexicon of development, few words sound as reassuring as “graduation,” which suggests progress past critical milestones and an escape from dependency. In global health, however, graduation increasingly creates a trap. When a country crosses the World Bank’s threshold from low- to middle-income status, it is deemed too rich to qualify for aid, even though it is not yet rich enough to cover its health costs. The implications of reaching this milestone (which is based on gross national income per capita) are therefore profound. Achieving middle-income status means that concessional loans will increasingly have to be replaced by market-rate borrowing, and that grants will shrink or disappear as global health programs wind down. But pathogens do not recognize income thresholds, and the resources available to health systems do not necessarily grow smoothly with GDP. In many countries, disease burdens remain stubbornly high long after aid eligibility has expired. If there is any lag in the growth of the government’s fiscal capacity, the result will be a widening gap between health needs and health financing. Neither markets nor donors are well equipped to fill it. This is a massive problem. Middle-income countries now account for over 70 percent of the world’s poor, for most deaths from tuberculosis, and for a still-high share of deaths from HIV and non-communicable diseases. Yet they receive a shrinking share of global health assistance, which is increasingly concentrated in a small number of fragile, low-income states. If graduation to middle-income status reliably coincided with robust tax systems, deep capital markets and comprehensive insurance schemes, it would make sense for recent grads to fend for themselves. But many middle-income countries face rising debt-service costs and collect less than 15 percent of GDP in taxes, owing to their large informal sectors. They may be richer on paper, but their health ministries are often poorer in practice. When donor-funded programs supported by institutions such as Gavi or the Global Fund taper off, governments are expected to assume full financial responsibility for vaccines, antiretrovirals and malaria control, often within the space of a few budget cycles. But such costs are often large, recurrent and have low visibility, which weakens political incentives to prioritize them over other spending. https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/s.text: China's Sinochem sells 14% Pirelli stake to Czech billionaire Michal Strnad Czech billionaire Michal Strnad, chairman and owner of Ammunition and arms maker Czechoslovak Group (CSG), arrives at Euronext Amsterdam in Amsterdam, Netherlands, January 23, 2026. REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw 31 July, 2026 Sinochem has sold a 14% stake in Pirelli to Czech billionaire Michal Strnad, the two parties said on Thursday, with the Chinese state-owned group significantly scaling back its investment in the Italian tyremaker. Sinochem said it had sold the shares, part of its overall 34.1% shareholding through a block-trade deal, cutting its stake to 20.1%, this becoming Pirelli’s second largest investor. In a separate statement, Strnad’s investment company Lumina Crown said it had acquired the 14% stake, becoming Pirelli’s third largest shareholder and aiming for a “long-term investment” in the company. Strnad is the controlling shareholder of defence and industrial group Czechoslovak Group (CSG). According to data reported on the Italian stock exchange website, the shares were sold at €6.50 each, valuing the 14% stake at around €987 million ($1.14 billion). Pirelli shares closed at 6.51 euros on Thursday. The sale draws a line under years of tensions between Pirelli’s main investors following Italy’s moves to curb Sinochem’s influence at the company. As a consequence of the deal, Camfin – the vehicle of Executive Chairman Marco Tronchetti Provera, the Italian businessman who has led the Milan-based tyre maker for more than three decades – becomes Pirelli’s largest shareholder with a 26% stake. Sinochem’s influence over the company has been sharply curtailed since the Italian government intervened twice, in 2023 and earlier this year, using its so-called “golden power” rules to protect strategic assets. Under more recent restrictions imposed by Rome, Sinochem got just three representatives on Pirelli’s 15-member board, which is effectively controlled by Camfin. Its appointees are also barred from holding key executive positions such as chairman or chief executive. Sinochem was advised in the deal by BNP Paribas; Lumina Crown was advised by Jefferies. https://maritime-executive.com/corporate.text: news features Podcasts magazine newsletter Jobs advertise subscribe 2517 Views Drought Makes Upper Rhine Unnavigable, Driving Barge Rates to New Record A handful of barges transit the Rhine near Kaub, Germany, July 30 (Copernicus / Sentinel-2) Published Jul 30, 2026 8:39 PM by The Maritime Executive Low summertime water levels are a routine problem for navigation on the River Rhine, especially in recent years, but the intense drought conditions affecting Western Europe have left the waterway all but unnavigable at a key chokepoint - sending freight rates to record highs. The limiting factor is the gage depth at Kaub, downriver from Wiesbaden. At present it is less than 12 inches, the bare minimum for most barges to transit in laden condition. The shutdown closes off access above Kaub on the Upper Rhine, which serves customers from Mannheim to Strasbourg to Basel, Switzerland. Even when passable, according to Reuters, barge loadings have been restricted to as little as 10 percent of capacity in order to minimize vessel draft and enable safe passage. This requires barge owners to charge more per tonne transported, since the vessel is still navigating the same route with reduced cargo. Since June, the price has roughly tripled. "Industry is transferring cargo to rail and road transport, but this is also expensive because of the extra demand," one trader told Reuters. A shutdown on parts of the Lower Rhine could begin as early as next week, according to Argus, with implications for inland refinery operators that rely on water transport to move products. Rail network capacity is already saturated, and commodity markets in the area are facing substantial disruption. Stay on Top of the Daily Maritime News The maritime news that matters most Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily. Drought is also affecting the Danube, where record-low water levels are disrupting traffic and exposing relics of bygone eras. Cruise and commodity traffic on the river has effectively come to a stop, and operators of two nuclear power plants in Romania and Hungary have had to shut down because of a lack of cooling water from the river. The low water levels are driven not just by lack of rainfall, but by extreme heat events that increase evaporation - all made more likely by recent adjustments to average atmospheric temperature, according to a new study by researchers at Imperial College London and ETH Zurich. Photograph: Kacper Pempel/Reuters View image in fullscreen Donald Tusk said Poland and other Nato countries had to be ready to counter other Russian attacks. Photograph: Kacper Pempel/Reuters Poland Russian plot to kill Ukrainian American thwarted in Warsaw, says Polish PM Donald Tusk says it is first time ‘someone on the order of Russia’ has sought to attack US citizen in Nato country Associated Press Thu 13 Aug 2026 15.32 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 18.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian American citizen in Warsaw was thwarted by Poland before it could be carried out, the Polish prime minister has said. Donald Tusk said it was the first time that “someone on the order of Russia” had sought to attack a US citizen on the territory of another Nato country. Western officials have previously warned that Russia stepped up a campaign of targeted killings since Vladimir Putin’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, saying they had disrupted several plots across Europe. But Tusk said this incident was unprecedented. The suspect, who was allegedly recruited by Russia’s secret services, was detained by Polish authorities on 7 August. He will be held in custody for three months, the Warsaw police said in a statement. The American Ukrainian citizen “was uncomfortable for the Putin regime”, Tusk said in a news conference, without elaborating. The operation was carried out in cooperation with US services, said Tomasz Siemoniak, Poland’s minister overseeing intelligence services. He said the targeted victim was a US citizen “of Ukrainian origin”. Officials did not immediately provide further details. The Russian foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The US state department said it was aware of the reports but said it had no additional information. Russia has long been accused of targeting its enemies abroad, including by using rare poisons. But intelligence officials previously told the Associated Press that Russia’s security services are now more brazen in their choice of targets, going after Russian activists and foreign supporters of Ukraine as well as military defectors. Tusk said: “We must assume that the Putin regime will try to eliminate people who are inconvenient for various reasons, in various places around the world.” He added that Poland and other countries must be prepared to counter such actions. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion A bungled bomb plot in Poland exposed a spy – but whose spy was he? Read more Western officials see the campaign as connected to Russia’s broader efforts to undermine European countries that support Ukraine. The AP has mapped about 200 acts of sabotage, arson and other disruption across Europe since the start of the war in Ukraine that officials have linked to Russia. Putin told the AP in June that Russia was not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe. In 2006, British authorities accused Russia of being behind the killing in London of the former FSB officer Alexander Litvinenko with radioactive polonium. The UK also blames Russia for the attempted killing of the former Russian military intelligence officer Sergei Skripal in Salisbury in 2018 with the nerve agent novichok. German authorities said Russia had organised the 2019 killing of Zelimkhan Khangoshvili , a former Chechen rebel commander who was shot in a Berlin park by Vadim Krasikov, a hitman who was later greeted by Putin after he was exchanged in a spy swap. In June, a Russian artist who was critical of Putin was shot and killed at close range near his home in eastern Poland. Tusk said at the time that the killing of Robert Kuzovkov , known by the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, had the hallmarks of a political assassination. He suggested it was possible Russia was behind it but Polish officials have not yet attributed it to Moscow. Last year French officials disrupted a plot that they believe was aimed at killing Vladimir Osechkin, a Russian exile who lives under police protection and works to help military defectors flee Putin’s war. Lithuanian officials also disrupted a plot last year to kill a Lithuanian supporter of Ukraine and another against a Russian activist. Officials in Germany have similarly broken up two plots: one to target the head of a German weapons company supplying Ukraine, the other against a Ukrainian military official. Polish authorities arrested a man in 2024 in what they said was a plot to assassinate the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy. That year, a Russian helicopter pilot who defected was killed in Spain – Russian operatives were the prime suspects. “This campaign is not by accident or chance,” a senior European intelligence official previously told the AP. “There is political authorisation.” Explore more on these topics Poland Russia Vladimir Putin Donald Tusk Europe Nato Ukraine news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

Photograph: Ben Montgomery/Getty Images Politics Nigel Farage set for decisive but arguably empty victory in Clacton Leader of Reform UK on course to defeat Count Binface and an assortment of fringe candidates as polls close in Essex Peter Walker Senior political correspondent Thu 13 Aug 2026 17.56 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 18.06 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Voting has closed in one of the UK’s more unusual and least tense byelections, with Nigel Farage set for a decisive if arguably empty victory against dozens of independent, fringe, extreme or otherwise oddball opponents. The Reform UK leader sought re-election to his Clacton seat in early July in an attempt to regain the political initiative following weeks of scrutiny over gifts he received and other aspects of his financial affairs. He framed the byelection as a chance for local voters to show their disdain for mainstream politics in a “people versus the establishment” contest, but was caught out after all the other main parties declined to stand candidates. Farage, 62, was instead left competing against a vast if decidedly niche field of 33 other hopefuls, including 20 independents, several representatives from tiny parties and no fewer than three candidates from the Official Monster Raving Loony party. The result, due to be announced from around 6am on Friday, will inevitably be a clear Farage win, with the only question being his margin of victory over Count Binface , the self-styled campaigning alien who is the most prominent of his opponents. View image in fullscreen Nigel Farage poses with a pint in a Clacton pub beer garden. Photograph: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock While Reform will necessarily style the result as a clear endorsement of Farage’s record in the Essex seat, and of his tactic in calling the byelection, opponents will seize on any signs of a lower-than-expected majority or a slim turnout. Farage is being investigated by the parliamentary standards watchdog over allegations he failed to declare gifts and donations, including a £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, first revealed by the Guardian. The process was paused when he resigned as an MP, but will resume once he is re-elected. If he is found to have breached declaration rules and suspended from the House of Commons, this could trigger a second byelection, which the other main parties would contest. While Farage insists he has relished a summer of knocking on doors in his constituency, he has been less visible on the national political stage – in part because of rules connected to how broadcasters must ensure balance during elections. Farage has insisted he did not need to declare the £5m from Harborne as it was given in advance of his return as Reform leader before the 2024 election. He has, however, given a series of explanations for the gift, including that it was for his security and a reward for Brexit. The parliamentary inquiry is also looking into allegations that Farage was financially supported by the crypto gambler and convicted fraudster George Cottrell , a close friend, after the Sunday Times reported that Cottrell’s support included security and social media staff who worked on Farage’s online content in the year before he was elected. The 34-candidate field in the Clacton byelection is a UK record, beating the July 2008 contest in Haltemprice and Howden, East Yorkshire, regained by the Conservative MP David Davis after he resigned his seat and stood again as a protest over civil liberties. Count Binface (left) and Nigel Farage are among the candidates on the ballot. Composite: Leon Neal/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Count Binface (left) and Nigel Farage are among the candidates on the ballot. Composite: Leon Neal/Getty Images Clacton byelection August 2026 Polls close in Clacton byelection where Nigel Farage faces slew of fringe candidates Longest ballot in UK voting history features likes of Count Binface and Howling Laud Hope alongside Reform leader Alexandra Topping Political correspondent Thu 13 Aug 2026 17.37 EDT First published on Thu 13 Aug 2026 02.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Polls have closed in Clacton, where thousands of residents in the Essex seat voted in a ballot featuring Nigel Farage and a range of novelty and fringe candidates led by Count Binface . The Reform UK leader resigned as the MP for Clacton at the start of July and forced a byelection in an attempt to address complaints over a deepening scandal about gifts he received. He is expected to face a formal investigation by the parliamentary standards watchdog , which was opened in May after the Guardian revealed he had received a £5m personal gift from Christopher Harborne, a Thailand-based crypto billionaire, in April 2024. Farage has denied the gift amounted to an inducement to run for office, insisting it was personal in nature. He has given a series of explanations for the gift, including that it was for his security and a reward for Brexit. The inquiry will look into allegations Farage was financially supported by the crypto gambler and convicted fraudster George Cottrell , a close friend, after the Sunday Times reported that Cottrell’s support included security and social media staff who worked on Farage’s online content in the year before he was elected. Reform UK claimed that was a “baseless and contrived story” and that no parliamentary rules had been broken. The inquiry, which was suspended on 8 July after Farage’s decision to force a byelection, could restart as soon as Friday if he is re-elected. If parliament imposes sanctions for failing to declare the gifts, he may be removed from the House of Commons and face a second byelection. All of the main parties have boycotted the byelection, announcing they would not stand candidates for a “media circus” and a “vanity project”. Instead, Count Binface , the self-declared “entirely independent space warrior” created by the comedian Jon Harvey, stepped into the void . A record number of candidates are seeking election, presenting voters with the longest ballot paper in British electoral history . Among the 34 candidates on the ballot paper are independents, the actor and rightwing political activist Laurence Fox and three figures from the Monster Raving Loony party: Howling Laud Hope, Baron Von Thunderclap and Nick the Incredible Flying Brick. As well as the town of Clacton-on-Sea, the constituency comprises rural villages, farmland and several seaside towns and villages including Frinton, Walton-on-the-Naze and Jaywick, which last year was named the most deprived neighbourhood in England for the fourth consecutive time since 2010. The three polls that Jaywick topped before 2025 were published in 2010, 2015 and 2019. According to figures from the Office for National Statistics, the population of Clacton is older than the average in England. A third of working-age people are economically inactive, compared with fewer than one in five in the east of England. Of Clacton residents who voted in the 2016 Brexit referendum, 70% favoured leave. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion After standing in multiple British elections since 1994, Farage was elected to the Commons as the member for Clacton in 2024. He won the seat with a majority of 8,400, taking 46.2% of the vote. The Conservatives came second and Labour third. The previous record for the largest number of candidates in a constituency election was held by the Haltemprice and Howden byelection in East Yorkshire in July 2008, which featured 26 candidates. It took place after Tory David Davis resigned his seat and stood again as a protest over the issue of civil liberties. The result may be seen as a benchmark to measure Farage’s relative success in this byelection. Davis won 72% of the vote in the election – which Labour and the Liberal Democrats did not contest – up from 47.5% at the 2005 general election, with a majority of 15,355. Farage’s critics argue that his standing as a contender to be the next prime minister has taken a serious hit as a result of the byelection, with much of the Reform leader’s time and energy spent in the Essex constituency. Last summer Farage was able to dominate the news agenda while the leaders of other main parties took summer holidays, helming seven press conferences in six weeks. This year he held his first press briefing on 3 August, his first national press conference since May. He has not appeared keen to debate with Binface or the other 32 candidates. Photograph: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe/AP View image in fullscreen Arjun Aravind and his lawyer Debra DeWitt during his arraignment in Concord, Massachusetts, on Thursday. Photograph: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe/AP Massachusetts Massachusetts teen accused of killing mother and brother used ChatGPT District attorney says Arjun Aravind, 17, used internet and AI to search for fantasy stories regarding killing of his family Marina Dunbar Thu 13 Aug 2026 17.34 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 18.14 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Massachusetts teenager accused of killing his mother and younger brother is being held without bail as authorities investigate a double-murder case that prosecutors say is connected to his use of ChatGPT. Arjun Aravind, 17, appeared Thursday morning for his arraignment in Concord district court, where a not-guilty plea was entered on his behalf to murder and several additional charges. Authorities allege Arjun killed his mother, 45-year-old Sudha Venkatesan, and his 14-year-old brother, Siddharth Aravind, inside the family’s home on Tuesday. The investigation began after the teenager’s tutor arrived for a scheduled appointment at the home Tuesday and “was unable to make contact with residents upon arrival”, prosecutors said. The teen’s father, who had last spoken with his wife before leaving for work that morning, then contacted police. Officers arrived at the residence and “located the two victims dead inside” shortly after 6.30pm, according to the district attorney. Officials said Siddharth’s body was discovered on the home’s first floor, while his mother’s body was found in the basement. As investigators examined what may have preceded the killings, authorities uncovered online activity they described as concerning. “The investigation has so far shown that Arjun had recently been demonstrating some concerning behavior, including using the internet and ChatGPT to make searches for theoretical ideas or fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family,” the Middlesex county district attorney, Marian Ryan, said in a press conference . Ryan said the teenager had planned the deaths of family members in the form of fantasy fiction. “He was engaged in the use of ChatGPT in creating fantasy stories, kind of the gothic novel kind of stories, asking questions, creating characters, asking what about this if this happened to that, and they seem to appear to relate to threats to his family,” she added. The official causes of death have not yet been determined, prosecutor Suzanne Wiseman said Thursday, according to CBS News , but she described what happened as a “physical and violent struggle”. “At this time, based on the evidence that was found at the scene, it was apparent that blunt force trauma was used in some fashion on both individuals,” Wiseman said. By the time the bodies were discovered, both Arjun and his mother’s vehicle, a 2014 green Honda Accord, were missing from the residence, officials said. Hours later, a search for them shifted about 13 miles (21km) away to Wayland after an alarm was triggered in a parking lot early Wednesday morning. Responding officers quickly connected the vehicle to the investigation. Arjun was found at approximately 3.40am inside his mother’s car and arrested. Investigators also recovered evidence from the vehicle that prosecutors say was connected to the scene at the family’s home. “A number of items were found in that car that correspond to the murder scene,” Wiseman said. Arjun faces two counts of murder, two counts of assault and battery on a household or family member, two counts of assault and battery, use of a vehicle without authority and theft of a motor vehicle. The Guardian has reached out to OpenAI , the parent company of ChatGPT, for comment. This is not the first time an AI chatbot has been connected to criminal acts. Earlier this year, Florida’s top prosecutor launched a criminal investigation into how OpenAI and its software tool ChatGPT may influence users’ threats of harm to themselves or others, including whether it “offered significant advice” to a gunman accused of conducting a mass shooting in the state last year. At the time, in a statement, a ChatGPT spokesperson said those shootings were a tragedy “but ChatGPT is not responsible for this terrible crime” and the tool had provided factual responses to questions with information that was broadly publicly available and “did not encourage or promote illegal or harmful activity”. https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text: A Flock Safety license plate reader on a road in Houston, Texas. Photograph: David Goldman/AP View image in fullscreen A Flock Safety license plate reader on a road in Houston, Texas. Photograph: David Goldman/AP Technology Flock Safety tries to curb police abuse of its surveillance cameras after scandals CEO announces steps after reports that system is used to target immigrants or people seeking out-of-state abortions Johana Bhuiyan Thu 13 Aug 2026 16.20 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 16.47 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google For nearly a decade, the company Flock Safety has gradually built out a network of cameras across the US that allows law enforcement officials to conduct about 20bn license plate scans every month. In that time, the company had largely left the decision to turn on safety measures up to its customers. Many of those organizations did not turn them on. Now, the company is doing damage control. Garrett Langley, Flock’s CEO, announced on Thursday that the company would begin mandating that law enforcement agencies switch on features that could help audit the way individual officers use its tracking capabilities. It had been reported that more than 50 law enforcement officers were accused of or charged with abusing Flock’s camera system, including to stalk ex-partners. “These changes reflect years of work and deliberation,” Langley wrote in a blogpost announcing the new guardrails. “They are not the end of that work, but simply the continuation of our commitment to both safety and privacy.” Four months ago, the company introduced a voluntary feature called Audit Assistance, which flags “abnormal activity” for administrative review. Langley said on Thursday that about a third of its customers turned it on. Now, the rest of its customers, which include law enforcement agencies, retailers , universities , and homeowner associations , have until the end of the year to activate it. Under the new system, when the system flagged behavior as “abnormal”, the user would be automatically suspended, pending a review. The announcement did not include details about what qualified as “abnormal”. The company will also now allow law enforcement agencies to restrict the information offered to other agencies on specific offenses rather than giving free rein to the agencies that they partner with to access all of their license plate scans. Now, the company wrote, agencies can limit the scans they share with other cities or states to specific types of investigations like stolen vehicle or missing persons cases. The feature in part addresses years of reports that the company’s system had been used to target immigrants or people seeking out-of-state abortions, at times in violation of state or local laws. In addition, Flock will now automatically set its license plate scan retention time to seven days, down from its existing default of 30 days. However, agencies can identify certain scans as part of a longer-term investigation if they want to maintain that data for longer, the company said, and can continue to choose “the retention period that fits its public safety strategy”. These concerns have grown since the US supreme court’s reversal of its Roe v Wade decision guaranteeing the right to abortions. The Guardian found in 2022 that some California police departments were sharing license plate reader data with states where abortion is banned, potentially in violation of California’s own out-of-state data-sharing laws. At the time, a Flock executive said that the company’s mission was to “eliminate crime” and that crime was defined by the state or municipality a camera operates in. Privacy experts question whether these features are enough to protect the more than 6,000 communities where these Flock cameras are situated. “I don’t think there’s such a thing as ‘mass surveillance, but with guardrails’. Ultimately, networked cameras sprinkled across the country are incompatible with a free society,” said Chris Gilliard, author of the forthcoming book Luxury Surveillance . Reports of misuse of Flock’s system as well as concerns over privacy infringement have dogged the company for years but have only recently had a significant impact on it. The company was vaulted into the public’s consciousness after Amazon Ring announced and then cancelled its plan to integrate Flock’s license plate reader technology into its doorbell cameras. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to TechScape A weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our lives after newsletter promotion Since then, there’s been a growing citizen uprising against Flock cameras, prompting Langley to call vigilantes taking down Flock cameras “terrorists” and then apologize. Now, more than 80 cities have dropped or are publicly considering dropping their contracts with Flock. Inside the growing vigilante movement to knock out Flock surveillance cameras Read more But Robert Frommer, a senior attorney at the Institute of Justice, which is representing the plaintiffs in two federal lawsuits against the warrantless use of license plate readers, said Flock’s new features only amount to police departments policing themselves. “This is yet more window dressing,” said Frommer. “Flock suggests that police departments limit their retention periods to seven days, while admitting that decision is still entirely up to the police departments themselves.” 38:58 Inside the vigilante movement destroying Flock cameras – Stateside with Kai and Carter Explore more on these topics Technology Surveillance Road transport news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK US politics World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine Football Newsletters Business Environment UK politics Science Tech Global development Obituaries

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: Ultrarunner Sophie Woods climbs up a rocky trail on her way to becoming the fastest person ever to run the Via Alpina, a 2,000km network of alpine trails through eight countries in Europe. Photograph: Zoe Salt/Zoe Salt @Zoe_salt_photography View image in fullscreen Ultrarunner Sophie Woods climbs up a rocky trail on her way to becoming the fastest person ever to run the Via Alpina, a 2,000km network of alpine trails through eight countries in Europe. Photograph: Zoe Salt/Zoe Salt @Zoe_salt_photography New Zealand ‘So much more respect for myself’: NZ ultrarunner Sophie Woods on smashing a 2,000km alpine run record Sophie Woods speaks about the challenges she overcame while completing the notorious Via Alpina across eight European countries Eva Corlett Thu 13 Aug 2026 20.07 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 20.14 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A couple of weeks into her record-breaking 2,000km run through Europe’s alps, Sophie Woods feared she might die. Woods and her photographer had just scaled a peak in Switzerland, when a severe thunderstorm engulfed them. “The lightning was going off around us ... there was nowhere to shelter in place [and] all the rocks around us were conductive,” Woods tells the Guardian, from her home in Andorra, nearly two weeks after she became the fastest person ever to run the Via Alpina, a 2,000km network of alpine trails through eight countries. “I was slightly concerned that one of us was going to die,” she says. “I ran so fast to get out of that.” ‘Maybe the suffering is the point’: what does it take to run 163km up and down a mountain? Read more Woods set off from Muggia, near Trieste, in Italy on 4 July to run the mountainous Via Alpina trail winding through Italy, Slovenia, Austria, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, France, and Monaco with an ambitious goal: complete it in record time. It was an Odyssean feat. As well as battling thunderstorms and several heatwaves, Woods faced another unexpected challenge. At one stage, she had been running since 3am through Austria’s mountains, amid unbearable heat. By mid-afternoon she was exhausted, hot and stressed about whether she and her crew had accommodation for the night. Then, a swarm of blood-sucking horse flies descended. View image in fullscreen Sophie Woods set a new fastest known time on the Via Alpina, completing the 2,000km route through mountains in Europe in 28 days, 17 hours and 59 minutes. Photograph: Zoe Salt/Zoe Salt @Zoe_salt_photography “They were biting me, and I was already at my wit’s end,” she says. “I’m screaming at them every time they bite me. All I wanted to do is curl up in the foetal position and cry.” Unable to outrun them, Woods put away her hiking poles and grabbed two handfuls of ferns. “I spent the next hour just whacking myself with these ferns everywhere and I looked completely nuts. It was horrendous.” In the face of extreme conditions, the 42-year-old New Zealander remained a cautious runner and kept focus – sometimes for 20 hours a day. One ankle sprain, or fall, could have scuppered her goal. Each day she consumed about 7,000 calories, and was supported by her husband, George Woods, and photographer Zoe Salt, who fed her, cooled her down and arranged rests and accommodation along the route. By week three, she felt stronger than ever. “My body was just like, ‘OK, this is our life now … we go out and eat mountains for breakfast.’” Map of the Via Alpina: a 2,000km trail through eight countries Map of the Via Alpina: a 2,000km trail through eight countries. Woods ran through the night to reach the finish line in Monaco on 1 August, shuffling into the glitzy city-state exhausted, and grateful she and her team were still in one piece. “You’ve used up everything … so it just was a sense of relief I don’t have to run any more,” she says. The journey had taken her a remarkable 28 days, 17 hours and 59 minutes – smashing the previous record of 35 days and 21 hours set by British runner Jake Catterall, and beating Dutch runner Tessa Caspers’ previous best women’s time of 38 days. The record, Woods says, also belongs to her team: “It’s a pretty massive thing to ask of anyone, and I’m just so grateful to them.” Realisations and inspiration Born and raised in Christchurch, New Zealand, Woods showed little interest in running as child. After moving to the UK, aged 20, she started running to improve her health, initially managing just 15-minute jogs. As her habit grew, she began running 10km races, which soon escalated to marathons. During the week, Woods worked at a hair salon, while her weekends were spent seeking out mountainous trails. After 16 years in London, she bought a camper van with her husband and spent the next seven years travelling Europe’s mountains, before eventually settling in Andorra. View image in fullscreen Sophie Woods tries to catch a nap while completing her 2,000km odyssey. Photograph: Zoe Salt/Zoe Salt @Zoe_salt_photography Woods has competed in dozens of premiere races, including running the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (a 170km mountain race) six times, the Tor des Géants (an extreme 330km endurance event) and more, over the past decade. But by 2025, her joy in running started to wane. After several years attempting IVF treatment, Woods and her husband had to come to terms with infertility. As a result, each race felt like she was “just going through the motions”. “I was really struggling with the fact … that my life wasn’t going to look different, that I wasn’t going to be changing nappies and doing school runs,” Woods says. From small-town New Zealand to Mont Blanc: how ultrarunner Ruth Croft made history Read more On seeing his wife struggling, George Woods suggested they focus on a new challenge – Woods running the Via Alpina, with him as crew. The endeavour would have a profound effect on her love for the sport and her sense of self. “I had come from a place with the IVF where I was not particularly in love with my body,” Woods says. “But my love and respect for my body, and what she can do for me now, is just so much more. What she allowed me to achieve, in a way that was joyful … I just have so much more respect for myself.” Since completing the trail, Woods has been flooded with messages from girls and women around the world who want to try a 5km run or push themselves further. Her Instagram account has gained more than 55,000 followers in recent weeks. Woods “never thought” she would be in a position to inspire others and the widespread interest in her feat has come as a surprise. “When you’re in the trail-running world, these things seem a lot more normal,” she says. “But it has blown up, and you start to understand that what you’ve just done is not normal at all.” Explore more on these topics New Zealand Running Ultrarunning Marathon running Europe features Share Reuse this content Comments ( … ) Sign in or create your Guardian account to join the discussion Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/13/survi.text: A man who survived a ferry disaster that claimed at least 46 lives on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba told the AFP news agency on Thursday how he watched helplessly as people tried to save themselves, with his best friend and seven of his relatives among the dead.The overloaded government ferry, a vital link for villagers and fish traders around the vast lake, overturned in choppy waters on Tuesday in one of the country's worst passenger boat disasters."Thank God that a wave pushed the sinking vessel and we managed to climb on top," Chance Siyamavhu said at a memorial service in the lakeside town of Kariba close to the border with Zambia.Perched on the upended boat, he watched as passengers struggled to survive, unable to save them."When the boat capsized, most of the people scrambled to get the life jackets but most of them did not even know how to use them," the 45-year-old told AFP. "Most people could not make it.""Our relatives were swept in another direction and they sank because we were not in a position to help them," he said.Dozens of mourners gathered in front of 44 coffins at the emotional service, as police announced that the death toll had risen to 46."The names of the victims who perished in the accident will be released in due course," a police statement said.Officials say the boat was authorised to carry 90 people but was packed with 114 adults, five crew members and an unspecified number of children.The civil protection unit said 77 people were rescued and there were fears that other passengers may be unaccounted for.Survivors said they had pleaded for the captain to turn back as the boat took on water.Anymore Chambati, who had been a security official on the vessel, told AFP he had tried to hand out life jackets as the boat began to sink."I managed to only give not more than 10," he said. "The ferry engines were filled with water because of the heavy winds and eventually they failed, save for one."

http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/13/hunga.text: The Hungarian Integrity Authority is setting up a register of economic operators excluded from public procurement after they were deemed to have committed criminal offences.This measure, which is essential for the resumption of EU funding, is intended not only to weed out abuses but also to offer a chance for self-cleaning, according to the government.Budapest argued on Thursday that those who can prove that they have "restored their trustworthiness" should have their names removed from the register.The Hungarian Integrity Authority is also launching the first registration procedures and will begin keeping a list of economic operators excluded from public procurement.The primary purpose of operating this publicly accessible database is to ensure that no economic operator can take part in public procurement procedures if its executive officer, member of the supervisory board, managing director or beneficial owner has been the subject to a final court decision for criminal offences as defined in the Public Procurement Act.The authority stressed that the measure concerns a clearly defined group in legal terms; while making the information public was not about stigmatisation, but about preventing further abuses and ensuring the integrity of public procurement.How can companies be removed from the list?The self-cleaning procedure is conducted ex officio by the Integrity Authority through electronic administration.If the economic operator concerned by the procedure lodges an objection, it must, in its response, set out and document that it has compensated the damage caused by the criminal offence to the extent accepted by the injured party, or has undertaken to do so by a specified deadline.It must also show that it has cooperated actively with the competent authorities, fully clarified the facts and circumstances of the case, and introduced the technical, organisational and personnel measures needed to ensure that no further criminal offence is committed.The relevant authorities then have 20 days to assess the appeals and entries and decide whether to remove the economic operator in question from the register. The new register is then made readily available in the Electronic Public Procurement System.

https://www.dw.com/en/romania-shuts-nucl.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5ImuD The Cernavoda nuclear plant gathers all its cooling water from the Danube Image: Alex Nicodim/Anadolu/picture alliance Advertisement Romania shut down its lone nuclear power plant on Thursday, a rare move amid the drought that has caused record lows on the Danube River and other major waterways in Europe . The Danube is the sole source of cooling water for the Cernavoda plant, which usually generates around one-fifth of Romania's electricity. The power station has only been shut down once before, in 2023, again as a result of drought and a hot summer . Meanwhile, Hungary was scrambling to dam the Danube, as it tries to keep its Paks nuclear power plant at least running at the minimal levels that it has maintained in recent days, which are far below capacity. Attempts to divert more water to Cernavoda earlier this month didn't prevent a shutdown Image: Alex Nicodim/Anadolu/picture alliance What did the operator and authorities in Romania say about the shutdown? Romania's Nuclearelectrica company had already shut one of the two reactors at Cernavoda last month. On Thursday, it said it needed to shut the second "because of the significant and ongoing drop in the water level of the Danube River." The company tried earlier this month , with help from the Navy, to improve the plant's chances of staying operational. Most memorably, it blew up a rocky outcrop exposed by the low water levels and strategically deposited the rocks on the riverbed in a bid to direct more water to Cernavoda. But ultimately, continued dry weather and sinking water levels prompted the total shutdown. "We do not foresee a restart within the next 10 days," the plant director, Romeo Urjan, told the AFP news agency. Romania's Energy Ministry said it was procuring alternative power sources, including from wind power but also from energy imports, to try to ensure adequate supplies. Still it appealed to the public to consume responsibly. It warned that as a last resort, large industrial users would have to face restrictions in the evening hours to save electricity. Carmakers Ford and Dacia had already committed to pausing production until August 19 to save power. Earlier in August, the Romanian Navy detonated submerged rocks as part of a bid to funnel more water to the power plant Image: Andreea Alexandru/AP Photo/picture alliance What is Hungary doing to try to prevent a similar shutdown of the Paks plant? Prime Minister Peter Magyar on Thursday visited Hungary's only nuclear power plant , the Paks facility that is also cooled by the Danube. "We have begun construction of the low weir that will permanently contribute to raising the Danube's water level," Magyar told reporters at the site, roughly 100 kilometers (about 60 miles) south of Budapest. Only one of Paks' four reactors is currently operational amid the drought. Nine days ago, the plant was at risk of a complete shutdown, but the government was able to abort those plans at the last moment as the Danube's levels ended up being a few millimeters higher than forecast. The unusually low river levels near the Paks plant are hard to miss at present Image: Robert Nemeti/Anadolu/picture alliance Under normal circumstances, the plant is responsible for around half of Hungary's electricity generation, and about one-third of its consumption. Before the completion of the weir, authorities plan to deliberately sink two 80-meter-long barges — placed end-to-end and perpendicular to the river's flow — to create an initial damming effect and raise the water level somewhat. Magyar said that Hungarian soldiers were working round the clock on the construction, and that it should be completed in the next four weeks. He said the project should elevate water levels in front of the Paks plant cooling system by more than a meter. The project might not be finished long before the summer starts to fade and the rains return, but the low water levels also provide a rare opportunity to undertake such construction projects relatively cheaply and easily. https://www.politico.eu/article/peter-ma.text: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar on Thursday cast doubt on a deal struck by his predecessor that would see Russia’s state nuclear company Rosatom expand Hungary’s nuclear power capacity. Weeks of extreme heat and drought have pushed the Danube River to record lows , slashing output at Hungary’s Paks nuclear plant — which normally supplies around a third of the country’s electricity — to little more than 10 percent . “These plans were accepted despite the fact that nuclear power plants that do not operate with a closed-circuit cooling system and are so exposed to the environment are no longer being built in the world,” said Magyar, per local media . Advertisement Advertisement Rosatom CEO Alexei Likhachev wrote that the Russian state nuclear company was still on schedule with two new reactors at Paks despite Hungary’s change of government in April , which saw Magyar oust Russia-friendly incumbent Viktor Orbán. Concrete preparation for Unit 5 is more than 80 percent complete, he said, while work on Unit 6 is advancing and reactor components are already being manufactured. “We are ready for dialogue,” Likhachev said, adding that Rosatom had received no questions from Hungary’s new government. Magyar challenged that account hours later. Under the original contract, Paks II should have been operating by 2024, he told reporters in a press conference Thursday. Instead, Hungary has spent roughly 1,000 billion forints (€2.8 billion) on a site he described as little more than depots and “two large concrete pits.” “I don’t really see that they have adhered to the contract,” Magyar said. His government is now carrying out a full review of the project , including its financing and cooling arrangements. The review cuts at one of Orbán’s signature deals with Russia. Orbán struck the Paks II agreement in Moscow in 2014 , handing Rosatom the two-reactor expansion backed by up to €10 billion in Russian state financing. Two years later, he called it the “deal of the century.” Those ties survived Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine . As recently as March this year, Orbán’s foreign minister Péter Szijjártó admitted to discussing EU sanctions with senior Russian officials after leaked calls showed him boasting that a bank linked to Paks had been kept off a sanctions list. Downstream, Romania shut the second and last operating reactor at Cernavodă on Thursday after the Danube fell too low to supply its cooling pumps. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ce85.text: Image source, World Food Programme/PA Image caption, Michael Ryan was among the 157 people killed on board the Ethiopian Airlines plane By Barry O'Connor BBC News NI Published 13 August 2026 The widow of an Irish United Nations employee, who died in 2019 following a Boeing 737 Max crash in Ethiopia, has been awarded $29m (Â£21.5m) in damages. A jury in Chicago in the United States awarded the sum to Michael 'Mick' Ryan's family after his widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against the aircraft manufacturer. Her lawyers have said the verdict "represents an important measure of accountability and justice". A Boeing spokesperson said the company is "deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones" and they "respect" the right for families to "pursue their claims". Michael Ryan, a father of two living in Cork but originally from County Clare, was among the 157 people killed on board the Ethiopian Airlines plane. He had worked as an engineer with the United Nations World Food Programme. 'A significant milestone' Lawyer Steven C Marks, who represented Ryan's widow, said: "While no financial award can ever replace a life or undo the profound loss his family has endured, we are grateful that the jury carefully considered the evidence and reached this decision." Marks said that Connolly Ryan has "pursued justice for Mick with extraordinary strength and determination" and his firm Podhurst Orseck have been "honoured to stand beside her in her unwavering pursuit to hold Boeing accountable". "Although the verdict marks a significant milestone, the broader effort to hold Boeing responsible for this tragedy, and to help prevent anything like it from happening again, is just as important," he added. In a statement, a Boeing spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones on Lion Air Flight 610 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302. "While we have resolved nearly all of these claims through settlements, families are entitled to pursue their claims through the court process, and we respect their right to do so." 'His impact was worldwide' Image source, Podhurst Orseck Image caption, Lawyer Steven Marks says Ryan's family have pursued justice with "extraordinary strength" On a United Nations memorial page to Michael Ryan , external it said he helped the World Food Programme "bring assistance to vulnerable people" in Afghanistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Ethiopia and Bangladesh. The organisation credits him with organising "the building of shelters and infrastructure" in Bangladesh "which saved tens of thousands of Rohingya refugees from the threat of landslides and floods". It also said he built medical centres in Liberia during the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak. Marks told BBC News NI that Ryan "will be missed by the world at large" as that was "who he served". "It's tragic to the public, but it pales in comparison to the loss for the family. "His impact was worldwide." What happened to Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 737 Max? Figure caption, Relatives pay their respects to those who died in the Ethiopian Airlines crash Flight ET302 took off from Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa at 08:38 local time (05:38 GMT) on 10 March for a two-hour flight to the Kenyan capital, Nairobi. Six minutes later, at 08:44, it crashed 30 miles southeast of the airport , near the town of Bishoftu. The impact was so great, both engines were buried at a depth of 10m (32ft), in a crater 28m wide and 40m long. The preliminary report into the accident, by Ethiopia's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, said the plane's take-off appeared normal. However, a short time later two sensors that measured the angle of the plane's flight began to record different readings. This triggered an automated safety system which repeatedly pushed the nose of the plane down - something that was also recorded during the fatal Lion Air flight. The Ethiopian authorities' 2019 report suggested the pilots followed steps to disengage the system, but even after manually trying to steady the plane, the system pushed the nose down until the aircraft crashed. A közel egymillió hordónyi kőolaj szállítására képes hajó még június végén feneklett meg egy, a partoktól nagyjából ötven kilométernyire található szigetnél, és eleinte úgy tűnt, hogy nem szivárog belőle az olaj. Ez már júliusban megváltozott, majd augusztusban szinte az egyik pillanatról a másikra ömleni kezdett a kőolaj az egyre jobban süllyedő hajóból. Mostanra már több száz, de egyes becslések szerint akár kétezer négyzetkilométernyi területet is érinthet a szennyezés. Az olajfolt szerdára kétszáz kilométernyire található tengerpartokat is elért , és akár egy háromszáz kilométernyire lévő szigetig is eljuthat. A hajót az ománi hatóságok eleinte csak monitorozták, augusztusban kezdtek el igazán megoldásokat keresni a természeti katasztrófával fenyegető olajszennyezés megállítására és a tanker biztosítására. Végül az Ambrey brit hajózási biztonsági cég segítségét kérték, ami most bejelentette, hogy megkezdték a mentési akciót a hajó és a rakomány biztosításához. Rejtélyes robbanás Az érintett hajó, a kameruni zászló alatt hajózó Caroline Bezengi a TankerTrackers.com adatai szerint május 13-án indult el a Fekete-tengernél található Novorosszijszk kikötővárosból, legalább nyolcszázezer, de akár egymillió hordónyi kőolajjal, amit a világ legnagyobb olajfinomító komplexumát kiszolgáló indiai Sikka kikötőjébe vitt volna. A tanker, amivel szemben az Európai Unió, Ukrajna, az Egyesült Királyság, Kanada és Svájc által bevezetett szankciók vannak érvényben, áthaladt a Szuezi-csatornán, mielőtt június elején történt vele egy incidens Jemen partjainak a közelében. A Vanguard tengeri biztonsági cég az AFP-nek azt mondta, hogy a hajót június 6-án három robbanás rázta meg , ezek után több helyen is víz szivárgott a hajótestbe, de azt nem lehet tudni, hogy támadás történt-e. A hajó június 11-én kikapcsolta a jeladóját, majd valamikor a rá következő egy-két hétben – az AFP vizsgálata szerint június 18. és 23. között, míg az Oman Muscat Daily ománi lap szerint június 21-én – egy szeles napon zátonyra futott a lakatlan al-Kiblíja sziget sziklás partjainál. A legénység három nappal később elhagyta a hajót, sorsukról nem tudni. Az ománi hatóságok megvizsgálták a hajót, de akkor nem volt észrevehető olajszivárgás – mondta az ománi környezetvédelmi hatóság vezetője az Oman TV-nek adott interjújában, amit a New York Times idézett. A hatóság közlése szerint július 1-jén mentek ki a helyszínre, de a vizsgálatok szerint akkor nem volt olajszennyezés – írta a Muscat Daily. Kevesebb mint két héttel később a helyzet már romlani kezdett, és a hatóságok július 23-án a hajó és a rakomány eltávolítására szólították fel a tulajdonost , amire feltehetően semmilyen választ nem kaptak. A megrongálódott és félig elsüllyedt Caroline Bezengi olajszállító hajó Omán partjainál 2026. augusztus 6-án – Fotó: Ambrey / Reuters A Caroline Bezengi a Sanghajban bejegyzett Rentoor Shipmanagement nevű cég tulajdonában van, üzemeltetője pedig egy szintén kínai, Villar Shipmanagement nevű cég, amiket a Reuters nem tudott elérni. A Maritime Executive hajózási szaklap szerint a Rentoor levelezési címe egy Sanghaj belvárosában található lakóépületben van. A lap úgy tudja, hogy az ománi hatóságok már júliusban elkezdtek terveket készíteni arra, hogyan tudnák megmenteni a hajót és rakományát, de jogi nehézségekbe ütköztek, amik megakadályozták a mentési munkálatok azonnali megkezdését. A Reutersnek nyilatkozó elemzők és biztosítótársaságok szintén azt mondták, hogy a hajózást és az olajszennyezéseket érintő háborús és szankciós jogszabályok bonyolult hálója nehezíti a mentési munkálatokat. Az olajszennyezések elszenvedőinek kompenzációkat nyújtó IOPC Funds nevű nemzetközi szervezet jelezte a Reutersnek, hogy nem lesz érintett az esetnél, mert az incidenst háborús cselekményként tartják számon, és nem egyszerű balesetként. Az egyelőre kérdés, hogy az orosz–ukrán vagy az iráni háborúhoz kötik-e a történteket. Az ukránok rendszeresen támadják az orosz árnyékflotta hajóit, de a Fekete-tengeren és a Földközi-tengeren. A Hormuzi-szoros közelében viszont több hajót is ért már iráni dróntámadás. Katasztrófa lehet Július közepén a Reutersnek nyilatkozó szakértők már arról számoltak be a hajóról készített műholdfelvételek tanulmányozása után, hogy a tankerből olaj szivároghat , és a hónap végén már látszott, hogy a kőolaj egyre nagyobb mennyiségben ömlik a vízbe. „A sötétebb olajfoltok arra utalnak, hogy a hajó egyik rekesze már vélhetően megsérült, és a hajóból szivárog a nyersolaj” – mondta a Reutersnek Wim Zwijnenburg, a Pax holland békeszervezet szakértője. Az események aztán felgyorsultak. A Greenpeace Germany szakértője, Nina Noelle az AP-nek azt mondta , hogy az olajfolt július végén 45 négyzetkilométernyi területet érintett, augusztus 2-re már 150 négyzetkilométert, majd két nappal később már 600 négyzetkilométernyi területre terjedt szét. A szervezet szombaton már arra figyelmeztetett, hogy az eset „pusztító következményekkel járó, példátlan olajkatasztrófát” okozhat, ha nem tesznek ellene semmit. Az ománi hatóságok akkor közölték, hogy figyelemmel kísérik a hajó sorsát, és készen állnak megtenni a megfelelő lépéseket. Közben John Amos, a SkyTruth nevű nonprofit szervezet CEO-ja és olajszennyezés-szakértő a Reutersnek arról beszélt , hogy „minél tovább várunk, minél jobban megsérül a tartályhajó, annál bonyolultabb, nehezebb és potenciálisan veszélyesebb lesz a mentési művelet”. Semmi nyomát nem találták annak, hogy az ománi hatóságok bármit is tettek volna a katasztrófa kivédésére. Az ománi környezetvédelmi hatóság hétfőn már arról számolt be, hogy a szennyezés majdnem négyszáz négyzetkilométernyi területre terjedt szét. Jelezték , hogy dolgoznak a hajó biztosításán, és megkezdték a felkészülést a rakomány biztonságos elszállítására. „A jelenlegi szakaszban a prioritás a szennyezés csökkentése, forrásának kezelése, valamint a hajó biztosítása és az olajrakomány elszállítása a lehető legmagasabb szintű biztonsági intézkedések mellett” – jelentette ki az ománi közlekedési minisztérium tengeri ügyekkel foglalkozó vezetője. A Muscat Daily akkori cikke szerint már zajlott a hajótest vizsgálata, valamint megoldások keresése a még a hajóban maradt olaj kiszivattyúzására. Szerdán az olajszennyezés már elérte Omán szárazföldi partvidékét , és a hajótól nagyjából kétszáz kilométernyire észak-keletre található Rasz Madraka partjait. Veszélyben van a háromszáz kilométernyire található Masirah sziget is. John Amos a Reutersnek azonban több mint kétezer négyzetkilométernyire tette a szennyezés miatt érintett terület kiterjedését. Ne egyenek a halakból, ne fürödjenek a vízben Az ománi hatóságok bejelentették , hogy tesztelni kezdik a helyi piacokon árult halakat, felszólították az embereket, hogy ne halásszanak, ne fürödjenek a szennyezéstől érintett területeken, és ne nyúljanak hozzá az olajfoltokhoz. A hatóságok közölték azt is, hogy a sótalanító üzemeknél nem találtak semmit, ami aggodalomra adhat okot. Az Ambrey kedden az AFP-nek , majd szerdán a New York Timesnak is bejelentette, hogy részt vesznek a tanker mentésében, amit csütörtökön egy közleményben is megerősítettek . „Ez egy rendkívül nehéz helyzet, amit a kedvezőtlen időjárási körülmények súlyosbítanak” – mondta a New York Timesnak a cég globális fellépésekkel foglalkozó igazgatója. A mentést nehezíti, hogy a területen éppen zajlik az erős szeleket és 4-5 méter magas hullámokat okozó monszun időszaka. Az Ambrey közölte , hogy egy vezető nemzetközi olajszennyezés-elhárító céggel kötöttek szerződést, de annak nevét nem hozták nyilvánosságra. A cég közlése szerint az ománi légierő segítségével szakértőket juttattak a hajóra, hogy felmérjék az állapotát, és megkezdjék stabilizálását. A helyszínre már elindultak speciális mentőhajók a tanker kiemelésére, és az akcióhoz több mint száz tonnányi eszközt vetnek be. John Amos arra figyelmeztetett , hogy az erős szelek és a hullámok hatására a hajó még jobban széteshet, és a rémálomszerű forgatókönyv az lenne, ha emiatt az összes, több mint 150 millió liter olaj kiömlene a hajóból. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/13/paks.text: Menü Kereső A Roszatom Paks II.-ről: Tartjuk magunkat az egyeztetett tervhez. Magyar Péter: Azért vannak kétségeim Belföld Bakró-Nagy Ferenc Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Jó ütemben halad a Paks II. atomerőmű építése, a Roszatom tartja magát a magyar megrendelővel egyeztetett tervhez – jelentette ki Alekszej Lihacsov, az orosz állami atomenergia-vállalat vezérigazgatója csütörtökön saját lapjuknak, a Sztrana Roszatom vállalati hírportálnak. A magyar kormányváltás nem befolyásolta a Paks II. atomerőmű építését című anyagban a Roszatom vezetője elmondta: felvették a munkakapcsolatot a magyar megrendelő új vezetésével. Lihacsov szerint készek a párbeszédre, mint ahogy arra is, hogy számok és tények nyelvén válaszoljanak a magyar vezetés bármely kérdésére, ám eddig nem érkezett hozzájuk ilyen megkeresés. A vezérigazgató nyilatkozatáról Magyar Péter a csütörtöki sajtótájékoztatón azt mondta, hogy kétségei vannak felőle, ugyanis ha tartották volna a szerződést, akkor 2024-ben már működnie kellett volna Paks II.-nek. Ehelyett most depók és két nagy betongödör van a helyén, amire 1000 milliárd forintot kellett költeni. „Nem igazán látom, hogy ők tartották volna a szerződéshez magukat” – mondta a miniszterelnök, aki szerint a finanszírozás sem igazán úgy alakul, mint az eredeti szerződésben szerepelt, hanem már a duplájába kerülne a megvalósítás. Épp emiatt zajlik a projekt átvilágítása, és amint végeztek ezzel a bonyolult és szerteágazó folyamattal, reagálni fognak a Roszatomnak is. Magyar emlékeztetett, hogy az Országos Atomenergia Hivatal szerint is megkérdőjelezhető a Paks II.-nek kiadott környezetvédelmi, hűtéssel kapcsolatos engedély ilyen vízállásnál. „Annak ellenére fogadták el ezeket a terveket, hogy a világon már nem nagyon épülnek olyan atomerőművek, amelyek nem zártláncú hűtőrendszerrel üzemelnek, hanem ennyire kitettek a környezetnek” – mondta Magyar. Lihacsov tájékoztatása szerint az erőmű ötödik blokkjának építkezésén februárban kezdődött a reaktorépület alaplemezének első betonöntése, a betonozás több mint 80 százaléka kész, több mint 18 ezer köbméter betont öntöttek eddig az erőműblokk alapjába. A hatodik blokknál a „nukleáris sziget” alapgödrének kialakításán dolgoznak, a terveknek megfelelően az év végéig itt is megkezdik a betonozás előkészítését. A Roszatom hírportálja szerint az új atomerőművi blokkokhoz már gyártják a berendezéseket is. A reaktor aktív zónájának olvadékcsapdája már elkészült, és azt le is szállították Magyarországra, az ötödik blokk reaktorához szükséges fémalkatrészeket is legyártották, hamarosan megkezdődik az összeszerelésük. A hatodik blokk reaktorának öntési munkálatai a terv szerint haladnak. A Sztrana Roszatom szakértők véleményére hivatkozva azt írta, hogy a Paks II. atomerőmű-projekt kulcsfontosságú paramétereinek esetleges felülvizsgálata az üzembe helyezés határidejének jelentős elhalasztását és a pénzügyi modell alapvető átalakítását tenné szükségessé.
