Nádor András 28 perce Lezárjuk a közvetítésünket Véget ért a paksi atomerőmű működéséhez kapcsolódó beruházásokról szóló csütörtöki kormányzati tájékoztató, ezért lezárjuk a közvetítésünket. Nagyon köszönjük a figyelmet! Krász Zsombor 28 perce Ezek voltak a kormányzat csütörtöki tájékoztatójának legfontosabb állításai Újra apadásnak indult a Duna, hétfőn érheti el azt a szintet, amikor a jelenleg üzemelő két turbinából egyet ismét le kellene állítani. A középtávú előrejelzések sem biztatóak, 6-7 napon belül –137 centire is visszaeshet a vízszint, –140 centinél már az egész erőművet le kellene állítani. Magyar Péter szerint a nulláról kellett elkészítenie a kormánynak a paksi terveket, mivel az előző kormány nem készült a jelenlegi helyzetre. A Telex kérdésére elmondta, emiatt személyi és intézményi felelősség is felmerülhet az előző kormányt és a paksi atomerőművet illetően. Több cég is jelentkezett, és komoly felajánlásokat tett technológiára, szállításra és alapanyagra a paksi beruházásnál. Magyar Péter felháborítónak tartja, hogy egy osztrák cégnek előbb jut eszébe ingyen felajánlani Magyarországnak a segítségét, mint a NER-es vállalkozóknak. A fenékküszöbről Magyar Péter elmondta, hogy a megépítéséhez összesen 145 ezer köbméter követ fognak önteni a Dunába. Előbb 35 ezer köbméter, később 110 ezer köbméter követ fognak megmozgatni. Arra utalt, hogy ezek nem Orbán Viktor apjának kőbányájából fognak jönni. Jelenleg nem nagyon tudnak a hajók haladni, vesztegelnek. Idővel helyre kell majd állítani a hajózás feltételeit. Közben az átmeneti megoldásnak számító, a vízszint emelésére alkalmas első bárkát tegnap, a másodikat pedig ma állították pozícióba. Egyelőre azonban óvatosak ezek besüllyesztésével, mert ez az áramlási viszony megváltozását, a beépítési területen pedig nehezebb munkakörülményeket eredményezhet. A gazdaság is megérzi az elmúlt heteket: nincs még konkrét számításuk, de korábbi modelljük alapján 0,1 százalékos csökkenést biztosan okozott az éves GDP-ben a jelenlegi helyzet. Nádor András 38 perce Vizsgálták a román példát is, a bárkák stabilabbak, mint az uszályok A Bloomberg a bárkák süllyesztéséről kérdezett, arról, hogy a romániai példát vizsgálták-e, ahol szintén több hajót is elsüllyesztettek, de ez csak pár centimétert emelt a vízszinten. Magyar Péter azt mondta, vizsgálták ezeket a szakemberek. Elmondta megint, hogy a bárkák elsüllyesztése csak haváriamegoldás. Gacsályi József, az Országos Vízügyi Főigazgatóság műszaki főigazgató-helyettese ezt megerősítette, azt mondta, megnézték, milyen közegben alkalmazták Romániában a süllyesztéseket. Elmondta, hogy a Romániában alkalmazott uszályoknál a bárkák stabilabbak. Magyar Péter a tájékoztató végén bejelentette, hogy ma vagy pénteken társadalmi egyeztetésre fogják bocsátani az energiatervet, ami az uniós fejlesztési terv része, „bármennyire is nem tetszik a konteókat gyártó kóklereknek”. Magyar Péter azt üzente a fideszes képviselőknek, hogy amíg ők a szabadságukon vannak, addig a kormány dolgozik. Azt kérte az ellenzéki képviselőktől, ne hazudjanak az embereknek, inkább segítsenek Magyarország energiaellátását biztonságosabbá tenni. Krász Zsombor 44 perce A gazdaság is megérzi az elmúlt hetek extrém időjárását A Portfolio kérdésére Magyar Péter elmondta, hogy egyelőre nincsen egzakt számítás arra, lehet-e érdemi hatása a gazdasági növekedésre az elmúlt néhány hétnek. Egy modelljük azonban van, ami alapján úgy számolnak: 0,1 százalékos csökkenést biztosan okozott az éves GDP-ben a jelenlegi helyzet, de ennél akár nagyobb is lehet végül a visszaesés. Nádor András 50 perce Magyar Péter szerint „blődség, hülyeség, dezinformáció” volt az, amit a Mi Hazánk mondott az erőműről Gulyás Balázs, a Kontroll újságírója arról kérdezett, hogy mit gondol Magyar Péter arról, hogy a Mi Hazánk magának vindikálja a bárkák/uszályok ötletét. Toroczkai László Magyar Péter szerint maga is elmondta a Sándor-palotában, hogy semmit nem tud az atomerőművekről. Hosszan sorolta, hogy szerinte mennyi „blődséget, hülyeséget, dezinformációt” hordott össze a Mi Hazánk. Szerinte 10 dolgot dobált be a párt, de ha ebből akár hármat megcsináltak volna, akkor már lehet, hogy le kellett volna állítani Paksot, az is lehet, hogy már nem lenne áram. A Kontroll másik kérdése arról szólt, hogy a miniszterelnök milyen összegű felajánlásokra számít a NER-es vállalkozóktól. Magyar erre azt mondta, nincsenek elvárásai, de felháborítónak tartja, hogy egy osztrák cégnek előbb jut eszébe ingyen felajánlani Magyarországnak a segítségét, mint az említett vállalkozóknak. De megint elmondta, hogy a duna@vih.gov.hu-ra várja a felajánlásokat. Krász Zsombor 55 perce Magyar: Semmi akadálya nincsen annak, hogy a környezetvédő szervezeteket is bevonják a fenékküszöb kivitelezésébe Magyar Péter az MTI kérdésére elmondta, semmi akadálya nincsen annak, hogy a kivitelezésbe a környezetvédő szervezeteket is bevonják. „Hallom a fenntartásokat, a félelmeket, tanácsokat. Ezeket meghallgatjuk, csak haváriahelyzet van.” Gacsályi József megerősítette: hidrobiológusokat már bevontak a tervezésbe. Az is előfordulhat, hogy a fenékküszöb nem kapja meg a szükséges engedélyeket. Nyitott kapukat dönget – mondta a miniszterelnök arra a kérdésre, hogy van-e terv egy összeurópai, a Dunával kapcsolatos koncepció kidolgozására. 15 éve fogadták el a Duna-stratégiát, aminek az a célja, hogy megőrizzük és közösen használjuk a Dunát. Magyar Péter szerint ezt azonban nem sikerült megvalósítani Magyarországon, épp ezért most életet kell majd lehelni ebbe a stratégiába. Emellett a magyar vízügyi megállapodások rendkívül régiek, teljesen más vízhozamhoz szokott időkben keletkeztek, ezért felül kell vizsgálni ezeket. Mind Ausztria, mind Szlovákia betartotta a hatályos vízügyi megállapodást, csak lehet, hogy a helyzet teljesen más, mint korábban volt – mondta Magyar. Nádor András ma 16:44 Egy hónapon belül el kell készülnie a fenékküszöbnek A köztévé kérdésére Magyar Péter elmondta, hogy a fenékküszöb lényegi részének egy hónapon belül el kell készülnie. Azt mondta, kijavították a szakemberek, hogy a fenékküszöb nem egyméteres vízszintnövekedést biztosít, hanem azt, hogy a víz –90 centiméteren álljon, így pedig biztosítva lehet az atomerőmű összes reaktorának működése. „Ha ezt a beruházást elvégezzük, az azt jelenti, hogy működik teljes kapacitással a paksi atomerőmű.” Krász Zsombor ma 16:41 Személyi felelősség is felmerülhet amiatt, hogy az előző kormány nem készült egy jelenlegihez hasonló helyzetre Mindenképpen biztosítható lesz, hogy hűteni tudják az erőművet akkor is, ha teljesen le kellene állítani a turbinákat – mondta a Telex kérdésére Magyar Péter. A miniszterelnök szerint egyrészt a biztonsági szivattyúk működése még a termeléshez szükséges vízszint alatt is rendelkezésre áll, ha pedig már ezek sem tudnak üzemelni, az vízen úszó szivattyúkkal még egy méterrel alacsonyabb vízállásig is tudják hűteni az erőművet. Magyar Péter szerint személyi és intézményi felelősség is felmerülhet az előző kormányt vagy a paksi atomerőművet illetően amiatt, hogy nem készültek tervekkel egy, a jelenlegihez hasonló haváriahelyzetre. Arra a kérdésre, hogy tervez-e személyi változást emiatt vagy ettől függetlenül a Paksi Atomerőműnél, a Mavirnál vagy a Magyar Energetikai és Közmű-szabályozási Hivatalnál, elmondta, nem lenne helyes ilyen döntést hozni a jelenlegi helyzetben. Nádor András ma 16:28 Magyar Péter azt ígérte, nem abból a kőbányából jönnek a kövek Az RTL arról kérdezte a miniszterelnököt, hogy korábban miért mondta, hogy nem lehet ideiglenes védművet építeni a Dunán. Valószínűleg rosszul fogalmaztam – mondta. „Az Országos Atomenergia Hivatal vizsgálata szerint nem befolyásolja a nukleáris biztonságot a fenékküszöb” – mondta a miniszterelnök. Nagyon fontos volt a kormánydöntés, ami gyorsított eljárásokat tesz lehetővé, a közbeszerzéseket rövidíti. „Nem abból a kőbányából fog jönni a kő, amitől sokan félnek” – mondta a miniszterelnök, aki egyértelműen Orbán Viktor apjának gánti kőbányájára gondolt. „Drága ott a kő, de ha megengedhetnénk magunknak, akkor se hoznánk onnan követ.” A polgárdi bányából viszont fog jönni kő. Fotó: Szigetváry Zsolt / MTI Nádor András ma 16:21 Magyar Péter szerint nincs környezetvédelmi veszélye a fenékküszöbnek Gondolnak mindenre a szakemberek, szeretik a Dunát – így nyugtatott mindenkit a miniszterelnök. Hatalmas munka az embereknek, de a Duna életét nem fogja nagy mértékben befolyásolni – mondta Magyar Péter. Szerinte például az ausztriai duzzasztó erőművek sokkal jobban befolyásolják a Duna életét. Minden vízhozamra lefuttatták a tervezők a modelleket. Az is előnye a beruházásnak, hogy „lépésről lépésre” lehet vele haladni. Meg lehet úgy oldani, hogy a hajózás feltételei rövid úton teljesíthetőek legyenek – mondta a miniszterelnök. Krász Zsombor ma 16:19 Ma a második bárkát is pozícióba állítják a Dunán Gacsályi József szerint egy bárka 20 centiméterrel, így az átmeneti megoldásként a vízbe süllyesztett két bárka a legoptimistább becslés szerint akár 40 centiméterrel is megemelheti a vízszintet. Egyelőre azonban óvatosak a bárkák besüllyesztésével, mert ez az áramlási viszony megváltozását, a beépítési területen pedig nehezebb munkakörülményeket eredményezhet. Hogy vigyázzanak a mederre és annak természetes állapotára, csak a legszükségesebb beavatkozásokat teszik meg és hajtják végre – mondta Magyar Péter. A miniszterelnök szerint tegnap megtörtént a munkaterület átadása és az első bárka pozícióba állítása. Ma, augusztus 13-án többek között a második bárkát is pozícióba állítják. Holnap a két bárka már rendelkezésre áll, létrejön a süllyesztésre kész állapot, szombaton megtörténik a nyomvonal megtisztítása és a szükséges geotextília leterítése, a jobb parton pedig a bárkahídfő építése. Augusztus 17. és 21. között elkészül a jobbparti bárkából álló ponton, amin keresztül a terméskő közvetlenül a mederbe fog jutni. Augusztus 18. és szeptember 4. között a bal part felől 8 ezer köbméter követ építenek be a vízszintemelő bordákba, ezzel párhuzamosan augusztus végéig 16 ezer köbméter kő kerül a mederbe. Szeptember első hetében a jobb parton további 8 ezer köbméter követ juttatnak a mederbe, szeptember közepén pedig a balparti utolsó, háromméteres szakasz bezárásával összezárják a két oldalról épülő vízszintemelő bordát, majd haladnak tovább a további 70 ezer köbméternyi kő beépítésével egészen októberig. Nádor András ma 16:08 Magyar Péter: Nem uszályok, bárkák Jelenleg nem nagyon tudnak a hajók haladni, vesztegelnek – mondta Magyar Péter a tájékoztatón. Azt mondta ugyanakkor, hogy idővel helyre kell majd állítani a hajózás feltételeit. Megjegyezte, reméli, hogy az újságírók mindent értettek abból, amit Gacsályi József, a vízügy műszaki főigazgató-helyettese korábban mondott. Bejelentette a miniszterelnök, hogy a Paksra érkező bárkák korábban a mohácsi Duna-híd építésénél teljesítettek szolgálatot, a vállalkozó-tulajdonos első szóra felajánlotta őket. Jelenleg folyik azoknak a cölöpöknek a kiépítése, amikhez rögzítik majd a bárkákat. De vízmérőket is telepítenek a bárkák fölé és alá, hogy percről percre lássák, hogyan hat a Duna vízszintjére a beavatkozás. Magyar azt mondta, egy bárka 20 centiméteres vízszintemelkedést okozhat. Egyben egyértelművé tette: bárkák, nem uszályok fognak érkezni Paksra, ezek az eszközök stabilabbak, mint az uszályok. Azt is elmondta, hogy péntek reggelre mindkét bárkának meg kell érkeznie Paksra. Gacsályi Pál arról beszélt, hogy a bárkák elsüllyesztése inkább „egy piros gomb”, amit csak akkor nyomnak meg, ha a fenékküszöb nem épül meg kellő időben. Gacsályi szerint „megnyugtató lesz, hogy a helyszínen lesznek a bárkák”. Krász Zsombor ma 16:02 Az augusztusi rekordalacsony vízszintet fél méterrel tudta volna megemelni a fenékküszöb Látni kell, hogy a kőmű feletti vízszintet folyamatosan befolyásolni fogja a beavatkozás – mondta Gacsályi József, a vízügyi főigazgatóság műszaki vezérigazgató-helyetese. Rendkívüli helyzetre tervezték a létesítményt: az augusztusi −140 centiméteres rekordalacsony vízszintet közel fél méterrel meg kell tudniuk majd megemelni a beavatkozással. Az is alapvető elvárás volt, hogy a beavatkozás ne jelentsen számottevő negatív hatást az árhullám-levezető képességre. Míg most csak a kisvíz által kimetszett mederbe avatkoznak be, egy árhullámnál nemcsak ebbe, hanem a főmederbe és a hullámtérbe is beavatkoznának. 600 köbméteres vízhozamnál közel 4 méter/másodperces áramlási sebesség fog kialakulni a küszöbnél. A kőmű, amit szárazon építenek Dunaszentbenedek felől, ekkor szárazon fog állni, csak a kövek felől átszivárgó víz fog némi vízmozgást eredményezni. 1000 köbméternél már a dunaszentbenedeki oldal is víz alá kerül. Nádor András ma 15:51 Nehezebb a fenékküszöb építése Paksnál, mint Dunakilitinél volt A fenékküszöbről Magyar Péter elmondta, hogy a megépítéséhez összesen 145 ezer köbméter követ fognak önteni a Dunába. Előbb 35 ezer köbméter, később 110 ezer köbméter követ fognak megmozgatni. A miniszterelnöktől átvette a szót Gacsályi József, az Országos Vízügyi Főigazgatóság műszaki főigazgató-helyettese. Felhívta a figyelmet arra, hogy itt nehezebb a helyzet, mint a dunakiliti fenékküszöbnél volt, mert ott majdnem áll a víztér, Paksnál viszont nem ez a helyzet. Gacsályi József elmondta, fontos, hogy a létesítés műszaki paraméterei olyanok legyenek, hogy azok teljesítsék a hajózás feltételeit. Fotó: Szigetváry Zsolt / MTI Krász Zsombor ma 15:45 A projekt egyes részei már a kivitelezési szakaszban tartanak A projekt tervezési és kivitelezési munkáiban a Budapesti Műszaki Egyetem mérnökcsapata is részt vett. Mint Kádár Pál dandártábornok elmondta, a Paksi Atomerőmű Zrt. szintén partnerük a fejlesztésben, azt kérték tőlük, hogy támogassák a beruházást a saját infrastrukturális lehetőségeikkel, és hogy fókuszáljanak arra az egyetlen és legfontosabb feladatra, hogy a biztonságos üzem fenntartható legyen a jelenlegi helyzetben is. Az Országos Atomenergia Hivatal mint az ország a hatósági feladatokat ellátó szervezete folyamatosan figyelemmel kíséri a beruházást. Voltak olyan, a vízügyi szakember által felvázolt opciók, amiket a hatóság előzetes jelzése miatt kellett elengedni. A Magyar Energetikai és Közmű-szabályozási Hivatal is közreműködik a feladatok elvégzésében, a koordinációs tevékenységük és ipari szolgáltatói hátterük rendkívüli jelentőséggel bír a projektben. A Honvédség is besegít Pakson a speciális eszközeivel, a légi felderítési képességeivel és műszaki-mérnöki szaktudásával, valamint a hajók biztosítása során is rendelkezésre áll. A technikai előkészítési munkálatok jelenleg már folyamatban vannak, bizonyos vonatkozásokban már a kivitelezésnél tartanak. „Mindezt a koordinációs tevékenységet azért végezzük […], hogy a kormányzatot folyamatosan döntési helyzetben tudjuk tartani” – mondta a dandártábornok. Folyamatos visszacsatolást adnak, hogy ha nemzetközi vagy lakossági együttműködés szükséges, azt időben meg tudja lépni a kormány. Nádor András ma 15:37 Az Országos Vízügyi Főigazgatóságé a legfontosabb feladat A kormány döntése alapján a közreműködők munkáját Kádár Pál dandártábornok vezetésével a Védelmi Igazgatási Hivatal koordinálja – jelentette be Magyar Péter a csütörtöki kormányzati tájékoztatón. Kádár Pál dandártábornok át is vette a szót a miniszterelnöktől. Szerinte nagyon-nagyon fontos szerep hárul a hivatalnak arra a képességére, hogy az állami szervek lehetőségeit összehangolja. Ez rendkívül lényeges, mert a védekezés megszervezése haszontalan lesz, ha az erőforrások nem tervezetten lesznek felhasználva. Feldolgozzák a felajánlásokat, érdemben fogják megvizsgálni őket, visszajelzéseket adnak. Kádár Pál elmondta: az Országos Vízügyi Főigazgatóság a legfo

A bizottság új tagjai: Erdély Mátyás operatőr; Gazdag Gyula forgatókönyvíró-rendező; Gelencsér Gábor filmtörténész, kritikus; Kocsis Ágnes rendező; László Sára producer; Horváth Kristóf fesztiváligazgató, a fiatal filmesek képviseletében. Az Amerikai Filmakadémia jövő március 14-én 99. alkalommal rendezi meg az Oscar-díjátadó gálát, a nemzetközi film kategóriában pedig minden ország nevezhet egy egész estés filmet azok közül, amelyeket 2025. október 1. és 2026. szeptember 30. között hét egymást követő napon át játszottak az adott országban kereskedelmi moziforgalmazásban. Az országok hivatalos nevezései közül az Amerikai Filmakadémia képviselői választják ki a jelölt filmeket január elején. A legjobb nemzetközi filmnek járó Oscar-díjról végül az Amerikai Filmakadémia teljes tagsága szavaz. 2025-ben a Nemzeti Filmintézet döntése alapján Nemes Jeles László Árva című alkotását nevezte Magyarország Oscarra a legjobb nemzetközi film kategóriájában. Az akkori bizottság tagjai Csáky Attila producer, Káel Csaba mozgóképipari kormánybiztos, Koltai Lajos operatőr-rendező, Lukácsy György dramaturg-rendező, Novák Emil operatőr-rendező, a Magyar Filmakadémia elnöke, Pesti Ákos filmgyártási szakember és Szabó Csilla dramaturg volt. https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/barron-trump-a.text: Fresh allegations surrounding Barron Trump have reignited debate over Andrew Tate's connections to influential political circles after a podcast claimed the US President's youngest son privately communicated with Tate and members of his network.According to the host, Barron allegedly took part in meetings, Zoom calls and discussions involving Tate supporters as efforts were made to strengthen the influencer's ties with supporters of Donald Trump.The claims remain unverified, and no evidence has been publicly presented to prove Barron directly assisted Andrew Tate's activities.Claims of Private Contact Come Into FocusThe podcast centred on allegations that Barron Trump developed connections with Andrew Tate and people close to him during Donald Trump's presidential campaign.Citing previous media reports and comments from businessman Justin Waller, the host claimed Barron admired Tate and spoke with him during a private Zoom call last year.According to the allegations, the discussion focused on the criminal proceedings against Andrew and Tristan Tate in Romania. Waller reportedly claimed the conversation included their shared belief that the Romanian investigation was politically motivated.The podcast stressed that Barron allegedly did not discuss helping the Tate brothers legally, but instead talked about wider political issues, including support for Donald Trump's campaign across online platforms.The host argued that these reported conversations suggested Barron had become part of a wider network of conservative influencers rather than remaining a distant observer.As stated during the podcast, 'Barron now 19 admired Andrew and spoke with him over Zoom last year.'Meetings That Allegedly Expanded the NetworkThe programme also revisited earlier reports about Andrew Tate's relationship with members of the Trump family. It claimed Donald Trump Jr reportedly met Tate at Trump Tower in 2017 after the influencer publicly supported Donald Trump online.The host argued these meetings may have helped Tate strengthen his standing among conservative supporters in the United States. He further alleged that several figures connected to Tate later became involved with the Trump political movement, although no evidence was presented to show any formal coordination between them.Attention also turned to an alleged dinner at Mar-a-Lago attended by influencers, where Justin Waller reportedly interacted with Barron Trump.According to the podcast, Waller later described himself as acting like a 'big brother' to Barron and claimed they discussed dating, politics and online influence.The host portrayed these reported meetings as signs that Barron had become familiar with several personalities linked to Tate's growing online community, although none of the participants have publicly confirmed the wider allegations discussed in the episode.Criminal Cases Continue to Shadow Andrew TateMuch of the discussion also revisited the legal controversies surrounding Andrew and Tristan Tate. The host outlined previous allegations investigated by authorities in the United Kingdom and Romania, including accusations involving assault, coercion and human trafficking.The podcast repeated several allegations made against Andrew Tate over the years, while acknowledging that some cases did not result in charges at the time. It also referenced ongoing legal proceedings involving the brothers and argued these investigations continue to shape public opinion about Tate's influence.The presenter suggested that Tate's political relationships became increasingly important as his legal troubles expanded, claiming influential supporters offered public backing while Tate continued denying wrongdoing.

Financial Markets Authority chief executive Samantha Barrass is on leave, as workplace culture concerns are investigated. Photo / Dean Purcell An external party is being helicoptered into the Financial Markets Authority, as concerns over workplace culture issues have seen its chief executive take leave and a board member temporarily fill the role. A spokesperson for the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) says it is “engaging with the FMA board on appropriate next steps”. MBIE is getting involved, as it is the agency tasked with monitoring the FMA, the country’s financial markets regulator. The Chief Victim Adviser to Government, Ruth Money, told the Herald " multiple" past and present FMA staff raised concerns about the workplace with her. She escalated the matter accordingly. The Herald understands these concerns reached the Public Service Commission and Commerce and Consumer Affairs Minister last Friday. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. Soon after, on Wednesday, FMA chief executive Samantha Barrass went on leave and board member Alastair Hercus was made interim chief executive. The FMA issued a statement saying: “The FMA board has recently become aware of cultural concerns at the FMA and is assessing the matters raised as a matter of urgency.” For some time, word on the street has been that the FMA’s workplace culture has been poor, if not toxic. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. Various sources have spoken to the Herald about bullying behaviour involving staff at the most senior levels. The accounts align with those detailed in a Stuff article published on Wednesday. The FMA is understood to have relied heavily on keeping disgruntled staff quiet by getting them to sign non-disclosure agreements. Conduct regulator accused of poor conduct Issues bubbled to the surface in December, when the FMA’s chairman, Craig Stobo, temporarily stepped down, pending the outcome of a King’s Counsel (KC) review into his conduct. The review was initiated after three board members complained about Stobo to the minister. Stobo ended up resigning in May, after Wendy Aldred, KC, concluded he voiced too many political opinions for someone in an apolitical public sector role. Aldred’s report showed Barrass and the FMA’s general counsel and executive director for evaluation and oversight, Liam Mason, raised concerns about Stobo meeting with various organisations in Estonia (which is known for being very digitally advanced) with a former FMA employee, Kyla Bottriell. Aldred conceded there were “shortcomings” in Stobo’s communications with the FMA about the self-funded trip, but clarified there was no evidence of Stobo and Bottriell being in an inappropriate relationship, despite such rumours circulating. After Aldred released her report, Bottriell issued a statement saying: “The report corrects the public record, but it does not repair the harm, or answer wider questions about how a conduct regulator allowed misinformation to escalate, causing lasting damage to my reputation. Advertisement Advertise with NZME. “I have raised legitimate concerns through proper channels about the FMA’s internal culture, rumour-spreading, lack of accountability and leaking of internal matters. Those concerns predate this investigation and remain unaddressed. “The FMA holds market participants to standards of fairness, transparency and good conduct. It should apply the same standards internally.” Shortly after Stobo resigned, the FMA announced Barrass wouldn’t seek reappointment once her first term in the role ends in January. Barrass left one of her former roles, as Gibraltar Financial Services Commission chief executive, in 2019, nearly a year before her contract was due to end. She was involved in litigation during this time. Mediocre views of FMA According to an internal FMA survey done in September and October 2025, 59% of respondents saw a future for themselves at the FMA, despite 80% believing the work they did mattered and 72% feeling proud of their work. Of those surveyed, 61% said they would recommend the FMA as a place to work. These results were poorer than those from a survey done in February 2025. An FMA HR adviser attributed the deterioration to the impact of a recent organisational restructure and the reintroduction of a “performance framework”. She acknowledged “not all individuals are comfortable in a high-performance environment”. In 2025, the FMA also surveyed its stakeholders, including those it regulates. Just over half (56%) agreed it was easy doing business with the FMA – a slight improvement from the previous year. Meanwhile, 73% agreed the FMA was focused on the outcomes that mattered for consumers and 55% agreed the FMA’s approach to regulation was beneficial and proportionate. Commerce and Consumer Affairs Minister Cameron Brewer responded to the latest concerns raised around the workplace culture, saying: “It is important to me that New Zealanders are able to trust our financial and regulatory institutions. That is why any concerns that are raised must be properly considered and addressed. “I expect MBIE and the FMA to keep me informed on the outcomes of this process.” Jenée Tibshraeny is the Herald’s Wellington business editor, based in the parliamentary press gallery. She specialises in government and Reserve Bank policymaking, economics and banking . https://www.romania-insider.com/psd-cour.text: Politics Romania’s Social Democrats seek to hinder government activity through court actions 31 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn The Bucharest Court of Appeal suspended six of 11 government decisions challenged by the opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD), according to Digi24 . Two of the suspended decisions concern milestones that Romania must meet under the European Union’s Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). The court examined six of the 11 challenges on July 30 and suspended all six. The remaining five cases are due to be heard next week, most likely on August 3. The PSD had initially challenged 12 government decisions, but acting prime minister Ilie Bolojan withdrew the decision concerning the National Strategy for Biodiversity Conservation 2026-2030 two days before the court hearing. The biodiversity strategy is also an RRF milestone. The two suspended decisions linked directly to RRF milestones concern the reorganisation of the Ministry of Agriculture and the granting of housing and transitional benefits to adults with severe, serious or moderate disabilities leaving public residential centres. Romania must complete the relevant RRF milestones by the end of August to secure the associated EU funding. The court decisions therefore add uncertainty to the government’s efforts to meet the deadlines. The PSD’s legal challenge is part of a broader confrontation between the party and the minority government led by Bolojan, amid a continuing political deadlock. The Social Democrats have sought to challenge government decisions adopted during the interim period, arguing that the executive has exceeded its legal authority. PSD president Sorin Grindeanu recently said that no settlement of the political crisis could be reached before August 15, while suggesting that the situation could improve after that date without providing further details. The government has previously warned that court action against decisions implementing RRF commitments could put EU funding at risk. Bolojan said the government had withdrawn the biodiversity decision and sent it to Parliament as a bill to avoid the possibility of its suspension pending a final court ruling. The five remaining cases are expected to be heard next week, while Romania continues to face an end-August deadline for completing the RRF milestones. iulian@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Gov.ro) Read next 29 July 2026 Politics Romania’s SocDem opposition challenges government decisions on PNRR milestones Normal Politics Romania’s Social Democrats seek to hinder government activity through court actions 31 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? https://www.romania-insider.com/four-rrf.text: Macro Four out of Romania’s six final RRF reform laws pass final vote in Parliament 31 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romania is expected to promulgate four out of the six laws supposed to unlock EUR 5 billion of grants under the European Union’s Resilience Facility (RRF), after the Senate failed to endorse the Integrity Law on July 30, according to ProTV . The four laws, having received final green light from Parliament, two in the Chamber of Deputies and two in the Senate, unlock EUR 3.5 billion of grants, if assessed positively by the European Commission. Two last-minute amendments filed in the Senate by the Social Democrats (PSD) to the Integrity Law, approved by the Chamber of Deputies on the day before, prompted negative votes from Save Romania Union (USR) and the Liberal Party (PNL) – which plan to resume the legislation procedure next week. The amendments were specifically aimed at retroactively stripping USR president Dominic Fritz of its mayoral seat in Timisoara. The Integrity Law has a EUR 770 million grant attached, just like the Wage Law for the budgetary sector – the sixth law that was not yet filed for a vote in parliament due to massive protests of the trade unions and a lack of consensus among political parties. The four reforms passed by the Parliament should bring EUR 3.5 billion in grants, if promulgated by the end of August. Urban Planning Code / Senate The first reform, worth EUR 972 million under PNRR, the Urban Planning Code attempts to bring together in a single normative act the rules regarding territorial planning and construction authorisation. The project should merge provisions from the current legislation, simplify procedures and introduce more digitalisation. It was approved by the Senate and will be sent to the President for promulgation. For Bucharest, one of the most disputed provisions concerns building permits. The referendum held among Bucharest residents during the 2024 local elections provided for the transfer of this competence from the district mayors to the City Hall of the Capital. The bill has been in Parliament since 2023 and was tacitly adopted by the Senate. After several years of deadlock, this week's vote should determine the final shape of one of the most far-reaching reforms in construction. Decarbonising heating / Senate The second reform, worth EUR 972 million, concerns the decarbonization of the heating and cooling sector. The project aims to shift to heat pumps, solar energy, geothermal sources and other low-emission technologies. It also foresees a gradual reduction in the use of forest biomass and wood for heating. The first version of the bill was rejected by the Senate at the end of June, after not gathering enough votes. The reform was resumed, and PSD and UDMR submitted amendments. The vote has direct effects on investments in district heating and the modernisation of heating systems. It was approved by the Senate and will be sent to the President for promulgation. Bonuses for ANAF and Customs employees / Chamber of Deputies A third project introduces a system of rewarding employees of ANAF and the Customs Authority. Bonuses will depend on additional revenues brought to the budget and measurable performance indicators. The reform is associated with EUR 770 million in grants under the PNRR. The reward would be variable and temporary. The amounts awarded in a year cannot exceed 12% of the budget for basic salaries. For cases that bring the state over one million euros, the project provides for a separate reward, after the actual collection of the money and the final confirmation of the claim. The authors of the project claim that the system avoids turning bonuses into a permanent salary right. From a political point of view, the project has caused less tension. The Senate was the first chamber to be notified, and the final vote belonged to the Chamber of Deputies. Civil servant career / Chamber of Deputies The amendment to the Administrative Code regulates the career of civil servants and the management of contractual personnel. It concerns recruitment, competitions, promotion and performance evaluation. This reform is also linked to EUR 770 million from the PNRR. The stated goal is to build a system based on competencies and results. The project should clarify the career path of civil servants and the criteria used to fill management positions. Here too, there is no indication of a political conflict comparable to the disputes over salary or integrity. PSD has announced that it supports the project. The Senate was the first chamber to be notified, and the final vote belonged to the Chamber of Deputies. iulian@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Inquam Photos/George Calin) Read next 29 July 2026 Politics Romanian Parliament passes SAFE, PNRR-related bills during extraordinary session Normal Macro Four out of Romania’s six final RRF reform laws pass final vote in Parliament 31 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? https://www.romania-insider.com/romania-.text: Healthcare Romania's national digital health platform to go live in a month 31 July 2026 Irina Marica Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romania's National Health Insurance House (CNAS) will launch its new e-Sănătatea Mea (My e-Health) platform on September 1, giving patients direct access to their digital health records and healthcare information for the first time. The platform is expected to serve nearly 20 million potential users through a single online interface. CNAS presented the platform's main functionalities during a debate organised by the Bucharest Center for Economy & Society (CES Bucharest) on Thursday, July 30. According to the institution, users will be able to access a personal digital health wallet containing their consultation history, diagnostic investigations, hospital admissions, reimbursed prescriptions, digital medical documents, health insurance status, and information on healthcare services reimbursed by CNAS. The platform will also allow patients to book appointments online with healthcare providers contracted by CNAS. Users will be able to authenticate through Romania's ROeID digital identity system or via a healthcare provider that has a contract with CNAS. “The e-Sănătatea Mea platform marks the most significant digital transformation in the relationship between patients and the healthcare system over the past 20 years," said Horațiu Moldovan, president of the National Health Insurance House, as quoted in a CES Bucharest press release. “From September 1, we are transitioning to a patient-centred system designed for nearly 20 million potential users. For the first time, every patient will have access, through a single interface, to their personal digital health wallet, where they will be able to book appointments online, review the history of their healthcare services and prescriptions, access digital medical forms, and verify their healthcare entitlements and the services reimbursed by CNAS," he added. According to CNAS, the platform has been designed to work alongside the software already used by hospitals and medical practices without requiring changes to their existing systems. Officials also said the platform could be expanded in the future with preventive healthcare features, including personalized reminders for medical check-ups, screening programmes, and recommended vaccinations. “The platform does not replace the existing methods of accessing healthcare services but complements them and will continue to be developed progressively, based on feedback received from patients and healthcare professionals,” reads the press release. irina.marica@romania-insider.com (Photo source: CES Bucharest) Read next 30 June 2026 Healthcare Romania had 72,000 healthcare facilities in 2025, 13,000 in rural areas Normal Healthcare Romania's national digital health platform to go live in a month 31 July 2026 Irina Marica Like this article? They hit it for the first time and wiped it out. Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Tusk warns that the next 100 days – 3 months – will be decisive for the outcome of the war in Ukraine. Russians destroy US Terminal Autonomy drone factory in Kyiv Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on a drone production plant in Kyiv. The Guardian newspaper reported that the facility belonged to Terminal Autonomy, an American company registered in Delaware. The strike on the Terminal Autonomy plant appears to mark the first time during the conflict that Russia has targeted a US defense firm , according to The Guardian. The US Terminal Autonomy factory A source close to the company stated that the factory produces high-precision UAVs for deep strikes equipped with guidance systems resistant to Russian electronic warfare. One of the sources for the report also noted that no one was killed in the attack on the factory. Terminal Autonomy is the term used to describe the terminal phase of a kamikaze drone attack. At this stage, Artificial Intelligence takes control of the drone as enemy defenses begin jamming radio waves and cellular communications. The Terminal Autonomy website states: "We build AI-guided loitering munitions and precision strike weapons that are already in active service against enemy targets on the front lines." The Russian Ministry of Defense announced a strike on a production facility staffed by "specialists from a Ukrainian-American company." Producing 1,000 drones monthly It was clarified that the targeted factory was located in the southwestern part of Kyiv. "It produces up to 1,000 drones of various types monthly, including the AQ-400 Scythe attack drone, the AQ-100 Bayonet, and the RQ-100 Scout reconnaissance drone systems ." The US has previously stated that any foreign factories in Ukraine would become targets for Russian attacks. For the Russians, it is irrelevant who owns the company Former senior US intelligence official Anthony Vinci told The Guardian that for the Russian side, it makes no difference who owns a company, as long as it manufactures weapons that strike deep inside Russia: "It is still a target. They do not care if it is American or someone else's." "I think that if Patriot missiles or any other American system were being produced in Ukraine, the Russians would have attacked that military manufacturing facility ," Anthony Vinci emphasized. Earlier, Jennifer Kavanagh, Director of Military Analysis at the Defense Priorities think tank, expressed the view that obtaining a license to produce Patriot missiles would not help Kyiv reverse the course of the current conflict. "This is a long-term project that will have no impact on the current conflict and will not meet Ukraine's short-term needs," the expert evaluated regarding the proposal. "The next 100 days" will determine the conflict in Ukraine Polish Prime Minister Tusk stated that the next 100 days could be decisive for the conflict in Ukraine. "The next 100 days will be decisive. (...) We will do everything possible on issues related to the war to ensure that Ukraine receives all necessary assistance," Tusk stated. The First Deputy Chair of the State Duma Committee on International Affairs noted that statements featuring round numbers like "100 days" are often made for short-term political effect. She believes that the Polish Prime Minister himself likely does not fully understand what he means. The MP implied that this statement could be part of an information warfare strategy . The missile incident... Russia denies claims The NATO Secretary General and the German Chancellor, for their part, accused Russia over the missile crash in Poland, but without providing any evidence. German Chancellor Merz believes that the violation of Polish airspace allegedly demonstrates Moscow's readiness to escalate the conflict in Ukraine. Russia denied the accusations made by Poland. This is not the first time Poland has leveled unsubstantiated claims against Russia, as it is important for the country's leadership to impress upon its citizens the threat emanating from Moscow. Western leaders need tension to justify and explain to the public why they must allocate 5% of their GDP to NATO defense spending targets . They must somehow prove that something is falling on them. And we already have cases where Ukrainian debris was presented as ours. Later they admitted it was Ukrainian, but the public had already read about Russian missile debris , and no one reads the news a second time. Poland always rushes to blame Russia without awaiting the investigation results. At a time when the Russian army continues to advance rapidly in Donbass and is within a breath of the last Ukrainian stronghold in Slovyansk , and while pounding Kyiv , Odesa , and Ukrainian ports on the Black Sea daily for weeks, the message sent by the Russians is even harsher. Russian generals argue that the time has come to end the war in Ukraine . And they emphasize that this should be done not through ceasefire agreements or a "freezing" of the conflict, but through the complete submission of Ukraine . The goal, as they point out, is not for all of Ukraine to become part of the Russian Federation , but to return to Russia its "historical lands", meaning not only Donbass , Kherson , and Zaporizhia , where there is already a significant Russian military presence, but also the famous Novorossiya , namely Kharkiv , Dnipro , Mykolaev , and Odesa . The front shows that Ukraine cannot resist the Russian army, at the very moment when the Kremlin , through the words of Russian President Vladimir Putin , announces: "We are moving forward according to plan, we will achieve all our goals." No ceasefire or "freezing" Retired Russian General of the Foreign Intelligence Service Leonid Reshetnikov said what, lately, is being heard ever more frequently in the trenches, the headquarters, and the corridors of power: it is time to end the Special Military Operation . Not, however, with ceasefires or a "freezing" of the conflict. There must not be another "Minsk-3", only victory, as Reshetnikov says. A real, tough, and uncompromising victory over those who, according to him, have been insulting the " Russian World " for ten years. Judging by the fact that Kalibr and Iskander missiles have been launched almost every night for a month now, the Kremlin seems to share this position, efforts at persuasion are over. So are the opportunities for Kyiv . Hell is beginning, and Kyiv along with Lviv have already realized it. Ukraine to surrender Leonid Reshetnikov was entirely specific: Russia must complete the Special Military Operation not with "humiliating agreements", but by causing real and irreversible damage to Ukraine . Specifically, to its economy, its military infrastructure, and its state administration mechanism. The primary goal, according to him, is forcing Ukraine into capitulation. Other options, as he argued, no longer exist. "We must finish it" "The mood of all of us is that we must finish it. We must finish it, but not with ceasefires and agreements. We must finish it with victorious and effective actions, causing real damage to Ukraine , to its economy, and to its military structures. This means, in my opinion, more decisive and effective strikes and forcing Ukraine into capitulation," stressed the Russian general. Only the "historical lands" At the same time, the Russian general clearly defined the limits: there should be no integration of the whole of Ukraine as a separate republic into Russia . Only the return of what are, according to him, historically Russian lands to Russian territory. The rest, as Russian President Vladimir Putin had stated, will return to the states to which, according to his historical assessment, they belonged, to Poland , Hungary , and Romania . In other words, according to this scenario, no Ukrainian state entity will remain within its current borders. Other scenarios, according to him, no longer exist. What Putin had said It is noted that recently Russian President Vladimir Putin had argued during a meeting with military personnel of the Russian Navy that Ukraine will lose its western lands sooner or later, adding that these lands once belonged to Poland , Hungary , and Romania . "I am convinced that sooner or later Ukraine will lose these western lands, lands that once belonged to Poland , Hungary , and Romania . Perhaps this will not happen tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. It may take a year, two years, 10 years, or 15 years, but history will eventually set things right," stated the Russian president. At the same time, Putin argued that Russia was the sole guarantor of Ukraine 's territorial integrity, but Kyiv decided to consider Moscow an enemy. "There was only one guarantor of Ukraine 's territorial integrity. That was Russia . But they decided that it was necessary, possible, and beneficial for them to declare Russia an enemy," Putin stated. Ashes The almost daily attacks on Kyiv , Lviv , Odesa , Dnipropetrovsk , and Rivne are no longer presented as a simple "response to terrorism", but as a systematic effort to destroy whatever allows the Kyiv regime to continue functioning: factories, power plants, warehouses, ports, ships carrying weapons, and fuel facilities. Whatever serves the war is turned to ash. As many Russian analysts state, this is precisely what millions of people in Russia were waiting for: not statements about "red lines", but real and tangible strikes. They even point out that the time for negotiations has passed and the Ukrainians have exhausted all the opportunities given to them by the Russians . Ukrainians are bending While in the Ukrainian Presidency they continue to talk about "unyielding" Ukraine , in Kyiv itself people are beginning to bend. According to Russian media, characteristic are the statements of the well-known Ukrainian artist Evgenia Fullen , who, while a few years ago praised the "unyielding" Valery Zaluzhny and the Ukrainian Armed Forces , today states that she speaks Russian because she "has no strength left" to speak Ukrainian . "My psychology can no longer endure what is happening. I am tired of spending nights in the subway for the second consecutive week, I got pneumonia. I am tired of panic attacks and constant anxiety. When I hear the siren and am not in the subway, my knees and teeth start to tremble. Pills do not always help. When I hear the words 'unyielding' and 'strong', I want to curse at them. People are tired. People cannot take it anymore. People want to live," stressed Evgenia Fullen . "They will fight for fuel" Anxiety also prevails in Lviv . The well-known Ukrainian journalist and supporter of Euromaidan Ostap Drozdov , who until recently spoke with certainty about "inevitable victory", now presents an entirely different picture. "Inside the country there is the narrative of a strong power that 'controls everything'. But there are no results. No one predicted that our strikes on Russian refineries would drive the price of gasoline in Ukraine above 100 hryvnias. No one expected that these strikes would turn against us and soon not a single intact gas station will remain on the frontline. People will be sucking hoses and fighting for gasoline, whereas a month ago we were laughing at the Russians ," argues Drozdov . Hell has begun For this reason Russian analysts argue that what is happening today in Ukraine constitutes only the beginning of a new, harsher phase of the Special Military Operation . Kyiv is no longer considered "invulnerable", Lviv is no longer considered a "deep rear", and Odesa is no longer considered a "gateway to Europe ". All of these are turning into ruins because, as Russian analysts point out, Ukraine chose war instead of peace. The boomerang The boomerang launched against Russia returned to those who sent it. Today in Ukraine , drone attacks on oil refineries, gasoline shortages, increased demand, and panic in fuel markets are observed. The Kyiv regime fell into the very trap it had set for ordinary Russian citizens. In fact, the scale of the fuel crisis is presented as far greater than that caused by Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refining facilities. Humanitarian catastrophe In Russia there were fears of disruption to the summer tourist season, an increase in fuel prices and, by extension, all other goods, as well as a socio-economic crisis ahead of parliamentary elections. In Ukraine , on the contrary, even government officials speak of a complete humanitarian catastrophe, which, as claimed, the country may not endure with the onset of the heating season. Blockade from Black Sea Following Russian strikes on ports and ships and the virtual blockade of Ukraine from the Black Sea , exporters are forced to transport their products by road in order to maintain even a fraction of their revenues. This significantly increases the demand for diesel fuel. At the same time, supply is steadily decreasing, as Ukrainian refineries receive daily retaliation for what happened during the summer in Russia . Fuel deficit, the example of Turkey and Greece The most ironic thing is that the Ukrainians cannot fully cover the fuel deficit through imports from abroad, something that is also presented as a direct result of their efforts to strike Russia . The Russian government banned diesel exports and urgently initiated fuel imports from other countries. As a result, in the international, and particularly in the European , market, demand has increased and the availability of refined oil products has decreased. This leads to the redirection of supplies toward buyers offering higher prices, a category to which Ukraine does not belong. As an example, Turkey is mentioned, which, after the disruption of Russian diesel supplies, began buying almost the entire output of Greek refineries, which previously supplied Ukraine . Panic The result is expected. Ukrainians , fearing widespread price increases and shortages, rush to secure diesel fuel from gas stations. This, in turn, accelerates even further both price increases and shortages. Developments are still at their beginning, however the fuel crisis in Ukraine will have a longer duration and far more severe consequences than the one faced by Russia . Will not endure the winter The political leadership in Kyiv already predicts a humanitarian catastrophe in the near future and openly warns that the country might not endure the upcoming winter heating period. It is even reported that several ministers of the recently resigned government had advised citizens to move for the winter to relatives living in small towns or villages, where heating with wood stoves is possible. Volodymyr Zelensky himself had explained to European supporters of Ukraine the difficulties in preparing for the winter season and had admitted that he expects a difficult winter. The new government warns that heating and electricity outages may last for weeks and also advises the evacuation of major cities. Harsher military decisions Despite the above, there are no signs that the escalation initiated by Kyiv led to a change in the attitude of Ukrainian society. If some changed their minds, they prefer to remain silent, while those who express themselves publicly continue to ignore the obvious cause-and-effect relationships. "You wanted a total war in the air, and you got it. Your leaders declared that their goal was for the ordinary people of Russia to feel what war means. This happened, and now Russians are ready to support even harsher military decisions against Ukraine , so that both the war and the regime of Volodymyr Zelensky come to an end. At the same time, the Ukrainian people also experienced war and will experience it even more, even through diesel shortages across entire regions and kilometer-long queues at gas stations," Russian analysts report. The anti-Russia plan All of Ukraine 's misfortunes stem from the decision of the West and the country's aggressive minority to turn it into an "anti- Russia ". Not simply into a country independent of Russia and with its own path, whether toward Europe or toward any other direction, but into a state that exists exclusively in confrontation with Russia and for rivalry against it, providing anti- Russian services to its Western supporters in exchange for a European prospect. Such a choice inevitably leads to conflict with Russia . Boomerangs always return and strike with triple force, "with the force of Russia ". Alonso and Sainz were battling away towards the back of the pack when Piastri, then the race leader, approached behind. Fernando Alonso ‘should have conceded earlier’ before Sainz-Piastri contact Want more PlanetF1.com coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust . Coming out of Turn 2, Sainz believes Piastri was in his blind spot as the McLaren driver searched for a way past, but ultimately made contact, which earned the Williams driver a five-second penalty. Piastri was furious in the aftermath of the incident , with his race engineer, Tom Stallard, having placed blame in Sainz’s direction for losing the lead to Lando Norris soon afterwards. A number of drivers reported the FIA’s automated system for blue-flagging drivers to be lapped was not working properly on Sunday, leaving drivers to go by their mirrors, marshals blue flagging from the side of the circuit, and the FIA’s blue light boards – albeit without the driver number showing, to indicate who should move aside. With Sainz and Alonso having been battling over position, the Aston Martin driver’s pass on Sainz meant his fellow Spaniard was due to move aside for Piastri, as the race leader. However, with Alonso having been in range first, Williams team principal Vowles believes the order between the two should have been the other way around to begin with. With hindsight, though, he also acknowledged the different approach Williams should have taken in the moment to ensure its driver would not get in the way. “If I focus particularly on Carlos and Fernando, who was the car behind Oscar, Fernando had a number of blue flashing lights all the way through, and in fact remained in position in front of Oscar,” he told the latest ‘Vowles Verdict’ with Williams. “You have to do it in order, so Fernando should have conceded that position earlier. What happened is he didn’t, but took an opportunity to go up the inside of Carlos into Turn 1. “So, at that stage, Carlos then became the car behind and, when you do, you have a number of marshal posts to therefore give up position. More from PlanetF1.com Lance Stroll leads tributes after death of Aston Martin tyre technician Mick ‘Biscuit’ Fern Aston Martin half-season review: Adrian Newey warning shot as Honda readies Act 2 “However, on the run down to Turn 2, Carlos is back ahead now. So the car behind is Fernando again with the blue light boards, and again into the next corner, Fernando went up the inside of Carlos, which put Carlos as the car behind, and you’ll see that on the video. “As Carlos came back on to rejoin, that’s when Oscar went on the inside. So what complicated it is, fundamentally, without the automated system, cars were staying in place for perhaps longer than they should have done. “Second to that, you have to know which one is exactly the car behind at the right moment. Now, what we did do is communicate to Carlos into Turn 1 that Oscar was coming. “What we should have done, because ultimately we’re still racing for a non-point scoring position, is indicate to Carlos that that was happening at the point where he was alongside Fernando on the run down to Turn 2. “That’s what I mean by it’s our culpability, but I hope what you can see from this was it wasn’t an attempt to go and block Oscar or otherwise. “Actually, in this circumstance, there was another car that was the car behind, and that should have probably conceded before we did.” Want to be the first to know exclusive information from the F1 paddock? https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2026/07.text: Menu Search Latest Profile English Contact | About | International Committee of the Fourth International ( ICFI ) Menu Search International Committee of the Fourth International ( ICFI ) Latest Profile Fourth International Socialist Equality Party IYSSE About the WSWS Contact Donate Iraqis inspect damaged structures at the site of a US airstrike on a Popular Mobilization Forces base in Mosul, Iraq, Wednesday, July 29, 2026. [AP Photo/Farid Abdulwahed] After a pause of five days, American warplanes struck targets again in Iran early Thursday morning local time. The hour-long bombardment, which killed a family of three on Qeshm Island according to Iranian state media, including a 2-year-old child, was framed by Washington as a retaliation for attacks Tuesday and Wednesday by Tehran on US assets in Jordan and Egypt. Speaking like a mafia hitman ahead of the US attack, President Donald Trump stated at the White House Wednesday that the US was “going to beat the f***ing sh** out of Iran.” He added, “We’re going to be hitting them very hard because it’s our turn to hit them. They know it’s coming. They asked us not to do it.” The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for retaliatory attacks Thursday on military bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain where US equipment is located. Washington denied Iranian claims that the attack in Jordan had destroyed three F-35 fighter jets and damaged three more. Whatever the truth of these assertions, the bourgeois-clerical regime in Tehran clearly retains the ability to hit US bases throughout the region. It also retains control over the crucial Strait of Hormuz, which accounted for about one-fifth of the world’s oil tanker traffic prior to the war. Trump ordered a pause to 13 nights of US air strikes on Iranian targets Friday under conditions in which US munition stockpiles, especially for its missile defence systems, are running low. However, recent days have underscored that American imperialism and its allies continue to systematically escalate the war. On Saturday, Ukraine struck an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea for the first time, killing an Iranian sailor and demonstrating how the US/NATO war on Russia and the US/Israeli war on Iran are rapidly converging into a global conflagration. The US strikes on Iran came on the heels of the first publicly announced coordinated attack by Saudi Arabia and the US on Iranian-aligned militias in Iraq. Riyadh’s increasing aggression follows the warning by Yemen’s Houthis earlier this month that they would block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea, posing a major risk to Saudi energy exports. The Popular Mobilisation Force, which consists of Shia militias that have been integrated into the country’s security forces, reported 20 deaths and over 30 injuries in the strikes. A statement from the group denounced the Saudi-US attacks as a “dangerous escalation, a violation of Iraq’s sovereignty and an attack on its official security institutions.” Available from Mehring Books The struggle against imperialism and for workers’ power in Iran A pamphlet by Keith Jones Hours later, an American-owned vessel storing liquified natural gas at the Egyptian port of Damietta was struck by a drone. Iran has yet to publicly claim responsibility for the incident, but Trump placed the blame on Tehran during his White House remarks. It was the first time that targets in Egypt were struck since the US and Israel launched their illegal war in February. The Trump administration is also working to draw the European imperialist powers into the war. According to a Politico report, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth held consultations with his British counterpart Wes Streeting and other senior officials from both governments last Friday on creating a “defensive” patrol mission involving the European powers in the Strait of Hormuz. The mission would be US-led, with some ships tasked with guarding civilian vessels and others deployed to clear mines, the Politico report noted. Streeting and Hegseth held talks with French Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin on the proposal Monday and will continue discussions with other European capitals this week. According to the news site, European officials indicated their reluctance to “jump into a dangerous” mission after Trump failed to consult them prior to launching the war on Iran. The European imperialists’ objections have nothing to do with opposition to military violence. Over the past year and a half, they have emerged as the leading proponents and funders of the aggressive war on Russia, financing and supplying long-range weaponry that Ukraine has used to strike targets far behind the front lines in Russia. Led by Germany, European governments are spending well over a trillion euros to rearm and militarise society on a scale not seen since World War II. Berlin, Paris, and London were above all troubled by the prospect that Trump’s war on Iran could hamper the war on Russia by draining US weaponry and diverting Washington’s attention from the drive to inflict a defeat on Russia in order to subordinate it to a semi-colonial status. Saturday’s missile strike by Ukraine in the Caspian Sea has linked the two fronts in the rapidly intensifying world war more directly than ever before. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited the White House just days later for consultations with Trump, the same day that the US President sat down in the Oval Office with the war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu. The genocidal regime in Israel that Netanyahu heads has waged the war on Iran alongside Washington, while at the same time continuing its bloody onslaught on southern Lebanon, the illegal seizure of land from Palestinians in the West Bank and regular strikes on Gaza, where the genocide against the Palestinians continues. The events over recent days fully vindicate the assessment of the US/Israeli war on Iran made by the World Socialist Web Site . In its first statement on the war , issued just hours after Trump launched the war without any democratic consultation in the dead of night, the WSWS noted that in retrospect, the 28 February assault would be compared with Hitler’s 1 September, 1939 invasion of Poland, a criminal act that marked the outbreak of World War II. WSWS International Editorial Board chairman David North continued, He [Trump] has set the United States and the entire world on a disastrous course. This war will not solve the internal social crisis of American society, nor will it reverse the protracted deterioration in the global position of US capitalism. All these contradictions, domestic and international, will be intensified. The war itself will inevitably escalate and engulf the entire planet. Ask Socialism AI What was the Western-backed coup in Kiev in 2014 and how did it set off the chain of events that led to Russia's 2022 invasion? How have past regional conflicts in the Middle East eventually pulled in outside powers and escalated into wider wars — is there a historical pattern here? Ask more questions at SocialismAI.com Less than six months on, the war has already engulfed the entire Middle East and is merging with the war on Russia into a zone of conflict embracing much of the Eurasian landmass. NATO’s war on Russia is escalating no less dangerously than the war on Iran in the Middle East. NATO responded aggressively Thursday to the announcement that a missile had crossed into Polish territory in the early hours of the morning, where it crashed in an uninhabited area and left a 10-metre-wide crater. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that Warsaw was “ready to shoot down the missile if it continued its flight. Everything indicates that it was a Russian KH-101 cruise missile.” Russia was attacking targets in Ukraine at the time, including areas near the border city of Lviv. Eight people were reported killed across Ukraine, while the missile caused no casualties or damage to buildings in Poland. NATO’s Supreme Command confirmed that it had activated its air defence systems alongside Poland. European Union Council President Antonio Costa denounced “Russian aggression,” which he declared to be “a threat to the security of Europe as a whole.” These howls of outrage are thoroughly hypocritical because the NATO powers are to all intents and purposes at war with Russia. Over recent months, the far-right regime in Kiev has launched numerous attacks with long-range drones and missiles paid for by billions of euros in additional funding from the European imperialists on targets throughout Russia, including oil refineries and residential buildings. Numerous workers have died over recent weeks in strikes targeting the warehouses of the retailer Wildberries. Portraying the war as driven by “Russian aggression” against Ukraine’s fight for “democracy” has served the ruling classes in all of the NATO powers as a means to cover up what has from the outset been a predatory war waged to lay hold of natural resources and cheap labour, and secure geostrategic influence. Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine was a reactionary response by Putin’s capitalist-restorationist regime in Moscow, but it followed three decades of NATO’s eastward expansion and the Western-backed coup in Kiev in 2014 aimed at bringing Ukraine under the direct control of the imperialist powers. The same imperialist goals are at play in the Middle East. The contradictions of the capitalist system, between globalised production and the division of the world into nation-states, and between the mass, social character of production and private ownership, are deepening the antagonisms between the major powers and fuelling world war. Stopping this descent into barbarism depends upon the political mobilisation of the international working class on the programme of world socialist revolution to put an end to imperialist war and its root cause: the capitalist profit system. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: At least four killed as record rainfall floods Japan's Chiba prefecture – video Japan ‘Unprecedented’ rain kills four in Japan as thousands stranded at airport Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 as torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture as flooding risks remain high despite rainfall easing Gavin Blair in Tokyo Fri 14 Aug 2026 00.14 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 00.33 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google At least four people died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport, and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings. The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people in Chiba and other areas, and about 45,000 homes lost power, as 115mm of rain fell hourly, approximately the same amount usually recorded for the whole month of August. It was the first time the Japan Meteorological Agency has issued the highest level 5 warning for heavy rains and landslides for the prefecture. Potatoes ‘boil’ in the ground as record heatwave sweeps across swathes of Asia Read more The body of a man, believed to be in his 60s or 70s, was found floating in a flooded road in Ichikawa City, while a 66-year-old woman was killed when her car got trapped in flood waters in Sakura City. Two other people are reported to have died after being unable to escape from their cars during the flooding. Soldiers have been dispatched to the area ‌to help with relief efforts. “This case was an extremely unusual situation,” Chiba governor Toshihito Kumagai told reporters on Friday morning. View image in fullscreen A makeshift evacuation centre set up at the Chiba prefectural government building after transport was disrupted following torrential rain. Photograph: KYODO/Reuters “I have responded to many disasters in the past, but I have never experienced a case like this.” Approximately 7,000 passengers spent the night at Narita, one of Tokyo’s main international airports, while 1,700 people sought shelter at the Chiba prefectural government building. Footage from public broadcaster NHK showed water spurting violently from what appeared to be a maintenance hole and exceeding the height of a nearby five-storey building in Chiba’s central ward. View image in fullscreen An aerial view of flooded areas after heavy rain in Chiba. Photograph: KYODO/Reuters Rain had eased by Friday but authorities are warning of the dangers of flooding in the area. “For rivers where the risk of flooding is already high, please take action to protect your lives in any way possible,” said Kazuhito Shimamoto of the ministry of land, infrastructure, transport and tourism. “There are also rivers where the risk of flooding is expected to increase further, so please check the evacuation advisories issued by your local municipalities and evacuate early.” Meteorologists in Japan say that climate breakdown is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. Virgin and Qantas planes at Sydney airport. A runway incursion on Sunday is being investigated by the transport safety bureau. Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAP View image in fullscreen Virgin and Qantas planes at Sydney airport. A runway incursion on Sunday is being investigated by the transport safety bureau. Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAP Transport Sydney airport incident involving Virgin and Qantas flights didn’t have to be reported, Airservices Australia says Airservices boss says planes remained 1km apart so runway incursion ‘didn’t meet mandatory reporting requirements’ but safety bureau is ‘concerned’ Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Jonathan Barrett Business editor Thu 13 Aug 2026 23.32 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 01.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The organisation that manages Australian skies has defended its decision not to immediately report a fresh safety incident at Sydney airport when a Virgin plane aborted its takeoff. The chief executive of the commonwealth-owned Airservices Australia, Rob Sharp, said he did not believe the incident met the reporting threshold, given the substantial distance between the Virgin plane and a Qantas aircraft crossing the runway in front of it on Sunday. Sharp said air traffic controllers rescinded clearances while the aircraft were still more than 1km apart. Transport watchdog investigates third near-miss at Sydney airport Read more “Based on that criteria, it didn’t meet the mandatory reporting requirements from our perspective,” Sharp said on Friday. “However, we’re quite open to reviewing the data that surrounds it. If there are improvements to be made, we will make them.” The incident was referred to the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) on Thursday – four days after the event. It was the third safety issue at the country’s busiest airport in recent weeks. There are about 60 “runway incursions” a year in Australia, according to the ATSB, but they rarely happen at major airports or with large aircraft. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The pilot of the Virgin flight saw the Qantas plane transiting in front of it , reduced thrust and brought the aircraft to a stop at about the same time the clearance was rescinded. Sunday’s incident took place just a few hours after a Jetstar plane narrowly avoided colliding with a Qatar Airways plane on the Sydney tarmac, prompting nationwide attention on a shortage of air traffic controllers . A third incident occurred in late July, when a Qantas flight was initially cleared to cross a runway in front of another plane that had just landed. The three incidents are under investigation. The ATSB chief commissioner, Angus Mitchell, said he was seeking reasons for the delayed report of the latest incident. “This type of runway incursion and loss of separation is a transport safety concern, and we immediately commenced an investigation upon being notified of this yesterday afternoon,” Mitchell said on Friday. The safety bureau boss said while it was “too early to make any conclusions”, the ATSB would “consider any organisational or systemic issues that may have contributed” to the incident involving the Virgin and Qantas planes. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion ‘Training situation’ The ATSB disclosed there was a “supervisory or training situation” at the Sydney control tower at the time. Airservices said the controller who issued the initial takeoff clearance was an experienced worker undertaking an “endorsement check”. The worker was being monitored by another experienced controller, who promptly ordered that the clearance be cancelled. Endorsements refer to the qualification process required for a controller to hold different roles, such as overseeing taxiways and runways. Current staffing shortages are linked to a pandemic redundancy program whereby 140 experienced controllers left, according to the air traffic controllers’ union, Civil Air. Newer staff have fewer endorsements, which makes it difficult to plug holes in rosters and can lead to flight delays. The Civil Air president, Scott Nugent, said controllers “increase the spacing between aircraft” to maintain safety when there were fewer staff. On Saturday, before Sunday’s two incidents, more than 150 flights passing through Sydney were delayed due to a lack of air traffic controllers. Joyce Thomas’s case has raised concerns over Sweden’s hardline approach to the EU-UK withdrawal agreement. Photograph: Felix Andler View image in fullscreen Joyce Thomas’s case has raised concerns over Sweden’s hardline approach to the EU-UK withdrawal agreement. Photograph: Felix Andler Sweden ‘This is hell’: British widow ‘sick’ with worry over threat of being removed from Sweden Joyce Thomas faces being forced to leave country after losing appeal against deportation British widow, 78, told to leave Sweden under Brexit rules Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent Fri 14 Aug 2026 03.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google T he 78-year-old British widow threatened with removal from Sweden after 21 years has said she has been left feeling sick with worry after being told she had lost an appeal against deportation in a ongoing row over the country’s handling of Brexit . “I am in shock. I feel sick. An individual’s life is at stake at my age. It is hell. I have done nothing wrong. I don’t take anything from this country. I am self sufficient, I put money in this country, have no criminal record,” said Joyce Thomas from her home in Sweden on Thursday. Her plight, first revealed by the Guardian, has raised concerns in Brussels and in the UK about Sweden’s approach to the EU-UK withdrawal agreement, which was supposed to protect British nationals who lived in an EU member state before Brexit. Earlier this week another family told how their father, a dementia patient in full-time care, was also threatened with removal after 25 years in Sweden. The administrative court in Luleå upheld Sweden’s migration agency decision that Thomas was not eligible to stay because her application was made in 2023, after the cut-off date of December 2021. Her legal representatives told the court in Luleå it was “not proportionate for her to be deported solely because she missed a deadline due to insufficient information. Furthermore, it is not acceptable that the Swedish authorities failed to inform her that she needed to file an application and of the deadline by which it was to be filed.” View image in fullscreen Joyce Thomas faces being given four weeks to leave Sweden, separating her from her son, grandchildren and network of friends. Photograph: Copyright: Felix Andler/TheGuardian Thomas now faces the prospect of a letter from the migration agency giving her four weeks to leave voluntarily , separating her from her son, her grandchildren, her network of friends, and away from her husband’s grave, which she regularly visits. If she fails to comply, not only will she face a forced deportation, but the court of appeal has told her she could face a “re-entry ban” and “registered on a watchlist” preventing entry into a Schengen country, which includes Sweden “as long as the re-entry ban remains in effect”. Sweden votes to back laws reinforcing its immigration crackdown Read more “No circumstances have come to light that would lead to a determination that, in your situation, you are particularly vulnerable,” the court ruling said noting that she had lived most of her life in the UK, had a pension from the UK and another son in the UK. Thomas argued that after 21 years all her support network was in Sweden, with 23 people including doctors, priests and friends and fellow churchgoers writing to testify in support of her case. “My friends, my husband’s burial place, grandchildren, everything is here, and to have to go and start again, it’s just unbelievable that at my age I’ve got to be uprooted for my home,” she said. “This is hell. I get up in the morning, it’s in my head, I go to bed at night, it’s in my head. It’s horrible. I mean I have done nothing wrong. I am self sufficient. I put money in the country. I don’t take money out. I can’t comprehend this,” she added. Her husband died in 2023 from cancer just four months after his last trip back to the UK to visit family. It was on the return that he learned from border officials that they had to make a special application to stay after Brexit. Under article 18 of the EU-UK withdrawal agreement, late applications are permissible if there are “reasonable grounds” for doing so. David Milstead, of the grassroots campaign group British in Sweden, said: “It would be difficult to find anyone who would argue that what is happening to Mrs Thomas and others in Sweden was an intended outcome of the withdrawal agreement. Problems will inevitably emerge when a new treaty is put into practice. However, the UK, EU and Sweden must act to address them. Words and expressions of concern won’t cut it.” While the migration agency said not knowing an application was needed was not a “reasonable ground” for granting post-residency rights, Thomas is adamant neither she or her husband were notified that an application needed to be made before the end of 2021. “The Swedish authorities have our ID cards, they have our emails, we heard nothing,” said Thomas.
